vision: An OTP-native task-execution engine an AI orchestrator drives end to end: it pulls tasks from the rmap roadmap, dispatches each to a headless coding agent (implementer) running in an isolated worktree, gates the result with a cross-family reviewer AI that runs the target project's own checks itself and fixes inline, merges approved work (lander rebase + ff-push), and audits landed commits post-merge with a third agent. The agent-gate workflow (worktree -> implementer AI -> reviewer AI -> MERGE -> audit AI, docs/agent-gate-workflow.md) is THE architecture: judgment lives in agents, harness code is mechanical substrate only. Consumer surfaces: the BEAM-native Elixir API (IEx, tidewave, another process), the Phoenix LiveView dashboard, and the native MCP server — a long-running OTP node orchestrating N registered target projects (Elixir, Rust, anything an agent can check) concurrently. harness is itself developed by dogfooding — from the core loop (Task 8) onward, every pending roadmap task is delivered by dispatching it through harness rather than hand-building it (load-bearing runtime scaffolding is the documented exception).

agent-gate.description: The agent-gate workflow rebuild (docs/agent-gate-workflow.md): worktree -> implementer AI -> reviewer AI (THE gate) -> MERGE -> audit AI, with no mechanical verification gate anywhere. The cross-family reviewer runs the project's checks itself, fixes inline, and writes .harness/review.json; harness reads it mechanically. Deletes Harness.Verification / CheckStack / presets / :verifying / review_green / the benchmark corpus.

agent-rules.description: Harden the prompt-to-agent pipeline: language-aware harness rule injection (don't ship Elixir conventions to non-Elixir targets) + capture the composed prompt+rules per run for post-hoc diagnosis

audit-agent.description: A third agent role beside implementer and reviewer: a batch-scoped post-merge audit agent. Each successful land enqueues an audit job (Oban :audit queue, unique per project); the audit agent gets a detached worktree of origin/<target>, reviews the unaudited commit range (last audit(...) commit -> HEAD), applies hygiene fixes inline, writes .audit/<sha>.md reports, commits as audit(...), and harness ff-pushes. Best-effort: never blocks, never reverts. Batch economics by design: one dispatch amortized over N commits — per-run grading stays the reviewer's seat.

autolanding.description: Close the autonomous loop: a green run lands itself on the target branch with the human as pure witness. Acceptance-criteria visibility onto %Item{}, a cross-family adversarial semantic gate, a serialized merge-train (ff/rebase + integrated re-verify + rmap write-back), post-merge auto-repair and conflict re-dispatch with a blocked sink, a read-only witness notification channel, and a blocking dispatch__await MCP tool. Also carries per-run token capture (Task 20, milestone-unpinned) — a routing-efficiency signal that's topically adjacent but not a landing-loop gate.

capability-bench.description: Fixed per-domain benchmark corpus dispatched across all agents; scored, persisted, decayed — the experimental capability dataset

chat-orchestrator.description: Tool-equipped LLM chat surface for harness — descripex-annotated driver surface as the single source of truth for both the in-process Session tool dispatch and the external MCP endpoint; LiveView UI at /harness/chat composes on the same annotations

closeout.description: v0.6 stabilization: align roadmap reality, refresh operator docs, and prove the README + harness-driver skill against Tidewave

config-centralization.description: Centralize harness configuration: one Postgres-backed settings store replacing the per-domain .tmp+rename term files (Cron/Agent/Landing), ConfigInspector reading defaults from their owning modules instead of hardcoded copies, and a declarative Harness.Config schema that makes operator-relevant knobs (run/verification timeouts) runtime-editable from the dashboard. Sequenced after the Phase-15 deletion pass so it never centralizes config keys the reviewer-pair architecture removes.

contract-proof.description: Conformance suite + a second adapter (Codex) — prove the AgentAdapter contract holds for two implementors before resilience builds on it

core-loop.description: Worktree lifecycle, rmap ingestion, verification runner, supervised run lifecycle

dashboard.description: Phoenix LiveView operational surface (project switcher, live multi-project status, per-run drill-down with stream-json transcript) + embedded Oban Web at /harness/oban for queue introspection

dashboard-chrome.description: mpp.dev-inspired dashboard repaint: shared Components module (navbar, footer, page_shell, bucket_badge, transcript_view + extracted message_row/tool_call/json_tree), Tokens overhaul (Geist family, tightened type scale, sticky navbar/footer styles, glyph badges), and run-detail transcript rework from raw stream-json `<pre>` to parsed chat-style turns with per-agent parser dispatch

dashboard-observability.description: The /harness dashboard only surfaces the implementer/reviewer/recovery STAGES of a run — the half of the pipeline driven by the Harness.Run gen_statem feeding RunFeed. The post-merge audit (Harness.Audit.Worker, a real third-family agent run) and every land operation (Harness.Lander: rebase / ff-push / conflict / resolver) are separate Oban workers that never broadcast to the dashboard, so they are invisible to the operator. Make them observable on a dedicated harness:ops feed + panel. Mantra-clean: count which agent/operation did what and relay the audit's own verdict, never recompute meaning. Distinct from dashboard-perf (load latency); this is coverage.

dashboard-perf.description: The /harness dashboard takes 12-15s to load while runs are active (vs 56ms for /harness/kpi), entirely server-side. Two synchronous costs in the LiveView lifecycle that balloon under active-run load: RoadmapSummary.for_projects firing N sequential rmap shell-outs on the mount render path, and StatusView.live_runs/0's per-run Run.status gen_statem fan-out blocking behind busy run processes. Measured 2026-06-08; mantra-clean (pure mechanics — parallelize, defer off the critical path, bound the reads).

deferred.description: Parked work — revisit after the core milestones ship

dispatch-economy.description: Tiny tasks cost a full implement->review->audit ceremony each, so a pile of fragments is token-expensive. Two outputs: MEASURE the per-task ceremony/fragmentation tax from the per-run token facts already captured (raw aggregation, no verdict), and replace roadmap_poller.ex's code-driven next-task/grouping selection with a full-context orchestrator AI gated by a mechanical upside-count (counting decides WHETHER to wake the smart layer; the AI decides the grouping). Mantra-clean: count facts in code, write the batching meaning with an AI.

judgment-collapse.description: The leitmotif made empirical (CLAUDE.md THE MANTRA): count facts in code, write the meaning of facts with an AI. Find and delete the places where harness still COMPUTES meaning — the CapabilityScore composite + routing arithmetic, the in-run stakes regex gate, the reflex grade-gaming blocklist, English-error classification — and route that meaning through an agent reading raw facts (or a structured signal at source). Persist facts; never let a formula pretend to know what they mean.

kpi-routing.description: Recommend-agent-per-domain routing surface (explore/exploit) + Oban cron benchmark scheduler — the behavior-change layer

multi-agent.description: Cursor and Grok adapters, capability + availability registry with quota fail-over

multi-project.description: First-class %Harness.Project{} + check-stack abstraction + Rust preset + GitHub source + Oban-backed dispatch with restart persistence + cron-driven autonomous polling + in-repo subdir recipe

postgres-results.description: Move run/batch result persistence from file-backed term storage into Postgres (already a hard dependency via Oban) behind the existing ResultStore behaviour, then push KPI aggregation and history queries down into SQL — the queryable substrate the capability-bench dataset and KPI ledger read from

production-kpis.description: Per-agent KPIs aggregated from existing run records — success rate, cost-to-green, tokens, repair burden — surfaced at a glance

resilience.description: Batch fan-out, failure-classified retry, autonomous repair loop

reviewer-pair.description: Replace every run-lifecycle judgment call implemented as procedural code (FailureClass regexes, repair loop, BaselineFilter, semantic gate, :no_changes disposition) with a cross-family reviewer agent that fixes inline in the implementer's worktree until the check stack is green or reports stuck in prose. Architecture: docs/reviewer-pair-architecture.md. Harness code shrinks to mechanical substrate; ~1,100 lines of judgment code deleted.

roadmap-durability.description: Make harness's own roadmap mutations safe under the multi-writer reality rmap.md documents. harness's dispatch lifecycle mutates the canonical roadmap/tasks.toml (rmap status transitions) but treats them as uncommitted local writes — no fetch+rebase before write, no commit, no push — so every harness run silently races sibling Claude sessions and cloud agents against the same shared file. Make the transitions git-durable.

run-history.description: Surface persisted run history in the dashboard: the index list and drill-down read only live state, so settled runs vanish from view on restart even though they persist as LogRecords under ~/.harness/results. Merge ResultStore history into the index + replay settled-run transcripts in drill-down. Display-only — no new storage.

scaffold.description: mix project scaffold + standard dep stack

self-heal.description: The self-healing run loop (planning doc: plan-a-refactor-of-happy-summit Workstream A). implement->review->audit today hard-fails on mechanical hiccups an AI or a simple retry could absorb. Two tiers, both mantra-clean: Tier-1 = zero-token bounded mechanical retry on transient substrate ops (git create/commit/fetch, Port spawn) — pure counting, classifies nothing; Tier-2 = ONE bounded, witnessed AI-recovery seam (.harness/recovery.json, repaired|dead) for the interpretive minority, generalizing Task 203's re-prompt and Task 189's resolver. No cond/regex error-classifier in harness (that is the tasks 153-163 bug class). Recovery never routes a genuine reject and never resumes past the reviewer gate.

settings-pq.description: Collapse harness's scattered settings (exs registration defaults + SettingsStore overlay + app-env cache + per-domain enable switches + ~/.harness/*.term files) into ONE Postgres table as single source of truth. Kills the silent-divergence class of bug (onchain landing-policy reverting on restart). repo_enabled:false = ephemeral (surfaced via a flash). Plus the Oban Lifeline rescuer for orphaned executing jobs that today's investigation surfaced.

surface.description: Agent-shaped MCP/CLI surface, human status view, run logging

workflow-substrate.description: Harness workflow as the source-of-truth operating contract all repos adopt, retiring the generic global includes

v0_1.name: Core loop & contract proof
v0_1.description: One rmap task driven end to end (Claude headless, isolated worktree, verified result), plus a second adapter (Codex) proving the AgentAdapter contract holds for two implementors

v0_10.name: Agent KPIs & Capability Routing
v0_10.description: Proves evidence-based per-domain agent routing beats the orchestrator's default self-reliance: capability KPIs — gathered by dispatching a fixed benchmark corpus across every agent and graded by the verification stack, never self-report — change which agent gets dispatched and lower cost-to-green. Tests the hypothesis that the orchestrator falls back to the one familiar agent (or hand-builds) because it flies dark on the others' real capabilities, and that a per-(agent,domain) trust signal placed in the dispatch path corrects that.

v0_11.name: Reviewer-Pair Lifecycle
v0_11.description: Tests the hypothesis that the recurring class of run-lifecycle bugs (failure misclassification, baseline masking, empty-diff wedges, gate rejections — 6 found in one week) is caused by judgment calls implemented as procedural code, and that moving all of them into a cross-family reviewer agent that fixes inline (never classifies) eliminates the class while raising delivery rate without re-dispatch.

v0_12.name: Agent-Gate Workflow & Post-Merge Audit
v0_12.description: Tests the hypothesis that removing the mechanical verification gate entirely — making a cross-family reviewer AI THE gate (it runs the checks itself, fixes inline, writes the verdict) and adding a post-merge audit AI — eliminates the run-lifecycle bug class (every bug from 2026-05-26 to 06-03 traced to harness verification machinery, zero to agent judgment) while raising delivery rate.

v0_13.name: Judgment Collapse — count facts in code, write meaning with an AI
v0_13.description: Tests the hypothesis that harness still COMPUTES meaning it has no business computing — KPI/capability composites, in-run stakes gating, grade-gaming blocklists, English-error classification — and that deleting this judgment-arithmetic (routing the meaning through an agent that reads raw facts instead) shrinks the codebase and removes a false-verdict bug class WITHOUT degrading routing quality. The empirical proof of the leitmotif: count facts in code; write the meaning of facts with an AI.

v0_14.name: Self-Healing Run Loop — mechanical failures heal inline, not surface as stupid errors
v0_14.description: Tests the hypothesis that the great majority of run failures are MECHANICAL (transient/structural — git locks, spawn races, malformed verdict files, checkout pollution, reviewer timeouts) and can self-heal inline so they never reach the operator, via a two-tier design — zero-token bounded mechanical retry for substrate ops + ONE bounded, witnessed AI-recovery seam for the interpretive minority — WITHOUT masking genuine rejections, and at a recovery token cost demonstrably lower than the hard-fail + manual-redispatch path it replaces. Same leitmotif applied to failure handling: count the failure facts (retries, recovery attempts, token spend) in code; let an AI write the meaning (repaired vs genuinely dead) into .harness/recovery.json.

v0_2.name: Batch & resilience
v0_2.description: Proves an unattended multi-task dogfood batch survives partial failure without human babysitting — failure-classified retry filters transient from terminal, the repair loop turns at least some red verdicts green via session resume, and a single red run never craters the batch.

v0_3.name: Multi-agent & quota fail-over
v0_3.description: Proves the AgentAdapter contract holds across N>2 implementors — adding Cursor, Grok, Antigravity, and Pi behind the same behaviour requires no Claude-/Codex-specific leak — and quota fail-over routes a batch around a capped subscription rather than failing it.

v0_4.name: Agent-facing surface
v0_4.description: Proves harness is observable enough that a fresh session can pick up where the dispatching session left off — structured run records survive process exit, mix harness.status shows fleet state without raw JSON parsing, and Harness.AuditReview gives the audit-review skill an objective second-grader dispatch without routing through verification.

v0_5.name: Multi-Project & Dashboard
v0_5.description: Proves harness scales beyond harness-on-harness — N registered projects (Elixir + Rust + ...) dispatched concurrently with restart-resilient Oban queues and a single LiveView dashboard is a workable shape, and the Postgres+Oban+Phoenix substrate doesn't crater the BEAM-native simplicity that made the single-project version work.

v0_6.name: Closeout & Release Readiness
v0_6.description: Proves the built system is coherent for a fresh AI orchestrator: roadmap state reflects reality, README and harness-driver instructions match the live Tidewave/dashboard surface, deferred work stays out of the normal queue, and the release smoke path is verified end to end.

v0_7.name: Chat Orchestrator
v0_7.description: Proves a tool-equipped LLM driven over a descripex-annotated harness surface can orchestrate dispatch end-to-end via natural language — replacing the two-eval mcp__harness__project_eval pattern as the default driver UX — and that the same annotated surface serves external MCP consumers (Sprite, Cursor BG, other Claude instances) without a separate Chat.Tools wrapper layer.

v0_8.name: Dashboard Operator UX
v0_8.description: Proves a unified, designed dashboard chrome (persistent navbar + footer + shared component vocabulary) plus chat-style parsed transcripts on the run-detail page make harness consumable by a human operator — not just an AI driver — without requiring the operator to read raw stream-json or context-switch between visually fragmented per-page headers.

v0_9.name: Autonomous Landing
v0_9.description: Proves harness can drive an rmap task from dispatch to a landed commit on the target branch with zero human gate — a cross-family adversarial grader approves the diff against its acceptance criteria, a serialized merge-train ff/rebase-merges and re-verifies the integrated state, post-merge reds and conflicts auto-repair via fresh re-dispatch, exhaustion routes to a blocked sink, and the human is a pure witness (notified, never asked). Tests the hypothesis that the autonomous loop's ceiling is set by acceptance-criteria visibility + grader adversariality, not by merge cleverness.

task.title: Scaffold the OTP application + standard dep stack
acceptance_criteria: `mix compile` is clean
`mix test` runs the default suite green
Styler is first in the `.formatter.exs` plugins list
The supervision tree starts under `Application`
task.body: Scaffold `harness` as an Elixir OTP application with a supervision tree — it orchestrates long-lived agent runs, so it needs one. Add the standard project dep stack and tooling per the global Elixir setup conventions (Styler, Credo, Dialyxir, Doctor, ex_unit_json, dialyzer_json, descripex, Sobelow, and Reach as a dev/test analysis dep), wired into `mix.exs`, `.formatter.exs`, and `cli/0` preferred_envs. Generate the baseline `.gitignore`, `README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.
task.implemented: Scaffolded OTP application with supervision tree, full standard dep stack (styler first, credo, dialyxir, doctor, sobelow, reach + boxart, ex_dna/ex_ast, descripex, tidewave+bandit), cli/0, dialyzer :apps_direct + priv/plts, all quality gates green (compile, test, format, credo --strict, doctor, sobelow, dialyzer 0 warnings).

task.title: Evaluate orchestration libraries — confirm thin-core
acceptance_criteria: Each candidate skimmed for whether it offers anything the thin OTP core doesn't
A written build-vs-adopt decision with rationale
Any borrowed design ideas are recorded with their source
A determination on whether `claude_code` / `codex_sdk` are CLI wrappers or native reimplementations, with a uniform-Ports-vs-SDK recommendation
out_of_scope: Writing any adapter or orchestration code — this task is evaluation only
Adding any candidate library as a dependency
task.body: Skim the source and docs of the candidate Elixir orchestration libraries — `opal`, `gen_agent` + `gen_agent_ensemble`, `altar_ai`, `ex_mcp`. The harness core is deliberately thin — a Port per run, a `gen_statem` per run, a `DynamicSupervisor` for batches, all stock OTP — and harness no longer needs a normalized event model, so the expected outcome is build-thin-core rather than adopt. Confirm that, and record any design ideas worth borrowing. Also settle the per-agent SDK question: determine whether `claude_code` and `codex_sdk` are CLI wrappers around the headless binary or native reimplementations. If they are wrappers, harness gains nothing from them — its raw-passthrough design discards an SDK's normalized event model, and OTP Ports already spawn the binary with better termination signals — so every adapter uses uniform Ports; only a native reimplementation that removes the external-binary dependency would justify the dep. Record both decisions in a concept doc.
task.implemented: Evaluated opal, gen_agent, gen_agent_ensemble, altar_ai, ex_mcp + the claude_code/codex_sdk SDKs. Outcome: build thin core, adopt none, uniform Ports for all adapters. claude_code and codex_sdk confirmed CLI wrappers (not native reimpls). Decision + borrowed design ideas recorded in docs/orchestration-library-evaluation.md.

task.title: Define the AgentAdapter behaviour — invocation + capture
acceptance_criteria: An `AgentAdapter` behaviour with documented callbacks for invoke / capture / terminate
Raw agent output is passed through untouched — no per-agent event normalization
A capability declaration each adapter fills in
Nothing Claude-specific leaks into the contract
out_of_scope: Building any concrete adapter
Any normalized or typed event model — explicitly cut
task.body: Define the core contract every agent adapter implements — a `behaviour` that, given a task spec plus run options, builds the agent's headless command line, spawns it, detects termination, and hands back the raw captured output plus wall-clock duration. Deliberately no normalized event model: harness does not parse or remap each agent's JSON — the consumer is an AI that reads raw transcripts natively, and harness derives run success from its own verification stack, not the agent's self-reported result. The behaviour also declares per-adapter capabilities (session resume, permission modes, and so on). Contract only — no concrete adapter.
task.implemented: Defined the Harness.AgentAdapter behaviour: 4 callbacks (capabilities/0, build_command/1, classify_message/2, terminate/1) plus generic AgentAdapter.invoke/2 (Port spawn) and supports?/2. Structs: Invocation, Run, Capabilities. Raw passthrough, no event model; :error vs :terminated split for retry classification; session-token extraction and version/0 probe deferred. No concrete adapter. The use-macro from the plan was dropped — Doctor's 100% spec gate does not pair @spec to a defmacro; adapters declare @behaviour directly.

task.title: Build the Claude Code headless adapter
acceptance_criteria: A headless prompt run captures raw output and reports termination
Working directory and permission mode are wired
Session resume works across two runs
Termination is derived from process exit + timeout, not `$?`
An idle timeout kills a run that emits no output for a configurable window, separate from the total-run budget
task.body: Implement the first concrete adapter — driving Claude Code headlessly via `claude -p` over Ports. Capture the raw output stream and hand it back unparsed. Wire working directory, permission mode, and session resume/continue. Detect termination from the process/Port closing plus two timeout guards — a total-run budget, and an idle timeout that kills a run emitting no output for a configurable window — never from the exit code, which is known to be unreliable.
task.implemented: Built Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude (claude -p, stream-json, --permission-mode bypassPermissions, --continue resume), the generic Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver enforcing total + idle timeout guards, the Outcome result struct, and the shared OSProcess port-lifecycle helper. Resume resolves the behaviour's session-token deferral via --continue (no new callback). 100% test + doc coverage; integration test green against real claude.

task.title: Worktree-per-job lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: Each run gets its own isolated git worktree
Concurrent runs do not collide on the working tree
Worktrees are cleaned up on success and retained on failure (configurable)
A crashed run does not leak an orphan worktree
task.body: harness runs every job in an isolated git worktree so concurrent agent runs never collide and the verification stack has a clean checkout to grade. Implement worktree creation per run, dispatch of the agent into it, and a keep-or-tear-down decision on completion (retain on failure for inspection; configurable). This is the automation of the repo's existing worktree-per-branch convention.
task.implemented: Harness.Worktree (create/2, finish/3, remove/1, retained?/1, base_dir/1) for per-run isolated git worktrees + Harness.Worktree.Sweeper boot-time orphan reaper. Harness.Git subprocess wrapper. Configurable via :harness, :worktree app env + HARNESS_WORKTREE_ROOT. 48 tests, coverage 100/93.6/85.2%.

task.title: rmap task ingestion
acceptance_criteria: harness fetches a task — by id, or the next pending one — from the rmap roadmap
The task renders to an agent-ready prompt suitable for the adapter
Ingestion reads the rmap source — it does not duplicate the roadmap
task.body: Let harness pull a task straight from the rmap roadmap — read `roadmap/tasks.toml` / `roadmap/data.json` (or shell out to `rmap`) and render the task as a ready-to-run agent prompt. `rmap delegate <id> --to <agent>` already emits a paste-ready prompt; harness consumes that instead of a human copy-pasting it. This is the input half of the loop — the roadmap becomes the job queue.
task.implemented: Added Harness.Roadmap.ingest/2 + Harness.Roadmap.Item. Shells out to rmap (show/next/delegate) with explicit --tasks-path; fetches a task by id or next-pending and renders the rmap delegate prompt verbatim. Error taxonomy: invalid_agent/invalid_selector/rmap_not_found/no_pending_task/task_not_found/roadmap_not_found/rmap_failed/rmap_bad_output. Covered by a unit suite with fixture roadmaps under test/fixtures/.

task.title: Verification runner — run the target project's check stack
acceptance_criteria: A configurable list of check commands runs against a given worktree
An Elixir preset is provided as the default check set
Each check's pass/fail and output are captured into a structured verdict
Any red check makes the overall verdict red
out_of_scope: Feeding failures back to the agent — that is the autonomous repair loop task
task.body: After an agent finishes, harness runs the target project's own check stack against its worktree and produces a structured pass/fail — this is what makes "did the job succeed?" objective and agent-agnostic, instead of trusting the agent's self-report. The check set is a configurable list of commands; ship an Elixir preset (`mix test.json`, `mix dialyzer.json`, doctor, sobelow, credo). Aggregate each check's result into one verdict the run lifecycle can gate on.
task.implemented: Harness.Verification grades a worktree by running a configurable check stack and aggregating per-check Results into a Verdict (any red => red). Ships elixir_preset/0: mix test.json, dialyzer.json, credo --strict, doctor, sobelow --exit. Each check is spawned over an OTP port bounded by an absolute per-check deadline (default 600_000 ms) so a hung check — idle or still streaming output — is killed rather than wedging the run; System.cmd was rejected as uninterruptible and subprocess-orphaning. Each Result carries a kind (:exited | :timed_out | :not_launched) so a consumer can distinguish a retryable timeout from a genuine red check. Check/Result/Verdict structs + config under :harness, :verification. 19 tests, 94% coverage.

task.title: Supervised run lifecycle process
acceptance_criteria: One job = one supervised `gen_statem` with observable state
It drives worktree → adapter → verification and settles on a verdict
A crashing run is isolated from siblings
Per-run timeout and external cancellation both work
task.body: Implement the supervised process that owns one job end to end — model it as a `gen_statem` moving through `dispatched → running → verifying → {done | failed}`. It creates the worktree, spawns the adapter, waits for termination, runs the verification stack, and settles on a verdict. Crash isolation (a failed run never touches siblings), a per-run timeout, and external cancellation. The run state must be observable. Completing this task is the single-agent core loop working end to end for one task; the contract-proof bundle (conformance suite + Codex adapter) then proves the adapter contract holds on a second agent.
task.implemented: Harness.Run :gen_statem owns one job end to end (dispatched → running → verifying → done/failed): carves the isolated worktree, dispatches the agent via AgentAdapter.Driver, runs the verification stack, settles a verdict. Harness.Run.Supervisor (one_for_one DynamicSupervisor, :temporary children) gives crash isolation between concurrent runs; a Registry maps run-id → pid; a Task.Supervisor parents every per-step async task so a crashing step is an event, not a crash. cancel/1 and a per-run lifetime-budget timeout both abort cleanly and SIGKILL the agent; status/1 exposes live state. AgentAdapter.Driver gained an :on_spawn hook so the lifecycle process can capture the run handle for cancellation. Verification is the sole grader — a timed-out agent is still verified. 23 new tests; suite green; dialyzer/credo/doctor clean.

task.title: Batch orchestrator with concurrency cap
acceptance_criteria: A batch of N tasks runs under a concurrency cap of M
Partial failure is tolerated — the batch completes and reports per-task status
Per-task verdicts are collected into one batch result
task.body: Implement the batch layer — fan a set of tasks out across run-lifecycle processes under a `DynamicSupervisor`, with a configurable concurrency cap, and collect the per-task verdicts. Tolerate partial failure: one failed or red run must not abort the batch; the batch result reports every task's outcome. A batch is typically an rmap bundle or an `rmap next-bundle` result.
task.implemented: Harness.Batch.run/4 + Harness.Batch.Result — fans tasks out across supervised Harness.Run children under a concurrency cap, tolerates partial failure (red/crashed run never aborts the batch), collects one Run.Result per task in input order. Delivered via parallel multi-agent dogfood, driven by Codex; commit on harness/run-1779373868703-29f9a9b0.

task.title: Retry policy with failure classification
acceptance_criteria: Failures are classified as transient, quota-exhausted, or terminal
Transient failures retry with capped exponential backoff
Quota exhaustion stops retrying that agent at once — no backoff loop against a multi-hour wall
Terminal failures are not retried
The policy is configurable per batch or per run
task.body: Add a per-run retry policy that first classifies the failure. Transient failures (a process crash, a flaky check) retry with capped exponential backoff. Quota exhaustion — a subscription agent hitting its cap — is NOT retryable on a useful timescale (the reset window is hours); it must stop retrying that agent immediately, marked for fail-over rather than backoff. Genuine terminal task failures are never retried. Make the policy injectable per batch or per run.
task.implemented: Harness.Run.RetryPolicy + Harness.Run.FailureClass — classifies a failed run transient/quota_exhausted/terminal; transient retries with capped exponential backoff, quota stops at once for fail-over, terminal never retried; policy injectable per run/batch via :harness, :retry_policy. Delivered via parallel multi-agent dogfood, driven by Cursor; commit on harness/run-1779373868714-f42cdd07.

task.title: Autonomous repair loop
acceptance_criteria: A red verdict triggers a repair attempt — failures fed back via session resume
The loop stops on green or at the attempt cap
A quota or terminal failure ends the loop instead of burning attempts
The number of repair attempts is configurable
task.body: Close the verify loop. When verification comes back red, feed the failing checks' output back to the same agent via session resume and re-run, up to a configurable attempt cap. The objective check stack is the grader, so an agent iterating against it is not self-grading. Stop on green, on the attempt cap, or on a non-repairable failure class (e.g. quota exhaustion — hand to fail-over instead).
task.implemented: Harness.Run repair loop + Harness.Run.RepairPrompt — a red verdict resumes the same agent with the failing checks fed back, re-commits and re-grades up to :max_repair_attempts (default 2); stops on green, the cap, or a non-repairable failure. Delivered via parallel multi-agent dogfood, driven by Claude; commit on harness/run-1779373868724-a4ceeede.

task.title: Reusable adapter conformance test suite
acceptance_criteria: A shared conformance module parameterized by adapter
The Claude adapter passes the full suite
Invocation, capture, termination, timeout, and adapter-level cancellation (`terminate` kills an in-flight run) are all covered
task.body: Build a reusable test module every `AgentAdapter` implementation must pass — exercising invocation, raw-output capture, termination detection, timeout, and adapter-level cancellation (the behaviour's `terminate` callback killing an in-flight run and releasing its Port/process). This is adapter-scope only: external cancellation *orchestration* — a caller telling the running system to cancel a job — is the supervised lifecycle's concern (Task 8) and is out of scope here. Run the Claude adapter against the suite. This suite is the gate Codex and every later adapter (Cursor, Grok, ACP) are held to: a leak gets fixed in the behaviour, not patched around in the adapter.
task.implemented: Built Harness.AgentAdapter.ConformanceCase — a reusable, adapter-parameterized conformance suite (use ConformanceCase, adapter: M) covering invocation, verbatim raw-output capture, termination detection, timeout (terminate/1 as the driver's timeout-branch handler), and adapter-level cancellation. Contract checks are agent-free (synthesized port messages + /bin/sleep stand-in); one :integration test drives the real agent through Driver.run/3. Run against the Claude adapter (ClaudeConformanceTest) and Harness.FakeAdapter (FakeAdapterConformanceTest, proving reusability). Made FakeAdapter contract-faithful (build_command/1 now rejects undeclared permission modes). Trimmed ClaudeTest to Claude-specific assertions. Delivered by harness's first fully-green dogfood run (run-1779367169148-29cf0bea).
