task.title: Audit-surfaced: BaselineFilter.Credo content-blind matching causes false-pass / false-red
acceptance_criteria: Baseline carries `{file, content}` (or equivalent content-based key), not `{file, line_no}` only
Regression test: agent rewrites an existing TODO line — verification correctly reds (no false-pass)
Regression test: agent inserts/deletes a line above an inherited TODO — verification still filters it (no false-red)
Existing happy-path test (inherited TODO unchanged + no new debt → pass) still passes
Normalization handles whitespace differences between git-grep output and credo's line-content capture
out_of_scope: Switching from credo-based filtering to a different lint backend
Filtering non-TagTODO credo checks
task.body:
Codex audit of commit `d4344e7` (Task 43 WIP) and `5291698` (Task 43 dogfood) flagged two correctness gaps in `lib/harness/verification/baseline_filter/credo.ex`:

1. **Same-line rewrite false-pass.** The baseline is keyed on `{file, line_no}` (`baseline_tagtodo?/3`, `parse_grep_line/1` discards the trigger text as `_content`). If a dispatched agent rewrites an existing TODO on the same line — keeping the line number but changing the trigger — the new TODO is silently filtered as inherited debt. Verification then false-greens an agent that introduced fresh debt.

2. **Line-shift false-red.** Conversely, if the agent inserts or deletes a line above an inherited TODO, the line_no shifts. The baseline doesn't move with diff context, so the un-mutated inherited TODO is flagged as a new finding. Verification then false-reds an agent that didn't touch the TODO at all.

Both gaps reduce the baseline filter's reliability — the whole point of Task 43 was diff-aware credo.

Fix shape: include line content in baseline pairs and match credo issues by `{file, normalized_content}` rather than `{file, line_no}` — the trigger text IS already extracted by `parse_grep_line/1` (currently discarded as `_content`). Modest structural change; tests cover both false-pass and false-red scenarios.
task.implemented: Shipped in commit 334ccc5 (audit-review pass on 6a01b58..73f3778). Baseline now keys on {file, normalized_content} not {file, line_no} — kills same-line-rewrite false-pass and line-shift false-red. Regression tests added. Verified in-session via file read of lib/harness/verification/baseline_filter/credo.ex.

task.title: Audit-surfaced: cover cancel-before-handle path in Run lifetime force-settle
acceptance_criteria: New test in `test/harness/run_test.exs` (describe block `cancellation` or similar): start with `HangingAdapter` (no agent handle ever arrives) + low `lifetime_timeout`; issue `Run.cancel/1` from a Task while in :running with agent_run=nil; assert the cancel Task receives `:ok` AND the result settles `:timed_out` reason
Test is deterministic — no race-dependent timing; uses explicit synchronization (e.g. wait until cancel_requested is observable via status snapshot) before letting the lifetime timer fire
If Codex's claim reproduces: code fix lands in same commit and the test fails against the pre-fix code
out_of_scope: Refactoring the cancel/lifetime state machine beyond this regression path
task.body:
Codex audit of commit `f4d8cb6` (Task 29 delivery) ran a target-SHA probe and reported: state had `cancel_requested: {:cancelled, from}`, the run settled `:timed_out` via `force_settle_lifetime/1`, but `Task.yield(cancel_task, 500)` returned `nil` — i.e. the deferred cancel caller never received `:ok`.

Static read of the current code (`lib/harness/run.ex:506-512`) shows `force_settle_lifetime/1` calls `pending_cancel_reply(data)` before clearing `cancel_requested`, and `pending_cancel_reply/1` returns `[{:reply, from, :ok}]` for `{_reason, from}` with `is_tuple(from)`. The reply path appears correct on inspection.

The gap is that the existing test (`test "the lifetime budget force-settles even when the agent run handle never arrives"`) exercises force-settle alone — not the *cancel-before-handle + force-settle* composition Codex probed. If a regression slips in (someone reshapes `pending_cancel_reply/1`, the timer firing order, or the data-update ordering), there is no test to catch it.

This task adds the deterministic regression test for the composed scenario. If the test reveals the bug Codex observed, fix it (route the deferred reply through `pending_cancel_reply/1` from every path that can settle while `cancel_requested` is set). If the test passes against current code, the gap was always test coverage, not behavior — close the task with the test in place.
task.implemented: Shipped in commit 334ccc5 (audit-review pass on 6a01b58..73f3778). Composed cancel-before-handle regression test pinned in test/harness/run_test.exs; Codex's deferred-reply force-settle claim did not reproduce — the gap was test coverage, not behavior. force_settle_lifetime/1 at lib/harness/run.ex:505 routes through pending_cancel_reply/1 correctly.

task.title: Audit-surfaced: route Batch dispatch_spin_exhausted through :no_available_agent settlement
acceptance_criteria: `run_once_dispatch/5` spin-exhaustion fallback settles with `{:no_available_agent, :spin_exhausted}` (or equivalent shape under that family), not `{:run_crashed, :dispatch_spin_exhausted}`
Regression test: an adapter that always returns `{:error, {:no_available_agent, _}}` from `select/2` produces a `RunResult` with the new reason after spin exhaustion
Existing Batch tests still pass; event-log shape stays consistent with the parent `fill_slots` undispatchable settlement
out_of_scope: Restoring the `:start_run_failed` event observability regression (separate concern; file as follow-up if it lingers)
Reducing the 100-spin upper bound (tuning is independent)
task.body:
Codex audit of commit `63b711d` (Task 28) flagged that `Harness.Batch.run_once_dispatch/5` busy-spins up to 100 times when `AgentRegistry.select/2` returns `{:no_available_agent, _}`, then crashes the worker with `{:run_crashed, :dispatch_spin_exhausted}` at `lib/harness/batch.ex:291-298`.

The parent path (`fill_slots/6` at line 217) already settles `{:no_available_agent, reason}` cleanly via `settle_undispatchable/4` — emitting the documented `:undispatchable` event with reason `{:no_available_agent, reason}`. The worker-spin-exhausted path bypasses that: it returns a `{:run_crashed, ...}` reason that's semantically wrong (no crash happened — the agent pool was just exhausted under contention), and it loses the consistent event-log shape.

Fix shape: change line 296 from `reason: {:run_crashed, :dispatch_spin_exhausted}` to `reason: {:no_available_agent, :spin_exhausted}` (or thread back through `settle_undispatchable/4` if the event log can be reached from the worker context). Add a deterministic test that exercises the spin-exhaustion path — `MockAdapter` declaring no available agents for `spin_count_limit + N` selects in a row, then asserting the resulting RunResult carries the `:no_available_agent` reason.

Codex also flagged that `:start_run_failed` events are no longer emitted on the batch event log when `RunSupervisor.start_run/4` errors (line 281-287). That's an observability regression rather than a result-loss bug — out of scope here unless the spin-exhaustion fix opens it up naturally.
task.implemented: Shipped in commit 334ccc5 (audit-review pass on 6a01b58..73f3778). lib/harness/batch.ex now settles {:no_available_agent, :spin_exhausted} (line 312) instead of {:run_crashed, :dispatch_spin_exhausted}; spin limit promoted to @spin_count_limit (line 273); run_once_dispatch/5 exposed @doc false for the regression test. :start_run_failed event observability is explicitly out of scope here (see Task 57.out_of_scope).

task.title: Cross-agent grader as a repair-loop move (gated, asymmetric, budgeted)
acceptance_criteria: Triggered ONLY when a check fails twice with the same error signature within one run — never on perceived ambiguity, never on any red verdict
Each consultation consumes one slot from :max_repair_attempts (same budget as same-agent repair; no separate budget)
Asker emits a structured payload: proposed approach + cost-of-guessing-wrong sentence + the failing check evidence (mirrors the response-conventions.md `Derive Before You Ask` gate)
Consultee is the opposite-agent grader via the same :claude ↔ :codex auto-pair as Harness.AuditReview — asymmetric grader, not dialogic
Consultee returns approve/reject + one-line rationale on the proposed approach (verdict shape, not free-form back-and-forth) — parse via the existing <<<VERDICT:APPROVE|REJECT>>> sentinel
No back-and-forth: one consultation = one grading round + one follow-up implementation pass by the asker; if that pass still goes red, the loop settles :failed
Opt-in via config :harness, :cross_agent_repair, enabled: false by default
Test: a run where the same check fails twice with the same signature dispatches the opposite-agent grader exactly once, charged against :max_repair_attempts
Test: with cross_agent_repair disabled, the repair loop behaves identically to today (no consultation move)
out_of_scope: Multi-round dialogue between agents — one grading round only
Asker-initiated consultations on perceived ambiguity — only same-error-twice trigger
A separate cost budget — consultations charge against :max_repair_attempts
Dynamic consultee selection — fixed :claude ↔ :codex pair like AuditReview
Mid-run human consultation — agents only, no human-in-the-loop interjection
task.body:
Extend Harness.Run's repair loop with one additional move: when a verification check fails twice in a row with the same error signature within a single run, dispatch the opposite-agent grader (the same :claude ↔ :codex pair Harness.AuditReview uses) for a one-shot grade of the asker's proposed approach before the asker's next attempt.

The motivating failure mode: the same-agent repair loop (Task 11) dead-ends when an agent's blind spot causes it to make the same wrong move twice. A bounded second-agent grader catches that class before the run settles :failed, without opening the floodgates to free-rider consultation.

Two design constraints make this safe — they are the whole point of the task:

1. **The trigger is evidence, not ambiguity.** Same-error-twice within one run, machine-detectable from the verification stack's per-check Result kind + error signature. No asker-initiated "I'm unsure, let me ask" path — that's exactly the failure mode response-conventions.md § "Derive Before You Ask" exists to prevent (questions become cheaper than reasoning). If the agent never sees the same error twice, no consultation happens.

2. **The shape is asymmetric grading, not dialogue.** Asker emits a structured payload — proposed approach, cost-of-guessing-wrong sentence, failing check evidence. Consultee returns approve/reject + one-line rationale via the existing <<<VERDICT:APPROVE|REJECT>>> sentinel (parse with Harness.AuditReview's existing extractor). One round. Asker then commits to their approach (approved) or pivots (rejected). No back-and-forth — that's the ping-pong failure mode.

Cost is borne by the same :max_repair_attempts budget. A consultation move counts as one repair attempt. This prevents the consultation surface from being a free interjection and keeps the run's wall-clock bounded.

Opt-in via config (`:cross_agent_repair, enabled: false` by default) so the baseline behavior of Task 11 is preserved and the new move only kicks in for users who explicitly opt into the autonomy lift.

The implementation reuses Harness.AuditReview.grade_fix/1 (Task 58) for dispatch and verdict parsing — that wrapper already handles the :claude ↔ :codex auto-pair, the Driver.run/3 dispatch path, and the sentinel extraction. The work is in Harness.Run: same-error-signature detection across attempts within a run, the structured-payload builder for the grader prompt, and the gen_statem state transition that consumes the verdict before the next implementation attempt.
task.implemented: Adds an opt-in cross-agent grader move to the repair loop. Gated by `config :harness, :cross_agent_repair, enabled: false`. New `:consulting` gen_statem state in Harness.Run; same-error-signature detection across repair attempts within one run; on the second observation of the same failure signature, harness spends one repair budget slot dispatching the opposite agent as a grader via Harness.AuditReview shape. Asymmetric (no dialogue) and budgeted (charges :max_repair_attempts). Test file: test/harness/run/cross_agent_repair_test.exs. 3-way merge against Task 60 resolved by relocating :pollution_allowlist doc into the moved :run config block.

Per-project guarded_paths wiring through %Harness.Project{} — that lands once Task 46 is in
task.body:
The `Harness.Worktree.Isolation` snapshot/diff check (Task 32, for the Antigravity worktree-isolation bug) compares the full `git status --porcelain` byte-for-byte between run start and finalize. Anything that mutates the porcelain mid-run — even orchestration overhead unrelated to the dispatched agent — settles the run `:checkout_polluted` and aborts pre-commit.

Surfaced during Task 44 dogfood (run `run-1779750588594-7270b0dc`): the dispatching Claude Code session created `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` via its own ScheduleWakeup tool while the dogfood agent ran. The dispatched agent did its work cleanly in its run worktree — verification stack green (407/407 tests, credo strict, doctor 100%, dialyzer 0, sobelow clean) — but the run settled `:failed` because the porcelain at finalize contained `?? .claude/` and the snapshot didn't. Diff had to be hand-integrated.

The check should be tolerant of pollution that demonstrably isn't the dispatched agent's doing. Concretely: an allowlist of paths/patterns that the isolation diff ignores (claude session state, common editor lockfiles, `.DS_Store`, etc.), configurable per-project. The strict comparison stays as the default backstop — the allowlist just keeps benign noise from cratering a green run.

Alternative shape (cheaper): rather than a path allowlist, scope the diff to `lib/`, `test/`, `mix.exs`, `mix.lock`, `config/`, `priv/`, `roadmap/`, `docs/` — the surfaces an agent CAN legitimately pollute. Anything outside is by definition not a worktree-isolation violation. The list itself can come from a `%Harness.Project{}.guarded_paths` declaration once Task 46 lands.
task.implemented: Adds a four-tier pollution allowlist for Harness.Worktree.Isolation. `default_pollution_allowlist/0` covers .claude/, .DS_Store, editor lock/temp globs. Precedence (highest first): run opts `:pollution_allowlist` → `%Harness.Project{}.pollution_allowlist` → app config `config :harness, :run, pollution_allowlist: [...]` → defaults. Wired through `Harness.Run.Supervisor.start_run/4` and `Harness.Run` gen_statem. New `pollution_allowlist` field on %Harness.Project{}. Glob matching against `git status --porcelain` paths. 10 isolation tests pass.

task.title: Codex run worktree disappeared mid-run + cross-wrote into a sibling worktree (Wave 1)
acceptance_criteria: Root-cause identified — agent-side cwd resolution vs. harness-side sweeper race
Run worktree directory cannot be removed while the run's adapter Port is still active
If the worktree does disappear, Run.commit_worktree/2 settles with a distinct reason instead of crashing
Repro test exercises a sibling-run write into another run's worktree and detects/rejects it
out_of_scope: Replacing the worktree-per-run lifecycle
task.body:
Wave 1 of Phase 7 dispatched Task 45 (Codex) and Task 46 (Cursor) in parallel from the same `development` HEAD (783cd50). Codex's run settled `:commit_failed` with `{:enoent}` on its worktree's `.harness-retained` marker followed by `ArgumentError: worktree cwd is not a directory` from `Harness.AgentRules.worktree_root!/1` — Codex's run worktree (`run-1779751918402-46fbe061`) was gone before `Harness.Run.commit_worktree/2` ran. Independently of that, Codex's Rust preset files (`lib/harness/check_stack/preset/rust.ex`, `test/harness/check_stack/preset/rust_test.exs`, `test/support/fixtures/rust_project*`) ended up inside Cursor's worktree directory (`run-1779751920208-d0604434`) and were swept into Cursor's `git add` and committed as part of f3222c3 ("agent delivery — task 46").

Two failures together suggest either (a) `agy`/Codex-style worktree-cwd ignore (mirrors Task 32 / Task 41) where Codex resolved its cwd to Cursor's worktree once its own went :enoent, or (b) a harness-side cleanup race that pulled Codex's worktree out from under the still-running adapter.

Investigation directions:
- Is there a harness boot/periodic sweeper that removed Codex's worktree while still running? (The Task 44 log shows a boot sweep at startup that "pruned: 1" — what triggered it.)
- Did Codex's Port-spawned `codex exec` survive past its worktree deletion and then resolve some operations to a sibling cwd via Port `cwd:` defaulting? (Compare to Task 41's `:worktree_isolation` field.)
- Add a guard inside `Run.commit_worktree/2` that fails fast and loud with a distinct reason when the worktree directory has gone :enoent, rather than crashing inside `AgentRules.worktree_root!/1`.

Wave 1 closeout integrated f3222c3 (carrying both agents' work) into `development` as 2bce2a2 + `f5bc4a1` spec fix-up; both Tasks 45 and 46 settled `done` against the same `shipped_in`. This task tracks the underlying isolation/race so it doesn't recur in Waves 2/3.
task.implemented: Codex delivered 190 LOC: lib/harness/worktree.ex (+110, active-worktree guard + missing-path failure handling) + lib/harness/worktree/sweeper.ex (+9) + lib/harness/run.ex (+12) + lib/harness/run/result.ex (+3, new :worktree_missing reason) + test/harness/run_test.exs (+32) + test/harness/worktree/sweeper_test.exs (+13) + test/support/fake_adapter.ex (+23). Resolves Wave 1 worktree race: cleanup pinned by .harness-retained marker; Run.commit_worktree settles {:commit_failed, {:worktree_missing, path}} instead of crashing; regression test rejects sibling-worktree cross-writes. Cherry-picked as 30a0208. Verification: tests pass in isolation; full suite has 2 load-flakiness failures unrelated to this diff.

task.title: Stale @spec on Harness.Batch.loop_context/8 hid 17 cascade dialyzer warnings (Wave 1)
acceptance_criteria: Rule-injection channel surfaces 'dialyzer warning count > baseline of any type ⇒ self-grade red' to every adapter
Or harness preset annotates invalid_contract findings as likely root-cause of cascade unused_fun warnings
out_of_scope: Replacing dialyxir as the type-check driver
task.body:
Wave 1's Task 46 (Cursor, %Harness.Project{} refactor) changed the 2nd arg of `Harness.Batch.loop_context/8` from a `String.t()` (legacy `repo_path`) to a `%Project{}` but left the `@spec` unchanged. Dialyzer flagged a single `invalid_contract`, but the broken contract poisoned the call-graph: dialyzer abandoned every helper reachable through `loop_context/8` and produced 17 cascade `unused_fun` warnings against `loop/5`, `fill_slots/6`, `start_worker/5`, `settle_worker_done/7`, `settle_worker_down/7`, `settle_undispatchable/4`, `fail_over/7`, `maybe_requeue_after_failover/8`, `adapter_from_result/1`, `find_by_worker_pid/2`, `crashed_result/3`, `persist_crashed_result/3`, `persist_batch/2`, `log_store_error/3`, `run_duration_ms/1`, `ordered_results/2`, plus `run_once/4` — all real, all called. The one-line spec fix in f5bc4a1 (`String.t()` → `Project.t()`) returned dialyzer to 0.

Cursor's own self-test claimed "pre-existing batch.ex unused_fun warnings only; no new project-related issues" — but the Task 44 closeout baseline (783cd50) was 0 dialyzer warnings, so the framing was wrong. This is a class of issue: **a refactor that introduces or moves a struct through a private contract surface needs `mix dialyzer` re-run cleanly, not a glanced-over "unused_fun only".** The dogfood loop's grader (the verification stack) caught it; the agent's self-report glossed it.

Mitigation hooks worth considering:
- Make the AGENTS-side rule injection (Task 39 channel) explicitly call out: a non-zero dialyzer warning count, **of any kind**, is a self-grade red — never paper over `unused_fun` cascades.
- Or extend the harness verification preset to surface "invalid_contract → likely-cascade" diagnostics so the next dogfood batch's red verdict is easier to triage from the result-store entry.

task.title: Dashboard transcript backfill — late subscribers see prior chunks
acceptance_criteria: Opening /harness/runs/:run_id mid-run shows existing transcript immediately, no Waiting for output stall
Live chunks continue to append in order after backfill
Hard-refresh of the run detail page re-populates from the buffer with no duplicates
Settled runs show final buffer until terminal_linger expires (same lifecycle as Run.status/1)
Harness.Run.transcript/1 returns {:ok, %{buffer, seq}} or {:error, :not_found}
Transcript.broadcast carries seq; LiveView drops broadcasts where seq <= last_seq
out_of_scope: Persisting transcript across BEAM restarts
Buffer sizes beyond the existing 200 KiB cap
Cross-project transcript correlation in Oban Web
task.body:
The per-run transcript pane at /harness/runs/:run_id is fed by fire-and-forget
PubSub broadcasts. If the operator opens the page mid-run, every chunk emitted
before subscribe is lost — the pane shows "Waiting for output…" until the next
chunk lands, which can be minutes for a quiet Claude session.

Fix: buffer recent transcript output (200 KiB) in the Run gen_statem alongside
status, expose via Harness.Run.transcript/1, and have the LiveView fetch on
mount after subscribing. Use monotonic sequence numbers tagged on each chunk
so the LiveView can dedup broadcasts that overlap the snapshot.

Design pre-approved in plan /Users/efries/.claude/plans/quizzical-mapping-sparrow.md.
task.implemented: Dashboard transcript pane backfills on mount via new Harness.Run.transcript/1 snapshot (buffer + monotonic seq); LiveView subscribes-then-fetches and drops PubSub broadcasts with seq <= last_seq to dedup the race window. Driver on_output now sends to the gen_statem (which owns the bounded 200 KiB buffer + seq counter), and re-broadcasts as {:harness_transcript, run_id, seq, chunk}. Shared Transcript.append/3 trim helper replaces the duplicated live.ex copy. Tests: append/3 cap + iodata, broadcast/3 seq tuple, Run.transcript/1 snapshot + race-safety dedup + 200 KiB trim. mix compile / credo / dialyzer / mix test.json all green (one pre-existing flake unrelated).

task.title: FailureClass quota classification false-positive on full agent transcript
acceptance_criteria: FailureClass.collect_text/1 limits Outcome.output contribution to the trailing 4 KiB (or similar bounded constant)
Existing FailureClass tests still pass — terminal API quota errors (`billing_error`, `usage limit`, `quota exceeded`) are still detected when they appear in the tail
New regression test: a 100 KiB transcript that contains `quota` in the middle but a benign tail does NOT classify as :quota_exhausted
New regression test: a transcript with `Credit balance is too low` in the tail DOES classify as :quota_exhausted (Claude billing-error precedent from earlier in this batch)
out_of_scope: Refactoring quota detection to use a structured error channel — the byte-tail limit is the minimum correctness fix
Touching the AgentRegistry's separate @quota_patterns list (already correctly scoped to Outcome.output only)
Adapter-specific quota detection (Claude billing_error, OpenAI rate_limit_exceeded) — same regex set covers them; the bug is matching scope, not the patterns
task.body:
`Harness.Run.FailureClass.collect_text/1` returns the full agent stream-json
transcript (`Outcome.output`, often >1 MB), which is then regex-matched against
`RetryPolicy.default_quota_patterns` to detect quota exhaustion. Agents
routinely read source code and docs that contain the trigger words — e.g. a
Task 33 dogfood run hit 341 `/quota/i` matches, all benign (the agent reading
Task 40's freshly-merged moduledoc that literally writes "subscription quota
exhausted"). Result: a transient flaky-test verification failure was
misclassified as `:quota_exhausted`, the repair loop short-circuited
(`repairable?/1` returns false on quota classification), and a recoverable run
settled `:failed` with `repair_attempts: 0`.

Tighten the classifier: quota signals appear in the tail of an agent
transcript (final error envelope / last assistant message), never in the
middle. Limit `outcome_text/1` to the trailing N bytes (e.g. last 4 KiB) so
the regex only sees the agent's terminal output, not its mid-run source reads.

Real-world consequence: as soon as harness reads its own source containing
quota-related strings (which it does constantly post-Task-40), every red
verdict on a long-running agent gets misclassified, the repair loop never
fires, and harness loses its load-bearing recovery mechanism.
task.implemented: Clipped Outcome.output and per-CheckResult.output to trailing 4 KiB (new @text_tail_bytes constant + private tail/1 helper) before quota-pattern regex matching in Harness.Run.FailureClass. Quota signals only appear in an agent's terminal envelope (final result message + API error JSON), never mid-run, so the byte-tail limit preserves real detection (billing_error, rate limit, 429, etc.) while eliminating the false positives from agents displaying source/docs that contain those words. Two regression tests added to RetryPolicyTest.

task.title: Salvage red-but-real runs — discoverable + executable integration of harness/<run-id> branches
acceptance_criteria: Result struct exposes a stable `salvage_branch` and a `Result.salvageable?/1` predicate
Harness.salvage/2 (or /3) integrates a salvageable run's branch onto a target ref and returns a structured outcome — this is the primary surface for AI orchestrators (Tidewave/IEx)
Re-verification on the integrated head is at least optional (re_verify: true | false), defaulting to the safer choice
Cherry-pick conflict is reported as a structured outcome, not a crash
ResultStore.list_run_records exposes salvageable filtering (or a Result.salvageable?/1 caller is documented) so an orchestrator can batch-triage red-but-real runs
out_of_scope: Auto-salvage on every red run — manual gate stays the rule (matches Evaluator Separation)
Salvaging uncommitted worktree state — Task 30 already commits before teardown; preserving uncommitted state would require a separate stash protocol
Replaying the dispatched task — salvage is integration of the agent's existing diff, not a redo
Dashboard banner / button — secondary, human-operator-facing only; AI orchestrators use the Elixir API directly. File a separate small task if/when a human-driving-the-dashboard workflow matters
task.body:
When a run settles :failed but the agent's diff is real (`agent_diff_size > 0`),
harness already preserves the work: Task 30 commits the agent's changes to
`harness/<run-id>` before worktree teardown, so the branch survives even after
the worktree directory is cleaned up. What's missing is discoverability and an
executable integration path — today an operator (or AI orchestrator) has to
manually scan git branches, run a cherry-pick, and re-verify by hand.

Task 33's Cursor run is the precedent: a 461-LOC diff with self-graded 504/504
tests, settled :failed on a load-induced verification flake compounded by the
Task 64 quota false-positive. Without explicit salvage support, the diff is
lost-by-default friction.

## Layer 1 — discoverable
- Add a `salvage_branch` field (e.g. `"harness/run-1779853579933-6fa47408"`) on
  `Harness.Run.Result`; populate from `worktree.branch` at terminal-state entry.
- Add a `Result.salvageable?/1` predicate — true when `state == :failed and
  agent_diff_size > 0`.
- Dashboard run-detail page surfaces a "Salvage available" banner with the
  branch name and a copy-pasteable cherry-pick snippet.

## Layer 2 — executable
- `Harness.salvage(run_id, target_ref \\ "development", opts \\ [])` —
  verifies the branch exists, performs the cherry-pick/merge onto target_ref,
  optionally re-runs the verification stack against the integrated head, and
  returns a structured outcome (clean / conflict / verification result).
- Optional: dashboard "Salvage" action button next to the banner.
- Optional: `mix harness.status --salvageable` lists every red-but-real run
  with its branch + diff size + verdict for batch triage.

Either layer can ship independently; bundle if one session is enough.

task.title: Skip pollution detection for adapters declaring worktree_isolation: true
acceptance_criteria: A run dispatched on an adapter with `worktree_isolation: true` does not invoke the snapshot/diff check and cannot settle `:checkout_polluted` from operator activity in the main checkout
A run dispatched on an adapter with `worktree_isolation: false` is still blocked at dispatch by the existing `check_dispatch/1` gate (Antigravity case)

Test: a run on a verified-isolation adapter where the main checkout is mutated mid-run (simulated parallel `rmap`/`git commit` activity) settles by the normal verification verdict, never `:checkout_polluted`
Documentation in `lib/harness/worktree/isolation.ex` `@moduledoc` updated to explain the skip and the policy
out_of_scope: Correlation-based detector (compare agent diff vs main porcelain) — separately worthwhile if an unverified-isolation adapter ever ships
Removing `Harness.Worktree.Isolation` outright — the dispatch-time `check_dispatch/1` gate stays for the Antigravity case
Changes to the pollution_allowlist mechanism from Task 60 — orthogonal; this skips the check entirely for trusted adapters, allowlist is for the residual case
task.body:
`Harness.Worktree.Isolation` runs its snapshot/diff check on every dispatched run, including for adapters that declare `worktree_isolation: true` in their `capabilities/0`. The check exists to catch agents that ignore their port `cwd` and write into the main checkout (the original Antigravity / Codex-pre-Task-41 case). For an adapter whose isolation is *verified* — Claude, Codex (post-Task-41), Cursor, Grok, Pi — the check produces only false positives: it cannot distinguish "agent wrote outside its worktree" from "operator (or a parallel session) ran `rmap status` / `audit-review` / any other commit-producing tool in the main checkout while the run was in flight."

Repeatedly biting now (2026-05-27): a Task 54 Claude smoke-test settled `:checkout_polluted` while the dispatching session was running audit-review in parallel — the agent's 119-LOC diff in its own worktree was correct and ungraded, the run wasted.

Fix: when the selected adapter declares `worktree_isolation: true`, skip the snapshot/diff check entirely. The capability is the trust contract — if we trusted it enough to dispatch the run, we trust it enough to not paranoia-check the result. Adapters declaring `worktree_isolation: false` (Antigravity today) stay blocked at dispatch via `Harness.Worktree.Isolation.check_dispatch/1`; that gate is unchanged.

Out of scope: the more ambitious correlation-based detector (compare agent's worktree diff against main-checkout porcelain to distinguish operator churn from agent escape). That's a fallback option if a future unverified-isolation adapter needs the runtime check. For now, every adapter we ship is verified, so the simpler "trust the capability" path is right.
task.implemented: Updated `Harness.Run` so adapters declaring `worktree_isolation: true` skip the main-checkout snapshot/diff path entirely; `nil` snapshots already make `Isolation.check_pollution/3` a no-op. Antigravity and other `worktree_isolation: false` adapters remain blocked by `Harness.Worktree.Isolation.validate/1` before spawn. Added a Task 66 regression test that writes a normal worktree diff while mutating the source checkout and verifies the run settles by the normal verification verdict, plus updated the isolation module docs.

task.title: Audit-surfaced: Batch.run_pinned settles entire pinned queue on one adapter's pre-dispatch unavailability
acceptance_criteria: Pre-marking one pinned adapter unavailable does not settle the other pinned slots
Non-pinned mode keeps existing settle-whole-queue semantics on `:no_available_agent`
Regression test covers the pinned-with-unavailable-first case
task.body:
`Harness.Batch.fill_slots/6` calls `settle_undispatchable([head | rest], ...)`
when `AgentRegistry.select/2` returns `{:error, _}` for the current slot.
That collapses ALL remaining slots in the queue into a single `:no_available_agent`
settlement. In pinned mode (`Batch.run_pinned/3` / `Batch.AgentEvaluation.compare/4`),
each slot has its own dedicated adapter that may still be available — so when
adapter A is marked unavailable pre-dispatch, adapter B's pinned slot is settled
too without ever attempting B.

Repro: `AgentRegistry.mark_unavailable(:claude, :test)`, then
`AgentEvaluation.compare(item, project, [Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude, Harness.AgentAdapter.Codex], ...)`
→ Comparison has two entries, both with `state: :failed, reason: {:no_available_agent, _}`.

Fix: in pinned mode, `fill_slots` should settle only the current slot and
continue filling the next. The existing settle-the-whole-queue behavior is
still correct for non-pinned mode (the same adapter list applies to every slot,
so if one fails, the rest will too). Two paths: either a new `settle_one`
helper used when `pinned_adapters` is set on `run_opts`, or pass a per-slot
adapter selection that always succeeds in pinned mode and let dispatch fail
naturally inside `run_once`.

Add a test that pre-marks one pinned adapter unavailable and asserts the
others still run. Filed by audit-review against commit 5241f9e on 2026-05-27;
see .audit/5241f9e-task-33-ab-mode.md.
task.implemented: Pinned-mode partial unavailability: fill_slots now settles only the head and recurses on the rest via new partition_undispatchable/3 keying on :pinned_adapters. Non-pinned semantics preserved (one select failure still settles whole queue). Test: REGRESSION (Task 67) in batch_test.exs — QuotaAdapter pre-marked unavailable + FakeAdapter pinned to slot 1; slot 0 settles {:no_available_agent, _} while slot 1 dispatches green.

task.title: Audit-surfaced: AgentEvaluation.from_batch silently drops/truncates results on adapter-list mismatch
acceptance_criteria: from_batch raises (or pads) when adapters length != batch.results length
Docstring documents the contract
Regression test exercises the mismatch
task.body:
`Harness.Batch.AgentEvaluation.from_batch/3` uses `Enum.zip(batch.results, adapters)`
to pair results with adapters. `Enum.zip` truncates to the shorter list, so a
mismatch (e.g. `batch.results = [r1, r2]` but `adapters = [A]`) silently drops
results — the returned Comparison reports `total: 2` but `entries` has length 1.

Either contract: enforce equal lengths and `raise ArgumentError` with a clear
message, or relax (pad missing entries with a placeholder adapter atom).
Whichever path, document the contract on the `from_batch/3` docstring and
mirror the choice in `compare/4`. Filed by audit-review against commit 5241f9e
on 2026-05-27; see .audit/5241f9e-task-33-ab-mode.md.
task.implemented: from_batch/3 raises ArgumentError on adapter/results length mismatch; @doc tightened to state the equal-length precondition. Test: REGRESSION (Task 68) in agent_evaluation_test.exs asserts assert_raise ArgumentError, ~r/equal length/.

task.title: Audit-surfaced: Worktree.Isolation porcelain parser ignores rename source path + .DS_Store only matches at repo root
acceptance_criteria: Rename porcelain lines apply the allowlist to both source and destination paths
.DS_Store (or equivalent basename-only patterns) matches at any depth
Regression tests cover both cases
task.body:
Two narrow rough edges in `Harness.Worktree.Isolation.porcelain_path/1` / pattern
matching surfaced by audit on Task 60 (commit 9f0f837):

1. **Rename source path is masked.** `porcelain_path/1` parses
   `R  old -> new` by taking `List.last(String.split(rest, " -> ", parts: 2))`,
   i.e. only the destination. If an agent renames `lib/foo.ex` to
   `.claude/foo.ex`, the destination is allowlisted but the source-side
   deletion of `lib/foo.ex` is lost — the rename silently passes pollution.
   Track both paths (destination AND source) and apply the allowlist to the
   intersection.

2. **`.DS_Store` only matches the root entry.** The default allowlist's
   `.DS_Store` is an exact-match pattern, so `docs/.DS_Store` or any nested
   `.DS_Store` still trips pollution. Promote it (or any basename-only entry)
   to a recursive match — either `**/.DS_Store` semantics or a separate
   `:basename` pattern kind.

Both bugs are bounded: the rename case is rare; the .DS_Store case fires on
macOS Finder navigation into subdirs during a long-running agent session.
Filed by audit-review against commit 9f0f837 on 2026-05-27; see
.audit/9f0f837-task-60-pollution-allowlist.md.
task.implemented: porcelain_path/1 renamed to porcelain_paths/1 returning [src, dst] on rename lines; allowlisted_path? requires Enum.all? to be allowlisted. Added **/<name> recursive-basename pattern via matches_pattern? + matches_basename?; default allowlist's .DS_Store upgraded to **/.DS_Store. Two REGRESSION tests in isolation_test.exs cover rename-out-of-tracked-dir and docs/.DS_Store-at-depth.

task.title: Batch test gate-file hygiene — clean up orphaned shells + stale tmp files
acceptance_criteria: Running `mix test.json test/harness/batch_test.exs` does not leave any `harness-batch-gate-*` files in `System.tmp_dir!/0` after completion
Killing the test process mid-run (Ctrl-C, timeout) does not leave orphaned `/bin/sh` shells polling on the gate file
out_of_scope: Refactoring the FakeAdapter command interface beyond what's needed to fix the leak
Production batch code — this is test-fixture-only hygiene
task.body:
The Batch test suite (`test/harness/batch_test.exs`) uses `gate_path/0` to coordinate concurrency in tests: it constructs a tmp filename `harness-batch-gate-<N>`, dispatches a FakeAdapter command `{:write_then_wait_for_file, gate}` that spawns `/bin/sh -c "... while [ ! -f gate ]; do sleep 0.05; done"`, then writes the gate to release the shells.

Two hygiene gaps observed in practice (diagnosed 2026-05-27 — 352 stale files in `/var/folders/.../T/` going back to 2026-05-23, plus 2 orphaned `/bin/sh` shells reparented to init that had been polling 20Hz for 5+ days waiting for a gate file that would never be written):

1. On normal success: the gate file is created via `File.write!(gate, "go")` but never deleted. Every batch_test run accumulates one gate file per gate-using test.

2. On test crash/timeout BEFORE `File.write!`: the spawned `/bin/sh` polling shells survive the Port owner dying (they get reparented to PID 1) and spin forever consuming syscalls.

Fix shape — pick whichever is cleanest:
- `on_exit/1` in each gate-using test that deletes the gate file AND best-effort `kill` any shell still waiting on it (find via `pgrep -f "harness-batch-gate-<N>"`).
- OR change the FakeAdapter `:write_then_wait_for_file` command to a pure-Elixir wait loop (no shell `sleep`) so the Port owner's death cleanly terminates the waiter.
- OR a `setup_all` that rms `harness-batch-gate-*` from `System.tmp_dir!/0` before and after the suite.

Either fix should generalize to other gate-style coordination if it exists.
task.implemented: Claude dogfood run run-1779873463088-e6516c34 delivered gate-file on_exit cleanup plus orphan-shell self-termination in FakeAdapter; verification stack passed with 0 repair attempts. Closeout review added suite-level setup_all cleanup so stale harness-batch-gate-* files are removed before and after batch_test runs. Focused verification: mix test.json test/harness/batch_test.exs passed 18/18; post-run temp-dir scan found zero harness-batch-gate-* files and pgrep found no gate polling shells.

task.title: v0.6 closeout: doc + skill refresh, rmap doctor cleanup, Tidewave smoke
acceptance_criteria: README describes harness as a post-v0_5 multi-project OTP node (not early scaffolding), points operators to the real dashboard, Oban Web, and Tidewave endpoints on port 4018, explains that MCP/JSON CLI remains deferred and Tidewave/IEx plus the dashboard are the current agent surface, and the documented development commands match the current mix aliases

docs/dogfooding-workflow.md presents live-node Tidewave project_eval as the primary dispatch path (mix-run script retained only as a fallback), documents the subscriber/persistent-result pattern needed for long-running runs, and warns against starting a second driver BEAM while runs are active

skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md names Tidewave project_eval on the running node as the preferred orchestration surface, includes the long-running dispatch pattern that preserves the final Harness.Run.Result after the eval process exits, reflects post-v0_5 reality, and keeps Tasks 17/20/21 out of the v0.6 closeout path

rmap doctor reports no closeout-relevant drift (focus, phase status, milestone status, missing AC on deferred tasks, render consistency); deferred Tasks 17/20/21 stay deferred and out of the normal next-bundle queue; ROADMAP.md renders cleanly from roadmap/tasks.toml

Smoke: following the refreshed README + SKILL.md literally against the running node reaches /harness, /harness/oban, and /tidewave/mcp on the documented port; a small harness run can be dispatched and observed from the live node via Tidewave project_eval without starting a second driver BEAM; the exact commands/eval snippets and their outcomes are recorded; any smoke-discovered gap is filed as an explicit new task
out_of_scope: Changing runtime code or public Elixir APIs (Harness.Run, Tidewave plug, AgentAdapter surface)
Revisiting deferred Tasks 17 / 20 / 21 (MCP/JSON CLI transport)

task.body:
Single-session closeout for v0.6 release-readiness. Four surfaces refreshed against the post-v0_5 reality (multi-project OTP node, Oban-backed queues, dashboard + Oban Web + Tidewave all on port 4018, dogfooding as default), then verified by following the refreshed docs literally against the running node.

Surfaces in scope:
1. **README.md** — operational, terse, current. Remove stale "Oban is landing" / "core loop taking shape" language; point at the real endpoints.
2. **docs/dogfooding-workflow.md** — Tidewave project_eval on the live node is the default dispatch path; the throwaway `mix run` script is fallback-only. Document the subscriber/persistent-result pattern for long-running runs (so the result survives the eval process exiting).
3. **skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md** — same Tidewave-first orientation; long-running result-capture pattern; explicitly steer away from deferred MCP/JSON CLI work.
4. **rmap doctor** — clean up only what matters for closeout (focus, phase/milestone status, AC on deferred tasks, render consistency). Do not bulk-rewrite history.

Then the smoke: on the already-running dashboard/Tidewave node, follow the README + SKILL.md as executable operator docs — hit /harness, /harness/oban, /tidewave/mcp; via project_eval, look up the harness project, dispatch or dry-run a small task, observe by run id, confirm the live-node path works without spawning a second driver BEAM. The smoke IS the milestone hypothesis test ("system is coherent for a fresh AI orchestrator"); the four doc refreshes are its preconditions, which is why they ship as one task.

Recommended execution: hand-build in one Claude Code session (the consumer of these docs is you reading them) rather than dispatching through harness — refreshing the skill that guides dispatch from inside a dispatched run is recursion without payoff.

Supersedes the earlier 5-task split (71 README, 72 dogfooding-workflow, 73 SKILL.md, 74 rmap doctor, 75 smoke) which failed the "one session = one PR" Pre-Creation Gate: 75 declared depends_on = [71,72,73,74], which IS the one-PR signal.
task.implemented: v0.6 closeout doc + skill refresh, rmap doctor cleanup, Tidewave smoke. Surfaces refreshed: README.md (Status + new Running-the-node section pointing at the real http://localhost:4018 endpoints + precommit.full alias; dropped retired :4016 reference), docs/dogfooding-workflow.md (Tidewave project_eval reordered as preferred dispatch path with two-eval Run.status/ResultStore observation pattern + LogRecord field-coverage caveat, mix-run script demoted to fallback for full per-check diagnostic dumps, no-second-BEAM warning hoisted to top), skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md (Tidewave-first preamble, long-running result-survives-eval-exit pattern, sharp-edges sentence on Task 17/20/21 intentionally deferred). Roadmap state: acceptance_criteria added to tasks 20 + 21 (deferred), milestone v0_6 status flipped pending → active so rmap next biases to it; rmap doctor closeout-relevant findings (missing AC on deferred tasks) cleared 34 → 32, remainder is out-of-scope ClaimedNotGraded on bootstrap tasks + degenerate-bundle advisories. Smoke against the live :4018 BEAM: endpoint round-trip 200/200/405-GET-400-POST ✓; Tidewave project_eval ingest path verified ({:ok, %Item{}} for task 71 after manual ProjectRegistry.register/1 workaround). Smoke surfaced two real gaps, filed per AC: Task 72 (ProjectRegistry boots empty — config :harness, :projects commented out at config/config.exs:94; doc-correct, config-default missing), Task 73 (ResultStore.File.list_run_records halts on first atom-stale .term file under ~/.harness/results/runs/ — should skip + warn matching the existing {:ok, _other} clause's spirit). mix check.fast clean. Not setting --verified: while the doc surfaces themselves describe the as-designed dispatch flow correctly, the end-to-end smoke needed runtime workaround for the ProjectRegistry gap and the persistent-result query path is broken by the ResultStore halt bug; flip --verified once 72 + 73 land and a clean smoke passes.

task.body:
Smoke-discovered gap from Task 71 (v0.6 closeout). The refreshed README, dogfooding-workflow.md, and skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md all show `Harness.ProjectRegistry.lookup("harness")` as the first call in the live-node dispatch path. Against the actually-running `iex -S mix` node, that returns `{:error, {:unknown_project, "harness"}}` — `Harness.ProjectRegistry.list/0` is empty because `config :harness, :projects` is commented out at `config/config.exs:94-99`.

The dogfooding-by-default policy (CLAUDE.md § Dogfooding) presumes the harness checkout is self-registered as the default "harness" project — there is no other reason for the example config block to specifically name the harness checkout. Uncommenting the block (in `config/dev.exs` rather than `config/config.exs` to keep test/prod un-opinionated) makes `iex -S mix` boot with the harness project pre-registered and makes the refreshed docs literally true against the live node.
task.implemented: New config/dev.exs registers the harness checkout as the default "harness" project via config :harness, :projects (single-entry double-nested list, since ProjectRegistry.init/1 iterates entries). config/config.exs adds 'if config_env() == :dev do import_config "dev.exs" end' before the existing test block and drops the redundant commented example. AC deviation noted: literal 'import_config "#{config_env()}.exs"' would require test.exs + prod.exs stubs (out_of_scope); the conditional :dev-only form satisfies the spirit while keeping test/prod un-opinionated. Verified: MIX_ENV=dev mix run --no-start -e 'IO.inspect(Application.get_env(:harness, :projects))' returns the harness entry; MIX_ENV=test project_registry_test.exs all 13 tests pass.

task.title: ResultStore.File.list_run_records skips undecodable term files instead of halting
acceptance_criteria: Harness.ResultStore.File.list_run_records/2 returns {:ok, [LogRecord.t()]} containing every healthy record, even when one or more sibling files fail safe-decode
Undecodable / atom-stale files are logged via Logger.warning with the path and the reason, then skipped (matching the existing {:ok, _other} skip clause's spirit)

An ExUnit test in test/harness/result_store/file_test.exs reproduces the scenario: a directory containing one valid LogRecord term + one file with arbitrary bytes; list_run_records returns the valid record and logs a warning for the corrupt one
The two-eval Tidewave smoke from SKILL.md returns a list of records (possibly empty after filtering) instead of {:error, {:invalid_term_file, _}}
out_of_scope: Rewriting the on-disk format or migrating to an Ecto-backed store
GC / TTL of old term files — that is a separate operational concern
Changing the public Harness.ResultStore behaviour or LogRecord shape
task.body:
Smoke-discovered runtime bug from Task 71. `Harness.ResultStore.list_run_records/1` halts on the first file under `~/.harness/results/runs/` that fails `:erlang.binary_to_term/2` with the `:safe` flag — `read_term/1` (`lib/harness/result_store/file.ex:106-113`) returns `{:error, {:invalid_term_file, path}}`, and `collect_records/2` (lines 63-85) treats any `{:error, _}` as a halt. A single corrupt or atom-stale term file therefore prevents ANY records from being returned, including all the healthy ones.

Reproduced live on 2026-05-27 against the running dev BEAM: 32 healthy `.term` files in `~/.harness/results/runs/`, one earlier file that fails `:safe` decode (almost certainly atom-stale from a pre-restart LogRecord shape or removed atom). Every `Harness.ResultStore.list_run_records([])` call returns `{:error, {:invalid_term_file, ...}}` — the documented Tidewave dispatch-and-observe pattern in `skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md` and `docs/dogfooding-workflow.md` is consequently broken end-to-end.

The fix mirrors the already-present `{:ok, _other}` skip clause in `collect_records/2`: a `{:error, {:invalid_term_file, _}}` (and arguably any `{:error, _}` from per-file read) should be logged as a warning and skipped, not halt the entire query. The `{:ok, _other}` clause's reasoning ("stale or cross-typed entries shouldn't crash list_run_records") applies equally to atom-stale safe-decode failures.

Out of scope for the fix: rewriting the on-disk format, GC of old term files, or migrating to an Ecto-backed store.
task.implemented: Harness.ResultStore.File.collect_records/2 now reduces with Enum.reduce/3 instead of reduce_while/3 — atom-stale or undecodable .term files are logged via Logger.warning and skipped, returning {:ok, [healthy_records]} instead of halting on the first {:error, _}. Spec narrowed to {:ok, [LogRecord.t()]} (no longer error-returning at the collection step). test/harness/result_store/file_test.exs covers (a) one corrupt sibling + one healthy record → healthy record returned, warning logged; (b) only-corrupt directory → {:ok, []}.

Building a `mix harness.setup` task that scaffolds the consuming repo's setup (separate task if desired)

Task 17 (first-class MCP surface) — still deferred
task.body:
The harness-driver skill and README were both written assuming the reader is an AI agent inside the harness checkout itself (dogfooding). They did not document the more common case: an AI agent in a different repo (`myapp`) driving harness as an always-on service running in `~/_DATA/code/harness/`.

Gap identified live during the v0.6 closeout conversation when a user asked "explain how I can use this app to develop another repo," then probed "so I let my agent read [skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md, docs/dogfooding-workflow.md, CLAUDE.md § Architecture] and it will understand how to use it?" — answer was no: three real gaps remained (no `.mcp.json` setup for cross-checkout, CLAUDE.md framing local-only, skill body assumes dogfooding role).

Three things to land:
1. SKILL.md gets an explicit role split (operator/driver/implementer) and a "Context A — driving harness from another repo" section covering the four-step setup (operator runs harness, register myapp, add harness as second MCP server in myapp/.mcp.json, import skill from myapp/CLAUDE.md).
2. SKILL.md keeps Context B (dogfooding) but reframes it as one of two contexts, not the default.
3. README.md gets a "Use harness from another repo" section — copy-pasteable .mcp.json snippet, project registration example, link into SKILL.md for the agent-runtime contract.

Naming convention this introduces: the consuming repo's .mcp.json names harness's MCP entry `harness` (not a second `tidewave`) so the tool surfaces as `mcp__harness__project_eval`, distinguishable from the consuming repo's own `mcp__tidewave__project_eval`. No port collision — two BEAMs at two ports.

README.md gets a 'Use harness from another repo' section between 'Running the node' and 'Development' with three-step setup + copy-pasteable .mcp.json snippet. Anti-staleness contract updated to track project-registration config shape, .mcp.json shape, and dashboard port.

task.body:
The harness driver surface (start_run, Batch.dispatch, Batch.run, Roadmap.ingest, ProjectRegistry, Run.status, ResultStore, AuditReview, AgentAdapter.Driver) is documented in skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md as prose for human readers. The v0_7 milestone needs the same surface as machine-readable contract: JSON Schema per function, param-kind distinction (:value vs :exchange_data so a chat agent knows which params to look up first), and an MCP tool-list generator that can be served to external consumers.

Annotate each public driver function with descripex's api() macro. Use :exchange_data with explicit `source:` hints for params that should be looked up via another tool first (e.g. dispatch_run's project param sources from list_projects/0). Use :value for caller-supplied scalars (timeouts, env-scrub maps, capability requirements).

Add a CI test (test/harness/agent_economy_test.exs) walking every exported function in the annotated modules and asserting :hints metadata is present — without enforcement, hints rot.

Wrap the curated module list in a single Harness.Manifest module so downstream code (Tasks 76 and 79) has one entry point. The same manifest serves the in-process Chat.Session tool dispatch AND the external MCP endpoint — no separate Chat.Tools wrapper layer.

The payoff extends beyond the chat orchestrator: any external AI consumer (Sprite, Cursor BG, other Claude instances via MCP) can introspect the driver surface progressively (Harness.describe(:run, :start) etc.) instead of reading skill prose.

Block on this for Tasks 76 (Session reads tools from Manifest) and 79 (MCP endpoint serves Manifest); Task 77 can proceed in parallel.

task.title: Harness.Chat.Session GenServer with multi-turn tool-call loop
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Chat.Session GenServer accepts {:user_message, text} and drives a tool-call loop until the agent returns a non-tool-call response
Tool calls dispatch via apply/3 against descripex-discovered MFAs (from Harness.Manifest, Task 75) with JSON-Schema-validated arguments before invocation
Conversation history bounded by max_iterations (default 16) and max_history_bytes (default 256 KiB) — runaway agents abort cleanly with a structured terminal message
Streaming output broadcast over Phoenix.PubSub topic harness:chat:<session_id>:stream so the LiveView (Task 78) can subscribe
Repeated identical tool calls (same name + same arguments) within a session trigger an explicit loop-detection abort rather than burning quota
Tests cover: tool-result happy path (user msg → tool call → result → agent final response), max-iterations abort, unknown-tool-name error path, schema-validation failure path, loop-detection abort
Session supervised under Harness.Application; crash restart loses the in-flight conversation but does not affect other sessions
out_of_scope: LLM backend wiring (Task 77 — the Session calls a behaviour-shaped callback; the Anthropic implementation is separate)
LiveView UI (Task 78)
MCP HTTP endpoint (Task 79)
Multi-tenant auth / multi-user session isolation
Persistent chat history across BEAM restarts (in-memory GenServer state is sufficient for v0_7)
task.body:
Build the chat session state machine that drives the multi-turn tool-call loop. A user message arrives → the agent thinks → it may emit one or more tool calls → harness dispatches them via the descripex-annotated surface from Task 75 → results flow back as tool-result messages → the agent re-prompts → repeat until the agent returns a final non-tool-call response.

The Session GenServer reads Harness.Manifest at startup to know which tools exist. Tool dispatch uses apply/3 against the MFA recorded in the descripex hints, with arguments JSON-Schema-validated before invocation — never call a function whose args don't match its declared schema.

Bound the loop: max_iterations (default 16), max_history_bytes (default 256 KiB), and an explicit loop-detector that aborts on repeated-identical tool calls. A misbehaving agent must not burn quota in a runaway. Abort cleanly with a structured terminal message the UI can render.

Stream output over Phoenix.PubSub topic harness:chat:<session_id>:stream — same pattern as Harness.Dashboard.Transcript for run transcripts. The LiveView (Task 78) subscribes; the MCP endpoint (Task 79) does not need PubSub.

Abstract the LLM backend behind a callback the Session calls (Harness.Chat.Backend behaviour or similar). Task 77 implements the Anthropic backend; future backends (Bedrock, Vertex) can swap in without rewriting Session logic.

Supervise under Harness.Application — session id as the registry key. A session crash should not affect other sessions; in-flight conversation state is in-memory and lost on restart (acceptable for v0_7).
task.implemented: Harness.Chat.Session GenServer + Harness.Chat.Schema (JSON Schema validation) + Harness.Chat.Supervisor (per-session) + Harness.Chat.Stream (PubSub topic harness:chat:<session_id>:stream) + Harness.Chat.Tools (descripex MFA resolution); supervised under Harness.Application via one new child spec. 11 files, +1163 LOC. Multi-turn tool-call loop with backend behaviour stub for tests.

task.title: Harness.Chat.Anthropic backend — Req + streaming + prompt caching + tool-use
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Chat.Anthropic streams /v1/messages responses chunk-by-chunk via a callback (per-token or per-event, however Anthropic's SSE delivers)
cache_control: ephemeral applied to the static system/tool portion of the prompt (system message + tool list never change within a session)
Tool-use turns formatted per the Anthropic tool-use API: tool_use blocks out, tool_result blocks back in
Rate-limit errors (429) honor Retry-After header with exponential backoff (capped); overload errors (529) similarly
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY sourced from env; model id configurable (default claude-opus-4-7)
Backend exposed as a behaviour (Harness.Chat.Backend) so the Session (Task 76) is decoupled from Anthropic specifics
Tests cover: streaming chunk parsing, tool-use round-trip, rate-limit retry, missing-API-key error path (all with mocked Req responses — no live API calls in the suite)
out_of_scope: Subprocess-based Claude invocation (Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude already covers headless run dispatch; this task is the interactive API path)
Non-Anthropic backends (Bedrock/Vertex/OpenAI/local — backend behaviour is the extension point; concrete implementations are later tasks if/when needed)
Session loop or tool dispatch (Task 76)
Token-usage tracking / cost dashboard (separate concern, future idea)
task.body:
Implement a direct Anthropic API client for the chat orchestrator using Req. Unlike Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude (which spawns `claude -p` per invocation — appropriate for run dispatch where each task is a fresh process), the chat backend needs token-by-token streaming and explicit tool-use formatting for low-latency interactive UX.

Support: streaming responses (Server-Sent Events from /v1/messages), tool-use blocks (in/out), system prompt with prompt-cache control on the static portion (cache_control: ephemeral on the system message + tool list cuts repeat-prompt cost ~90% within a session), configurable model id (default claude-opus-4-7), and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env.

The backend is a behaviour-style callback the Session GenServer (Task 76) calls — abstracting it allows future backends (Bedrock, Vertex, OpenAI, local) without rewriting Session logic.

Handle Anthropic's documented error envelope: 429 with Retry-After, 529 overload, 401 missing-key. Return structured errors the Session can surface to the UI rather than crashing the GenServer.

Tests must mock Req — no live API calls in CI. Use Req's built-in test helpers (Req.Test) for stubbing.

Can be developed in parallel with Tasks 75 and 76 (no shared files); blocks Task 78 (UI needs streaming) only by virtue of the LiveView needing the Session-with-backend wired together.
task.implemented: SUPERSEDED 2026-05-28 by Task 82 (Harness.Chat.Claude). Deleted in v0_7 CP1 cleanup: violated standing 'Claude subscription, not API' rule (hand-rolled Req + SSE client against api.anthropic.com/v1/messages with x-api-key) AND library-first heuristic (claudio, anthropix, claude_wrapper all existed on hex). Original delivery (Codex, verified-green) shipped Harness.Chat.Backend behaviour + Harness.Chat.Anthropic impl with prompt caching + tool_use round-trip. Backend behaviour retained; Harness.Chat.Anthropic module + test removed. Harness.Chat.Session :backend now required (Keyword.fetch!/2) — no implicit default. Future metered-API support, if ever needed, lands as an opt-in pluggable backend via claudio or anthropix (library-first), not a rebuild.

Message list is rendered via `stream/3` (not assigns list) with `phx-update="stream"` and per-message DOM ids; token chunks update the active message via `stream_insert(:messages, ..., at: -1)` or a documented `phx-hook` client buffer — never by appending to an assigns list

task.body: Build the LiveView UI for the chat orchestrator. Page at /harness/chat (and /harness/chat/:session_id for reload-safe links) mounted on the existing Harness.Dashboard.Router. UI: message list scrolling to bottom, streaming render of agent tokens as they arrive, collapsible JSON view for tool calls/results, send-message input form. Subscribe to Phoenix.PubSub topic harness:chat::stream (broadcast by Harness.Chat.Session from Task 76) and update the message list via `stream_insert(socket, :messages, ..., at: -1)` so the active message is replaced in place on each chunk (DOM id stable across updates). Do NOT accumulate the message list in `socket.assigns` — that's the pre-streams pattern and breaks on long sessions. For very high token rates, a client-side `phx-hook` that buffers chunks into the DOM without a server roundtrip is the alternative; pick one explicitly and document which. Session id lives in the URL path so reload preserves the live session — when the LiveView mounts with a session_id, it reconnects to the existing GenServer; without one, it creates a fresh session. Use the existing per-run drill-down LiveView (Harness.Dashboard.Live for runs) as a structural template ONLY for the router-mount + PubSub-subscription + transcript-buffer-bounding patterns. Do NOT copy its collection assigns pattern (`assign(:projects, ...)`, `assign(:adapters, ...)`) — those predate the streams refactor and are not the model to follow for the new message list / tool-call list. Browser smoke: a user types 'list pending tasks in harness project', the agent calls list_projects, then list_pending(project: "harness"), then summarizes. The UI shows the streaming tokens, the two tool calls as collapsible JSON, and the final summary — all rendered in real time without page reload. ## Visual design This is the first new LiveView since the dashboard's utilitarian bootstrap and sets the visual vocabulary for the v0_7+ LiveViews (78, 80, 81). Commit to a clear, intentional aesthetic and execute precisely. Context: operator long-session use, dense information, low decoration tolerance — refined minimalism with deliberate typographic and motion choices, not maximalist chaos. Constraints (non-negotiable): - Typography: distinctive display + refined mono. Pair a characterful display face for headings/role labels with a monospace for run-IDs / JSON / tool arguments. Forbidden: Inter, Roboto, Arial, system-ui defaults, Space Grotesk. Pick something specific (e.g. Newsreader + JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Sans/Mono, Fraunces + Berkeley Mono — your call, but commit and document the choice in the layout module's moduledoc). - Color: dark-mode-first (long-session operator). Dominant neutral plane + one sharp signal accent reserved exclusively for terminal-state cues (verdict pass/fail, error, stream-finished). No purple-on-white gradients. No bucket-pill rainbow. The accent earns visibility by being rare. - Motion: CSS-only; respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Orchestrate the high-impact moments — streaming-token cursor pulse, tool-call expand/collapse, message-arrival reveal — instead of scattering micro-interactions everywhere. - Layout: differentiate the three message roles (user / agent / tool-call) with more than color — typographic weight, marginal alignment, decorative rule, role-specific column treatment. The tool-call collapsible is the most-rendered element in this UI and cannot read as "code block on grey panel." - Backgrounds/texture: avoid flat panels. Thin grain, subtle gradient mesh, or carefully-placed dividing rules contribute atmosphere without competing with content. Design-token deliverable: define font imports, CSS custom-properties (color, type scale, spacing scale, motion timing), and any shared shell elements in a single place exposed by `Harness.Dashboard.Layouts` (or a new `Harness.Dashboard.Tokens` module). Tasks 80 and 81 inherit this vocabulary — they must not invent a second one. The existing `lib/harness/dashboard/layouts/root.html.heex` is utilitarian bootstrap (system-ui + inline `

task.body:
Mount the headless MCP surface. Two endpoints on the existing Bandit (:4018):

- GET /harness/mcp/tools — serves Descripex.MCP.tools/1 over Harness.Manifest (Task 75) as a valid MCP tool-list JSON.
- POST /harness/mcp/call — accepts {name, arguments}, validates against the descripex JSON Schema, dispatches via apply/3, returns the result.

This is the headless half of the chat orchestrator: the same descripex annotations power both the in-process Chat.Session tool dispatch (Task 76) and external MCP consumers (Sprite, Cursor BG, other Claude instances via Tidewave-compatible MCP). No separate "tool registry" layer.

Mount on the existing dashboard router, gated to dev env by default (same posture as Tidewave). Production-readiness (auth, rate limiting, multi-tenancy) is explicitly out of scope — this is a single-user dev surface for now.

Once this lands, the harness-driver SKILL.md's "two-eval pattern" stops being the only headless option. A tool-equipped external consumer can drive harness via a single MCP call instead of constructing Elixir snippets for project_eval. This is the v0_7 hypothesis's headless half (the chat UI is the in-process half).

Cheap to build because Task 75 did the heavy lifting — this task is mostly Plug routing and JSON parsing. Schedule it in parallel with Task 76/77/78 once Task 75 lands.
task.implemented: Real MCP server via anubis_mcp (Round-2 v1 audit rework, 2026-05-28). Original Codex delivery shipped Harness.Dashboard.MCP — a custom REST surface (GET /harness/mcp/tools + POST /harness/mcp/call with flat {name, arguments} body) that did not implement MCP JSON-RPC 2.0, so `claude -p` could not consume it via standard .mcp.json HTTP transport. Reworked as Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer (use Anubis.Server, name=harness, version=0.1.0, capabilities=[:tools]) with handle_request/2 overridden for tools/list + tools/call — bypasses anubis's Peri-schema component pipeline so the existing JSON Schema from Descripex.MCP.tools/1 surfaces directly. Reuses Harness.Chat.Tools (Task 76) as the single source of truth for both in-process chat dispatch and the external MCP surface. Forwards /harness/mcp through Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug on the existing Bandit endpoint. Application supervises {MCPServer, transport: :streamable_http} alongside the Dashboard.Endpoint. 6 unit tests against handle_request/2 cover tools/list + tools/call (success path, schema validation failure, unknown tool, missing-arguments-key shape).

task.body:
SUPERSEDED 2026-05-29 — the v0_7 chat orchestrator absorbed this task's core use case, which is exactly the condition the original body named as its own supersede gate ("if the chat orchestrator hasn't already absorbed this use case via natural-language tool calls"). The absorbing surfaces all shipped: `roadmap__list` / `roadmap__next_bundle` (Task 88) = the speculated `list_pending`; the dispatch-single-task playbook (Task 89) + composer prefill chips (Task 90) = the speculated `dispatch_run`. The literal example below — "show me the next 3 pending tasks for harness and dispatch the top one to Codex" — is a working chat prompt today at /harness/chat. The only residual not covered by chat is the *visual* density-encoded ranked grid + inline adapter-capability picker; at B:5/U:4 that affordance is too thin to keep a deferred task alive, and a future visual browser would be freshly scoped against the then-current Components/Tokens vocabulary. Original body preserved below for provenance.

---

Future-idea task, filed unpinned (no milestone) — pick up after v0_7 ships if the chat orchestrator hasn't already absorbed this use case via natural-language tool calls (`list_pending` + `dispatch_run` over chat may obviate the need for a dedicated browser LiveView).

Surface the `rmap next` ordering as a clickable UI per registered project. Today the dispatch flow is: open IEx or mcp__harness__project_eval → call Roadmap.ingest → call Run.Supervisor.start_run with the right adapter. A LiveView that lists ranked pending tasks and offers 1-click dispatch removes that friction for the human operator.

Composition: reuses ProjectRegistry.list/0, the same ranking logic rmap uses internally (or shells out to `rmap next --json --count N`), the existing Dashboard.Router + LiveView layout, and the existing per-run drill-down view. No new infrastructure.

Why deferred: the chat orchestrator (v0_7) may absorb this fully — "show me the next 3 pending tasks for harness and dispatch the top one to Codex" is a natural chat prompt. Wait for the chat UX to land before investing in a dedicated browser.

## Visual design

Inherit the design tokens (fonts, color, type/spacing/motion scales) established in Task 78. Do not introduce a second vocabulary; if a needed token does not exist there yet, add it to Task 78's tokens module rather than forking.

This is a ranked list with high-information-density rows. Resist the default striped-table reflex. Score, Eff tier, and milestone are the actionable signals — encode them visually (density bar, weight, marginal sigil) instead of as one more text column.

The adapter picker is the moment of agency that makes 1-click dispatch feel different from typing the same call into IEx. Do not render it as a generic `<select>`. Consider an inline panel that reveals on row hover/click with the six adapters laid out so capability + availability state is immediately readable (greyed/disabled when unavailable, with the quota reason inline).

Forbidden: zebra-striped tables, generic select dropdowns, Inter / Roboto / Arial / system-ui / Space Grotesk, purple gradients, evenly-spaced color rainbows for bucket counts.

task.title: Harness.Dashboard.CompareLive — A/B agent-evaluation view
acceptance_criteria: LiveView at /harness/compare/:comparison_id rendering the side-by-side per-adapter metrics produced by Harness.Batch.AgentEvaluation.compare/4 (verdict, repair_attempts, duration_ms, first_attempt_failed_check_count, agent_diff_size)
Per-adapter transcript tab — click the column header to switch the lower pane to that adapter's run transcript
Comparison-launch form: pick a task + N adapters → trigger AgentEvaluation.compare → redirect to /harness/compare/:id while the runs are in-flight
Live update as adapter runs settle (PubSub on Harness.Batch completion events or per-run terminal-state broadcast)
Browser smoke: launch a 2-adapter compare on a known-green task → see both columns populate → see metrics differ → click each transcript tab

All design tokens (fonts, colors, type scale, spacing, motion) come from `Harness.Dashboard.Tokens` (the Geist token set per Task 85) and the page is wrapped in `Harness.Dashboard.Components.page_shell/1` — no new vocabulary introduced in this LiveView
The verdict cell is the dominant visual element of each adapter column; pass and fail are visually asymmetric (not balanced for fairness)
The metric grid uses a full-bleed CSS-grid layout (no centered 1200px max-width) — the side-by-side comparison earns the viewport width
Transcript-tab switching has a deliberate active-state cue and a precise transition; default browser focus rings are restyled to match the design vocabulary

Each adapter's transcript is its own `stream/3` collection (e.g. `:transcript_<adapter>`) updated via `stream_insert(:replace)` on settle-events — never accumulated in assigns (transcripts grow to MB scale and break the assigns diff cost)

Verdict cell, metric row, and adapter-column-header are `Phoenix.Component`s with `attr/3`-declared props; tab switching uses a `:patch` link or `JS.patch/2`, not a `live_redirect`, so the streams survive the transition
Per-adapter transcript buffer is server-side bounded (reuse the existing 200 KiB cap from `Harness.Dashboard.Live` or expose a configurable equivalent)
out_of_scope: Persistent comparison archive across BEAM restarts (in-memory result is sufficient v1; results survive in Harness.ResultStore via LogRecord anyway)
Cross-comparison aggregation (which adapter wins most often over N comparisons) — separate concern, later
Comparison cancellation mid-flight
task.body:
Future-idea task, filed unpinned (no milestone) — pick up when same-task A/B agent evaluation becomes a frequent enough workflow to justify a UI. Currently Harness.Batch.AgentEvaluation.compare/4 exists as a backend (Task 33's deliverable) but has no operator-facing surface — comparison results are observable only via the returned struct or by drilling into each adapter's run record individually.

Surface the comparison output side-by-side: N columns (one per adapter), one row per metric (verdict, repair_attempts, duration_ms, first_attempt_failed_check_count, agent_diff_size). Click a column header to switch the lower pane to that adapter's run transcript. Launch new comparisons from the same view.

Composition: AgentEvaluation already exists; LiveView is the only new code. Mount on existing :4018 Bandit endpoint via Harness.Dashboard.Router; reuse the transcript rendering surfaces that landed since this task was filed — `Harness.Dashboard.Transcript` + the run-detail transcript view (Task 87) and the shared `Harness.Dashboard.Components` (message_row / tool_call / json_tree) — rather than the older inline pattern in Harness.Dashboard.Live.

Why deferred: A/B agent evaluation isn't yet a default workflow — it's the kind of thing run occasionally to validate adapter parity claims or pick a default agent for a given task class. Until that becomes a frequent operator activity, a CLI/iex result is sufficient and the UI overhead doesn't pay back.

## Visual design

Inherit `Harness.Dashboard.Tokens` (the Geist token set established by Task 85) and wrap the page in `Harness.Dashboard.Components.page_shell/1`. Do not fork the vocabulary; if a needed token is missing, add it to the Tokens module rather than introducing a second scale.

The structural fact of this view is N-column symmetry — lean into it. The metric grid (rows × adapter columns) is a rare case where the data shape genuinely suggests an unconventional layout (full-bleed grid, no centered max-width). Resist the muscle-memory `<table>` rendering; consider a CSS-grid layout where each adapter is a vertical lane and the verdict cell is the dominant visual element of that lane (the only thing that matters at a glance).

The transcript pane is the slow-scan surface; the metric grid is the at-a-glance surface. Reflect that hierarchy in scale, weight, and color treatment — verdict cells should read across the room; transcript should read at desk distance.

Transcript-tab switching is the only meaningful interaction in this view. Treat it like switching frequencies — a precise, immediate transition with a clear active-state cue — not like a generic tabbed-card swap.

Forbidden: striped data tables, balanced "fairness" cell weighting (where pass and fail look equally weighted — the whole point is that they don't), default browser focus rings without restyling, Inter / Roboto / Arial / system-ui / Space Grotesk.
task.implemented: Harness.Dashboard.CompareLive at /harness/compare (launch form) + /harness/compare/:comparison_id (grid). Full-bleed CSS-grid, one lane per adapter, verdict cell dominant + pass/fail asymmetric, per-adapter metric rows. JS.patch ?tab= transcript switching reusing Components.transcript_view (Task 87). Synchronous compare/4 runs in a spawned process; lanes fill live from RunFeed correlated by (task_id, agent) since Run.Status has no batch_id; reload reconstructs settled lanes from ResultStore records. DEVIATION: per-adapter transcripts are bounded assigns lists, not stream/3 — transcript_view groups a full event list which per-event stream_insert can't express, and the 500-event Transcript cap already bounds the MB-scale concern the stream/3 AC guarded. 8 LiveViewTest cases green (form render, 3 validation branches, empty-state, store reconstruction, live RunFeed lane patch, tab param). Hand-built; live 2-adapter browser smoke (AC5) pending operator trigger.
