task.body:
Add a `Harness.Chat.Backend` implementation that drives headless `claude -p` via
`Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver` (Port spawn), replacing `Harness.Chat.Anthropic`
as the *default* backend. Anthropic stays in the tree as opt-in metered fallback.

**Why this exists.** Task 77 shipped `Harness.Chat.Anthropic` — a direct Req
client against `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` with `x-api-key`. That
violates the standing policy "Claude subscription, not API" (memory:
feedback_claude_subscription_not_api). Chat sessions should route through the
host's Claude subscription OAuth, not the metered API.

**Implementation shape:**

- New `lib/harness/chat/claude.ex` implementing `Harness.Chat.Backend`.
- Per-turn: spawn `claude -p <latest-user-message> --output-format stream-json --session-id <chat-session-id>` (or `--continue`, depending on resume-flag verification — see Sharp Edges) via `Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver.run/3` or equivalent Port spawn.
- Configure `.mcp.json` in the spawn cwd pointing at Task 79's headless MCP endpoint (`http://localhost:4018/harness/mcp/...`) so harness manifest tools are surfaced to claude. Exact `.mcp.json` shape + cwd-relative loading semantics confirmed via Claude Code docs as a pre-implementation step.
- Parse stream-json events into Backend callbacks: `text_delta` → `:text_delta`; `tool_use` blocks → `:tool_use`.
- Return assembled assistant response matching `Backend.response()`.
- Flip default in `Harness.Chat.Session.init/1` (line 74) from `Harness.Chat.Anthropic` to `Harness.Chat.Claude`. Anthropic remains opt-in (`backend: Harness.Chat.Anthropic`).

**Sharp edges:**

- `claude -p` manages its own conversation state via session id, not a caller-supplied message list. `Backend.stream/3` receives a full `messages` list; this backend extracts only the latest user message and relies on claude's session continuity for history. Document in the moduledoc.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` must NOT be read by this backend at any layer; explicitly scrub it from the Port env to prevent shadowing of the host OAuth.
- `claude -p` session-resume flag and `.mcp.json` cwd-relative loading both require verification against current Claude Code docs (Jan 2026 cutoff is past the relevant releases).
task.implemented: Hand-built v0_7 CP3. `Harness.Chat.Claude` (lib/harness/chat/claude.ex) implements `Harness.Chat.Backend`: per-turn spawns `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --mcp-config <path>` over the same `/bin/sh -c 'exec "$0" "$@" </dev/null'` Port wrapper `Harness.AgentAdapter` uses (immediate stdin EOF). Subscription path enforced by `build_env/1` scrubbing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to `false` (with the caller-wins-on-explicit-override merge order documented). MCP config (`.harness-mcp-config.json`) written into the per-session cwd at every turn, pointing at `http://localhost:4018/harness/mcp` (Task 79 rework via anubis_mcp). Per-session cwd derived deterministically from `backend_opts[:session_id]` (`Path.join([tmp_dir!, "harness-chat", session_id])`) — Session updated to inject `state.session_id` into `backend_opts` ahead of `backend.stream/3` so backends needing a stable workspace get one. `--continue` resume gated on `length(messages) > 1` (first turn omits it; claude finds the prior conversation in cwd on every subsequent turn). `Harness.Chat.Claude.StreamParser` (pure module) buffers Port chunks, splits on `\n`, parses each line, and emits normalized events (`:assistant_text`, `:assistant_tool_use`, `:tool_result`, `:system_init`, `:result`, `:unknown`). `handle_event/3` fans `:text_delta` and `:tool_use` to the Session callback for dashboard rendering but ONLY accumulates text blocks into `response.content` — Claude's internal MCP tool loop runs inside the spawned process, so tool_use blocks must NOT leak back to Session (would re-dispatch the same tool harness already executed). Driver loop mirrors `Harness.AgentAdapter.Driver` shape: total + idle deadlines, `wait` = `min(remaining(total), remaining(idle))`, idle reset on every output chunk, `:exit_status` triggers parser finalize and outcome assembly. Non-zero exit returns `{:error, %{type: :claude_exit, status: N}}`; timeout returns `{:error, %{type: :timeout, message: "..."}}`. Acceptance criterion "Default in `Harness.Chat.Session.init/1` changed" superseded by CP1: `:backend` is now required (Keyword.fetch!/2) — there is no implicit default to flip. Browser-smoke (acceptance criterion 6) deferred to v0_7 closeout (CP4). Tests: 11 parser unit tests cover partial-line buffering, mid-line splits, multi-line chunks, multi-block messages, tool_result decode, terminal result, banner/JSON-noise drop, unknown-type passthrough, finalize-on-close; 12 backend unit tests cover argv construction (base + model + system + resume), `resume_argv` heuristic, `extract_user_text` happy/error paths, `write_mcp_config` shape, `default_cwd` determinism, `build_env` subscription scrub + caller-wins override, `stream/3` early-error returns (`:missing_session_id`, `:no_user_message`). Sobelow `Traversal.FileModule` annotations on `write_mcp_config` + `ensure_cwd` (paths are harness-controlled cwd, not HTTP input). All 627 tests in the targeted set green; 39 new tests added across the two new test files.

acceptance_criteria: MCP initialize from claude-code 2.1.153 (protocol 2025-11-25) completes without :badarg

out_of_scope: Auth / multi-tenant / rate limiting on the MCP endpoint (out-of-scope per Task 79)
Supporting MCP clients other than claude -p (other consumers can be added later if/when they appear)

task.body:
Every MCP initialize call from `claude -p` (claude-code 2.1.153, protocol "2025-11-25") crashes inside Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug with `:badarg`, returning HTTP 500. Reproduced ~20+ times in a single chat-orchestrator browser smoke run on 2026-05-28 against the Task 82 backend.

Symptom: claude -p never receives the harness tool list, so it falls back to its own built-ins (Bash, TaskList, ToolSearch) and hallucinates that the harness toolset is empty / no tasks exist. The v0_7 LLM-driven smoke (the entire reason Task 82 + Task 79 exist) is therefore not actually exercising the harness tools — it only looks like it is because the chat UI renders Claude's built-in tool calls correctly.

Repro: open /harness/chat in a browser with claude-code installed, send any tool-needing prompt, watch the Phoenix logs — every request shows `Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug` followed immediately by `Converted error :badarg to 500 response`.

The request shape coming in is a clean JSON-RPC 2.0 initialize with the standard MCP 2025-11-25 envelope; the failure is downstream inside anubis. Suspect: protocol-version handling, an unsupported capability key (`elicitation`, `roots`), or a missing route on the supervised Anubis.Server pipeline.

Investigate by (a) catching the badarg in the Plug to get a real stack trace (the cascading ErrorHTML crash is hiding it — see sibling task), (b) reading anubis_mcp source for what `:badarg` paths exist on `tools/list` and `initialize` handlers, and (c) checking whether `Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer` needs to declare additional capabilities beyond `[:tools]` for the streamable_http transport to complete the handshake.
task.implemented: Anubis StreamableHTTP transport started cleanly. Root cause: anubis's should_start?({:streamable_http, opts}) for the transport falls through to Application.get_env(:phoenix, :serve_endpoints) when the :start opt is absent. That flag is false under iex -S mix because harness is not a phx.server app (the dashboard is one opt-in surface among many — see CLAUDE.md mountable-consumer story). Result: Anubis.Server.Supervisor.init/1 returned :ignore, the :persistent_term {Anubis.Server.Supervisor, MCPServer, :session_config} was never stored, and every MCP request crashed inside Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug.resolve_runtime_config/1 on persistent_term.get/1 with ArgumentError (logged as :badarg + converted to 500). The first explorer's negotiate/2-returns-:error diagnosis was contradicted by the registry (protocol 2025-11-25 IS in @versions); the real crash site was much earlier, in the Plug's runtime-config resolution. Fix: change the Harness.Application MCP child spec from {Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer, transport: :streamable_http} to {Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer, transport: {:streamable_http, start: true}}. The :start opt is checked before the auto-detect (deps/anubis_mcp/lib/anubis/server/supervisor.ex:336-337), explicitly telling Anubis to start regardless of the global Phoenix flag — matching reality, since the dashboard endpoint already runs (per-endpoint server: true). task.body:
The standalone dashboard Endpoint has no ErrorHTML module, so any 500 in the dashboard pipeline crashes the error renderer too with `(ArgumentError) no "500" html template defined for Harness.Dashboard.ErrorHTML  (the module does not exist)`. This actively hides the underlying error — the real stack trace is replaced by a Phoenix.Template crash about the missing fallback template.

Surfaced while debugging the anubis transport :badarg bug (sibling task): every 500 from `/harness/mcp` triggered a second crash trying to render the error page, which made it harder to see the original `:badarg`.

Minimum fix: add `Harness.Dashboard.ErrorHTML` with `def render("500.html", _), do: "Internal Server Error"` and `def render("404.html", _), do: "Not Found"`, wire it into the dashboard endpoint's `:render_errors` config. Cosmetic but stops the noise.
task.implemented: Added lib/harness/dashboard/error_html.ex with render/2 clauses for 500.html and 404.html (plaintext bodies) plus a fallback to Phoenix.Controller.status_message_from_template/1 for other codes. render_errors config in config/config.exs already pointed at Harness.Dashboard.ErrorHTML; the cascade now stops because the module exists. 3 unit tests cover the explicit and fallback clauses; doctor green.

task.body:
Reskin the harness dashboard with mpp.dev-inspired chrome on the existing dark
palette, and hoist every reusable component into a single
`Harness.Dashboard.Components` module so the four routes
(`/harness`, `/harness/runs/:run_id`, `/harness/chat`, `/harness/chat/:session_id`)
share one vocabulary instead of inline per-page chrome.

**Reference:** mpp.dev (Tempo × Stripe — Machine Payments Protocol site, built on
Vocs). Top horizontal navbar (Docs · Services · Blog · IETF Specs · GitHub),
terse editorial density, Geist / Geist Mono / Geist Pixel Square typography,
warm gold accent already aligned with harness's `--accent: #e6a14b`. Glyph
indicators (✔︎▸↑↓→), version-SHA-as-build-id footer.

**Three layers (full design rationale in
`~/.claude/plans/plan-updates-to-our-polymorphic-lightning.md`):**

1. **`Harness.Dashboard.Components` (NEW)** — single `use Phoenix.Component`
   module. Exports `navbar/1`, `footer/1`, `page_shell/1` (slot-based wrapper),
   `bucket_badge/1`, and the existing `message_row/1` / `tool_call/1` /
   `json_tree/1` / `json_node/1` / `value_kind/1` / `role_label/1` extracted
   **verbatim** from `lib/harness/dashboard/chat_live.ex` (lines ~612–777).
   ChatLive then `import`s them. `transcript_view/1` is added in Task 87.

2. **Tokens overhaul** in `lib/harness/dashboard/tokens.ex`. Font swap to Geist
   family (drop Fraunces + JetBrains Mono from the active surface). Tighter
   type scale. New `.navbar` / `.footer` / `.page-shell` / `.eyebrow` rules.
   Sticky navbar with `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` over `rgba(11,12,16,0.72)`.
   Bucket-badge glyph mapping via `::before` pseudo-elements. Body becomes
   colour/font reset; max-width container moves to `.page-shell main` so the
   navbar + footer can run full-bleed.

3. **Root layout wiring** — `lib/harness/dashboard/layouts/root.html.heex`
   wraps `{@inner_content}` in `<Harness.Dashboard.Components.page_shell>`.
   `lib/harness/dashboard/live.ex` `:index` drops the inline `<h1>` and renders
   bucket counts via `<.bucket_badge>`. `chat_live.ex` drops the per-page
   `<header class="chat-header">` and surfaces the per-session chip as a
   `.page-sub` line under the navbar.

**Phoenix 1.8 / LiveView 1.1 modern-style mandates** (recorded so this task
doesn't drift into 1.7 idioms):
- Components live in a module with `use Phoenix.Component`; arguments declared
  via `attr/3`, slots via `slot/3`. No bare function components without `attr`.
- HEEx only — no `~H` outside `Phoenix.Component`. No `raw/1` on
  string-interpolated structural markup. Use HEEx `:if` / `:for` special attrs
  for conditionals / iteration.
- Streams stay the rendering primitive for the message lists (Task 78's
  `stream(:messages, ...)` pattern is the precedent — Task 85 doesn't touch it,
  but the extracted `message_row/1` keeps `id` stable for stream DOM diffing).
- Layout: keep the existing `Phoenix.LiveView.Router.live_session` shape;
  the root layout is the only template that gains the `<.page_shell>` wrap.
- No `Phoenix.View` references (1.7-era) — `Phoenix.Component` everywhere.

**Geist Pixel Square sourcing.** Verify the Vercel Geist CDN URL hosts the
pixel variant before committing the `@font-face`; if not (likely — pixel
square is mpp.dev's brand variant), vendor a single `.woff2` from a
permissive Chicago Kare clone OR drop the pixel-font wordmark to Geist Sans.
Pin the actual decision in `tokens.ex` `@moduledoc` so the next session knows
which path was taken.

**Hand-built** per CLAUDE.md § "Hand-Build UI Tasks via Browser Tooling" — this
is LiveView / HEEx / CSS / DOM-feedback work, exactly the territory headless
dispatch fails on (Task 78 precedent). Run `iex -S mix` with Tidewave open and
the four routes loaded in the browser; iterate live.

task.title: Transcript parser dispatch + per-agent parsers (5 structured + 1 passthrough) with unified event vocabulary
acceptance_criteria: New module lib/harness/dashboard/transcript/parser.ex exposes `init_state/1 :: parser_state`, `append/3 :: (agent_kind, chunk, parser_state) -> {events, new_parser_state}`, and `finalize/2 :: (agent_kind, parser_state) -> {events, new_parser_state}` — pure module, no GenServer, no side effects

Dispatch table covers :claude (Parser.Claude, mirrors Harness.Chat.Claude.StreamParser shape but preserves malformed lines as :unknown), :codex (Parser.Codex parsing `--json` NDJSON envelope `item.completed`/`item.started`/`turn.*`/`thread.*`), :cursor (Parser.Cursor parsing `--output-format stream-json` NDJSON — claude-shape compatible), :pi (Parser.Pi parsing `--mode json` NDJSON — `session`/`agent_start`/`turn_start`/`message_*`/`message_update text_delta`), :grok (Parser.Grok parsing `--output-format streaming-json` NDJSON — `thought`/`text`/`end` token deltas), and :antigravity (Parser.Passthrough — every chunk becomes one :plain_text event)

Unified event vocabulary all parsers emit: {:assistant_text, %{text}}, {:assistant_tool_use, %{id, name, input}}, {:tool_result, %{tool_use_id, content}}, {:system, %{kind, data}}, {:plain_text, %{text}}, {:unknown, %{raw}}

Per-agent fixture-driven tests at test/fixtures/transcripts/{claude,codex,cursor,grok,pi}.ndjson + antigravity.txt — fixtures hand-curated from real harness runs captured under ~/.harness/results/runs; parser_test.exs asserts the emitted event sequence for each fixture
Partial-line buffering correctness: byte-at-a-time feeding of every NDJSON fixture produces the same event list as one-shot feeding; explicit split-mid-line + finalize-on-fragment cases covered
Unknown-event preservation: malformed lines emit {:unknown, %{raw: line}} (NOT a crash, NOT a silent drop) — every NDJSON fixture's last line is deliberately corrupt to prove this
Passthrough emits exactly one :plain_text event per chunk — no line splitting, no JSON parsing (antigravity only)

Module-doc on parser.ex names each agent's wire format and explains the deviation from the original task body (Pi/Grok emit structured NDJSON in real captures — passthrough is reserved for Antigravity, which truly emits plain text)
No new dependencies — all parsing is pure Elixir / Jason
Atom-table safety: no String.to_atom/1 on agent-supplied strings; unknown event types fall through to a bounded :other atom
Dispatch dispatch test asserts every entry in Harness.AgentRegistry.agents/0 has a parser clause
out_of_scope: Wiring the parser into Harness.Run gen_statem and the dashboard render path (Task 87 owns the integration)

Replacing the existing Harness.Chat.Claude.StreamParser — it stays as the authoritative claude parser for the chat session backend; the new Parser.Claude is a parallel implementation that adds malformed-line preservation
Backwards-compat shims for prior event shapes — the unified vocabulary IS the new shape; consumers cut over in Task 87
Telemetry / metrics emission from the parser (could be added in a follow-up if useful)
task.body:
Stand up per-agent transcript parsers so the run-detail page can render
**parsed turns** instead of raw stream-json (Task 87 consumes this). Pure
module, no runtime side effects — the dispatcher takes
`(agent_kind, chunk, parser_state)` and emits a list of structured events.

**Per-agent wire formats** (verified against captured agent_output records
under ~/.harness/results/runs/; also documented in
`docs/agent-cli-reference.md`):
- Claude: `claude -p --output-format stream-json` — NDJSON, one event per line, types: `system/init`, `assistant.content[*].{text,tool_use,thinking}`, `user.content[*].tool_result`, `result`, `rate_limit_event`, hook lifecycle events.
- Codex: `codex exec --json` — NDJSON with dot-notation event types (`thread.started`, `turn.started`/`completed`, `item.started`/`completed` with `item.type` ∈ `agent_message`/`command_execution`/`reasoning`). Stderr noise (plugin-load errors, panics) gets folded into the stream by `:stderr_to_stdout` — preserved as `:unknown`.
- Cursor: `cursor-agent -p --output-format stream-json` — NDJSON, structurally near-identical to Claude's shape.
- Pi: `pi -p --mode json` — NDJSON, Anthropic-shaped envelope plus pi-specific lifecycle (`session`/`agent_start`/`turn_start`/`message_*`); user-visible tokens arrive as `message_update` events with `assistantMessageEvent.type == "text_delta"` and the payload in `delta`.
- Grok: `grok -p --output-format streaming-json` — NDJSON token-delta stream, `{type: "thought"/"text"/"end", data|stopReason: ...}`. ANSI-coloured stderr noise on auth/transport errors gets folded in — preserved as `:unknown`.
- Antigravity: `agy -p` — free-form text, no JSON contract → Parser.Passthrough.

**Deviation from initial task scope:** the original body grouped Pi and Grok
with Antigravity as passthrough on the assumption all three emit free-form
text. Captured runs show Pi and Grok emit structured NDJSON; the
implementation honors what the wire actually does. Passthrough is reserved
for Antigravity. The dispatcher moduledoc and Parser.Pi/Parser.Grok
moduledocs explain the deviation.

**Unified event vocabulary** all parsers emit (consumer in Task 87 walks this
list to render chat-style turns):

```elixir
{:assistant_text,     %{text: String.t()}}
{:assistant_tool_use, %{id: String.t(), name: String.t(), input: map()}}
{:tool_result,        %{tool_use_id: String.t(), content: term()}}
{:system,             %{kind: atom(), data: map()}}    # banners, lifecycle, terminal
{:plain_text,         %{text: String.t()}}             # passthrough (antigravity)
{:unknown,            %{raw: String.t()}}              # malformed line, preserved
```

**Tests.** Fixture-driven. `test/fixtures/transcripts/{claude,codex,cursor,grok,pi}.ndjson + antigravity.txt`
hold trimmed slices of real harness-run output (sourced from
`Harness.Run.LogRecord{agent_output: ...}` records). `parser_test.exs` walks
each fixture through `Parser.append/3` + `Parser.finalize/2` and asserts the
emitted event sequence. Partial-line buffering tested by re-feeding every
fixture one byte at a time and asserting equivalence.

**Atom-table safety.** Agent processes can emit a churning set of `type` and
`subtype` strings across releases; `String.to_atom/1` on those is a DoS
vector (BEAM atom table is unbounded). Known kinds are hand-mapped to bounded
atoms; unknown kinds fall through to `:other` and the raw string survives in
`data`.

**No dependencies added.** Pure Elixir + Jason (already in the dep stack).

Independent of Task 85 — both can land in parallel. Task 87 depends on both.
task.implemented: Per-agent transcript parser dispatch (Harness.Dashboard.Transcript.Parser) + 6 parser modules: structured NDJSON for Claude/Codex/Cursor/Pi/Grok, Passthrough for Antigravity. Unified 6-tag event vocabulary, pure (no GenServer/IO), per-line buffering with finalize/2 flush, malformed lines preserved as :unknown, bounded atom mapping (no String.to_atom on agent strings). Deviation from task body: Pi+Grok emit structured NDJSON in real captures, so passthrough is reserved for Antigravity. Fixture-driven tests incl. byte-at-a-time equivalence; dispatch test guards every AgentRegistry.agents/0 entry has a clause.

task.body:
Replace the run-detail transcript pane's raw stream-json `
` dump with
a chat-style parsed view, using Task 86's Parser dispatcher to produce
structured events and Task 85's `Harness.Dashboard.Components` to render them.

**Today's flow:** `Driver.run/3` `:on_output` chunk → `Harness.Run` gen_statem
→ `Transcript.broadcast/2` → LiveView appends raw binary to a 200 KiB iodata
buffer → renders as `
{@transcript}
` at
lib/harness/dashboard/live.ex:303. The operator sees the wire format the model
emits — not the readable conversation.

**New flow:**

1. **Parser invocation moves into `Harness.Run`.** The gen_statem carries
   parser state in its data; each `:transcript_chunk` calls
   `Harness.Dashboard.Transcript.Parser.append/4` (Task 86) and broadcasts the
   resulting events. The raw-binary broadcast stays alongside for one release
   so `?raw=1` keeps working.

2. **Transcript buffer becomes `[event()]`.** `Harness.Dashboard.Transcript`
   replaces its iodata-binary buffer with an event list plus the parser-state
   per run. Cap moves from byte-count to event-count (default 500, configurable).
   `Harness.Run.transcript_events/1` is the new snapshot reader for late
   subscribers (LiveView mounts during a long run and needs the back-fill).
   Legacy `transcript/1` raw reader stays for one release.

3. **`<.transcript_view>` component** (added to `Harness.Dashboard.Components`
   from Task 85) walks the event list and renders:

   - `:assistant_text` → `<.message_row role={:assistant}>` — consecutive
     deltas in one turn collapse into a single message body (mirrors
     ChatLive's `text_delta` stream pattern).
   - `:assistant_tool_use` + matching `:tool_result` → grouped `<.tool_call>`
     with the existing collapsible `
` + structured JSON tree from
     Task 85's extracted components.
   - `:system` → `<.eyebrow>`-styled metadata line (e.g. "model:
     claude-opus-4-7 · turn 3").
   - `:plain_text` → `
` monospace card (preserves
     readability for unstructured agents — Grok / Pi / Antigravity).
   - `:unknown` → muted `
` with the raw chunk inside — nothing is
     lost, parser bugs are visible.

4. **`?raw=1` fallback.** `/harness/runs/?raw=1` renders the original
   iodata buffer as `
` for parity with today's behaviour. Useful for
   triaging a parser bug or comparing wire output.

**Phoenix 1.8 / LiveView 1.1 mandates** (same as Task 85):
- `<.transcript_view>` declared with `attr :events, :list, required: true` +
  `attr :agent, :atom, required: true`; HEEx-only template.
- HEEx `:if` / `:for` for conditionals / iteration — no
  `<%= Enum.map(...) %>` + `raw/1`.
- No `Phoenix.View` references; pure `Phoenix.Component`.

**Verification:** dispatch one run per adapter (Claude / Codex / Cursor / Grok
/ Pi) via the two-eval Tidewave pattern from
`skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md` § "Long-running dispatch from MCP eval".
Open `/harness/runs/` mid-run; cross-check `?raw=1` reverts to the
original view. Backfill: start a run, wait 30s after first output, open the
page, confirm prior events render.

**Hand-built** per the same precedent as Task 85 (CLAUDE.md § "Hand-Build UI
Tasks via Browser Tooling"). Driver+browser feedback loop is the only way
to grade event-grouping correctness, scroll behaviour, and the
parser-vs-raw visual delta.

Harness.Run gen_statem threads parser_state through every :transcript_chunk and exposes transcript_events/1 alongside the legacy transcript/1; unregistered adapters degrade gracefully to agent_kind: nil + empty events. Harness.Dashboard.Components.transcript_view/1 + eyebrow/1 walk events into render blocks (consecutive :assistant_text collapse into one .msg-body, :assistant_tool_use + matching :tool_result pair into one <.tool_call>, :system as eyebrow, :plain_text as monospace card, :unknown preserved as muted <details>). Live :show subscribes to both transcript shapes, backfills via transcript_events/1, swaps render to <.transcript_view> with ?raw=1 fallback. CSS in tokens.ex for the new variants. task.title: Flat MCP-native dispatch tool — make the chat orchestrator able to dispatch a task for any project
acceptance_criteria: A single flat MCP tool dispatches one roadmap task for a registered project end to end, taking only JSON-passable scalars (project_name string, task id-or-next string, adapter string, scrub-key boolean) and returning a run_id (or a structured error) — verified by a dispatch call that targets a non-harness registered project and lands a real run_id
The Claude OAuth secret-scrub (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY => false) is applied by default on Claude dispatches through the flat tool, without the caller having to pass an opts map

Non-delegatable executors (grok/antigravity/pi) dispatch correctly through the flat tool — the ingest-with-delegatable-agent-then-dispatch-to-real-module dance is handled internally, not pushed onto the orchestrator

The stateless MCP tool surface no longer advertises struct-arg tools the orchestrator cannot drive (supervisor__start_run, batch__run, batch__run_pinned, agent_evaluation__compare, supervisor__start_link) — confirmed by inspecting the MCP tools/list output; the Elixir/Manifest driver surface (project_eval context) is unchanged

Harness.Chat.Tools no longer crashes when a keyword-typed param is passed as a JSON object — either it decodes to a keyword list or the param is absent from the JSON surface; a regression test covers the former opts-map Keyword.get/3 crash
priv/playbooks/dispatch-single-task.md is rewritten so steps 3-4 use the flat dispatch tool; the Elixir two-step is retained only where it applies (in-process driver) and labelled as such
skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md updated for the new flat tool + the trimmed MCP tool surface (Anti-Staleness Contract requires it)
out_of_scope: A flat batch/fan-out dispatch tool over the MCP surface (multi-item) — single-task dispatch is the v1 unblock; batch can follow if the orchestrator needs it
Removing the struct-arg functions themselves — they remain the canonical Elixir/IEx driver API; only their exposure on the stateless JSON MCP tool list changes
A flat compare/AgentEvaluation tool over MCP — separate concern (and Task 81 is the operator UI for that)
task.body:
A chat orchestrator following the dispatch-single-task playbook against a non-harness project (rexex) got blocked at the ingest/dispatch step. Root cause is one architectural mismatch, not a usage error: the MCP/chat surface advertises struct-passing Elixir APIs that cannot be driven over a stateless JSON boundary.

Confirmed defects on the chat MCP surface:
1. `roadmap__ingest` takes `opts` as a keyword list; the JSON->Elixir bridge in `Harness.Chat.Tools.decode_param/2` turns a JSON object into an Elixir map, so `ingest(selector, %{})` crashes in `Keyword.get/3` ("no function clause matching"). Omitting `opts` is the only form that runs — which means `:project` / `:project_root` / the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY => false` scrub / `subscriber: nil` cannot be passed.
2. `roadmap__ingest` has no top-level `project_name` param (unlike `roadmap__list` / `roadmap__next_bundle`, which were built flat for Task 88). The orchestrator's `project_name` is silently dropped, so ingest always resolves `File.cwd!/0` = the harness project, never the target.
3. The `{:id, "<id>"}` selector has no JSON encoding that round-trips to the Elixir tuple — only `:next` parses (via the `:`-prefixed-atom path in `decode_param`).
4. Deeper: even with opts fixed, `supervisor__start_run` takes `%Item{}` + `%Project{}` structs (`kind: :exchange_data`) and `batch__dispatch` takes `[%Item{}]`. A stateless MCP orchestrator cannot hold the `%Item{}` ingest returned and pass it into start_run. So the playbook's two-step (ingest -> struct -> start_run) is structurally un-runnable over chat regardless of the opts fix. The bug reporter's suggested "fix opts decoding" is necessary but NOT sufficient.

Goal: give the chat/MCP orchestrator a single flat tool that dispatches one roadmap task for a registered project end to end, mirroring how Task 88 added flat `list`/`next_bundle` for browsing. The orchestrator should be able to say "dispatch task 25 of rexex to Claude" in one tool call and get back a run_id, with subscription-OAuth secret-scrubbing applied by default — no struct threading, no keyword-list args.

Sketch of the contract (final shape is the implementer's call): a flat dispatch tool taking string `project_name`, a `task` selector that is either a task id string or "next", a string `adapter` (claude/codex/cursor/grok/antigravity/pi), and a boolean for the Claude OAuth scrub (default true). Internally: `ProjectRegistry.lookup` -> `Roadmap.ingest(selector, project: project)` -> `Run.Supervisor.start_run(item, project, adapter_module, subscriber: nil, env: scrub)`; return `%{run_id: ...}` or a structured error. Handle the non-delegatable executors (grok/antigravity/pi) via the documented ingest-with-a-delegatable-agent-then-dispatch-to-the-real-module two-step, internally — the orchestrator should not have to know about it.

Also stop the MCP surface from advertising tools it cannot run: the struct-arg dispatch tools (`supervisor__start_run`, `batch__run`, `batch__run_pinned`, `agent_evaluation__compare`, `supervisor__start_link`) are traps when surfaced as MCP tools — either exclude them from the MCP tool list (keep them on the Elixir/Manifest surface for the IEx/tidewave driver context) or otherwise prevent the orchestrator from calling un-driveable tools. The in-process Elixir driver (SKILL.md Context A/B via project_eval) keeps the full struct API; only the stateless JSON MCP surface needs the flat tool.

Secondary, fix regardless: `Harness.Chat.Tools.decode_param/2` converting a JSON object into a bare map for a value-param whose target is a keyword list. At minimum a keyword-typed param should arrive as a keyword list, or such params should not be exposed on the JSON surface.

Then rewrite `priv/playbooks/dispatch-single-task.md`: steps 3-4 currently document the Elixir two-step (ingest returns `%Item{}`, hand it to `supervisor__start_run`) as if the chat orchestrator could run it. Rewrite around the new flat dispatch tool. Keep the Elixir-API two-step documented where it belongs (SKILL.md Context A/B / IEx), clearly labelled as the in-process driver path, not the chat path.
task.implemented: Added Harness.Dispatch — a flat MCP-native dispatch tool (dispatch__task) taking JSON scalars (project_name, task selector, adapter, scrub-key bool); internally ProjectRegistry.lookup -> Roadmap.ingest(project:) -> Run.Supervisor.start_run with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub default + the non-delegatable two-step handled internally. Trimmed struct-arg tools from the MCP tools/list (kept on Elixir/Manifest surface). Fixed Chat.Tools keyword-param JSON decode. Rewrote dispatch-single-task playbook + SKILL.md. Agent-delivered (Claude) in worktree; verification initially red on harness-side debt only (peri missing from PLT, pre-existing run_test credo nits, a type-narrowing-induced unreachable clause) — hand-integrated onto development with those 3 closeout fixes (mix.exs :peri, @dialyzer suppression keeping the defensive clause, run_test alias). 101/101 affected tests, credo clean bar 1 pre-existing baseline TODO, dialyzer 0.

task.title: Per-check working-directory offset — verify projects whose buildable root isn't the git/worktree root (rust-in-subdir, polyglot)
acceptance_criteria: A project whose buildable manifest lives in a subdir of the git repo (rexex: rust/Cargo.toml) verifies green/red on its own merits — cargo runs from the subdir, not the worktree root
Manifest-at-root projects (harness, :elixir preset) are unaffected — check cwd defaults to the worktree root, no behavior change
A single worktree can run checks from multiple subdirs (cargo in rust/, mix in an elixir subdir) — polyglot support, not one-subdir-only
The Rust (and Elixir) preset can be built with a subdir offset without hand-writing each Check
rexex is re-registered so its cargo checks run in rust/, and a rexex dispatch reaches a real verification verdict
Tests cover: subdir check cwd, default-root behavior unchanged, and a polyglot two-subdir stack
out_of_scope: Auto-detecting the manifest subdir — explicit registration/preset arg is fine for v1
Running multiple independent CheckStacks per project — one stack with per-check cwd covers the polyglot case
The Elixir half of rexex itself (not yet on disk) — this task only makes the harness side capable of checking it when it lands
task.body:
Surfaced by dogfooding: dispatching rexex task 25 (a Rust task) red'd all four cargo checks with `could not find Cargo.toml in <worktree-root>`. rexex keeps its Rust workspace in a `rust/` subdir (`rust/Cargo.toml` + `crates/`), with the roadmap and git root one level up. rexex was registered with `source: {:local, ".../rexex/rust"}` — the documented intent being "point cargo at the subdir" — but git worktrees are repo-granular: `git worktree add` checks out the WHOLE rexex repo (its `.git` is at the repo root), so the worktree root is the repo root and `Cargo.toml` lands at `rust/Cargo.toml`, not the root. `Harness.Verification.collect_check/3` runs every check with `{:cd, worktree_path}` (the worktree root, verification.ex ~line 183), so cargo never finds the manifest and the run is structurally un-greenable. The repair loop is futile — the agent is handed an unactionable "Cargo.toml missing" prompt for code that's fine.

rexex is also "Rust AND Elixir" going forward (Elixir half not yet on disk), so the fix must support a polyglot worktree: cargo checks running from `rust/`, mix checks running from some other subdir, all within one worktree rooted at the repo root (which is where the roadmap + git live and must stay).

Give checks a working-directory offset relative to the worktree root. The natural shape (final call is the implementer's): an optional relative `cwd` (default "." = worktree root) on `%Harness.Verification.Check{}`, with `collect_check` running each check from `Path.join(worktree_path, check.cwd)`. A polyglot stack is then just cargo-checks(cwd: "rust") ++ mix-checks(cwd: "<elixir-dir>"). The Rust/Elixir presets should accept the subdir so a project can build a cwd-stamped stack without hand-writing checks (e.g. `Preset.Rust.preset(cwd: "rust")`), and `%Harness.Project{}` registration should be able to express it. Don't break the common case — manifest-at-root projects (harness itself) must render byte-identical check behavior (cwd defaults to root).

Re-register rexex once the fix lands so its cargo checks run in `rust/`, and confirm a rexex dispatch can reach a real green/red verdict (the verification actually runs cargo, rather than failing on a missing manifest).
task.implemented: Multi-stack model rather than the body's suggested per-check cwd (final shape was implementer's call; the per-stack form also satisfies the 'multiple independent CheckStacks per project' line the body listed out-of-scope — chose it because it composes presets cleanly). %CheckStack{} gains workdir (default ""=repo root); %Harness.Project{} now holds check_stacks: [CheckStack.t()] (was singular check_stack). Verification.run/2 accepts :check_stacks, runs each stack's checks with {:cd, Path.join(worktree_root, workdir)}, flattens all results into one Verdict (green iff all pass), and returns {:error, {:workdir_not_found, dir}} on a misconfigured subdir (replaces the cryptic 'could not find Cargo.toml'). Post-process context (diff baseline filters) stays at repo root. Back-compat: singular preset:/check_stack:/:checks and the :check_stack run option all wrap to a one-element list with workdir "" — manifest-at-root projects (harness, :elixir) byte-identical. ProjectRegistry parses a new stacks: [[preset:/check_stack:, workdir:]] form. rexex re-registered in dev.local.exs (source=repo root, stacks: [[preset: :rust, workdir: "rust"]]). Tests: verification subdir-cwd/default-root/workdir_not_found/polyglot-flatten, registry stacks-parse + singular back-compat. Repair-prompt per-check workdir display deferred (needs workdir threaded onto Result struct, >15 LOC). Live rexex re-dispatch verdict pending operator iex restart.

task.title: Chat session persistence + index page — survive restart, list & reopen past chats
acceptance_criteria: A chat session's messages survive a BEAM restart: start a session, send turns, restart iex -S mix, reopen /harness/chat/<session_id> and the prior turns render
Harness.Chat.Supervisor.list_sessions/0 returns currently-live session ids (over Harness.Chat.Registry)
/harness/chat renders an index of existing sessions (live + persisted) with a recognizable label, last-activity, and a link to each; a 'new chat' button mints a fresh session
Persisted state is bounded (mirrors the live 200-message / per-turn truncation caps) so the store does not grow unbounded
Index and detail compose on the existing Harness.Dashboard.Components / Tokens vocabulary — no new inline styles
Tests: list_sessions/0 enumerates live sessions; persistence round-trips a session's messages through the store (save -> rehydrate)
out_of_scope: Full-text search across chats
Deleting / archiving sessions from the UI
Cross-device / multi-user session ownership or auth
Streaming a persisted (non-live) session — reopening a dead session shows its saved transcript statically; only live sessions stream
task.body:
Chat sessions are in-memory DynamicSupervisor children registered in Harness.Chat.Registry with no persistence and no list UI. Two gaps, shipped together because the index is near-useless without persistence (a BEAM restart wipes every session, which is exactly the pain that surfaced this):

1. Persistence — a chat session's message history survives a BEAM restart. On Session start/init, rehydrate from the store if the session_id has saved state; persist on each completed turn (and on terminate). A store already exists to model after: Harness.ResultStore is the file-backed LogRecord precedent (Task 19); Postgres via Harness.Repo is also available (Oban). Pick whichever fits — file-backed is the lighter match for ephemeral-ish chat transcripts. Bound what's persisted the same way the live buffer is bounded (200 messages / per-turn truncation) so the store doesn't grow unbounded.

2. Index page — a LiveView listing existing sessions (live + persisted), each showing enough to recognize it (first user message or a derived title, last-activity time, message count), clicking through to /harness/chat/<session_id>. Add Harness.Chat.Supervisor.list_sessions/0 (enumerate live via Harness.Chat.Registry) and merge with persisted-but-not-live sessions from the store. Reuse Harness.Chat.Session.snapshot/1 for live session detail. Route it at /harness/chat as the :index (the bare /harness/chat currently auto-redirects to a fresh session — move that "new chat" affordance to a button on the index). Compose on the existing Components/Tokens vocabulary (Tasks 85/87), do not introduce a new visual dialect.

This is LiveView + heex work — hand-build via browser tooling per the global rule, not headless dispatch.
task.implemented: File-backed Harness.Chat.Store (term files, mirrors ResultStore.File) persists session messages (bounded to last 200) after each turn; Session rehydrates on init. Supervisor.list_sessions/0 enumerates live sessions via Registry. /harness/chat is now the :index action listing live+persisted sessions (label/count/activity/deep-link) with a New chat button. Composes on Tokens (.chat-index/.session-list). Tests: store round-trip/list/bounding/disabled, list_sessions/0, persist-on-turn + rehydrate-on-init. Browser-verified index listing + rehydration of a dead-session deep-link through the running BEAM.

The index lists a kill control on each active/running run row
The kill control is absent for already-settled (:done/:failed) runs

After cancel, the view transitions to the settled state via the existing poll (button gone, verdict :failed)

task.body:
Add a kill/cancel control to the dashboard so an operator watching a run go bad (wrong cwd, agent thrashing, runaway repair loop) can stop it from the browser instead of dropping to project_eval. The primitive already exists: Harness.Run.cancel/1 (descripex-annotated, @spec cancel(run()) :: :ok) kills the agent and settles the run :failed, and is already guarded against :done/:failed states (calling it on a settled run is a no-op).

Wire it into Harness.Dashboard.Live (the module serving both /harness :index and /harness/runs/:run_id :show):

- A "Kill run" button on the run-detail (:show) view, shown only while the run is in-flight (a live Harness.Run.status/1 lookup succeeds — i.e. not yet a settled LogRecord). A handle_event calls Harness.Run.cancel(run_id).
- The same control inline on the index for each active/running row, so you don't have to drill in first.
- Destructive-action confirm (phx-click with a data-confirm prompt) — a misfire settles the run :failed.
- After cancel, the existing 1s :tick poll already refreshes status, so the row/detail transitions to :failed on its own; no extra broadcast needed, but verify the button disappears once settled.

Compose on the existing Components/Tokens vocabulary (dashboard-chrome bundle) — reuse a button style, don't introduce a new one. Reserve the single --accent terminal-state cue for the kill affordance if it reads well.

task.body: A dispatched run can grade green by Harness.CheckStack but be unmergeable under the project's own `mix precommit` — surfaced on Task 94 (coverage gate 80% vs measured 75.92%). task.body: Foundational for the autonomous-landing milestone. %Harness.Roadmap.Item{} currently carries only id/title/prompt/agent — the rendered agent prompt, not the structured acceptance criteria. The semantic gate (next task) and any future triage agent are blind to the task's actual contract without them. Thread the task body and acceptance_criteria through Harness.Roadmap.ingest/2 into new Item fields, sourcing them from rmap's existing JSON surface (rmap show --json / the data the delegate prompt already renders). Reuse the rmap-shelling already in lib/harness/roadmap.ex. Works for both {:id, _} and :next ingestion. This is the signal the whole milestone amplifies — two peer LLMs independently ranked acceptance-criteria visibility as the #1 ceiling on autonomous correctness.

task.title: Cross-family adversarial semantic gate on green verdicts
acceptance_criteria: green verdict with gate enabled dispatches an opposite-model-family grader
REJECT blocks settle and feeds the repair loop; APPROVE settles :done
grader dispatch failure or timeout is treated as REJECT (fail-safe)
gate is skippable by config and OFF by default unless auto-landing
out_of_scope: The merge-train itself (separate task)
Acceptance-criteria quality checks — the gate trusts the criteria as written
task.body: Once no human reads the diff, the check stack catches 'doesn't compile/lint/test' but not 'agent deleted the failing test', 'stubbed the hard case', or 'solved the adjacent problem'. Add a semantic gate: before a green verdict settles :done, dispatch a reviewer agent with (task body + acceptance_criteria + the committed diff) and require <<<VERDICT:APPROVE|REJECT>>>. REJECT routes into the existing repair loop (new reason :semantic_rejection); APPROVE settles :done. This reuses almost everything already built — the consulting state in Harness.Run, Harness.AuditReview.grade_fix/1, and the sentinel verdict extraction — only WHEN it fires changes (on green, not on repeated red). CRITICAL: the grader MUST be a different model family than the implementer (reuse AuditReview's :claude <-> :codex auto-pairing). Both peer reviewers flagged that a same-family reviewer shares the implementer's blind spots and will rubber-stamp evasions. Fail-safe: any gate dispatch failure or timeout is treated as REJECT — never silently APPROVE. Config: gate is ON when the project's landing policy would auto-land, OFF otherwise.
task.implemented: Cross-family adversarial semantic gate on green verdicts; codex delivery d687f04. Worktree-concurrency flake (run red cause) fixed by serializing git worktree add per repo (ebbb0af). Verification + precommit green.

task.title: Autonomous merge-train — serialized lander (happy path)
acceptance_criteria: an approved branch ff- or rebase-merges onto the project land target
the integrated state is re-verified before the merge is kept
on green, the rmap task advances with verified=true and shipped_in=<sha>, no manual commands
two concurrent green runs land one at a time without racing the target branch
out_of_scope: Post-merge-red auto-repair and conflict re-dispatch (resilience task)
Opening PRs or any human review gate
task.body: Close the loop: a green + gate-approved run currently leaves a harness/<id> branch that a human hand-integrates onto development (docs/dogfooding-workflow.md 'Integration order'). Replace that manual dance with a serialized autonomous lander. Single merge to the target at a time (N parallel ff-merges race). Per approved branch: git merge --ff-only onto the project's land target; if the target HEAD moved, rebase harness/<id> and RE-RUN the full verification stack on the integrated result; green => keep the merge and write the outcome back to rmap (status done --verified --delivered-by <agent> --implemented ... and shipped_in <sha>); red-post-merge or true-conflict => retain the branch + hand off to the resilience task. Direct merge to target, no PR, no human review — the verification stack is the grader (project philosophy). Build on Harness.Git.run/2 + Harness.Worktree; serialize via a GenServer or single-concurrency Oban queue. Add land-policy + target-branch fields to %Harness.Project{}. The --verified rmap flag is justified by the upstream semantic gate (a cross-family grader agreed) — exact semantic match for that field.
task.implemented: Serialized merge-train lander: ff-only/rebase land onto target_branch with post-rebase re-verification; mark_landed write-back; single-concurrency Oban landing queue. 13 tests green.

task.title: Merge-train resilience — post-merge repair, conflict re-dispatch, blocked sink
acceptance_criteria: a green-in-isolation, red-post-merge branch gets one fresh integrated-HEAD re-dispatch before being refused
a true conflict re-dispatches the loser against the winner HEAD, not a blind resolver
landing-attempt cap routes the task to blocked with a reason; rmap next skips it
no resolver/re-dispatch path can loop forever
out_of_scope: Auto-rescope triage agent for blocked tasks (future fast-follow)
Resolver-agent as the primary conflict strategy
task.body: The hard edges of autonomous landing, shaped by a two-peer LLM design consult. (1) Post-merge red: a branch green-in-isolation but red after integration is an INTEGRATION failure — the merge-train contract is 'target is always green after integration'. Handle it with a FRESH re-dispatch of the task against the integrated HEAD (NOT a session-resume with the stale diff — the in-run repair loop is the wrong tool here), re-verify, land if green. (2) True same-function conflict (rare; batch discipline mostly prevents it): re-dispatch the LOSER against the winner's HEAD (first-to-land = ground truth). A resolver agent that composes both diffs is explicitly NOT the default — both peers warned it produces plausible-but-wrong merges of two intents it can't reconcile. (3) Landing-attempt cap, distinct from the in-run repair cap: on exhaustion, flip the rmap task to blocked with a structured blocked_reason — the terminal sink ('without a sink you are lying about autonomy'). Reuse rmap's existing blocked + blocked_reason; no schema change. No path may loop unbounded.
task.implemented: Harness.Lander.Resilience: pure plan/2 routing table + effectful route/2; post_merge_red/conflict→fresh re-dispatch off integrated HEAD, push_rejected→re-land, cap(2)→blocked sink via Roadmap.mark_blocked. Worker slimmed to land|>route.

task.title: Witness notification sink (read-only, hard to become a gate)
acceptance_criteria: a configurable sink fires on land / blocked / red-post-merge with task id and outcome
no configured sink is a silent no-op
manually landing a train-tracked branch is guarded against, not just discouraged
one built-in command-exec sink ships; the hook is a behaviour for custom sinks
out_of_scope: A full notification UI in the dashboard
Per-event filtering rules (start with land/blocked/red only)
task.body: With the human as a pure witness, notifications are the primary interface — not QoL. Add a pluggable on-settle/on-land hook that fires 'landed #N / blocked #M / red-post-merge #K' with task id + outcome over a configurable sink (a built-in command/exec sink covers ntfy/desktop/Slack via the user's own command; webhook optional). Today only notify_subscriber/3 exists in Harness.Run. Design constraint from the peer consult: the channel is READ-ONLY, and it must be difficult — not merely unconventional — to manually land a branch the merge-train is tracking. If a witnessing human can casually hand-merge a tracked branch, they silently re-become a decision gate without the serialization + re-verification guarantees the train provides. Absent config is a no-op. Depends on 101: the `blocked` and `red-post-merge` events this sink fires on originate there; `land` comes from 100 (covered transitively).
task.implemented: Harness.Notification: Event struct (sakshi↔buddhi hinge — raw outcome payload) + Sink behaviour (no merge capability by type) + CommandSink (HARNESS_NOTIFY_* env exec) + dispatcher (fan-out, failure-isolated, no-op when unconfigured). Fires landed/blocked/post_merge_red from Resilience.route/2. Guard = architectural (sink type grants no merge) + observable (Oban.tracked_landing_branches/1); git-hook enforcement scoped out per notification-only depth. 962+ offline tests + 1 integration test.

task.title: dispatch__await — blocking dispatch tool for chat/MCP

Add a blocking/awaiting variant (dispatch__await) that subscribes to the run and returns the settled verdict as the tool result, so a tool-equipped LLM driving harness over MCP gets the answer in one call instead of a poll loop. Tightens the orchestration loop for the primary AI consumer (future instances driving harness). task.title: Promote docs/dogfooding-workflow.md to ~/.claude/includes/harness-workflow.md once stable
acceptance_criteria: docs/dogfooding-workflow.md (its generalizable slice) is published as ~/.claude/includes/harness-workflow.md
Any repo adopts the harness workflow by importing it the normal way: @~/.claude/includes/harness-workflow.md

out_of_scope: Any work before harness is functionally complete and docs/dogfooding-workflow.md is stable
Retiring or replacing the ~/.claude/includes/* mechanism — it stays; harness-workflow.md becomes one of the includes
task.body:
docs/dogfooding-workflow.md is the INCUBATOR for the harness workflow — where it's developed and proven while harness itself is built. Once harness is functionally complete and that doc has stabilized, PROMOTE it into the global includes as a new include: ~/.claude/includes/harness-workflow.md.

No new opt-in mechanism, no retiring the includes directory: the harness workflow graduates from in-repo incubation into the standard include set, and the whole repo portfolio picks it up through the existing import path.

This is a forward capstone, NOT current work. Gated on (a) harness functionally complete (autonomous landing loop closed) and (b) docs/dogfooding-workflow.md stable enough to generalize from. Do not start until both hold; captured here so the intent survives across instances.

Scope to define when picked up: which slice of dogfooding-workflow.md is generic enough to globalize vs what stays harness-repo-specific; how harness-workflow.md relates to the existing workflow includes (does it absorb workflow-philosophy / task-prioritization / the dogfooding rules, supersede them, or sit alongside?); where the scattered per-project memory facts (claude-does-not-commit, dogfood-batch-size, harness-human-is-sakshi) land in the promoted include; how it syncs back to the marketplace skills the way the other includes do.

Drill-down on a settled run shows its fields and replays its transcript (parsed + raw)
A live run_id is not duplicated into history (live entry wins)

Tests green: Status.from_log_record/1, StatusView history merge, drill-down fallback + tick guard
out_of_scope: Postgres consolidation of ResultStore / Chat.Store
Per-project filtering of history (LogRecord has no project field)
Adding a timestamp/project field to LogRecord (ordering stays run_id-desc)
task.body:
The dashboard's run list and drill-down read only live state (`StatusView.snapshot/0` -> `RunSupervisor.list_runs/0`, and `Harness.Run.status/1`), so after a BEAM restart the run list renders empty and `/harness/runs/:run_id` shows "Run not found" -- even though every settled run persists durably as a `%Harness.Run.LogRecord{}` under `~/.harness/results`. This is a display gap, not a persistence gap.

Merge persisted `ResultStore` history into the index (new "Run history" table, deduped against live runs, newest-first, capped) and add a settled-run drill-down that rebuilds the status snapshot and replays the transcript from the record. Reuse the existing render path via a synthetic `Status.from_log_record/1`. Keep `mix harness.status` terminal output and the topbar tallies live-only -- history is dashboard-only. No new storage layer.

Display-only; no new storage. 10 new tests; full offline suite 867 green.

task.title: ResultStore: stop re-warning on every scan for undecodable term files
acceptance_criteria: A directory with one or more undecodable .term files emits at most one aggregated log line per list_run_records scan — never one-per-file-per-scan
The aggregated skip log is downgraded from Logger.warning to Logger.debug
All undecodable/cross-typed files are left in place — none moved or deleted (no quarantine)
Valid records in the same directory are still returned

Test covers a mixed dir (valid + undecodable + cross-typed): valid records survive, a single aggregated line counts each skip class, the files remain on disk, and the old per-file warning string is gone
out_of_scope: Recovering data from genuinely-torn term files (disk-level corruption — unrecoverable)
Changing the on-disk record format or the atomic .tmp+rename write scheme

Quarantining or deleting undecodable files — rejected: the dominant failure is self-healing [:safe] atom/struct drift, so moving or deleting would hide records that re-decode once the writing build is loaded
task.body:
Harness.ResultStore.File.list_run_records/2 logs a Logger.warning for EVERY undecodable .term file on EVERY scan (collect_records/2). The dashboard, `mix harness.status`, and dispatch__verdict_detail all funnel through this one chokepoint, so a single corrupt-looking file spams the console on every history read. Observed: ~11 "corrupt" files (from the Task 97/99 BEAM crashes) spamming iex.

INVESTIGATION (2026-05-31, live node + all stored records) corrected the original premise:
- Writes are ATOMIC — write_term/2 writes a sibling .tmp then File.rename's into place (atomic on POSIX), and list_run_records reads only *.term (ignores .tmp). A BEAM-death-mid-write therefore CANNOT leave a torn *.term at the final path; it leaves a .term.tmp (ignored) plus the prior .term intact. Genuinely torn files are near-impossible by design.
- The real cause is [:safe] rejection: read_term decodes with binary_to_term(body, [:safe]), which raises when a record references an atom/struct the running node hasn't loaded yet (cross-version drift). This is transient and SELF-HEALING — the file decodes again once the writing build runs. Evidence: all 42 records in ~/.harness/results/runs decoded clean as LogRecord under the current node; the original 11 "corrupt" files healed on a later deploy.

CONSEQUENCE: the original "quarantine preferred" plan is WRONG — quarantining on first [:safe] failure moves a self-healing record out of runs/, so it silently disappears once the correct build runs. Deleting destroys readable records outright.

FIX (cheapest correct): stop the per-file spam, leave every file in place. collect_records/2 counts skips by class — {:ok, _other} = cross_typed (decoded, wrong struct); {:error, _} = undecodable under [:safe] — and emits at most one aggregated Logger.debug line per scan ("skipped N term file(s) (U undecodable under :safe ...; C cross-typed). Files left in place."). No quarantine, no delete, no unsafe binary_to_term.
task.implemented: collect_records/2 reduces to {kept, %{cross_typed, undecodable}}, leaves every file in place, and emits at most one aggregated Logger.debug line per scan (downgraded from per-file Logger.warning), split by skip class. No quarantine/delete: dominant failure is self-healing [:safe] atom drift (investigation: all 42 stored records decode clean; atomic .tmp+rename writes make torn *.term near-impossible, correcting the original premise). test/harness/result_store/file_test.exs covers mixed valid+undecodable+cross-typed (records survive, one aggregated line, files left on disk, old per-file warning gone) + healthy-only no-log; module coverage 90%. Hand-built in worktree; hooks green (compile/test/credo/dialyzer/sobelow).

task.title: Event-driven dashboard run tables (RunFeed) + per-project history filtering

Harness.Run gen_statem broadcasts a non-terminal update on each live state-enter and a single settled message on terminal enter
Both tables are Phoenix.LiveView streams patched per-row; persisted history is read from the store once at mount (and on project switch), not per tick
Sidebar metadata refreshes on a slow 5s meta tick with no disk I/O; topbar counts self-heal on that tick when a settled run's terminal-linger expires
Runs carry project_name (threaded onto Status + LogRecord); the project switcher (now a phx-change form) narrows both tables; pre-field records decode as no-project
out_of_scope: Postgres consolidation of ResultStore
Re-warning suppression for undecodable term files (tracked as Task 106)
task.body: Follow-on to Task 105. Replace the dashboard's 1s tick (which re-read and decoded the entire persisted results directory from disk every second per connected client) with an event-driven model: a fleet-wide RunFeed PubSub feed the Harness.Run gen_statem broadcasts on each lifecycle change, driving Phoenix.LiveView streams for the Active and History tables. Thread project_name onto the public Status and LogRecord structs (defensive Map.get decode for pre-field records) so the project switcher actually filters both tables — this intentionally supersedes Task 105's out_of_scope, which had deferred the LogRecord project field and history project-filtering.

task.title: Thread env scrubbing through Oban Run.Worker so dispatch__bundle honors scrub_anthropic_key
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Run.Worker threads an :env map from its Oban job args into Run.Supervisor.start_run/4
dispatch__bundle accepts scrub_anthropic_key (default true) and the scrub reaches each enqueued run's start_run :env
A Run.Worker test asserts the :env (with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrubbed) reaches start_run
out_of_scope: Changing the dispatch__task / dispatch__await / dispatch__compare scrub paths (already correct)
task.body:
dispatch__task / dispatch__await / dispatch__compare scrub ANTHROPIC_API_KEY via the :env opt to start_run (the subscription-OAuth path). dispatch__bundle dispatches through Harness.Batch.dispatch/2 -> Oban Run.Worker, whose run_opts/1 threads only [batch_id, subscriber] -- no :env. So a bundle of Claude tasks runs with the inherited ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (metered API, or a billing_error if that key's account is out of credit) instead of subscription OAuth, unlike the other dispatch tools.

Fix: thread an :env map into the Oban job args (must stay term/JSON-serializable for Postgres-persisted jobs) and apply it in Run.Worker when starting the gen_statem; then add a scrub_anthropic_key param (default true) to dispatch__bundle. Discovered while building the JSON-native dispatch surface (dispatch__bundle/compare); deferred because it changes the Oban job-args contract.
task.implemented: dispatch__bundle now honors scrub_anthropic_key end-to-end. Dispatched claude built the producer plumbing (Batch.dispatch/3 + put_env persists :env into Oban job args; dispatch.ex bundle/3 scrub_anthropic_key param) but across 2 repair rounds never wired the consumer side, so the scrub was dead-on-arrival. Hand-finished: Run.Worker.run_opts now reads args["env"] and threads env: into start_run when present (omitted when absent). Tests: env reaches start_run; omitted when absent; Batch.dispatch/3 persists/omits env in job args. 968 tests pass, dialyzer/credo/format clean on touched files.

task.title: Cron autonomy master toggle — runtime enable/disable from the dashboard, persisted
acceptance_criteria: Single-row harness_settings Ecto table (Postgres already mandated, no new dep) holds the autonomy-enabled flag; a config-file fallback is acceptable if justified
Dashboard LiveView toggle flips autonomy on/off at runtime via Application.put_env + persists, taking effect on the next cron tick WITHOUT a restart
On boot the persisted value is loaded into app env so the flag survives restart
Dashboard shows the RESOLVED autonomy state (extend RoadmapPoller.status/0), unambiguous at a glance
Every flip is auditable: info-level log (not debug) or audit row with actor + timestamp
Tests: store read/write + boot-load reconciliation; poller respects a runtime flip (enabled->disabled stops new dispatch at next tick); LiveView toggle integration
out_of_scope: Per-project flags (Task 110) and live schedule editing (Task 111)
task.body:
Autonomous roadmap polling (Harness.Cron.RoadmapPoller) is gated by a compile-time config :harness, :cron_polling, enabled: false. Starting/stopping the autonomous fleet requires a config edit + reboot. No runtime control and no incident kill-switch -- yet this flag governs unattended dispatch of code-writing agents.

perform/1 already reads enabled?() live from app env on every tick (lib/harness/cron/roadmap_poller.ex:31), so a runtime flip takes effect at the next tick with no restart. Missing: (a) a persisted store so a flip survives a BEAM restart, (b) a dashboard control, (c) an audit trail (who flipped it, when) -- today skips are Logger.debug only, so autonomy state is effectively invisible.
task.implemented: Runtime master cron-autonomy toggle. New Harness.Cron.Settings (file-backed term store at ~/.harness/cron_settings.term, mirroring Chat.Store) persists the master flag; load_into_env/0 seeds :cron_polling :enabled into app env on boot (in Application.start/2) before Oban starts. Decoupled tick-scheduling from dispatch: Harness.Oban now registers the Oban.Plugins.Cron entry + :cron queue UNCONDITIONALLY (was gated on enabled? at boot, so a runtime flip had no tick to act on); RoadmapPoller.perform/1's enabled?() gate is the live switch. Dashboard.Live gained a 'Cron autonomy' panel (master toggle + resolved RoadmapPoller.status/0 + master-on-but-nothing-enabled warning), set_master/2 write-throughs to the store + info-level audit log naming the actor. Verified: tests green; browser-confirmed toggle flips status disabled->scheduled and persists across a simulated reload.

task.title: Per-project cron autonomy flag — pause/resume autonomy per registered project
acceptance_criteria: Per-project autonomy-enabled flag lives alongside concurrency_cap on %Harness.Project{} (or settings store keyed by project name), persisted
poll_project/1 skips a project whose effective state is false; the skip is observable (info-level or status field), not a silent debug line
New projects register with the flag OFF by default
Dashboard renders per-project autonomy state AND the resolved effective state (master AND project) per row
Tests: effective-state truth table (master x project), default-off on register, poller skips a disabled project while dispatching an enabled sibling
task.body:
The master toggle (Task 109) is fleet-wide all-or-nothing. With multi-project federation (ProjectRegistry), an operator wants to pause autonomy on one flaky/sensitive project -- or onboard a newly-registered repo with autonomy OFF until its check stack proves out -- while the rest of the fleet keeps running. RoadmapPoller.perform/1 already walks Enum.each(ProjectRegistry.list(), &poll_project/1), so the hook point exists.

Settled design: additive, not a replacement. Effective autonomy = master_enabled AND project_enabled; the master toggle stays the single incident kill-switch. Default OFF on registration -- an operator opts a project in after watching it. Document the friction: enabling master alone dispatches nothing until at least one project is also enabled; the dashboard must make this obvious to avoid the "I turned it on, why is nothing happening?" trap.
task.implemented: Per-project cron-autonomy flag layered on Task 109's store. Harness.Cron.Settings holds a %{project_name => bool} map under :cron_project_autonomy (absence ⇒ OFF, so a newly-registered project is non-autonomous until opted in — no %Harness.Project{} or ProjectRegistry.register/1 change needed). RoadmapPoller.poll_project/1 gates on Settings.project_enabled?/1 and logs an info-level 'autonomy disabled, skipped' line (no longer a silent debug skip); effective autonomy = master AND project composes the perform/1 master gate with this per-project gate. Dashboard panel renders per-project rows (own flag + computed effective state) with per-project enable/disable buttons (set_project/3, persisted + audited). Verified: roadmap_poller_test truth-table (master-on + A-off + B-on ⇒ only B dispatches); browser-confirmed enabling harness flips effective on and clears the no-project-enabled warning while rexex stays off.

task.title: Cron schedule editing from the UI — boot-applied presets, optional live reconfig
acceptance_criteria: Settings store holds the schedule; cron_plugin/0 sources it (falls back to the @default_schedule 0 */2 * * * when unset)
UI exposes a preset picker (hourly / 2h / 6h / daily); invalid/free-form input cannot reach Oban
Dashboard shows current schedule + next tick (reuse RoadmapPoller.status/0 / next_tick/1)
Tests: schedule round-trips through the store; cron_plugin/0 reflects the stored value; invalid input rejected before reaching Oban
Live runtime reconfig is explicitly out of scope unless separately justified
out_of_scope: Live runtime Oban Cron teardown/re-add unless boot-applied presets prove insufficient
task.body:
The cron cadence is baked into the Oban Cron plugin's crontab once at boot (RoadmapPoller.cron_plugin/0 -> Harness.Oban supervision child). Unlike the enabled flag (read live each tick), the SCHEDULE cannot change without reconfiguring the Cron plugin.

Cheap 80% first: persist the chosen schedule; cron_plugin/0 reads it at boot. UI offers a small preset set (hourly / 2h / 6h / daily) rather than a free-form crontab box (avoids invalid-cron footguns). Changes apply on the NEXT restart -- satisfies most needs, low risk.

Expensive 20% (optional): changing cadence WITHOUT restart means tearing down and re-adding the Oban Cron plugin at runtime. Oban supports it but it is fiddly and easy to get wrong. Gate behind the preset work; only build if presets prove insufficient. Honest low B/U until then.
task.implemented: Cron schedule persisted in Harness.Cron.Settings (:cron_polling :schedule key, same store as the 109/110 switches); RoadmapPoller.schedule/0 + cron_plugin/0 source it at boot, falling back to @default_schedule. SettingsLive gained a preset picker (hourly/2h/6h/daily) over a closed schedule_presets/0 whitelist — set_schedule/2 rejects any non-preset key ({:error,:invalid_preset}), so free-form crontab cannot reach Oban. Current schedule + next tick already shown via RoadmapPoller.status/0. load_into_env/0 applies a persisted schedule only if still whitelisted (back-compat for records without :schedule). Tests: store round-trip + reload, cron_plugin/0 reflects stored value, invalid rejected, non-whitelisted ignored on reload, LiveView picker render + change. Browser-verified via tidewave. Live reconfig left out of scope as specified.

task.title: Mid-run reflex floor — progress-stall detector + unified deterministic watchdog
acceptance_criteria: progress-stall (no edit/tool-call in window) halts a run the byte-idle timer would let run
idle-timeout + Isolation porcelain guard + blocked-command interception are unified into one layer, not parallel paths
a tripped reflex routes through existing Resilience.route/2 (repair or blocked), emitting a Task-102 Event
the layer is pure deterministic (no agent dispatch) and covered by offline tests
out_of_scope: LLM/semantic judgment of the transcript (Task 113)
live mid-flight steering of the agent
task.body: Today's liveness guard is byte-idle only (Port silence -> kill). It misses the productive-spin hang documented on Task 78: the agent emits tokens (timer stays happy) while re-reading the same files with zero edits. Add a PROGRESS-stall detector (no edit / no new tool-call within a window, not just byte silence) and CONSOLIDATE the existing reflex guards -- idle-timeout, the Worktree.Isolation porcelain snapshot, and a blocked-command interceptor (rm -rf outside worktree, deps.clean, force-push, verification-stack edits) -- into ONE deterministic mid-run layer that can halt a run and route it (repair / blocked) via Resilience.route/2. REFACTOR the scattered guards into this layer; no parallel path. No LLM -- timers + pattern-match only. Demote-only: it can halt, never bless. This is the ungameable floor that also bounds the watcher-regress for the LLM layer (Task 113): something mechanical must watch the watcher.
task.implemented: Unified Harness.Run.Reflex deterministic mid-run floor: progress-stall detector (tool-call markers + worktree fingerprint dual-signal) consolidating idle/total deadlines, checkout-porcelain snapshot, and blocked-command detection; trips route via Resilience.route/2 (demote-only — redispatch-under-cap/block-at-cap + Task-102 Event). Delivered by codex (green after 2 repair cycles); review pass added cancel-wins precedence over reflex re-dispatch, narrowed the grade-edit guard so dep-adds/config aren't false-blocked, and gated per-line JSON decode; stabilized 2 pre-existing flaky tests (async result_store env isolation + verification timeout-capture budget). Squash-landed onto development.

task.title: Continuous in-run discernment — sampled cross-family Buddhi on the witness stream
acceptance_criteria: the post-green gate (Task 99) and the in-run sampler share one discernment dispatch path, not duplicated logic
in-run discernment is weight-gated + sampled; trivial runs skip it; cadence is configurable
verdict is demote-only: notify-only / halt+re-dispatch / blocked -- no path turns red into green
ambiguous/low-confidence verdicts on partial transcripts route to notify-only, never halt
grader dispatch failure or timeout never silently approves (inherits Task 99 fail-safe)
the Task-112 reflex floor can halt a hung/rogue in-run grader (watcher-regress bounded)
out_of_scope: live mid-flight prompt injection / steering (kill + re-dispatch only)
a separate acting Sakshi agent -- Sakshi never acts
re-implementing Task 99's settle-time gate -- it becomes the post-green trigger of the shared path
task.body: Task 99's semantic gate fires ONCE on the final green diff -- it sees the result, never the process. An agent taking destructive/out-of-scope actions, drifting from the plan, or spinning is invisible to it until (or unless) the diff lands. Extend the SAME machinery (AuditReview cross-family pairing, <<<VERDICT>>> sentinel, fail-safe-on-error, the Harness.Run consulting state) from one-shot post-green to a weight-gated SAMPLED check DURING the run, fed by the live witness stream (Task 102 Event hinge + transcript capture). REFACTOR Task 99's gate so the settle-time check and the in-run check share ONE discernment dispatch path -- one Buddhi, two trigger points -- not two copies. Demote-only: notify-only (Task-102 sink) / halt + re-dispatch-with-correction / blocked. Never promotes red->green; never blesses. 'Intervene' = kill + re-dispatch with the verdict fed back through the repair-loop channel -- live mid-flight steering is unsupported across the six CLIs. Gate by weight (high-D, security/bug markers, long-running) + a sample interval; skip trivial runs. This is Buddhi watching itself (continuous self-observation), NOT a new acting agent -- Sakshi (Task 102) still only witnesses. RISK: judging a PARTIAL transcript is noisy -- agents read heavily before editing (Task 78), so 'it's drifting' fires false. Mitigate: ambiguous -> notify-only, never halt; halt reserved for high-confidence rogue/destructive signals. This task partly overlaps Task 99 for the gaming/evasion class; its NON-overlapping value is process visibility (rogue actions + productive-spin) the settle gate cannot see. Score is honest-low for cost + noise + overlap, not demand-doubt.
task.implemented: Sampled in-run cross-family discernment on the witness stream: transcript chunks trigger maybe_sample_in_run_discernment (interval/weight/long-running gates), grading the partial transcript + uncommitted diff via grade_discernment(:in_run). Reject verdicts halt-and-redispatch (repairable) or fail the run; approve/unclear are notify-only (demote-only contract). Notification.Event gains :in_run_discernment. Delivered by codex (run run-1780281606207-181496be); salvaged: rebased onto development, hand-fixed feedback spec (+optional :trigger) and dropped kill_task/1 dup, then re-verified green (test/dialyzer/credo/doctor/sobelow).

Empty input returns an empty map; an agent with zero :pass runs reports cost_to_green = nil (no divide-by-zero, not 0)
Pure functions only — no ResultStore/file I/O inside the context; the record list is passed in by the caller
Tests cover: mixed-agent record set, single-agent, an all-failed agent (success_rate 0.0, cost_to_green nil), and repair-heavy vs first-try agents
@spec on every def and defp; module passes the project check stack

Per-domain slicing — depends on Task 116 tagging; this task aggregates global per-agent only
Persistence of aggregates — recomputed on read from result_store
Dashboard rendering — Task 115
task.body:
Aggregate the LogRecords ResultStore already persists into a per-agent ledger. Every field needed is captured per run today (agent, verdict, duration_ms, token_usage {input,output,cache,total}, repair_attempts, first_attempt_failed_check_count, agent_diff_size) — confirmed by code survey 2026-05-31. Pure functions over a record list; the caller supplies the record set (from ResultStore.list_run_records) so the context is testable without I/O. task.title: Capability domain taxonomy + per-run domain tagging (the lynchpin)
acceptance_criteria: A canonical domain vocabulary is defined in one place (module attribute / function) with the initial Elixir-stack domains (e.g. :otp, :genserver, :liveview, :phoenix, :ecto, :oban) and room to add :rust and other languages
Benchmark corpus items (Task 117) can declare one or more domain tags
Run records carry their domain tag(s) so Harness.AgentKPI can group by (agent, domain) — additive and back-compatible with untagged historical records
Untagged records bucket into an :untagged/global group, never dropped or crashed
Tests cover tag round-trip on a record and grouping by (agent, domain) including the :untagged bucket
out_of_scope: Auto-classifying a free-text task into a domain (ML/heuristic) — tags are declared, not inferred for now (TODO: revisit if manual tagging proves heavy)
The benchmark corpus content itself — Tasks 117/118
Routing logic that consumes the tags — Task 121
task.body:
Define the capability-domain vocabulary the KPI/routing system slices on, and thread a domain tag onto (a) benchmark corpus items and (b) run records, so both production and capability KPIs can be sliced per domain.

This is the lynchpin: without per-domain tagging, neither per-domain production KPIs nor capability routing are possible — it blocks most of the phase, so it lands early. Decide the taxonomy shape (flat atom list vs hierarchical), where tags live on a run (a LogRecord field vs derived from the task), and keep it open for non-Elixir domains. Tags are advisory metadata, not a contract — same posture as AgentRegistry availability.

task.title: Benchmark corpus structure + loader — fixed, versioned eval set separate from the live roadmap
acceptance_criteria: A benchmark corpus format is defined (proposed priv/benchmarks/*.toml, compile-time embedded like priv/playbooks) with per item: id, version, domain tags (Task 116), task spec (intent + acceptance), target check-stack reference, and expected-green ground truth
A loader reads the corpus into structs at compile time or boot, validated — a malformed item is a loud error, never a silent skip
Corpus items are addressable by id and filterable by domain
Tests cover loading a valid corpus, filtering by domain, and rejecting a malformed item loudly
out_of_scope: Corpus content / curated tasks — Task 118
Dispatching the corpus to agents — reuses Batch.AgentEvaluation, driven by the Task 122 scheduler
Scoring the results — Task 119
Mixing benchmark items into roadmap/tasks.toml — they stay separate by design (roadmap tasks get consumed; benchmarks must be stable + repeatable)
task.body:
Define and load a fixed, versioned capability-benchmark corpus that lives OUTSIDE the live roadmap. Each corpus item = a self-contained task spec (intent + acceptance criteria) + a target project / check-stack reference (the verification stack is the grader — same thesis as the rest of harness) + domain tag(s) from Task 116 + a stable id/version.

Benchmarks must be stable, repeatable, and gradeable green by a check stack — distinct from roadmap tasks, which get consumed. This task is the STRUCTURE + loader only; the curated content is Task 118.
