task.title: Initial Elixir-domain benchmark corpus content (OTP / LiveView / Oban / Ecto)
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark items spanning OTP/gen_statem, LiveView, Oban, Ecto, and plain Elixir (target ~2-3 per domain — decide final count at pickup), each carrying domain tags from Task 116
Each item is independently gradeable green by its referenced check stack — verified by running a reference solution (or the empty-then-green path) through harness
Items are sized for a single dispatch (not multi-session epics) so cross-agent comparison stays apples-to-apples
A short rationale documents what each domain's items probe, so the corpus's representativeness is auditable rather than arbitrary
out_of_scope: Rust / non-Elixir corpus — separate later tasks once the Elixir set proves the format
Corpus loader / structure — Task 117
Scoring / persistence — Task 119
task.body:
Curate the first real benchmark tasks — the high-value, hard content work. A representative set across the Elixir-stack domains, each self-contained and gradeable green by a check stack so scoring is objective (not LLM-judged).

A weak or biased corpus measures the wrong thing confidently — coverage and representativeness are the deliverable, not just count. This is where the capability benchmark earns its value or doesn't. Rust and other languages are explicitly later tasks.

task.title: Capability scoring + persistence — per-(agent,domain) score from AgentEvaluation comparisons
acceptance_criteria: A capability score is computed per (agent, domain) from corpus-run results: success_rate, cost_to_green, mean repair_attempts, plus a documented composite (success-rate-dominant, cost as tiebreaker)
Scores persist with a scored_at timestamp and the corpus version they were measured against
Raw per-run metrics are retained alongside the composite so it can be recomputed/retuned without re-dispatching
An unmeasured (agent, domain) cell is representable as 'no data' — distinct from a measured-low score
Tests cover: scoring a domain from a seeded Comparison set, the no-data cell, and recomputing the composite from retained raw metrics
out_of_scope: Re-running the comparison primitive — Batch.AgentEvaluation (one task -> N agents -> Comparison) already exists and is reused as-is
Decay / staleness logic — Task 120
Routing decisions that consume the score — Task 121
Scheduling the benchmark runs — Task 122
task.body:
Turn the per-adapter metrics Batch.AgentEvaluation already produces (verdict, repair_attempts, duration_ms, token_usage, first_attempt_failed_check_count) into a per-(agent, domain) capability SCORE, persisted with scored_at. The comparison primitive exists; this adds the missing ranking + storage: a composite per agent per domain aggregated over the benchmark-corpus runs for that domain, written to a store so routing (Task 121) and staleness (Task 120) can read it.

Define the composite honestly — success-rate-dominant, cost as tiebreaker — and retain the raw metrics alongside the score so the composite can be retuned without re-running the (expensive) benchmark.
task.implemented: Harness.CapabilityScore: composite per (agent, domain) from Batch.AgentEvaluation comparison metrics — success-rate-dominant, cost-to-green tiebreaker, raw per-run metrics retained for recompute without re-dispatch. Persisted via ResultStore save_capability_score/get_capability_score (File + Postgres backends, capability_scores table keyed agent+domain+corpus_version, scored_at). :no_data distinct from measured-low. Landed with hand-resolved conflicts vs 139/138.

task.title: Capability score staleness / decay + re-benchmark-needed signal
acceptance_criteria: A staleness check classifies each (agent, domain) score as fresh / stale given its scored_at and a configurable window (default ~30 days, mirroring rmap's scored_at decay)
A function lists stale + unmeasured (agent, domain) cells as 're-benchmark needed' candidates
Stale scores are flagged, not deleted — routing decides how to treat them
Tests cover fresh, stale, and unmeasured cells against an injected reference date (no Date.utc_today/0 inline, for determinism)
out_of_scope: Actually scheduling / running re-benchmarks — Task 122 consumes this signal
Background timers — this is a pure classification over persisted scores
Per-agent release detection — staleness is time-based, not version-diffed (TODO: revisit if agent version metadata becomes available)
task.body:
Capability scores measure a specific model snapshot; agents ship 40+ releases, so a 3-month-old score measures a different agent. Add a freshness window + decay on capability scores (mirror rmap's 30-day scored_at decay) so routing can discount or flag stale scores, and emit a 're-benchmark needed' signal per (agent, domain) cell older than the window — which the Task 122 scheduler consumes to prioritize what to re-run.

Pure read over the persisted scored_at; no background process here. Cheap but load-bearing: without it the orchestrator routes confidently on stale data.
task.implemented: Combined run (run-1780357162037-745d7291). Task 120: CapabilityScore.freshness/2 (configurable 30-day window, injectable reference_time), discounted_composite_score/2 (0.5 stale discount), rebenchmark_candidates/1,2 listing stale + unmeasured cells; stale scores flagged, never deleted. Task 121: CapabilityScore.recommend/2 explore/exploit routing (unmeasured cells = explore candidates, measured exploit best discounted score, fallback when no data); surfaced as Dispatch.recommend/2 + MCP dispatch__recommend; dispatch__task/await default adapter switched claude -> recommend so routing sits in the dispatch path; new ResultStore.list_capability_scores callback on File + Postgres; SKILL.md updated.

task.title: recommend-agent-per-domain routing surface (explore/exploit) in the dispatch path
acceptance_criteria: recommend/1 (or /2 with opts) takes a domain and returns a ranked agent recommendation with rationale (exploit best-known vs explore-this-unmeasured-cell)
Unmeasured cells are surfaced as explore candidates, distinct from measured-low agents; stale scores (Task 120) are discounted
The recommendation is reachable over the driver/MCP surface AND referenced in the dispatch / next decision path — not dashboard-only
Exploration is bounded/configurable (an explore rate, or 'recommend exploration when the cell is unmeasured/stale') so it does not always route to untested agents
Tests cover: all-measured (exploit best), an unmeasured cell (explore), a stale-best cell (discount + maybe explore), and the no-data-at-all fallback
skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md updated — recommend is a public driver surface
out_of_scope: Auto-dispatching without orchestrator confirmation — recommend returns advice; the orchestrator/consumer decides
Multi-armed-bandit tuning beyond a simple explore/exploit rule (TODO: revisit if the naive rule misroutes)
The benchmark scheduler — Task 122
task.body:
The anti-fly-dark mechanism. Expose recommend(domain) -> agent that consults persisted capability scores (Task 119) with explore/exploit: an UNMEASURED (agent, domain) cell is not a low score — it is an exploration candidate, so the orchestrator tries under-measured agents BECAUSE there is no data, not despite it; measured cells exploit the best score, discounting stale ones (Task 120).

Surface this over the driver/MCP surface AND in the dispatch / next path so the orchestrator actually consults it at the decision point instead of defaulting to Claude/self. A recommendation in a dashboard nobody queries changes nothing — it must sit in the path. This task is the whole point of the milestone: it changes orchestrator behavior, not just reporting.

task.title: Oban cron capability-benchmark scheduler — fill unmeasured/stale cells autonomously
acceptance_criteria: An Oban cron job (behind a config toggle, default off in test) periodically selects unmeasured/stale (agent, domain) cells (Task 120) and dispatches the relevant corpus items across the available agents via Batch.AgentEvaluation
Results are scored + persisted via Task 119; fresh cells are skipped (no needless re-runs)
Unavailable agents (AgentRegistry) are skipped gracefully; concurrency is capped; skipped/deferred cells are logged, never silently dropped
The schedule + which cells were (re)benchmarked is observable (log or dashboard) so a human witness can see autonomy working
Tests cover: cell selection (stale/unmeasured chosen, fresh skipped), the availability skip, and that a run persists a score
out_of_scope: The cron master on/off toggle UX — Task 109 owns runtime cron enable/disable; this registers a job that toggle governs
A new dispatch primitive — reuses Batch.AgentEvaluation
Routing consumption — Task 121
task.body:
Periodically run the benchmark corpus (Task 117) through the available agents via Batch.AgentEvaluation, persist the scores (Task 119), and prioritize the (agent, domain) cells Task 120 flags unmeasured or stale and Task 121 wants explored. Builds on the existing Oban.Plugins.Cron (Task 51) — queue-per-project + cron are already in the stack.

Respect agent availability (AgentRegistry) and cost: do not re-benchmark fresh cells, cap concurrency, and log what was skipped (no silent truncation). This closes the loop — the system keeps its trust signal current without a human kicking off benchmarks.
task.implemented: Harness.Cron.CapabilityBenchmarkScheduler: Oban cron worker (default 03:00 daily, config :cron_capability_benchmark, enabled: false default) selects unmeasured/stale cells via CapabilityScore.rebenchmark_candidates/1, prioritizes unmeasured > stale, caps cells per tick (truncations logged), skips unavailable agents via AgentRegistry, runs corpus items through Batch.AgentEvaluation.compare/4, persists via CapabilityScore.score_domain/4. Harness.Benchmark.as_roadmap_item/2 bridges corpus items to dispatchable roadmap items. Oban.ex composes RoadmapPoller + scheduler cron entries into one Cron plugin.

task.title: Decouple semantic gate from auto-land so dogfooding dispatches get green-verdict scrutiny
acceptance_criteria: Semantic gate (Task 99) can be enabled for a project whose landing_policy is :manual — a config setting selects always | auto_land_only (current default) | off, defaulting to current behaviour (on iff auto-landing)
A per-dispatch override (start_run :semantic_gate opt, surfaced on dispatch__task/await) forces the gate on for one run regardless of landing policy
Test: a manual-landing project with the gate enabled dispatches the cross-family grader on a green verdict and routes REJECT into the repair loop (mirror Task 99's test under manual policy)
Default behaviour unchanged: gate stays OFF for manual-landing projects unless explicitly enabled
out_of_scope: Acceptance-criteria quality checks — inherits Task 99's stance: the gate trusts criteria as written
Changing the grader/pairing logic or the sentinel verdict extraction (reused from AuditReview/Task 99 unchanged)
task.body:
Concrete evidence: Task 108 was dispatched through harness and settled green while objectively incomplete — the agent built the producer plumbing (Batch.put_env persists :env into Oban job args) but across two repair rounds never wired the consumer side (Run.Worker.run_opts reading args["env"] into start_run) and wrote no AC test, so the scrub was dead-on-arrival. The check stack passed it because it grades suite-green, not AC-met. Hand-finished on land.

The mechanism that would have caught this already exists: Task 99's cross-family semantic gate dispatches an opposite-family grader with (body + acceptance_criteria + committed diff) and REJECTs exactly "stubbed the hard case / solved the adjacent problem". But its trigger is hardcoded "ON when the project's landing policy would auto-land, OFF otherwise". The harness self-project is landing_policy: manual + target_branch: nil, so the gate is OFF for harness's own dogfooding dispatches — the core of its methodology runs with the one AC-aware check disabled.

Fix: decouple gate-enablement from auto-land. A project-level config (always | auto_land_only | off) plus a per-dispatch override lets a manual-landing project opt the gate on. Low difficulty — the gate machinery (consulting state in Harness.Run, AuditReview.grade_fix/1, sentinel extraction, :semantic_rejection repair route) is built by Task 99; only the WHEN-it-fires predicate changes.
task.implemented: Decoupled semantic gate from auto-land: Project.semantic_gate (:always/:off/:auto_land_only) + Run.project_semantic_gate_enabled?/1 + per-dispatch :semantic_gate override. Salvaged (rebased onto dev; flaky audit_review idle-timeout fixed via widened guard, not sleep); re-verified green post-integration (compile + 113 targeted tests).

task.title: Language-aware harness rule injection — stop shipping Elixir conventions to non-Elixir targets
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch against a Rust-language project does NOT include the :elixir section in the injected rules (system-prompt file / AGENTS.md / .cursor rules / prompt preamble, whichever channel the adapter uses).
An Elixir-language project still receives the :elixir section (no regression); unknown/unspecified language defaults to including it.
AgentRules.render/1 stays pure (no Project/Registry coupling inside it); the language-to-opts mapping happens at the call site.
Tests cover: Elixir target includes the section, non-Elixir target excludes it, default-when-unknown includes it.
No change to the verification-gates exclusion behavior.
task.body:
`canonical.md`'s `# Elixir conventions` section (`@spec` on publics, tagged-tuple errors, `TODO(Task N)`, doctest-vs-ExUnit split) is injected into EVERY agent invocation regardless of target language. `RulesInjection.{claude_flags,install_codex_rules,install_cursor_rules}` and `prepend_prompt` all call `AgentRules.render/1` with default opts, so a dispatch against a Rust-preset project (the Rust CheckStack shipped in Task 45) tells the agent to write `@spec`s.

The section-filter machinery already exists — `render(only: ..., exclude: ...)` with `@default_exclude [:verification_gates]`. What's missing is a wire from the target project's known language to the render opts. Thread the project/check-stack language (the same signal that selects the `:elixir` vs `:rust` preset) through to the rule-injection call site so non-Elixir dispatches exclude `:elixir` (and, if added, include a `:rust` section). Keep the default (Elixir, since harness dogfoods itself in Elixir) when language is unknown.

Scope: the language signal must reach the injection site. Today `Invocation` does not carry it; either add a language field to `Invocation` (populated from `%Project{}`/`%CheckStack{}` at dispatch) or pass render opts down. Prefer the minimal plumbing that keeps `AgentRules` pure.
task.implemented: Language-aware rule injection: Invocation.language threaded from Run.project_language/1 (derives from check_stack name); RulesInjection.render_opts/1 maps :rust -> exclude [:verification_gates,:elixir], else default; AgentRules stays pure. Tests cover Rust-excludes / Elixir-includes / unknown-defaults.

task.title: Capture the composed prompt+rules per run for post-hoc diagnosis
acceptance_criteria: After a run completes, the composed prompt+rules sent on each attempt is retrievable from the run's persisted result record (not only the raw transcript).
Repair attempts are captured distinctly from the initial dispatch (the resume prompt carrying failing-check output is recorded).
Capture works across rule channels (system-prompt file, ephemeral AGENTS.md / .cursor rules, prompt preamble); the recorded artifact reflects what each adapter actually sent.
Does not break the ephemeral-cleanup invariant (nothing extra committed to the target repo; capture lands in the result store, not the worktree).
Tests cover initial-dispatch capture and at least one repair-attempt capture.
task.body:
The exact bytes sent to an agent for a given run are not reconstructable after the fact. Harness-owned rules are rendered into ephemeral worktree files that `AgentRules.cleanup_injected_rules/1` deletes before delivery; the task prompt is the in-memory `Invocation.prompt` (verbatim `rmap delegate` output) and repair prompts are in-memory strings built in `run.ex`. After a run finishes, there is no record of the COMPOSED artifact — task prompt + injected rules + any repair/cross-agent feedback — that the agent actually received.

For dogfooding, that composed artifact is exactly what you want when diagnosing why an agent failed a task. Capture it at the dispatch boundary (where `attach_rules` + `build_command` have assembled the final prompt/rules for a given attempt) and persist it into the run's result record alongside the existing LogRecords under `~/.harness/results`. Include each repair attempt's prompt, not just the first dispatch.

Companion to Task 20 (per-run token capture) — same "record what happened per run" shape, observability not a landing gate. Default to always-on capture since the artifact is small relative to transcripts and the diagnostic value is highest exactly when you didn't think to enable it.
task.implemented: Captured composed prompt+rules per dispatch attempt (prompt, rule_files bytes, argv, session, rule_channel) threaded AgentAdapter.Run.composed_input -> Run.composed_inputs (tagged attempt/phase initial|repair) -> Result.composed_inputs -> LogRecord (subscriber-visible + ResultStore-persisted). Salvaged the best of 3 overnight codex attempts on design merit; fixed one brittle test + added sobelow_skip. delivered_by codex, verified via check.fast + 61 tests by claude.

task.title: Run change-set view on the run-detail page (live edited-files + settled git diff)
acceptance_criteria: Settled run (:done/:failed) drill-down shows the real unified diff read on demand from the harness/<run_id> branch (HEAD...branch, across all repair commits)
In-flight run shows the files being edited, derived from parsed transcript tool-call events (no commit exists yet)
A run whose branch was merged/cleaned up renders a graceful 'no longer available' note, not a crash (:branch_absent)
Unregistered/nil project resolves to :unknown_project without raising
Patch is capped (~80KB tail) with UTF-8-safe truncation; file list shows +adds/-dels per file
Tests: RunDiff happy path + multi-commit repair + :branch_absent + :unknown_project + nil; LiveView assigns run_diff for settled and derives live edited-files
out_of_scope: New persistence on LogRecord (diff reconstructed on demand from the live branch; no stored base_sha or copied patch)
Per-commit/per-repair-attempt granularity (one aggregate run diff)
git blame / line-level authorship
Lazy phx-click diff loading (eager load is fine on the cold path)
task.body: The run-detail page (/harness/runs/:run_id, Harness.Dashboard.Live :show) shows metadata + transcript but no view of what the agent actually changed. The change set is fully recoverable without new persistence: every run commits to a harness/<run_id> branch that teardown never deletes (Worktree.remove removes only the working dir). Split by lifecycle: live run -> surface files being edited from streaming transcript tool-call events (no commit yet); settled run -> read the real git diff on demand from the branch.
task.implemented: Added Harness.RunDiff (read-only git diff of harness/<run_id> branch via three-dot merge-base diff HEAD...branch; 80KB tail cap with UTF-8-safe truncation; reasons :branch_absent / :unknown_project / :repo_unavailable). Wired Harness.Dashboard.Live :show to load run_diff for terminal runs and derive live edited-files from transcript tool-call events; new Components.run_diff_view / edited_files_live + diff CSS tokens. 27 tests green (run_diff_test + live_test).

task.title: Configuration inspector LiveView — read-only operator view of the resolved harness config
acceptance_criteria: New LiveView at /harness/settings (router scope, :index action) renders the RESOLVED effective config — the value actually in app env after config.exs + runtime.exs env-var overrides, not the source literals.

Surfaces the full operator-relevant surface from config/config.exs: dashboard (enabled/port), :run timeouts (total/idle/lifetime/terminal_linger/max_repair_attempts), :verification (checks count + timeout), :cron_polling (enabled + schedule), :cross_agent_repair, :semantic_gate, :notification_sinks (sink module names), :result_store backend+root, :chat_store root, :project cache_root, :worktree (base_dir/retain_on_failure/sweep_on_boot), :retry_policy. Group by concern with section headers.

Each row shows the resolved value AND whether it is a compile-time default, a config.exs override, or a runtime env-var override (e.g. HARNESS_DASHBOARD_PORT) so the operator knows what reboots vs. what env-vars change it.
Secrets are masked or omitted: secret_key_base, DB password, and any sink/adapter opt that looks like a credential MUST NOT render in plaintext.
Registered projects (ProjectRegistry.list/0) render as a sub-section: name, source, roadmap_path, concurrency_cap, check-stack preset(s) + workdir per stack.
Reachable from the dashboard nav (link in the layout alongside the existing KPI / chat links).

Tests (LiveViewTest): page mounts and renders each section; a configured override (e.g. set :run max_repair_attempts) renders the overridden value, not the default; a secret key is asserted ABSENT from rendered HTML (refute html =~ secret); empty :notification_sinks renders an explicit empty-state, not a crash.
out_of_scope: Mutating config from the UI — runtime-editable settings are owned by Tasks 109 (cron master toggle), 110 (per-project autonomy), 111 (schedule). This page is read-only; it may LINK to those controls but does not duplicate them.
Editing config files on disk or writing to Harness.Settings.
Exposing secret_key_base / DB password / any secret value (mask or omit).
task.body:
harness is a long-running headless OTP node an operator drives remotely (dashboard / MCP / IEx). There is no way to SEE how the node is configured without shell access to read config/config.exs, config/runtime.exs, and config/dev.local.exs and then mentally resolving env-var overrides. The dashboard router (lib/harness/dashboard/router.ex) mounts run-feed (/harness), KPI (/harness/kpi), and chat (/harness/chat) — no settings/config view exists.

This task adds the READ-ONLY half: a Configuration inspector LiveView that surfaces the resolved effective config (the table an operator would otherwise reconstruct by hand) grouped by concern, distinguishing compile-time default vs config.exs override vs runtime env-var override, with secrets masked. It is the natural home/sibling for the runtime-mutable controls that Tasks 109/110/111 add (cron autonomy toggle, per-project flags, schedule editing) — it may link to them but does not implement mutation.

Most of harness's config is boot/compile-time and cannot be safely mutated at runtime (Endpoint, Repo, worktree base_dir, result_store backend); read-only is the honest scope for those. The genuinely-runtime-mutable subset (cron enabled/schedule) is read live from app env on each tick and is owned by the autolanding bundle (109/110/111). Keeping inspection (this task) separate from mutation (those tasks) avoids a god-page and lets the read-only view ship independently — no dependency on 109's Harness.Settings store.

UI work -> handbuild (hand-build via tidewave + browser per project policy; headless dispatch idle-times-out on LiveView with no visual reward signal).
task.implemented: Read-only config inspector card on /harness/settings: new Harness.Dashboard.ConfigInspector.resolve/0 (declarative spec, provenance heuristic env>config>default, secret redaction) + Components.config_inspector/1 component + SettingsLive assign/render + CSS. 12 concern sections + registered-projects sub-section. 17 tests green; verified live in browser after iex restart (hand-built, no separate grader).

task.title: Per-agent enable/disable from the Settings page
task.body:
Let an operator take an agent out of dispatch rotation from /harness/settings, persisted across a BEAM restart.

Mirror the cron-autonomy pattern (Tasks 109/110): a file-backed term store (Harness.Agent.Settings, ~/.harness/agent_settings.term) seeds an app-env cache (:harness, :agent_disabled, a list of disabled agent atoms, absence means enabled) on boot via load_into_env/0; setters write-through and log an info-level audit line. Gate AgentRegistry.select/2 on operator-enablement (composed with the transient available?/1 quota hint, kept distinct per that module's soft-hint design): a disabled agent is skipped, yielding :no_available_agent when no enabled+capable adapter remains, so runs, batches, and cron ticks all honour it. Surface an Agents card on the Settings LiveView with a toggle + enabled/disabled pill + not-installed hint per adapter, reusing the existing dark design-system components. Agents default ON; disabling is opt-in.
task.implemented: Harness.Agent.Settings (file-backed term store at ~/.harness/agent_settings.term, app-env cache :harness/:agent_disabled, load_into_env/0 on boot in application.ex). AgentRegistry.select/2 gated via dispatchable?/1 = enabled? AND available?, keyed by @module_to_agent (test doubles stay dispatchable). Settings LiveView Agents card: per-adapter toggle + enabled/disabled pill + not-installed hint, reusing existing components. Agents default ON; disable opt-in, persisted across restart, audited at info level. Tests: agent/settings_test.exs (8), agent_registry_test.exs operator-gate describe (3), settings_live_test.exs agent card (2). 39 touched-file tests green; browser-verified card render + toggle round-trip + live select fall-over.

task.title: Cron poller: dispatch the parallel-safe ready batch, skip handbuild
task.body:
BUG: autonomous cron polling selected work via Roadmap.ingest(:next) -> rmap next, which has no --dispatchable/negative-marker filter, so it dispatched handbuild UI tasks headless (idle-timeout, zero diff; observed task 127 -> Claude). It also enqueued only one task per tick.

FIX (harness-only, option B): add Roadmap.ready/1 (rmap ready --dispatchable --fields id,model,markers), excludes handbuild + returns full deps-done set. Poller enqueues one Run.Worker per task; Oban per-project queue caps concurrency at concurrency_cap (harness self-project set to 10). Inserts unique over {project_name,item_id} across non-terminal states. Per-task agent routing: model field (harness convention) -> cx/csr markers -> :claude; disabled/quota-unavailable agents skipped via AgentRegistry.select/2.
task.implemented: Added Harness.Roadmap.ready/1 (rmap ready --dispatchable --fields id,model,markers) — excludes handbuild, returns full deps-done set as bare-array routing rows. Rewrote RoadmapPoller.poll_project to fan the whole set out: one Run.Worker per task, unique over {project_name,item_id} across non-terminal states, per-task agent via model->cx/csr->:claude, disabled/unavailable agents skipped through select/2. Removed the single :next ingest + queue_headroom gate (Oban per-project queue limit = concurrency_cap now caps concurrency). harness self-project concurrency_cap: 10 in dev.exs. Tests: roadmap_test ready/1 block (4), roadmap_poller_test rewritten for batch (8). 33 touched-file tests green; live rmap ready verified: 5 dispatchable (3 codex/2 cursor), handbuild 127/81/111 excluded.

task.title: Route autonomous dispatch on assignee — consume rmap's formalized agent-routing field, stop overloading model
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Roadmap.ready/1 requests --fields id,assignee,markers (not id,model,markers); the roadmap__ready MCP docstring matches
RoadmapPoller.task_agent/1 routes on assignee (rmap's validated agent set); model is never consulted for routing — it is a free-text LLM pin
Tasks with assignee = "human" are skipped by autonomous dispatch (never enqueued)
Tasks with no assignee, or an assignee with no harness AgentAdapter (e.g. droid), fall back to :claude; the fallback is documented in the poller moduledoc
Harness roadmap migrated: agent-name model values (codex/cursor) moved to assignee; genuine LLM pins (e.g. claude-opus-4-7) stay in model; rmap validate green after migration
skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md ready/1 bullet reflects the assignee-based routing surface
Tests: task_agent/1 truth table (assignee present / absent / human / unknown-adapter), poller fixtures migrated off model-as-agent
out_of_scope: rmap-side changes — shipped in ../rmap task 40 (commit 21cbe65): delegate --to now defaults to assignee, rmap.md documents the three-way assignee/model/--to split
New AgentAdapters (droid stays renderable-but-not-dispatchable)
cx/csr marker semantics (remain discovery/filter tags, not routing)
task.body:
CROSS-REPO (../rmap). The harness roadmap encodes the target agent in the `model` field (values "codex"/"cursor"), but rmap.md documents `model` as a free-text LLM id, distinct from the agent environment (rmap delegate --to), with cx/csr markers as the delegation channel. The harness cron poller currently routes on `model` then cx/csr as a workaround.

rmap is ours: add a first-class per-task agent/delegate field (or formalize that model-naming-an-agent IS the route), so consumers route on one documented field instead of overloading model. Update rmap.md + the poller's task_agent/1 to use it.

UPDATE 2026-06-02: the rmap half is shipped (../rmap task 40, commit 21cbe65) — `assignee` is now THE documented agent-routing field, validated against human|claude|codex|cursor|grok|antigravity|pi|droid, and `rmap delegate <id>` defaults `--to` from it. Remaining scope is harness-side consumption only: route the poller on assignee, skip human-assigned tasks, migrate this roadmap's agent-name model values to assignee, and update the harness-driver skill doc.
task.implemented: Codex delivery (run run-1780363855046-3eb6a3a8): RoadmapPoller.task_agent/1 routes on rmap's assignee field (human skipped via :human_assigned, unknown adapter/missing -> :claude documented in moduledoc); Roadmap.ready/1 + roadmap__ready docstring request --fields id,assignee,markers; harness roadmap migrated model agent-names -> assignee (11 tasks); SKILL.md updated; task_agent/1 truth-table tests + poller fixtures migrated. Landed in 5ba6862 after fixing an unrelated pre-existing red (stale Adapters assertion from cebe648, fixed in a0636da) that caused the run's false-red verdict.

task.title: Cron poller: mark dispatched tasks in_progress to stop re-dispatch of completed-but-unlanded work
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap.mark_in_progress/2 added, mirroring mark_blocked/2 — shells `rmap status <id> in_progress` against the project's roadmap_path (opts: :root required, :rmap_bin override for tests); returns {:ok, output} | {:error, {status, output, args}}
Writeback owner is the run lifecycle (Harness.Run.Worker), NOT the poller — the moduledoc already states claiming is the run-lifecycle's concern; the poller keeps only enqueuing
On run START the worker claims the task in_progress (best-effort: a failed writeback logs but does not fail the run), so the next cron tick's `rmap ready`/`next` no longer return it

A green-but-unlanded run LEAVES the task in_progress (never reverts to pending) — under landing_policy :manual this is exactly what stops the re-dispatch loop; only an explicit land transitions it to done
A terminal-failure run (red verdict after repair exhausted, or run crash) reverts the task to pending so a later tick retries it — use pending, not blocked, for ordinary failures
Tests cover: claim-on-start, green-unlanded-stays-in_progress, terminal-failure-reverts-to-pending, and a Roadmap.mark_in_progress unit test mirroring the mark_blocked test (stub rmap binary)
task.body:
The poller never marks a dispatched task in_progress, and harness lands manually (landing_policy :manual). So once a run completes green but is NOT auto-landed, the task stays pending and the next tick re-dispatches it -> same green-but-unlanded tasks re-run every tick forever. Oban {project_name,item_id} uniqueness only dedups WHILE in-flight, not completed-then-pending.

FIX: on dispatch, transition the task to in_progress (rmap status <id> in_progress) so rmap ready/next stop returning it; on terminal failure return it to pending/blocked. Decide writeback owner (poller vs Run lifecycle). Required for unattended autonomy to converge instead of looping.
task.implemented: Roadmap.mark_in_progress/2 + mark_pending/2 (shell rmap status, :root/:rmap_bin opts, tagged-tuple return). Run.Worker claims in_progress on start (best-effort, logs on failure) and reverts to pending ONLY on terminal failure via FailureClass.classify==:terminal — green-unlanded stays in_progress (stops the re-dispatch loop under :manual landing), transient snoozes without reverting. Poller untouched. Seam-based worker tests + mark_in_progress/mark_pending unit tests. Delivered by grok, run run-1780277844276-9fec2836 (verdict pass), cherry-picked e47e5bf.

task.title: Sync harness ingest/dispatch to rmap's widened delegate --to vocabulary
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap.ingest accepts all six harness adapters (claude/codex/cursor/grok/antigravity/pi) and renders each natively — no claude-rendered two-step
ingest(agent: :droid) is rejected as {:invalid_agent, :droid}; dispatch rejects "droid" as {:unknown_adapter, "droid"}
AgentAdapter.Registry maps grok/antigravity/pi to their own render agent (not :claude); @delegatable_adapters and AgentRegistry @delegatable_agents cover all six
Stale 'non-delegatable two-step' narrative reframed to 'renderable vs executable' across CLAUDE.md, harness-driver SKILL, both priv playbooks, agent-cli-reference, dogfooding-workflow
Tests lock the inverted contract green (roadmap/agent_registry/dispatch + new AgentAdapter.Registry test)
task.body: rmap shipped a widened `delegate --to` enum (claude/codex/cursor/grok/antigravity/pi/droid), so the harness premise that grok/antigravity/pi are *non-delegatable* (render-via-:claude two-step) is now false — rmap renders native prompts for all six. Invert the contract: make the six first-class `Roadmap.ingest(agent: …)` targets dispatched directly on their own adapter, drop the two-step, and reject `droid` (renderable by rmap, but harness has no Droid adapter). Reframe every doc/playbook that described the old non-delegatable two-step. Keep the worktree-isolation axis (Antigravity `worktree_isolation: false`) distinct and unchanged.
task.implemented: Inverted the renderable-vs-executable contract: AgentAdapter.Registry @adapters now maps grok/antigravity/pi to native render agents (was :claude) and @delegatable_adapters covers all six; AgentRegistry @delegatable_agents widened to six; Roadmap @valid_agents widened to six (droid rejected, no adapter). dispatch.ex needed no logic change (delegates to registry). Reframed CLAUDE.md, harness-driver SKILL, both priv playbooks, agent-cli-reference, dogfooding-workflow, playbooks.ex. Tests inverted (roadmap/agent_registry/dispatch) + new test/harness/agent_adapter/registry_test.exs; ~190 green across touched suites.

task.title: Project dispatch queues not started at boot — enqueued runs sit 'available' forever
task.body:
OBSERVED (dev node, 2026-05-31): after the cron poller enqueued 5 Run.Worker jobs to queue "project_harness", all sat state=available indefinitely. Oban.config(Harness.Oban).queues was [:cron] only — the per-project dispatch queue was never a running queue. Manually calling Oban.start_queue(Harness.Oban, queue: :project_harness, limit: 10) immediately drained all 5 into executing.

This makes autonomous dispatch inert: a cron tick enqueues work that no producer ever runs. Harness.Oban has start_or_scale/1 + bootstrap_project_queues/0 (oban.ex) intended to register a project_<name> queue (limit = concurrency_cap) when a project registers, but for the boot-time config :projects registration it evidently did not run (ordering: projects registered before Oban up? bootstrap never invoked?).

FIX: ensure every registered project's dispatch queue (and landing queue) is started when Oban comes up — call bootstrap_project_queues/0 after Oban starts, or have ProjectRegistry.register trigger start_or_scale once Oban is running, with a boot-time reconcile for projects registered pre-Oban. Add a test asserting Oban.config.queues includes project_<name> after boot/registration.
task.implemented: ensure_project_queue/1 + queue_headroom?/1 guarded on Process.whereis(Harness.Oban), always nil since Oban registers via Oban.Registry ({:via,...}) not a global name — so every config-project queue start was silently skipped (queues stuck at [:cron], cron-enqueued Run.Worker jobs sat 'available' forever). Swapped both guards to a new oban_running?/0 helper using Oban.whereis/1. Confirmed live: bootstrap_project_queues/0 now starts project_/landing_ queues. Added :integration regression test (test/harness/oban_queue_bootstrap_test.exs) booting a real Oban + asserting check_all_queues lists the queues after register/1.

task.title: Dashboard run feed is stale: no live-update for out-of-band runs + no persistent history
task.body:
OBSERVED: ran a cron-dispatched batch overnight; the open /harness dashboard never updated to show the runs (or their completion), so the operator didn't notice any of it happened.

ROOT: the index run list is built from in-memory live runs (StatusView.snapshot — gen_statems currently in the registry). The LiveView's :meta_tick refreshes the project sidebar but not the run list, and runs started by the Oban worker (cron path) fire no PubSub event the index subscribes to, so the list doesn't refresh on run appearance. When a run settles + terminal_linger expires it leaves the registry and vanishes — and there is no persistent run-history panel. Compounding: ResultStore had ZERO records for the overnight runs (confirm whether the cron->Run.Worker terminal path actually calls ResultStore.record_run, or records land elsewhere/filtered) — so even a history view would show nothing.

FIX: (1) drive the index run list off a PubSub topic so runs started/settled out-of-band refresh live (or a short tick that re-reads snapshot); (2) add a persistent run-history panel backed by ResultStore.list_run_records (most-recent N), so settled/pruned runs remain visible; (3) confirm + fix ResultStore recording on the Oban-dispatched path. handbuild (LiveView/PubSub UI work).

## STATE CORRECTION (2026-06-02) — scope narrowed to a backend gap; UI is done

FIX(1) live PubSub-driven index run list, FIX(2) the ResultStore-backed run-history panel, and FIX(3) happy-path recording all SHIPPED in commit 8bbbc5e (RunFeed.broadcast_update on every state transition; broadcast_settled + ResultStore.record_run in Run.settle/2 at run.ex:987-996,1076-1090). Do NOT rebuild the dashboard UI — it works for runs that settle normally.

THE ONE REMAINING GAP IS BACKEND, NOT UI: when the supervised run *process crashes* it never reaches its own settle/2, so it is never recorded nor broadcast. In `Harness.Run.Worker.await_run/3` (lib/harness/run/worker.ex:109-124) the `{:DOWN, ref, :process, _pid, reason}` branch synthesizes a `%Result{state: :failed, reason: {:run_crashed, reason}}` and returns it to Oban, but bypasses ResultStore.record_run AND RunFeed.broadcast_settled — so a crashed cron/overnight run is invisible on the dashboard (matches the "ZERO records overnight" observation). Secondarily, setup_failure_disposition/2 (worker.ex:53-62) handles pre-run setup failures that also never produce a record (lower priority — there is no run to show, but consider whether a placeholder belongs).

SCOPE: route the worker's crash-path synthesized Result through the same persistence + settled-broadcast the happy path uses — reuse Harness.Run.Result -> LogRecord.from_result -> ResultStore.record_run and Harness.Dashboard.RunFeed.broadcast_settled (mirror run.ex persist_run_record/2 + settle/2). The worker lacks the full run `data` (worktree, batch_id, durations), so build the record from what await_run has (run_id, task_id, item.agent, project, adapter) — extend the synthesized Result / LogRecord builder minimally rather than faking a full run data map. Add a regression test (test/harness/run/worker_test.exs) asserting a crashed run (monitored pid dies) produces a ResultStore record AND a RunFeed settled broadcast. Marker stays handbuild only by history; this residual is headless-dispatchable backend work.
task.implemented: Crash-path recording in Run.Worker: the await_run :DOWN branch now builds a LogRecord via LogRecord.from_result and routes it through ResultStore.record_run + RunFeed.broadcast_settled (mirroring run.ex settle/2), so crashed Oban/cron runs are persisted and visible on the dashboard. Regression test in oban_dispatch_test.exs (monitored pid crash => record + settled broadcast). UI/PubSub/history half shipped earlier in 8bbbc5e; this run (run-1780355012564-c5ab5bd9, codex, verdict :pass, 0 repairs) closed the backend residual.

task.title: harness MCP tool names use '__' delimiter — rejected by grok (and strict MCP clients)
acceptance_criteria: harness MCP tool names no longer contain '__' more than once after a client namespaces them as <server>__<tool> — i.e. the group/action delimiter is not '__'
A grok dispatch (or any client treating '__' as reserved) loads the full harness MCP toolset with zero 'Skipping MCP tool' errors
The descripex api() namespace + action naming convention is updated at the source (not patched per-tool) so all 33 tools change consistently
MCP server + in-process chat dispatcher (Harness.Chat.Tools) stay the single source of truth — both surfaces rename together
task.body:
OBSERVED 2026-06-01 in a grok dispatch transcript (run-1780277844276-9fec2836): grok's MCP client emitted 33x `ERROR Skipping MCP tool: qualified name contains '__' more than once ... server=harness tool=dispatch__task qualified=harness__dispatch__task`. harness names its MCP tools `<group>__<action>` (dispatch__task, roadmap__list, result_store__load_batch). When a client namespaces a server's tool as `<server>__<tool>`, harness tools become `harness__dispatch__task` — '__' twice — and grok rejects ALL of them. Net: harness's entire MCP surface is unusable from grok (and any client reserving '__' as a namespace boundary).

Names derive from descripex api() annotations + per-module `namespace:` (namespace: "/dispatch" -> dispatch__task). Fix at the convention source so all tools change together; do NOT special-case grok. Candidate: a single delimiter that is not '__' consistent with MCP tool-name charset ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]). Keep Harness.Chat.Tools + MCP server as single source of truth so both rename in lockstep. Verify by dispatching to grok: zero skip errors + tools callable.
task.implemented: Manifest.@tool_name_delimiter "-" + tool_name_delimiter/0 as single source; transform_tool_name/1 post-processes descripex's hardcoded '__' joiner to '-' so client <server>__<tool> namespacing yields exactly one '__'. struct_arg_tool?/1 + Chat.Tools.resolve_tool! reverse-split on the delimiter. All 35 tool names + docstrings + tests updated at the convention source; MCP server + Chat.Tools stay single source. New invariant test asserts no tool name contains '__'. Delivered by grok (run run-1780279364278-38f3dc26); harness verdict was a spurious deps-missing env failure — independently verified 15/15 green with deps present, cherry-picked ef56bb0.

task.title: Grok parsed transcript shows reasoning + text only — no tool-call/tool-result blocks (parser gap)
task.body:
OBSERVED 2026-06-01 dogfooding task 135 to grok (run-1780279364278-38f3dc26): grok produced a 10-file diff (real edits) yet the run-detail PARSED transcript rendered ONLY reasoning cards — block tally showed transcript-thought >0 but tool-call=0, msg-assistant=0, eyebrow=0. So an operator watching a grok dogfood run sees it THINK but never sees it ACT (no file edits, no commands, no tool results).

ROOT: lib/harness/dashboard/transcript/parser/grok.ex maps only two shapes — {:assistant_text, ...} and {:system, kind: :thought, ...}. It emits NO :assistant_tool_use or :tool_result events, which Task 87's component (Components.transcript_view/1) renders as .tool-call blocks. Claude's parser maps these; grok's does not.

INVESTIGATE: (1) does grok's streaming-json wire format expose tool-call / tool-result events (check a real grok transcript in agent_output, and grok CLI --output-format streaming-json docs)? (2) if yes, map them to :assistant_tool_use / :tool_result in grok.ex mirroring claude.ex; (3) if grok does NOT stream structured tool calls, document that limitation in the parser moduledoc and surface SOMETHING (the raw action lines) rather than dropping them. Add grok_test.exs cases for tool-call/tool-result like the other parser tests. Browser-confirm the parsed view shows grok's actions.
task.implemented: grok.ex parser maps tool_call/tool_result wire events to :assistant_tool_use/:tool_result transcript blocks (mirroring claude.ex), so the parsed run-detail view shows grok's actions, not just reasoning. Tests added in parser_test.exs. Delivered by grok (run run-1780281607656-c514b65a); harness verdict was a spurious deps-missing env failure (2nd occurrence, filed as Task 143); independently re-verified via Harness.Verification.run against the rebased worktree — all 5 checks pass.

task.title: Postgres-backed result store — run_records/batch_results schemas + ResultStore.Postgres backend + repo_enabled config flip
acceptance_criteria: Migrations migrate up and roll back cleanly

Harness.ResultStore.Postgres passes the same contract test suite as ResultStore.File — record/list round-trip preserves every LogRecord field, including {tag, inner} reason tuples and non-UTF8 agent_output binaries
record_run/save_batch return {:error, _} and never raise when the Repo is unavailable (best-effort contract preserved)
ResultStore.configured/0 resolves to the Postgres backend when repo_enabled, the File backend when repo_enabled is false, and an explicit :result_store override always wins
mix test.json --exclude integration passes with no Postgres running — DB-backed tests are tagged :integration and use a shared Harness.DataCase
Existing ResultStore consumers (StatusView, Dashboard.Live, AgentKPI, Harness.Dispatch) need zero changes
out_of_scope: Importing pre-existing ~/.harness/results term files (Task 138)
SQL aggregation fast paths for KPIs/history (Task 139)
Chat store, settings stores, ProjectRegistry persistence (deferred phase-6 tasks)
Removing or deprecating Harness.ResultStore.File — it stays first-class for repo-less library consumers
task.body:
Postgres is a hard runtime dependency (Oban) but holds only the oban_jobs table; every settled run's LogRecord goes to file-backed term storage (~/.harness/results) that the dashboard/KPI layer must load wholesale to query anything. Move run/batch result persistence into Postgres behind the existing Harness.ResultStore behaviour. Three parts, one PR:

1. Schemas + migrations. run_records table mapping %Harness.Run.LogRecord{} (lib/harness/run/log_record.ex): run_id (string, unique index); batch_id / task_id / project_name / agent / adapter / state / verdict / agent_outcome_kind as strings; duration_ms / repair_attempts / first_attempt_failed_check_count / agent_diff_size / agent_exit_status as integers; reason / token_usage / composed_inputs / failure_cause / check_output as jsonb (reason is a {tag, inner} tuple — needs a tuple-to-map round-trip helper); agent_output as bytea (transcript tails can carry non-UTF8 bytes); timestamps(). Secondary indexes: batch_id, agent, project_name, inserted_at. batch_results table: batch_id (unique), total, max_concurrency, payload bytea via term_to_binary — the only read path is whole-struct load_batch/2, so don't normalize the embedded results list into rows.

2. Harness.ResultStore.Postgres implementing the existing 4-callback behaviour (record_run / save_batch / load_batch / list_run_records — lib/harness/result_store.ex). record_run upserts on run_id. Never raises: the best-effort contract (result_store.ex moduledoc) means store failures return {:error, _} and the run continues. list_run_records translates the documented filter keys (run_id, batch_id, agent, adapter, verdict, project_name) to a dynamic where and returns %LogRecord{} structs (not schema structs) ordered inserted_at DESC, so existing consumers need zero changes. Optional :repo opt (default Harness.Repo). Test infra: test/support/data_case.ex wrapping the Sandbox pattern proven in test/harness/oban_queue_bootstrap_test.exs; DB tests tagged :integration; extract the File-backend assertions into a shared contract test run against both backends.

3. Config flip in config/runtime.exs (where Repo config already lives): default :result_store to the Postgres backend when repo_enabled, keep the File backend when repo_enabled is false (library-mounted consumers) and in the test env. An explicit operator :result_store override always wins.

First consumer: Task 139 (KPI/dashboard SQL paths) and the phase-13 capability-bench dataset (scored, persisted, decayed) need run records queryable by agent/project/verdict — a directory of term files cannot serve that. Update skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md if it documents the result-store surface.
task.implemented: Postgres-backed result store: run_records/batch_results schemas + migration, Harness.ResultStore.Postgres (4-callback behaviour, upsert on run_id, never-raise best-effort), shared ResultStoreContract test run against File + Postgres backends, DataCase sandbox infra, runtime.exs config flip (Postgres when repo_enabled, File otherwise, explicit override wins). Delivered by grok via harness dispatch; salvaged by hand: sobelow skip placement + 3 jsonb codec roundtrip bugs (top-level lists vs :map cast, check_output string-key atomization, token_usage struct identity) — caught only by --include integration against real Postgres, which the grader never runs.

task.title: mix harness.import_results — one-shot file-store to Postgres importer
acceptance_criteria: Importing a fixture results dir into a test DB yields matching counts (N runs, M batches)
Re-running the import is idempotent — upserts, no duplicates, no errors
Corrupt/undecodable term files are skipped, counted, and logged; exit status stays 0
Tagged :integration — does not run in the offline suite
out_of_scope: Automatic on-boot import (explicit one-shot mix task only)
Deleting or modifying the source term files after import
task.body:
Optional cutover tool for Task 137: import existing file-backed run/batch records (~/.harness/results) into the Postgres result store. A Mix task modeled on lib/mix/tasks/harness.status.ex. Reads the configured file-store root, decodes runs/*.term and batches/*.term with the tolerant-read semantics ResultStore.File already uses (skip + log corrupt or atom-stale files), and upserts each into Postgres via ResultStore.Postgres. Idempotent — re-running is an upsert no-op. Prints an imported/skipped summary. Accepts --root and --repo flags.

Operators who don't need pre-cutover history skip this entirely; the Postgres store starts empty and fills from the next settled run. Unpinned from the v0_10 milestone on purpose: it's operational continuity tooling, not part of the routing-hypothesis test.
task.implemented: mix harness.import_results: one-shot file-store -> Postgres importer with --root/--repo flags, tolerant decode (corrupt/cross-typed term files skipped + counted, exit 0), idempotent upserts, imported/skipped summary. Tagged :integration. Combined run with task 139.

task.title: Dashboard/KPI SQL fast paths — aggregate in Postgres instead of loading every run record into memory
acceptance_criteria: KPILive renders identical numbers against the File and Postgres backends for the same seeded records (golden parity test)
History/list queries do not load agent_output transcript binaries (verified by test); only the single-run drill-down/transcript replay selects that column
The KPI view issues one aggregate query, not one per agent
Dashboard run-history ordering uses inserted_at, newest first, replacing the run-id string-sort recency hack
File-backend deployments (repo_enabled false) keep working through the in-memory fallback path
out_of_scope: Failure-breakdown (GROUP BY reason) and fleet token-burn (SUM) views — trivial follow-ons once the table exists, but no consumer asked yet
Visual/layout changes to KPILive or Dashboard.Live — same data shapes, same rendering
task.body:
The KPI ledger (Harness.AgentKPI.aggregate via Dashboard.KPILive), run history (StatusView.history, Dashboard.Live mount), and verdict drill-downs all call ResultStore.list_run_records with no limit and aggregate/filter in Elixir — every settled run record, including transcript binaries, is decoded into memory to compute scalar aggregates or render 200 rows. With the Postgres store (Task 137) this becomes SQL:

1. Per-agent KPI aggregation: an aggregate-by-agent store operation (optional behaviour callback with a default that falls back to AgentKPI.aggregate(list_run_records()) so the File backend stays first-class). Postgres impl: GROUP BY agent with COUNT / FILTER / AVG / percentile_cont over duration_ms, repair_attempts, token_usage, success rate. Returns the same AgentKPI.t() shape so KPILive rendering code is untouched.

2. History: list_run_records gains a :limit option and orders by inserted_at DESC — replacing the run-id string-sort recency hack in status_view.ex. List-path queries must not select the agent_output bytea column.

3. Point lookups (run_id:, batch_id: filters) ride the unique/secondary indexes from Task 137.

Consumer evidence: Tasks 114/115 (production-kpis bundle, done) shipped the in-memory KPI aggregation this pushes down into SQL; Task 134 documents the operator pain of run history as load-everything in-memory state. The capability-bench dataset (Tasks 116+) reads the same per-(agent, domain) facts.
task.implemented: ResultStore.aggregate_by_agent/1 behaviour callback: Postgres issues one GROUP BY agent aggregate query (count/filter/avg/array_agg), File falls back to AgentKPI.aggregate(list_run_records). list_run_records gains :limit + inserted_at DESC ordering, list queries omit agent_output bytea (run_id point lookups keep it). StatusView history drops the run-id string-sort hack. Golden parity test File vs Postgres. Combined run with task 138. Landing fix: run_records timestamps to usec precision (migration 20260602010000) — second-precision inserted_at made recency ordering non-deterministic.

task.title: Chat session store: behaviour seam + Postgres backend
acceptance_criteria: Existing chat store tests pass unmodified against the facade-to-file path
The Postgres backend passes the same contract (save/load round-trip, 200-message cap, list ordering by recency)
The disabled (false/nil) short-circuit is preserved
Chat.Session and Dashboard.ChatLive callers are unchanged
out_of_scope: Chat transcript full-text search — that is the consumer that would justify promoting this out of deferred
Changing the 200-message persistence cap
task.body:
Harness.Chat.Store (lib/harness/chat/store.ex) is a concrete file-backed module today (Task 93 chose file as the lighter match — a conscious decision). Convert it to a facade + behaviour mirroring the ResultStore pattern: lib/harness/chat/store/file.ex (current logic moved verbatim — atomic .tmp+rename, 200-message cap, tolerant read), lib/harness/chat/store/postgres.ex (new), and a chat_sessions table (session_id unique, messages jsonb capped at 200, timestamps). Config flip on repo_enabled, same pattern as Task 137. Keep derive_label/1 on the facade.

DEFERRED on purpose: chat data is bounded (200 messages/session) and has no cross-session query consumer today. This earns dispatch only after the run-results Postgres substrate (Task 137) has landed AND a chat-search or cross-session-analytics surface is actually wanted. Honest low score reflects that — capture, not endorsement.
task.implemented: Chat.Store converted to behaviour+facade (save/3·load/2·list/1) mirroring ResultStore; File backend (verbatim logic) + new Postgres backend + chat_sessions table; backend via :chat_store_backend (default File). Salvaged from antigravity run run-1780544645702-1a831f01 (backends built, facade unwired + Sobelow String.to_atom flag); facade + tests hand-finished by claude. verified NOT set — no independent reviewer ran (hand-built/checked: full precommit stack green).

task.title: Persist runtime ProjectRegistry registrations to Postgres
acceptance_criteria: A project registered at runtime via ProjectRegistry.register/1 survives a BEAM restart
Config-declared projects (config :harness, :projects) still win on name conflict
repo_enabled false keeps today's memory-only behavior
Per-project Oban queues are bootstrapped for restored registrations at boot
out_of_scope: Migrating config-declared projects into the table — config stays the canonical source for the static fleet
A dashboard CRUD surface for projects

task.title: Consolidate agent/cron settings term files into a Postgres key-value store
acceptance_criteria: Both settings modules read/write through one shared store seam
Boot-time load_into_env/0 behavior is unchanged (settings seeded into app env before dispatch/Oban start)

A settings UI beyond the existing dashboard toggles
task.body:
agent_settings.term and cron_settings.term (~/.harness/) are tiny boot-time key-value files read once into app env, each with its own atomic .tmp+rename plumbing. Honest assessment: files are genuinely fine here — no query need, no growth, no dashboard surface beyond the existing toggles. This task records the consolidation option (one harness_settings KV table replacing two term files and their duplicated write plumbing).

task.title: Verification bootstraps the worktree (deps seed / setup step) — stop grading on a missing-deps environment
acceptance_criteria: A fresh worktree with zero agent-side mix invocations still gets a real verdict: verification compiles and runs the check stack itself
Setup/bootstrap failure (e.g. deps.get network error) is classified as an environment error, NOT a red verdict — it never enters the repair loop as if the agent's code failed
Elixir presets (:elixir, :elixir_precommit) declare the bootstrap (mix deps.get); Rust preset documents why it needs none (cargo fetches on build)
The known-sharp-edge entry in docs/dogfooding-workflow.md is updated to reflect the fix
Test: verification against a worktree without deps/ goes green when the underlying code is green (regression for the grok-runs class)
out_of_scope: Caching/sharing deps or _build across worktrees for speed (separate optimization task)
Per-agent prompt rules telling agents to run deps.get (fix the grader, not the agents)
task.body:
OBSERVED twice: every grok dispatch fails verification spuriously because grok never runs `mix deps.get`, and a fresh git worktree has no deps/ or _build/ (gitignored). Task 135 (run-1780279364278-38f3dc26): grok delivered a correct 10-file diff, harness verdict red on missing deps, hand-verified 15/15 green and cherry-picked as ef56bb0. Task 136 (run-1780281607656-c514b65a): same — first attempt red with all checks failing on missing deps, repair attempt burned to have grok run deps.get. Codex/cursor happen to bootstrap deps themselves, masking the gap.

ROOT: Harness.Verification.run/2 has no environment-bootstrap step; the grader's correctness depends on the implementer's habits — exactly the implementer/grader coupling harness exists to remove. docs/dogfooding-workflow.md 'Known sharp edges' documents this and instructs filing it.

FIX (design choice for the implementer): either (a) a non-grading setup phase on %Harness.CheckStack{} (e.g. setup: [%Check{name: :deps, command: "mix", args: ["deps.get"]}]) run by Verification.run/2 before checks, with failure -> {:error, {:setup_failed, ...}} (environment error, distinct from a red verdict); or (b) Worktree.create/2 seeds deps/ from the source checkout. Option (a) is language-honest (each preset declares its own bootstrap) and keeps Worktree generic; prefer it unless implementation reveals otherwise. The repair loop must never see a setup failure as agent-caused.
task.implemented: Verification.run/2 now bootstraps the worktree before grading: a non-grading setup step seeds deps (mix deps.get) so fresh worktrees aren't graded on a missing-deps environment. Delivered by cursor (run run-1780282646180-4a4b4ae0), salvaged after a hot-reload crash killed the original run's persist; re-verified green via Harness.Verification.run.

task.title: Capture requested model through dispatch so codex/grok runs show a model on the dashboard
acceptance_criteria: The requested model from a task's `model` field is threaded through the dispatch path into the meta given to `LogRecord.from_result/2`.
`LogRecord.model` resolves to the reported model when `AgentModel.parse/2` returns a value, else the requested model, else nil.
A codex or grok run dispatched with a pinned model shows that model (not '—') on the index Model column and the run-detail Model row.
Unit tests cover precedence (reported > requested > nil) and the dispatch-to-record threading.
task.body:
`Harness.AgentModel.parse/2` (shipped 83c2be0) extracts the *reported* model from a transcript, but only claude and cursor self-report it — codex, grok, and antigravity emit no model field, so their runs render "—" on the index Model column and run-detail Model row.

Thread the *requested* model (the rmap task's own `model` field, already surfaced by `rmap delegate` as a `## Context` bullet) through the dispatch chain into `LogRecord.model`, used as a fallback when transcript parsing yields nil. This completes "which model ran this?" for every agent, not just the self-reporting two.

Plumbing: the task's `model` → the dispatch boundary (`Harness.Dispatch.task` / `Run.Worker` / `Run.Supervisor.start_run`) → the run meta passed to `LogRecord.from_result/2`. The reported model (ground truth from the transcript) MUST win over the requested model when both are present; requested is only the fallback. Optionally distinguish the two in the UI (e.g. an italic/"(requested)" hint) so a reader knows whether the value is observed or merely pinned.
task.implemented: Requested model threaded through dispatch (Dispatch.task -> Run.Worker -> Run.Supervisor meta -> LogRecord.from_result); reported model from transcript wins over requested; dashboard index Model column + run-detail row show requested model as fallback for codex/grok/antigravity. Delivered by cursor via harness dispatch (0 repairs), verification stack green.

task.title: Verification can't grade :integration-tagged tests — DB-backed code passes green while broken against real Postgres
acceptance_criteria: A project/check-stack can opt into running :integration-tagged tests during verification when a database is available
Worktree verification provisions the test DB it needs (create + migrate) without touching the host's dev/test DB state
A re-dispatch of a 137-class task (DB-backed contract tests) gets its integration tests actually executed by the grader
Projects that don't opt in see zero behavior change
task.body:
OBSERVED (task 137 dispatch, run-1780287087805-fddb178d): grok's ResultStore.Postgres had 3 real roundtrip bugs (top-level lists failed Ecto :map cast, check_output string keys atomized on read, token_usage struct identity lost). The check stack graded the delivery green-except-sobelow because DB-backed tests are tagged :integration and every preset runs `--exclude integration`. The bugs were only caught by hand-running `mix test.json --include integration` against the local Postgres in the worktree.

GAP: the grader structurally cannot verify the primary deliverable of any DB-backed task. Acceptance criteria like 'passes the contract suite against Postgres' are unenforceable.

FIX DIRECTION (implementer's call): a check-stack option to include integration tags when the environment supports it — e.g. preset opt `include: [:integration]` plus a worktree test-DB provisioning step (MIX_ENV=test ecto.create + ecto.migrate, mirroring the Task 143 deps bootstrap). Concurrent worktrees share one Postgres instance; the Ecto sandbox handles isolation but migrations from divergent branches need thought (per-worktree DB name, e.g. harness_test_<run_id>, dropped at finish).
task.implemented: Check.env field with {:harness, :test_database} dynamic resolution; :include / :database opts on :elixir_precommit; test-db-create/migrate setup steps under MIX_ENV=test + per-worktree HARNESS_DB_NAME. Run's verification died environmentally (worktree swept mid-deps); salvaged from run branch, merged with task 147's warm-up setup (deps+deps.compile + postgres steps), verified by hand: precommit green (1195 tests, 83.25% cover) + 5/5 Postgres integration tests.

task.title: MCP result_store-list_run_records rejects JSON-caller filters (no function clause matching)
acceptance_criteria: result_store-list_run_records accepts a JSON object of documented filter keys (run_id, batch_id, agent, adapter, verdict, project_name) and returns matching records
Unknown filter keys are ignored, not a crash
A test covers the JSON-shaped (string-keyed map) input path
task.body:
OBSERVED: calling the MCP tool result_store-list_run_records with a filters argument from a JSON caller (e.g. {"filters": {"run_id": "run-..."}}) raises 'no function clause matching'. ResultStore.list_run_records/2 expects a keyword list of filter atoms; the MCP/JSON boundary delivers a string-keyed map and nothing translates it. The Elixir-native path (tidewave, IEx) works fine.

FIX: translate the JSON map to the documented filter keyword list at the Chat.Tools/MCP boundary (string keys -> known filter atoms, unknown keys ignored for forward compat — same contract as ResultStore.Postgres.apply_filters), with a test exercising the MCP-shaped input.
task.implemented: Per-key tolerant atomization in Chat.Tools.decode_param for kwlist params from JSON: known keys atomized via String.to_existing_atom, unknown keys dropped (forward compat, same contract as ResultStore.Postgres.apply_filters). Test covers documented keys, mixed known+unknown, and empty filters. Delivered by grok via harness dispatch (run run-1780302552463-36e17abd); run graded red on a pre-existing development bug (Task 148), salvaged by hand after full-suite + coverage grade went green.

task.title: Warm worktree at provision time — run check-stack setup (deps.get + deps.compile) before agent dispatch
acceptance_criteria: Verification.prepare/2 runs stack setup commands in each stack's workdir and returns :ok / {:error, {:setup_failed, _}} / {:error, {:worktree_not_found, _}} / {:error, {:workdir_not_found, _}}
Run gen_statem provisions the worktree (prepare/2) between worktree creation and agent spawn; agent only spawns into a warmed worktree
A provision failure settles the run :failed with an environment-error reason, never a red verdict, and never spawns the agent
Elixir preset/0 and precommit/1 declare setup [deps.get, deps.compile]
Existing run lifecycle tests still pass (raw :checks runs provision as a no-op)
task.body:
OBSERVED: grok runs failing in fresh worktrees. Headless reproduction (grok 0.2.14, exact harness Task-137 prompt, fresh worktree, run from a shell) showed grok handles `mix deps.get` fine and completes the task — but inside harness the worktree is carved with no deps/ and no _build/, so the agent's first mix command silently fetches + compiles ~60 deps for multiple minutes; the Driver's idle/progress reflex (5 min default) kills runs during that silent cold build. The check-stack setup (`mix deps.get`) only ran at verification time, after the agent finished.

FIX: provision the worktree before the agent spawns. (1) Harness.Verification.prepare/2 — runs every resolved stack's setup commands (no grading checks) against the worktree, same opts/error vocabulary as run/2. (2) Harness.Run :dispatched state runs prepare/2 in a task after Worktree.activate + Isolation.validate, transitioning to :running only when provisioning succeeds; a setup failure is an environment error ({:worktree_failed, {:setup_failed, _}}), worktree retained. (3) Elixir presets gain a second setup step `mix deps.compile` so the expensive dep compile happens at provision time (no idle killer) and is a fast no-op at verification time.
task.implemented: Verification.prepare/2 (provision pass: runs stack setup only, same error vocabulary as run/2); Run :dispatched state now provisions the worktree after activate+isolation and only then transitions to :running — provision failure settles {:worktree_failed, {:setup_failed, _}} without spawning the agent; Elixir preset/precommit setup is now [deps.get, deps.compile]; ProjectFixture default stack switched to a neutral no-setup pass-stack; FakeAdapter gained :snapshot_worktree fixture; SKILL.md documents provisioning + the new failure reason. 153 tests green across the 7 affected files.

task.title: StatusView.classify/1 missing :consulting — concurrent suite crashes poison every dispatched run's verification
acceptance_criteria: StatusView.classify/1 has a clause covering :consulting (both the repairing and in_flight guard lists)
A test covers classify/1 for a :consulting-state Status (with and without repair_attempts > 0)
Full suite (mix test.json) is green on development — the dashboard/StatusView/harness.status tests no longer fail under concurrency
task.body:
OBSERVED (run run-1780302552463-36e17abd, grok, Task 146): the run's actual task work was clean and on-scope, but verification graded red on test failures in files the agent never touched — Harness.Dashboard.LiveMountTest, Harness.StatusViewTest, Mix.Tasks.Harness.StatusTest all crash with 'no function clause matching in Harness.StatusView.classify/1'. Root cause: the semantic-gate work added a :consulting state to Harness.Run (lib/harness/run.ex state typespec + consulting/3 handler) but never added :consulting to StatusView.classify/1's guard lists. Any concurrent test whose run sits in :consulting while another test calls StatusView.snapshot() crashes the snapshot. The StatusView tests pass 10/10 in isolation — this only fires under full-suite concurrency, so every dispatched run on current development gets graded red regardless of agent quality, breaking the dogfooding loop.

FIX: add :consulting to both classify/1 guard lists (repairing + in_flight). The grok run already wrote exactly this fix during its repair attempts — salvageable from worktree commits ed5d11c + b935293 in /Users/efries/_DATA/worktrees/.harness/harness/run-1780302552463-36e17abd (branch still exists). Add a classify/1 test for :consulting so the gap can't silently reopen.
task.implemented: Added :consulting to both StatusView.classify/1 guard lists (repairing + in_flight). Fix authored by grok during run run-1780302552463-36e17abd repair attempts (the run that exposed the gap), salvaged by hand. Full offline suite 1157/1157 green + coverage 82.88% in the run worktree before landing.

task.title: Parameterize the :rust preset (target_dir/release/timeout/env) for durable rexex config — env field itself shipped in 145
acceptance_criteria: :rust preset accepts `{:rust, opts}` via Preset.fetch(:rust, opts) + Preset.Rust.preset/1: :target_dir (adds --target-dir to clippy/test/build, omitted on fmt), :release (default keeps `cargo build --release`; false => plain `cargo build`), :timeout_per_check, and :env (a %{String => Check.env_value} stamped onto the stack's checks, reusing the Check.env field shipped in task 145); bare `:rust` is unchanged (back-compat test)

rexex's config/dev.local.exs expresses its tuned Rust stack struct-free and DURABLY via `preset: {:rust, target_dir: ..., release: false, timeout_per_check: 1_800_000, env: %{"DATABASE_URL" => "postgres://localhost/rexex_test"}}`; the node boots cleanly and a restart no longer reverts rexex to the stock preset
A test proves the :rust preset's :env opt lands on the test check and reaches the spawned cargo command (builds on task 145's Check.env Port threading)
task.body:
UPDATE 2026-06-01 — task 145 landed concurrently (edd81f6): FIX item (1) below SHIPPED. `Harness.Verification.Check` now carries an `env` field (`env_value :: String.t() | false | {:harness, :test_database}`), threaded into each check's Port via `port_options`/`maybe_put_env` (binary=set, false=scrub, `{:harness, :test_database}`=resolved from run_env), proven by 145's Postgres integration tests. The env MECHANISM exists at the per-check level — sufficient; a stack-level `env` is NOT needed. This task is RESCOPED to FIX items (2)+(3): parameterize the `:rust` preset (incl. an `:env` opt that stamps onto its checks, reusing Check.env) so rexex's tuned stack — shared target-dir + no `--release` + DATABASE_URL — is expressible DURABLY in config via `preset: {:rust, opts}` (the `{name, opts}` config path already routes through ProjectRegistry.resolve_stack to Preset.fetch/2, so NO registry change is needed). Scores lowered: the load-bearing env field + Verification threading are done.

--- original intent at filing (2026-06-01), retained verbatim ---

OBSERVED: rexex (a registered Rust project) cannot be correctly graded by harness as-is. Two gaps surfaced while making it dispatch-ready:

1. Its `cargo test` suite (rust/crates/indexer-core/tests/db.rs) REQUIRES `DATABASE_URL` + a Postgres server — it uses `#[sqlx::test]` ephemeral per-test DBs and even ships a canary test (`database_url_must_be_set`) with setup instructions. In a fresh isolated worktree there is no DATABASE_URL, so the `test` check is RED on every dispatched run regardless of the agent's work (14/14 db tests fail with `DATABASE_URL must be set: EnvVar(NotPresent)`).

2. The stock `:rust` preset recompiles the heavy `reth` git-dep per worktree (no shared target dir) and runs a redundant `cargo build --release` (a second full compile on top of `cargo test`'s debug build).

Neither tuning is expressible declaratively today: Harness.CheckStack / Harness.Verification.Check have NO `env` field, and a project config entry cannot carry a `%Harness.CheckStack{}` struct literal — config is evaluated before harness modules are compiled/loaded, so a struct literal in dev.local.exs breaks BOOT (confirmed: `Harness.Verification.Check.__struct__/1 is undefined` at config-eval). The only working path right now is a node-global `System.put_env("DATABASE_URL", ...)` hack plus a tuned struct built at runtime via `ProjectRegistry.register/1` — both lost on the next BEAM restart.

FIX:
(1) Add a declarative `env` field to Harness.CheckStack (a `%{String => String}` map applied to EVERY check in the stack) and thread it through Harness.Verification (run + prepare) into the `System.cmd` `:env` option. This is the load-bearing part: DATABASE_URL MUST be an environment variable — cargo/sqlx read it from the environment, it cannot be passed as a flag.
(2) Parameterize the `:rust` preset: `Preset.Rust.preset/1` + `Preset.fetch(:rust, opts)` accepting `:target_dir` (threads `--target-dir DIR` into clippy/test/build args, omitted on fmt which does not compile), `:release` (bool; default preserves the stock `cargo build --release`, `false` => plain `cargo build`), and `:timeout_per_check`. Mirror the existing `{:elixir_precommit, opts}` precedent in Preset.fetch/2.
(3) Let a project config entry carry `env:` (and `preset: {:rust, opts}`) in ProjectRegistry.resolve_stack so dev.local.exs expresses rexex's stack struct-free and DURABLY, e.g.:
    stacks: [[preset: {:rust, target_dir: "/Users/efries/.cache/harness/cargo-target/rexex", release: false, timeout_per_check: 1_800_000}, workdir: "rust", env: %{"DATABASE_URL" => "postgres://localhost/rexex_test"}]]
Then rexex's tuned registration survives a restart instead of relying on the runtime register hack.

CONTEXT: empirically (this machine) the cold reth compile is ~1 min/check, not the tens-of-minutes initially feared, so `:target_dir`/`:timeout_per_check` are hygiene/headroom; the `env` field (item 1) is the actual correctness blocker for grading rexex. Backend-only (Verification / CheckStack / preset / registry) — headless-dispatchable, no UI.
task.implemented: Preset.fetch(:rust, opts) + Preset.Rust.preset/1 with :target_dir (threads --target-dir into clippy/test/build, omitted on fmt), :release (false => plain cargo build), :timeout_per_check, and :env (stamped onto all checks via Check.env from task 145). Bare :rust unchanged. dev.local.exs.example documents the durable rexex registration. Landed minus an out-of-scope StatusView catch-all (superseded by ff625de's guard).

task.title: Run recovery — hold/steer/resume gen_statem API (operator-mediated mid-run recovery)
acceptance_criteria: hold/1 from :running parks in :held at the next settle boundary (graceful); hold(run, interrupt: true) kills the agent and parks immediately
while :held the lifetime timer is suspended and the Task-112 reflex watchdog does not fire; resume/1 re-arms the lifetime timer
steer/2 stashes operator text; resume/1 re-enters :running and build_invocation/1 emits a session: :resume Invocation carrying the operator prompt into the same worktree
max_hold_timeout elapsing settles :failed with reason :hold_expired; cancel/1 from :held tears the worktree down as usual
steer/2 on a session_resume: false adapter returns {:error, :resume_unsupported}
Run.Status exposes held? + hold reason; offline gen_statem tests cover every branch via the test-double adapter
out_of_scope: Live mid-flight stdin steering of the running agent (EOF-spawn constraint; deferred from Task 112)
Dashboard Hold/Steer/Resume UI controls + worktree-path surface (Solution 2 — separate hand-built UI task)
Multi-operator concurrent co-drive of one worktree
task.body:
Backend half of the run-recovery design — full spec in docs/run-recovery-design.md (authored this session; this task IS that doc's Solution 1). Solution 2 (dashboard Hold/Steer/Resume controls) is a separate hand-built UI follow-on and depends on this API.

PROBLEM: an operator watching a run struggle (wandering, stuck mid-repair, about to exhaust attempts) has only cancel/1 today — kill + settle :failed (run.ex:883-892). No "freeze for a human, then continue" path. Re-dispatching from scratch throws away the worktree's partial work AND the agent's conversation.

CONSTRAINT (do not fight it): the spawn feeds stdin /dev/null EOF (agent_adapter.ex:79,363-371), so there is NO live mid-flight stdin steering — exactly what Task 112 deferred. Operator input lands at a transition BOUNDARY, riding the existing repair-resume path: :running re-enter -> build_invocation/1 -> session: :resume in the same cwd-keyed worktree (run.ex:477-492,664-672,1169-1175). Claude --continue resumes by cwd; grok session log is cwd-keyed too.

BUILD:
1. New :held gen_statem state. Lifetime timer SUSPENDED while held ({{:timeout,:lifetime},:infinity,:lifetime}; re-arm on resume — run.ex:415,867); Task-112 Reflex/progress-stall watchdog does not run (no live agent). Worktree retained (held is not a settle). A max_hold_timeout safeguard (config under :run, default 30 min, :infinity disables) arms a {:state_timeout,:held_expired} so a forgotten hold can't leak a worktree — expiry settles :failed reason :hold_expired.
2. hold/1 + hold/2: graceful by default (set hold_requested; park at next settle boundary, run.ex:536-545); interrupt: true kills the agent now (mirror do_cancel terminate_agent/1) and parks immediately. No-op from :held; {:error,:terminal} from :done/:failed.
