3. steer/2 (run, text): stash data.operator_feedback + repair_prompt_kind: :operator_steer. Callable while :held or :running (queues to boundary). Append-accumulate multiple notes.
4. resume/1: from :held -> {:next_state,:running} (re-enter spawns fresh agent via build_invocation, re-arm lifetime). {:error,:not_held} otherwise.
5. New build_invocation/1 clause for :operator_steer -> operator_steer_prompt/1 wrapping the operator note (optionally folding the last verdict's failing checks), session: :resume. Clear operator_feedback + reset repair_prompt_kind on green/settle like the existing repair clauses (run.ex:647).
6. Adapter capability degradation: resume gated by capabilities.session_resume (claude.ex:52, agent_adapter.ex:433). For session_resume:false adapters (antigravity) steer returns {:error,:resume_unsupported} (explicit over silently lossy — operator falls back to co-editing the worktree + fresh re-dispatch).
7. Surface held?/hold reason in Run.Status so status/1 and the dashboard reflect it.

Follow the descripex api(...) + :gen_statem.call pattern used by cancel/1.
task.implemented: Run recovery API (run-1780357158951-028c67a8, 2 repair attempts). New :held gen_statem state: hold/1 graceful (parks at next settle boundary) + hold(run, interrupt: true) (kills agent, parks now); lifetime timer suspended while held, re-armed on resume/1; steer/2 stashes operator feedback (append-accumulating) and rides the existing repair-resume path as repair_prompt_kind :operator_steer with session: :resume into the same worktree; max_hold_timeout safeguard (default 30 min) settles :failed reason :hold_expired; steer on session_resume: false adapters returns {:error, :resume_unsupported}. Run.Status gains held?/hold_reason; StatusView classifies :held as in-flight. Offline gen_statem tests via FakeAdapter :operator_steer mode.

task.title: Agent evaluation corpus — stand up the Elixir corpus repo + prove Mode-B hidden-grader isolation
acceptance_criteria: A new per-language corpus repo (~/code/agent-corpus-elixir) exists as a real Elixir project (mix.exs, lib skeletons) with roadmap/tasks.toml as the benchmark, registered as a %Harness.Project{} (landing_policy :manual — corpus runs are scored, never merged)

Grader-isolation Mode B is PROVEN on one unfamiliar-library task (zen_websocket or mpp): the agent's worktree never contains the grading test, the grader is injected/applied only at verification time (realization (a) — confirm whether CheckStack.setup already supports post-agent/pre-check injection or add the minimal feature), and the agent is graded on a hidden behavioral spec
One Mode-A visible-spec task also passes end-to-end (in-repo tests the agent makes pass) to exercise both grading modes

Running the two tasks via Harness.Batch.AgentEvaluation.compare/4 across >=2 enabled adapters populates Harness.CapabilityScore per (agent, domain, corpus_version) and renders in Harness.Dashboard.CompareLive
corpus_version is recorded (git SHA of the corpus repo or a documented bumped string) so scores are version-comparable; tasks are append-mostly
out_of_scope: Authoring the full v1 set of 6-10 corpus tasks — this task proves the grading pattern on 2 tasks first; the rest is a follow-on once the Mode-B injection mechanism is settled
The Rust corpus repo (~/code/agent-corpus-rust) — a later clone of the proven Elixir pattern
Anti-contamination hardening beyond keeping Mode-B graders out of the agent worktree (e.g. private answer-key repo) — decide during this task, harden later
task.body:
Design + rationale: ~/_DATA/concepts/agent-corpus/README.md (canonical). This task is the v1 bootstrap that proves the grading pattern; do NOT author the full corpus here. Spans harness + a new ~/code/agent-corpus-elixir repo.

WHY: harness already shipped the machinery that consumes an agent-evaluation corpus but has no corpus to feed it — CapabilityDomain (:otp/:genserver/:liveview/:phoenix/:ecto/:oban/:rust/:elixir), CapabilityScore + ResultStore.get_capability_score/4 keyed by (agent, domain, corpus_version), AgentEvaluation.compare/4, and CompareLive (Task 81). A per-language corpus repo registered as a %Harness.Project{} is the missing input. Per-language repos (not a monorepo) so each carries one coherent toolchain check_stack.

THE LOAD-BEARING DECISION — grader isolation (two modes, see concept doc):
- Mode A (visible-spec / TDD): grading tests in the repo, agent makes them pass. Mainstream Elixir/OTP/LiveView surfaces. Measures implementation skill.
- Mode B (hidden-grader / unfamiliar library): the whole point of a zen_websocket/mpp task is the agent has provably never seen the API — does it read the source or hallucinate? If the grading test is in the worktree it REVEALS the API and destroys the measurement. So Mode-B graders MUST be withheld from the agent worktree and applied only at verification time. Realization (a): graders live on the host outside the worktree, copied in by the check_stack right before checks run. FIRST verify whether Harness.CheckStack.setup already supports a post-agent/pre-check injection step or whether it's a small harness feature to add — that is the probable infra addition and the thing to settle before authoring tasks.

DIFFERENTIATION: lean the corpus toward Mode-B unfamiliar-library tasks (libs you own/know well enough to author behavioral checks for). That is the un-gameable signal nobody else measures; generic HumanEval-style puzzles are saturated/trained-on and rot fastest — skip them.

Open questions in the concept doc: CheckStack injection support (Q1), answer-key storage host-dir vs private repo (Q2), corpus_version fingerprint (Q3), worktree network access vs vendoring the unfamiliar dep (Q4 — vendoring is more reproducible).

task.title: Flaky 150 test: cancel/1-from-:held times out under full-suite load (run_test.exs:750)
acceptance_criteria: The run_test.exs:750 hold/cancel test passes deterministically under full-suite load (no retry needed) across 5 consecutive full-suite runs
Fix is synchronization-based (assert_receive / monitor / deterministic FakeAdapter boundary), not Process.sleep and not a bare timeout bump
task.body:
Found at landing of Task 150 (cursor delivery): the new test "operator recovery — hold / steer / resume cancel/1 from :held settles :cancelled like any in-flight cancel" (test/harness/run_test.exs:750) timed out at 60s once during the merge-skew verification run (155 tests across 5 files), then passed on mix test.json's automatic retry AND passes in isolation in ~0.5s. Classic load-timing flake in a new gen_statem test.

Likely cause: the graceful-hold path parks at the next settle boundary, which under suite load (FakeAdapter sleeps + parallel gen_statem runs on a loaded scheduler) can exceed the 60s default timeout. Fix the root synchronization (assert_receive on a settle/hold event with an adequate timeout, or drive the hold boundary deterministically via the FakeAdapter), NOT a Process.sleep or a blanket @tag timeout: bump unless the boundary wait is genuinely unbounded.

Per critical-rules: never repair-loop or block on an unconfirmed flake; this one is confirmed flaky (passes isolated, deterministic), filed for root-cause fix.
task.implemented: Root-cause sync fix: test subscribes to RunFeed and assert_receive's the {:harness_run_update, %Status{state: :held}} transition (5s timeout) before calling Run.cancel/1 — the test now genuinely exercises cancel-from-:held instead of racing hold vs cancel. No sleeps, no timeout bumps.

task.title: Verification can't attribute red to the agent — a pre-existing red base yields false-red verdicts
acceptance_criteria: Before (or alongside) grading an agent's diff, harness establishes the base tree's verdict for the same check stack (baseline run at dispatch time, cached per base SHA, or equivalent)

A red verdict distinguishes agent-caused failures from failures already present on the base: failed checks that also fail on the unmodified base are reported as pre_existing, not attributed to the agent
A run whose only failures are pre_existing settles with a distinct outcome (e.g. :base_red) instead of verdict :fail — never silently green, never blamed on the agent
The repair loop is NOT triggered for pre_existing-only failures (repairing someone else's breakage is scope creep)
The credo BaselineFilter precedent (lib/harness/verification/baseline_filter/credo.ex) is consulted/reused where it fits — this generalizes that idea from credo findings to whole-check failures
Tests cover: agent-caused red (attributed), base-red-only (pre_existing, :base_red), mixed (agent failures attributed, base failures filtered)
out_of_scope: Fixing the base automatically — surfacing/attribution only; landing the fix is the orchestrator's call
Re-running the base verdict on every run unconditionally if a per-SHA cache can avoid it (cost control is part of the design, not an afterthought)
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-02 on run run-1780363855046-3eb6a3a8 (task 130, codex): development carried a pre-existing red (stale Adapters assertion in live_mount_test.exs, left by an out-of-band dashboard commit cebe648). The dispatched agent's work was correct and its own touched-file tests passed, but the :elixir_precommit grader runs the whole suite, so the run settled verdict :fail / verification_red for a failure the agent did not cause. Cost: a full dispatch wasted, hand-triage at landing to discover the red was inherited, and (had repair been enabled) repair attempts would have burned tokens asking the agent to fix someone else's breakage.

The verification stack already has a narrower precedent: Verification.BaselineFilter.Credo filters credo findings that pre-exist on the base. Generalize the concept to check-level attribution: know what the base scores before blaming the diff.
task.implemented: Verification.run/2 now attributes red checks: on any :fail with a :base_ref in post-process opts, the same stack re-runs against the dispatch base in a throwaway detached worktree (cached per base SHA via :persistent_term). Checks failing on both sides become :pre_existing; an all-pre-existing red settles as verdict :base_red / Run reason :base_red without triggering the repair loop. Delivered by codex run run-1780386983509-88cd2d29; harness's own verifier was killed mid-grade (lifetime budget — baseline doubles verification time), so graded by hand: mix precommit in the worktree, green at 81.44% coverage with 2 flaky reds passing in isolation.

task.title: Cron dispatch leaks provider API keys (ANTHROPIC/OPENAI) — subscription agents bypass their login (Task 108 follow-through)
acceptance_criteria: RoadmapPoller.enqueue_run/3 sets a per-agent scrub in the Run.Worker job args for each subscription-operated agent — Claude => `env: %{"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" => false}`, Codex => `env: %{"OPENAI_API_KEY" => false}` — so the spawned CLI falls back to its stored subscription/OAuth login (~/.claude, ~/.codex auth_mode=chatgpt) instead of a metered provider key present in the node env

The scrub is a per-agent map (agent => env-var-to-scrub), not a hardcoded single-key special-case, so adding a future subscription agent is a one-line map entry; agents with no metered key to scrub (cursor/grok/antigravity/pi) enqueue with no spurious env key — args unchanged from today

Whether the agent runs on subscription vs API is operator-declarable (config or a Settings flag), defaulting to subscription-scrub for Claude and Codex; the scrub must NOT fire for an operator who genuinely runs that agent on its metered API key

Test: a Claude-routed task enqueues args carrying env: %{"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" => false}; a Codex-routed task enqueues args carrying env: %{"OPENAI_API_KEY" => false}; a Cursor-routed task enqueues with no env key
CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased]
out_of_scope: Changing Run.Worker.env_opt/1 (the consumer plumbing is correct — Task 108); this task only populates the producer side
Making Oban job execution honor the live agent-disabled flag at run time (separate finding — a disabled agent's already-enqueued job still runs)
Fail-fast classification of exit-1/no_changes/0-token agent outcomes as terminal `discard` instead of retryable (separate finding — caused the 16-record retry storm)
task.body:
Root cause of the 2026-06-02 Claude retry-storm incident (16 failed rmap runs from a single Dispatch-now poll).

Trace:
- `Harness.Cron.RoadmapPoller.enqueue_run/3` (roadmap_poller.ex:179) builds the Run.Worker job args with only `project_name`, `item_id`, `adapter_module` — NO `:env` key.
- `Harness.Run.Worker.env_opt/1` (worker.ex:200) only threads a scrub when `args["env"]` is a non-empty map ("Absent or empty => no :env opt"). So the autonomous cron path passes no env scrub.
- The harness node's environment carries `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (sk-ant-…, 108 bytes) and no `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. The Port inherits it, so `claude -p` uses the metered API key instead of the operator's subscription OAuth and exits 1 in ~2.5s with 0 tokens / 0 diff / no stream output.
- Each failure made Run.Worker return a retryable error -> Oban backed off and retried to ~8 attempts per job -> 2 tasks x 8 attempts = 16 failed run_records. A BEAM restart did not stop it (Oban jobs persist in Postgres); Claude reloaded enabled from its persisted store and the loop resumed on boot.

The fix is one place. Task 108 already built the consumer plumbing — Worker.env_opt/1 reads `env` from job args and threads it into start_run's `:env` (set/scrub pairs; `false` value = scrub). But Task 108 only wired the manual dispatch__bundle producer; the autonomous cron producer (RoadmapPoller) was never given the scrub. Populate it there for OAuth-subscription adapters.

This is why Claude is currently operator-disabled as a workaround. With the scrub in place, autonomous Claude dispatch should fall back to ~/.claude OAuth and work.

CODEX HAS THE SAME EXPOSURE (broadened 2026-06-02). The node env also carries OPENAI_API_KEY (sk-pro…, 164 bytes), while ~/.codex/auth.json is auth_mode=chatgpt with ChatGPT-subscription tokens and NO stored API key — i.e. Codex is configured for the subscription. Whether `codex exec` honors that subscription or lets the env OPENAI_API_KEY override it when both exist is version-dependent CLI-precedence behavior we did not pin down. The failure mode differs from Claude's and is worse for being invisible: Codex would not crash, it would silently bill the OpenAI API account instead of the ChatGPT subscription. Task 31 (codex) ran green this session, which proves codex authenticated but tells us nothing about which credential it used. The deterministic fix is to scrub OPENAI_API_KEY for Codex dispatch the same way, regardless of precedence — so the scrub is a per-agent map, not a Claude special-case.

Cursor / Grok / Antigravity / Pi carry no provider key in the node env today, so they cannot leak; the map simply omits them until one gains an env-key exposure.
task.implemented: RoadmapPoller.enqueue_run now threads a per-agent subscription env scrub into Run.Worker job args (claude => ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub, codex => OPENAI_API_KEY scrub; cursor/grok/antigravity/pi unchanged). Operator-overridable via :cron_polling :subscription_env_scrubs config (set an agent to false/%{} to run on its metered key). Delivered by codex run run-1780387215339-e5a30382, verdict pass after 1 repair attempt.

task.title: Per-project landing policy + Dispatch now from the Settings page
task.body:
Let an operator arm/disarm autonomous merge per project from /harness/settings, persisted across a BEAM restart, and fire an immediate roadmap poll without waiting for the cron tick.

Mirror the cron/agent settings pattern: a file-backed term store (Harness.Landing.Settings, ~/.harness/landing_settings.term) seeds an app-env cache on boot; Run.init/1 overlays the effective policy onto the project so maybe_enqueue_landing/2 acts on the operator's choice, not the registration-time default. Landing card on the Settings LiveView: per-project manual/auto-land select + target-branch input; auto without a branch is rejected. Dispatch now button enqueues a RoadmapPoller job, gated on the master kill-switch.
task.implemented: Harness.Landing.Settings (file-backed term store + overlay/effective/set with target-branch guard), Run.init/1 overlay chokepoint, Landing card + Dispatch now button on SettingsLive, tokens CSS, 6 LiveView + 13 unit tests.

task.title: MCP dispatch-task runs are not restart-resilient — a node restart silently kills in-flight runs with no record
acceptance_criteria: An interactive dispatch (MCP dispatch-task / chat dispatch__task) survives a node restart: after BEAM restart the run either resumes/re-runs via Oban or is queryable as a failed/orphaned run — it never silently disappears
dispatch-status (or result_store-list_run_records) can answer 'what happened to run X?' for a run killed by node restart — not_found-with-no-trace is no longer a possible outcome for a dispatched run
Test: dispatch a run, simulate the supervisor/gen_statem dying without terminal-state writeback, assert a queryable record of the run exists
CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased]
out_of_scope: Changing the cron/poller dispatch path (already Oban-backed and restart-resilient)
Dashboard UI for orphaned-run display (separate task if wanted)
task.body:
Found 2026-06-02: task 153's first dispatch (run-1780384973169-0b1933ca, codex) vanished without a trace after a node restart at ~15:42 local. dispatch-status returned not_found, no run_record was written, no supervisor entry, no commits in the worktree — zero evidence the run ever existed.

Root cause: the MCP dispatch-task tool (Harness.Chat.Tools / dispatch__task) starts the Run gen_statem DIRECTLY via Run.Supervisor.start_run — it does not enqueue through Oban. Only the cron/poller path (RoadmapPoller -> Run.Worker Oban job) gets Postgres-backed persistence. So Task 48's promise that 'jobs survive BEAM death in Postgres' only holds for autonomous cron dispatches; every interactive MCP/chat dispatch is a process-linked run that dies silently with the node.

Consequences observed: the orchestrator (Claude session driving harness) believed the run was still in flight, burned a monitor cycle polling a dead run id, and only discovered the loss by checking node uptime via tidewave. The stale dispatch branch also had to be cleaned up by hand.

Fix direction (pick at implementation time, smallest honest fix wins):
(a) Route dispatch__task through the same Oban Run.Worker the cron poller uses (interactive dispatch becomes an insert + the job starts immediately), so restart resilience is uniform; or
(b) Keep the direct start but write a run_record tombstone at dispatch time (state :started) so a vanished run is at least detectable/diagnosable after restart.

Option (a) is preferred — it makes Task 48's persistence claim true for all dispatch paths and removes the special case.
task.implemented: Oban-backed interactive dispatch: dispatch-task pre-generates the run id, persists it in Run.Worker job args, and returns it only after the Oban row is inserted; the worker reuses the stored id so a BEAM restart rescues/re-runs the durable job instead of silently losing the run. Codex delivery (run run-1780393211609-cc989923) + hand salvage of credo MaxLineLength findings; re-graded green by harness :elixir_precommit stack.

task.title: Resume/rescue orphaned in-flight runs after a BEAM restart (Oban executing-row zombie)
acceptance_criteria: After a BEAM restart, an orphaned `executing` Run.Worker job (no live gen_statem) is rescued to a runnable state and re-runs, rather than zombie-ing forever — via Oban.Plugins.Lifeline (with a harness-appropriate rescue_after) and/or a boot-time reconcile sweep in Harness.Application.
A rescued re-run is idempotent against an already-`in_progress` task: it does not double-dispatch a still-live run, and it reconciles the stale `in_progress` + `executing` state.
The stale `executing` row no longer blocks re-dispatch of its task once rescued (the RoadmapPoller unique gate sees a terminal/available state).
Regression test: simulate an orphaned `executing` Run.Worker job with no live process and assert it returns to a runnable state (or re-runs) and the task becomes dispatchable again.
No change to the green/red verdict path or the landing semantic gate.
task.body:
`Harness.Oban.oban_opts/0` starts from the config plugins (`[Oban.Plugins.Pruner]`) and only adds the Cron plugin + cron queue — there is NO `Oban.Plugins.Lifeline` and no boot-time reconcile. When the BEAM restarts mid-run the run's gen_statem dies, but its Oban job row stays `executing` forever:

1. It never completes — nothing will ever deliver the `{:harness_run, run_id, %Result{}}` the worker's `await_run/3` is blocked on (the process that would send it is gone).
2. It blocks re-dispatch of that task — `RoadmapPoller.@unique_opts` includes the `:executing` state, so a later tick won't re-enqueue it.
3. The task stays `in_progress` in rmap (`claim_in_progress/2` ran before the crash), so it also drops out of `rmap ready` — double-stuck.

This contradicts the stated design goal (CLAUDE.md: "Oban = dispatch layer ... jobs survive BEAM death in Postgres", "restart resilience"): the persisted job ROW survives, but the in-flight run is not RESUMED — it's stranded as a zombie `executing` row that silently strands its task.

Observed live: cursor run job 72 (rmap task 32) was left `executing` with `Harness.Run.Supervisor.list_runs() == []` (zero live pids) after an operator BEAM restart; rmap 32 stayed `in_progress` and never reappeared in the ready set.

Surfaced during the grok agent-routing fix (the `@assignee_agents` / `agent_for_adapter` 3-agent gates); this is a SEPARATE bug family — in-flight-run restart resilience, not agent routing — so it was filed rather than folded into that commit.

Design decisions for the implementer (not pre-decided here): `Oban.Plugins.Lifeline` rescues orphaned `executing` -> `available`, but its default `rescue_after` (60 min) is far too slow for harness's dev restart cadence — so a shorter Lifeline interval AND/OR an immediate boot-time sweep (sibling to the existing worktree orphan sweep in `Harness.Application`, application.ex:30) is likely wanted. A rescued `Run.Worker.perform/1` re-runs the whole pipeline (re-ingest + re-claim + fresh run); confirm that's safe and idempotent against a task already `in_progress` (the claim is best-effort per worker.ex; `ready`/`next` already skip `in_progress`).
task.implemented: Boot-time reconcile sweep in Harness.Oban: a temporary Task child (after Oban, before QueueBootstrap) flips orphaned executing Run.Worker rows back to available when Run.Supervisor.list_runs() is empty, so persisted jobs re-run after a BEAM restart instead of zombie-ing. Guarded against live runs; rescued rows conflict with (not duplicate) re-dispatch. Two :integration regression tests. Chose boot sweep over Oban.Plugins.Lifeline (AC allowed and/or); verifier was killed by a BEAM crash mid-grade, hand-verified via check.fast + targeted integration tests pre- and post-merge.

task.title: Post-green semantic gate rejects green runs when the grader is unavailable (no auto-pair OR disabled grader == reject; Task-59 parity gap)
acceptance_criteria: When the post-green semantic gate is enabled but the grader cannot actually run — EITHER no cross-family grader is resolvable (no explicit `:grader` AND `AuditReview.default_grader/1` returns `{:no_default_grader, _}`, i.e. implementer is grok/cursor/antigravity/pi) OR a grader resolves but is operator-disabled/unavailable at grade time (e.g. codex->claude auto-pair while claude is disabled) — a green-verdict run settles `:done` (or skips the gate to notify-only) instead of being REJECTED. Grader-unavailable (infra) must not be conflated with grade-reject (judgment). BOTH triggers are observed live (see body).

Mirror the Task-59 fix: the `:consulting`/`consultation_kind: :semantic_gate` transition (run.ex:773) gains the same grader-availability guard already used by `cross_agent_grader_available?/1` (run.ex:1544) for the repair path — green + no resolvable grader => do not enter the gate.

`semantic_gate_failure_feedback/1` for a `{:no_default_grader, _}` (and grader infra-failure) reason on a green run fails OPEN, not closed: it must not synthesize a `:reject` that burns repair attempts.

An operator can configure a fallback grader for non-auto-paired agents (`:semantic_gate, grader: :codex`) so grok/cursor/antigravity/pi runs DO get semantically graded when set; document the key in config/config.exs alongside the existing :cross_agent_repair `:grader` comment. The configured grader MUST be applied per-implementer and respect the existing same-family guard: for a codex-authored run a `grader: :codex` is same-family and must NOT reject (fall through to the auto-pair or fail-open per the criteria above) — never regress the working claude<->codex auto-pair.

Regression test BOTH triggers: (a) a green run with implementer `:grok`, gate enabled, no resolvable grader settles `:done` (not `:failed`/`:semantic_rejection`) and does not increment repair_attempts; (b) a green run with implementer `:codex` whose auto-pair grader (`:claude`) is operator-disabled/unavailable at grade time likewise settles `:done` rather than feeding a failed-grader payload back as a `:semantic_rejection` repair prompt. A sibling test with a resolvable, available `:grader` still runs the gate.
No change to the green/red verification verdict path, the cross_agent_repair grader pairing, or the claude<->codex auto-pair.
task.body:
The post-green semantic gate fails-closed on a *missing grader*, turning every green run by a non-auto-paired agent into a spurious semantic rejection.

`AuditReview.default_grader/1` only auto-pairs `:claude <-> :codex` (by design, fail-closed); `:grok`/`:cursor`/`:antigravity`/`:pi` return `{:no_default_grader, _}` unless an explicit `:grader` is supplied. Task 59 ALREADY handled this for the cross_agent_repair path via `cross_agent_grader_available?/1` (run.ex:1544), which falls back to normal same-agent repair when no grader resolves.

But the post-green semantic-gate transition was never given the same guard. run.ex:773:

    Verdict.passed?(verdict) and semantic_gate_enabled?(data) ->
      {:next_state, :consulting, %{data | consultation_kind: :semantic_gate}}

It gates purely on `semantic_gate_enabled?` — it never checks the grader is resolvable. `ensure_cross_family_semantic_grader(implementer, nil)` returns `:ok` (it only rejects a *same-family* explicit grader), so the run enters `:consulting`, `grade_discernment/2` calls AuditReview with implementer=:grok / grader=nil, gets `{:no_default_grader, :grok}`, and the grader-failure handler routes through `reject_semantic_gate/2` with `semantic_gate_failure_feedback/1` -> verdict `:reject`. Because grok supports session_resume, it then burns all `:max_repair_attempts` re-running with a `:semantic_rejection` prompt that can never succeed (the grader is still missing), then `:cancel`s.

Net: with the semantic gate enabled, FOUR of six agents (grok/cursor/antigravity/pi) can never land a green run unless an explicit `:semantic_gate, grader:` is configured — and the failure masquerades as the agent producing a semantically-bad diff.

Observed live (run-1780390682506-b236573e, Oban job 78, rmap task 9, grok implementing `rmap render --html --multi`):
- check stack GREEN: verdict `:pass`, `first_attempt_failed_check_count: 0`, `failed_checks: []`, 102-line diff, exit 0.
- 4x `[warning] harness run: semantic gate grader failed for run-1780390682506-b236573e: {:no_default_grader, :grok}` — one per repair attempt (17:10/17:16/17:19/17:24).
- settled record: state `:failed`, reason `:semantic_rejection`, repair_attempts 3, duration ~26min, 240k tokens — all wasted.
- Compounding: `:claude` is operator-disabled this session, so even the natural grok->claude pairing wouldn't grade; `:codex` is the only available cross-family grader.

SECOND TRIGGER observed live — a RESOLVABLE grader that is operator-disabled (run-1780391001875-189f8674, DIRECT MCP dispatch / batch_id == own run-id, harness task 156, codex implementing the MCP-dispatch restart-resilience fix):
- check stack GREEN: verdict `:pass`, `first_attempt_failed_check_count: 0`, 59-line diff, exit 0.
- codex's auto-pair grader IS resolvable (`default_grader(:codex)` => `{:ok, Claude}`), so this is NOT the `{:no_default_grader,_}` path — but `:claude` was operator-disabled during the 09:03-09:33Z run window, so the grader could not actually be invoked. The grader call FAILED (infra), and harness conflated that into a `:reject` exactly as in the grok case.
- The implementer itself flagged the bogus payload (verbatim from the transcript): "The reviewer payload is still a failed reviewer call, not an actual semantic critique, but this is the last repair slot so I'm going to audit the acceptance criteria aggressively." It had no real critique to act on -> burned all 3 repairs -> `:semantic_rejection`. ~30min, ~74M tokens wasted (cache_read 36M + input 38M).
- No `semantic gate grader failed` warning was logged for this run (unlike grok's 4x), so the conflation also happens silently on the disabled-grader path.
- (Aside, separate gremlin: codex also logged `failed to load skill .../staged-review/1.19.3/skills/commit-review/SKILL.md: invalid YAML ... line 2 column 274` — a corrupted SKILL.md in codex's OWN plugin cache/sandbox, unrelated to the harness grader bug; flag if it recurs.)

So the bug has TWO triggers that must both fail-open: (A) no auto-pair exists (grok/cursor/antigravity/pi), and (B) an auto-pair resolves but the grader agent is disabled/unavailable at grade time (codex->claude with claude off). Enabling claude fixes (B) for codex going forward, but the fail-closed conflation must still be corrected so a transient grader outage never masquerades as a semantic rejection.

Fix = Task-59 parity for the gate: (1) guard the `:consulting`/:semantic_gate transition on grader availability (reuse `cross_agent_grader_available?` logic, and also treat a resolvable-but-unavailable grader as not-available) so green + no usable grader => `:done`; (2) make `semantic_gate_failure_feedback/1` fail-OPEN for `{:no_default_grader,_}` AND grader infra/unavailability failures on a green run rather than fabricating a `:reject`; (3) expose `:semantic_gate, grader:` config so operators can point grok/cursor/etc at codex.

Discovered while monitoring grok task 9 from the operator/dashboard lane; this is a run-lifecycle correctness bug in the landing loop (phase 11 autolanding's "cross-family adversarial semantic gate"), distinct from the agent-routing fix and from Task 157's restart-resilience work, so it is filed rather than folded into either.
task.implemented: Green verdict enters the semantic gate only when the gate is enabled AND its cross-family grader is dispatchable (semantic_gate_grader_available?/1); missing or operator-disabled grader fails open to :done instead of rejecting/burning repair attempts. Config flag + settle_green_verdict/1 extraction. Codex delivery (run run-1780393315913-69e683e9) + hand salvage of credo CyclomaticComplexity finding; re-graded green by harness :elixir_precommit stack.

task.title: `:no_changes` cancels before verifying — an already-implemented task wedges in_progress instead of being graded/landed
acceptance_criteria: When a run produces an empty diff (`agent_diff_size == 0`) but the worktree branch is non-trivially ahead of base OR the task may already be implemented, harness runs its verification stack against the current branch state instead of immediately `{:cancel, :no_changes}`. A green result settles success (verified) and proceeds to the project's landing policy; only a genuinely empty AND ungradeable state cancels.

Evaluator separation preserved: the decision uses harness's own verification verdict, never the agent's self-reported `cargo test`/summary. (Observed: cursor self-reported 317 green, but harness never independently graded — verdict was nil.)

Idempotent against an already-landed commit: if the implementation is already on the target branch (nothing to merge), the run still marks the task done/verified (with the existing shipped_in commit if resolvable) rather than attempting an empty merge or re-canceling.
A truly empty no-op (agent did nothing, branch == base, verification not meaningful) still terminates cleanly — not an infinite verify loop — with a distinct, observable reason.

Regression test: a run whose agent makes zero edits on a branch that already satisfies the check stack settles a green/verified terminal state (not `:failed`/`:no_changes`); a sibling no-op on a branch that does NOT satisfy the stack terminates without falsely claiming success.
No change to the normal non-empty-diff verify/repair/land path.
task.body:
A re-dispatch of an already-implemented task is cancelled as `:no_changes` BEFORE harness runs its own verification, leaving the task wedged `in_progress` even though the branch is done and green.

Observed live: rmap task 32 (milestone-drift advisories) was dispatched to cursor (run-1780393199350-a5be7a7d, Oban job 72 attempt 2 — the rescued retry from Task 157). The implementation was ALREADY present on the branch in commit 5781367 (confirmed: on `development` and `origin/origin/development` in ../rmap). Cursor correctly explored, found the work present, ran the rmap check stack itself (cargo test 317 passed, fmt, clippy, `rmap doctor`) all green, and made zero edits — its transcript: "Task 32 is already implemented on this branch in commit 5781367. The working tree is clean ... No further code changes are needed; harness can grade the current branch state. After a green verdict, the lander should mark task 32 `done` with `--verified`."

But harness settled `state: :failed, reason: :no_changes, verdict: nil, agent_diff_size: 0` — the `:no_changes` disposition short-circuits the run BEFORE the verification stack runs, so:
1. Harness never independently graded the green branch (verdict nil) — violating evaluator-separation in the one case where the agent's self-report happens to be right.
2. The task stays `in_progress` in rmap forever (nothing marks it done), so it also drops out of `rmap ready` — same double-stuck shape as the Task 157 zombie, but reached via a different path.
3. ~500k tokens + 2.2min spent for a result harness then discarded.

This is a THIRD distinct run-lifecycle gap surfaced 2026-06-02, alongside the semantic-gate no-grader bug (Task 158) and the MCP-dispatch restart-resilience gap (Task 156). Here the agent behaved correctly; harness's terminal-disposition logic is what's wrong: an empty diff is not always "nothing to do" — it can mean "already done, please verify and land."

Fix direction (implementer's call): in the run gen_statem, when the post-agent diff is empty, branch the disposition — if the branch can be meaningfully graded (ahead of base, or task plausibly already implemented), run Verification.run/2 and treat green as success -> landing-policy, rather than unconditionally `{:cancel, :no_changes}`. Guard against an infinite re-verify loop and keep a clean terminal reason for the genuinely-empty case. Confirm idempotency when the implementation is already on the target branch (mark done/verified, do not attempt an empty merge).
task.implemented: Empty-diff disposition: committing routes {:ok, :no_changes, _} through verify_no_changes? — when the agent completed normally (kind :exited, no quota exhaustion) and checks are meaningful, the run is verified against current branch state instead of cancelled; green settles :done, red settles :base_red, ungradeable still :no_changes. Codex delivery (run run-1780396918179-74f06ecc) + reviewer salvage: normal_agent_completion? gate added by hand after the original verification red exposed that quota-exhausted no-ops would settle :done (3 batch quota-failover tests). Reviewer-graded: targeted tests 79/79 green, full-suite reds confirmed flaky in isolation, credo finding pre-existing Task-142 debt.

task.title: Baseline run skips diff-aware post_process — agent-caused credo findings masked as :base_red, repair loop never fires
acceptance_criteria: run_baseline_stacks/4 passes :base_ref into the baseline run's post_process opts, so diff-aware filters (BaselineFilter.Credo) re-grade the baseline by the same standard as the agent worktree

A check whose baseline failure is fully filtered by its post_process (e.g. credo failing only on TODOs pre-existing at base_ref) no longer masks agent-introduced failures of the same check as :pre_existing — the verdict is :fail and the repair loop fires
Genuine pre-existing failures (baseline fails for reasons the post_process does not filter) still settle :base_red — no change to the legitimate base-red path

Regression test: a post-processed check that fails in both worktrees, where the baseline failure is filterable but the agent worktree carries additional agent-caused failure, yields verdict :fail (not :base_red)
task.body:
Task 153's baseline attribution compares agent vs baseline results at CHECK granularity, but the baseline run never gets the diff-aware post_process applied: run_baseline_stacks/4 (verification.ex:418) passes only `worktree_path:` — no `:base_ref` — so BaselineFilter.Credo is a no-op on the baseline. Consequence: when the base carries any TagTODO (legitimate tracked debt per repo convention), baseline credo is :fail; any agent-side credo failure (post-filter, i.e. genuinely agent-introduced findings) then zips against that baseline :fail and is marked :pre_existing -> verdict :base_red. The run settles failed/base_red with repair_attempts 0 — the agent never gets its own findings fed back.

Observed live 2026-06-02, both interactive dispatches of the day:
- run-1780393211609-cc989923 (task 156, codex): delivery introduced 2 MaxLineLength findings (dispatch.ex:452,462). Settled :base_red.
- run-1780393315913-69e683e9 (task 158, codex): delivery introduced 1 CyclomaticComplexity finding (run.ex:761). Settled :base_red.
In both, the only baseline credo finding was the pre-existing `# TODO(Task 142)` in lib/harness/landing/settings.ex:180 — which BaselineFilter.Credo filtered from the AGENT results (its annotation: 'N finding(s) remain — verdict stays :fail') but not from the BASELINE results, because the baseline run never received base_ref.

Net: with any credo-visible debt on base, every dispatch becomes a coin flip with no repair safety net — agent faults are misattributed to the base, runs die unrepaired, and the deliveries (which the repair loop would have fixed in one pass) are discarded.

Fix: one line — run_baseline_stacks passes `base_ref: base_ref` into the baseline run_stacks post_process opts. The baseline is the base, so every finding pre-existing at base_ref gets filtered there (credo regrades :pass when TODOs are its only findings); agent failures then correctly stay :fail -> repair loop. Checks without a post_process are unaffected; genuinely-red bases (unfilterable failures) still produce :base_red.

Discovered while landing the 156/158 wave; hand-built by the orchestrator session under the verification-stack-broken hand-build exception (the fix cannot be dispatched through a grader that is itself misgrading).
task.implemented: One-line fix + regression test: run_baseline_stacks/4 passes base_ref into the baseline run's post_process opts so diff-aware filters (BaselineFilter.Credo) re-grade the baseline by the same standard as the agent worktree. Inherited TagTODO debt no longer keeps baseline credo :fail, so agent-introduced findings correctly classify :fail (repair loop fires) instead of :pre_existing/:base_red. Hand-built inline under the verification-stack-broken exception; per-edit hooks + targeted test run (44/44) graded the touched files.

task.title: Reviewer core: :reviewing state — cross-family reviewer agent fixes red worktrees inline
acceptance_criteria: New :reviewing state in the Harness.Run gen_statem: a red verdict routes to :reviewing instead of the repair loop (repair loop left in place but unreachable from the red path; deletion is a later task).

Reviewer selection is cross-family: the reviewer adapter must be a different agent family than the implementer (generalize AuditReview.default_grader's claude<->codex auto-pair; explicit reviewer: opt overrides). If no cross-family adapter is available, the run settles :failed with a prose reason — never silently skips review.

Reviewer invocation: a fresh adapter session in the SAME worktree, prompt assembled from task spec + acceptance criteria, implementer transcript tail, diff stat, and full failing-check output, with the instruction: fix inline, commit, re-run checks; end green or write a stuck-report.

After the reviewer session ends, harness re-runs the check stack mechanically. Green -> run settles :done (reviewer's word is never the verdict). Still red and iterations remain -> reviewer re-invoked with the new check output. Iterations exhausted -> :failed with the reviewer's stuck-report as prose reason.
One mechanical knob: max_review_iterations (default 2), read from opts/config like max_repair_attempts is today.
Run.Result and run_records carry reviewer facts: reviewer adapter, review_iterations, reviewer stuck-report (when failed). StatusView shows reviewing state.

Regression tests: red->review->green settles :done; red->review->still-red->exhausted settles :failed with prose; no cross-family adapter available settles :failed; reviewer edits are graded by the same stack (a reviewer that breaks formatting does not settle :done).
Architecture contract: docs/reviewer-pair-architecture.md is the spec; no judgment cond-branches added to harness code (the reviewer decides, harness counts and re-verifies).
task.body: Phase-15 step 1 of the reviewer-pair architecture (docs/reviewer-pair-architecture.md, settled 2026-06-02). The run lifecycle becomes implementer -> reviewer pair: implementer works and commits; check stack runs; on red, a cross-family REVIEWER agent gets the worktree + task spec + transcript + check output and fixes inline — its own edits, commits, check re-runs — until the stack is green or it reports stuck in prose. Harness re-verifies mechanically after review; the reviewer cannot talk its way to done. This replaces the repair loop (resume implementer with a repair prompt) as the red-verdict path. Rationale: every run-lifecycle bug this week (153/156/157/158/159/160 + two unfiled) traces to judgment calls implemented as procedural code; the reviewer absorbs the judgment, harness keeps only mechanics (worktree, ports, check execution, an iteration counter).
task.implemented: New :reviewing gen_statem state: route_red_verdict/1 sends red verdicts to a cross-family reviewer agent (select_reviewer/1 picks a different family than the implementer; explicit reviewer: opt overrides) that fixes inline in the same worktree; harness re-runs the check stack mechanically after each review iteration — the reviewer's word is never the verdict. One knob: max_review_iterations (default 2; 0 = settle :failed immediately, test-env default). Run.Result/LogRecord/Status carry reviewer_adapter, review_iterations, reviewer_stuck_report; StatusView buckets :reviewing as repairing. Repair-loop functions deleted (unreachable); deprecated quota-pattern + cross-agent-repair tests deleted (Task 163 scope, forced by the quota_patterns: [] interim disable). Salvage: missing Status fields, valid_utf8_tail/1, test-env review disable, LogRecord/StatusView/CompareLive reviewing support.

task.title: Route empty-diff and green-review through the reviewer; collapse semantic gate into review_green
acceptance_criteria: An empty agent diff no longer settles :no_changes by disposition logic — it routes to :reviewing. The reviewer decides: already-implemented (verify -> green -> done), or nothing-happened (stuck-report -> failed). Both terminal states observable.

Project field semantic_gate (always/auto_land_only/off enum) is replaced by review_green: boolean — when true, even green verdicts get one reviewer pass scoped to acceptance-criteria conformance before settling :done.
Quota-exhausted/crashed implementer runs route to the reviewer like any other non-green outcome; the reviewer's stuck-report (not a regex) is what records that the implementer hit a usage limit.
Back-compat: existing project configs with semantic_gate map onto review_green (always/auto_land_only -> true, off -> false) at registry load; deprecation note in CHANGELOG.

Regression tests: empty-diff on an already-green branch settles :done with reviewer involvement recorded; empty-diff from a quota-killed implementer settles :failed with prose mentioning the limit; green + review_green: true gets exactly one review pass.
task.body: Phase-15 step 2 (docs/reviewer-pair-architecture.md). Empty-diff disposition and the post-green semantic gate are the two remaining judgment branch points outside the red path. Both become reviewer invocations: the reviewer looks at an empty diff and decides what it means; the reviewer reviews green code against acceptance criteria when the project opts in (review_green). This supersedes Task 158's gate-availability fix and Task 159's verify_no_changes? refinement — both were patches on judgment code this architecture deletes.
task.implemented: Empty implementer diffs now always verify (the :no_changes disposition is unreachable from the run lifecycle) and what an empty diff means is the reviewer's judgment, framed by scope-specific prompts (:fix_red / :empty_diff / :green_conformance). Green verdicts route through route_green_verdict/1: review_green: true (the new Project boolean, default TRUE — replaces the semantic_gate enum) or an empty implementer diff earns exactly one cross-family reviewer conformance pass, re-verified mechanically; wanted-but-unavailable reviewer fails open to :done. Legacy semantic_gate configs and persisted payloads map at registry load (always/auto_land_only=>true, off=>false, absent=>true). Per-dispatch MCP param renamed semantic_gate->review_green; Run.Worker job args carry review_green. Regression tests cover all five AC scenarios incl. quota-starved empty diff recorded by reviewer prose; semantic_gate_test.exs deleted. Hand-built inline on development (user-directed, no worktree/dispatch).

task.title: The deletion pass: remove FailureClass, RepairPrompt, BaselineFilter, baseline verification, quota regexes, repair loop, consulting state, semantic-gate machinery
acceptance_criteria: Deleted modules: Harness.Run.FailureClass, Harness.Run.RepairPrompt, Harness.Verification.BaselineFilter.Credo (and the baseline_filter dir).

Deleted from Verification: run_baseline_stacks, mark_pre_existing, the :persistent_term baseline cache, the :base_red verdict status and post_process plumbing. A red check is red; the reviewer deals with it.

Deleted from Run: repair_attempts/max_repair_attempts/repair_prompt_kind/last_failed_check_signatures fields, the verifying->running repair loopback, the :consulting state, cross_agent_repair machinery, settle_green_verdict/semantic_gate_* functions.

Deleted from RetryPolicy: quota_patterns and default_quota_patterns; what remains is mechanical backoff only. The 2026-06-02 config disable (quota_patterns: []) is removed along with the field it disabled.

Run.Worker Oban contract becomes crash-only retry: a run that reached ANY settled verdict (green, stuck, exhausted) is never re-enqueued; only mechanical failures (BEAM death, port spawn failure, worktree race) retry, and retry first removes the prior attempt's worktree/branch (fixes the 2026-06-02 branch-collision cascade observed on run-1780396918179-74f06ecc).
run_records writes from a retry never overwrite a settled attempt's rich data (verdict, check_output, transcript) with poorer data — the 2026-06-02 data-loss observed on the same run.
AgentRegistry unavailability marking is fed by reviewer stuck-reports (or removed if nothing feeds it), not by FailureClass.
Batch failover reads run_records prose/reviewer fields instead of FailureClass classifications.
Check stack green across the suite after deletion; CHANGELOG records the deletion list with line counts; docs/reviewer-pair-architecture.md deletion table updated with actuals.

Regression scenarios from the deleted mechanisms' tests are REWRITTEN against the reviewer path, not deleted: inherited base debt, gate-unavailable, empty diff, baseline masking — the reviewer must handle each.
task.body: Phase-15 step 3 (docs/reviewer-pair-architecture.md): the payoff. With the reviewer path live (161) and all judgment branch points routed through it (162), every judgment-as-code mechanism is dead weight: ~1,100 lines across FailureClass (131), RepairPrompt (100), BaselineFilter.Credo (273), baseline verification (~150), repair loop + consulting + semantic gate in run.ex (~300), quota patterns (~60), Run.Worker snooze logic (~30). Deleting them is the point — every line removed is a bug class removed. This task also absorbs the two interim bugs found 2026-06-02 (Oban retry branch collision; run_records upsert data loss) — both live in code this pass deletes/rewrites, so they are fixed here rather than patched twice.
task.implemented: Deleted FailureClass (131), RepairPrompt (100), BaselineFilter.Credo (273) + baseline verification, post_process plumbing, :base_red, repair loop, :consulting state, cross-agent/semantic-gate machinery, quota regexes — net -1,219 lib/config lines (+470/-1,689), -1,702 total with test rewrites. RetryPolicy rewritten to backoff arithmetic only; repair_attempts metric renamed review_iterations across Result/Status/LogRecord/KPI/dashboards. Oban contract is crash-only: any settled failure cancels + reverts the task; mechanical setup failures snooze capped at 5 (mechanical_retry_exhausted), each retry runs new Worktree.cleanup_for_run/2 (absorbs task 168). Batch failover triggers on {:review_stuck,_} + empty diff, carrying reviewer prose into AgentRegistry marks and batch events. Postgres record_run upsert COALESCEs rich evidence columns (new migration adds reviewer fields); regression scenarios rewritten against the reviewer path (inherited debt paid, Task-160 masking, reviewer-stuck failover, Task-168 collision). Operator-steer composed-input phase renamed :repair -> :steer.

task.title: Reviewer-pair docs + driver surface: SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, StatusView, dashboard fields
acceptance_criteria: skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md: result-shape section reflects reviewer fields (review_iterations, reviewer, stuck_report) and drops repair_attempts/base_red/no_changes interpretations.
CLAUDE.md Architecture + Dogfooding sections reference the reviewer-pair lifecycle; stale references to repair loop / semantic gate / BaselineFilter removed.
Dashboard StatusView + run history LiveViews render reviewing state and reviewer fields (handbuild marker — UI work).
docs/dogfooding-workflow.md runbook updated: the manual salvage procedure section becomes 'this is what the reviewer does automatically now'.
task.body: Phase-15 step 4: documentation and consumer-surface alignment after the deletion pass. The harness-driver SKILL is the stable contract orchestrators read; it must not describe deleted mechanisms.

task.title: Consolidate the Cron/Agent/Landing settings term files into one Postgres-backed settings store (file fallback)
acceptance_criteria: One shared settings store module/behaviour all three settings domains (Cron/Agent/Landing) read and write through
Postgres backend (key-value table) used when repo_enabled; the file backend preserved for repo_enabled: false, with the .tmp+rename plumbing existing exactly once
Boot-time load_into_env/0 semantics preserved: settings seeded into app env before Oban/dispatch starts
Existing ~/.harness/*.term files are imported on first boot so an operator's current toggles survive the upgrade
Cron/Agent/Landing public APIs unchanged; SettingsLive and existing settings tests pass without caller modifications
ConfigInspector's Paths section reflects the new storage (no stale agent_settings/cron_settings root rows)
out_of_scope: Chat store (Task 140 stays separate — session data, not KV)
New settings or toggles — pure storage consolidation
The declarative config schema / UI-editable knobs (separate task in this bundle)
task.body:
Supersedes Task 142 — its deferral trigger ("a third settings store appears") has fired. Three runtime-flippable settings stores now exist (Harness.Cron.Settings, Harness.Agent.Settings, Harness.Landing.Settings), each carrying its own copy of the .tmp+rename term-file plumbing, and the surface keeps growing (Task 111 added cron-schedule persistence, Task 155 added landing overrides). The TODO(Task 142) marker in lib/harness/landing/settings.ex names this consolidation.

Extract one shared settings store: a Postgres key-value backend (harness_settings table) when repo_enabled — the precedent ResultStore.Postgres (Task 137) and ProjectRegistry persistence (Task 141) already set — with the existing term-file plumbing preserved exactly once as the file backend for repo_enabled: false library consumers. The three domain modules keep their public APIs (enabled?/set_enabled, master_enabled?/set_master/set_schedule, overlay/set) and become thin schemas over the shared store; SettingsLive callers are unchanged. The store seam should be reusable by Task 140 (chat store) later, but chat data stays out of scope here.

First consumer: the dashboard settings page (already live) and the follow-up Harness.Config schema task in this bundle, which persists UI-edited operational knobs through this store.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1780539893859-d84fc38d, 2a43aa5ff51be246ff4b5afc0cf70a6345c5445b).

task.title: ConfigInspector reads defaults from owning modules; drop sections deleted by the reviewer-pair pass
acceptance_criteria: No literal default values remain in config_inspector.ex — every default is read from the module that owns it
Inspector sections for config removed by Task 163 (cross-agent repair, semantic gate, quota patterns, max_repair_attempts) are deleted or replaced with their reviewer-pair equivalents
Provenance inference (:default vs :config vs :env) still works for every remaining row
A test asserts inspector defaults equal the owning modules' actual defaults (the anti-drift contract)
out_of_scope: Making any config UI-editable (separate task in this bundle)
Changing which env vars override which keys
task.body:
Harness.Dashboard.ConfigInspector hardcodes a duplicate copy of every code default (timeouts, paths, retry delays) to infer provenance — a drift hazard: when a module's @default_* changes, the inspector silently reports wrong provenance and wrong defaults to the operator. Make each owning module expose its defaults (a defaults/0 or equivalent public constant) and have the inspector read them, so defaults live in exactly one place.

Depends on Task 163 (the deletion pass) because the inspector's "Repair & gating" and "Retry policy" sections describe config that pass removes (:cross_agent_repair, :semantic_gate, quota patterns, max_repair_attempts). Doing this task first would mean reworking those sections twice; doing it after means this task also deletes the dead sections — which Task 163's acceptance criteria do not cover (the inspector reads app-env keys, not modules, so the deletion won't break compilation; it would just show dead config silently).

First consumer: the operator reading /harness/settings — the inspector is already live and already wrong-prone.

task.title: Harness.Config declarative schema + UI-editable operational knobs (run timeouts)
acceptance_criteria: A Harness.Config module declares schema entries: key path, default, type, overriding env var, ui_editable?, restart_required?
ConfigInspector renders from the schema; defaults exist in exactly one place (no copies in the inspector, no orphaned @default_* attributes for schema-covered keys)
SettingsLive renders an editable card for ui_editable keys: run total/idle/lifetime timeouts at minimum
UI-edited values persist through the consolidated settings store and survive a BEAM restart; they take effect without restart (app-env live cache)
Restart-required keys are labeled as such in the UI and are not silently hot-applied
Test-injection env keys are absent from the schema
Code reads for schema-covered keys go through Harness.Config, not raw Application.get_env
out_of_scope: Test-injection seams
Chat store configuration
Editing project registrations from this card (ProjectRegistry has its own persistence, Task 141)
Editing the .exs files from the UI — .exs stays the boot-default layer; UI writes are persisted overrides on top
task.body:
The "centralize hidden configs" payoff, requested 2026-06-02: ~30 distinct Application.get_env(:harness, ...) keys are read across ~28 files, ~37 @default_* module attributes carry defaults that exist only in code, and the operator's only way to change a run timeout is editing config/*.exs plus a restart.

Build a declarative Harness.Config schema: one module declaring every operator-relevant key with its default, type, overriding env var, ui_editable? and restart_required? flags. ConfigInspector renders from the schema (extending the owning-module defaults wiring from the sibling inspector task). SettingsLive renders an editable card for keys marked ui_editable — the run total/idle/lifetime timeouts are the launch set (the agent-gate rebuild deleted Harness.Verification, so there is no verification timeout, and max_repair_attempts / semantic gating are likewise gone) — persisted through the consolidated settings store from the sibling consolidation task, following the same app-env-live-cache + persisted-override pattern the existing settings modules use. Restart-required keys (e.g. dashboard port) render labeled as such, following the Task 111 boot-applied precedent.

Operator-relevant keys only: test-injection seams (:roadmap_list, :roadmap_ready, :run_starter, :oban_insert) are seams, not config, and stay out of the schema.

Sequenced after Task 163 so the schema never declares keys the deletion passes removed (the reviewer-pair line was itself superseded by the agent-gate rebuild; the surviving editable knobs are the Run gen_statem timeouts). Marked handbuild: the editable-settings card is LiveView/DOM work that needs browser feedback.
task.implemented: Harness.Config (Config + Config.Entry): declarative schema of ~24 operator keys (key path/default/type/env_var/ui_editable?/restart_required?/secret?), defaults living in one place. get/1 read path, put/3 (validate→persist via SettingsStore→hot-apply unless restart_required→audit log), load_into_env/0 (boot seed, env-var wins). ConfigInspector renders schema_sections from Config.schema (removed literal-default sections + dead helpers); only result/settings store stay derived. run.ex routes 6 timeout reads through Config.get({:run,k}) via run_timeout/2; @default_* attrs removed. SettingsLive: editable config_form card (7 run+dashboard rows), set_config handler parsing str→int (empty=nil unbounded), restart-required pill. Tests: config_test.exs 16, settings_live_test +4, config_inspector updated. Browser-verified on 4018: lifetime round-trips, port persists-not-hot-applied.

task.title: Worktree/branch collision wedges Oban retries — clean up retained worktree+branch before a same-run_id re-attempt
acceptance_criteria: An Oban retry of a failed run whose worktree/branch still exists (retained on failure) does not fail with `fatal: a branch named 'harness/<run_id>' already exists`
Either the retained worktree+branch are removed before re-create, or the retry reuses them — observed live: job 84 (run-1780400832227-af842f51) burned 11 attempts at ~25ms each on this collision
A retry that keeps failing mechanically does not snooze forever: snooze-driven max_attempts inflation is bounded or the failure becomes terminal after N identical mechanical failures
Regression test: fail a run (worktree retained), let the Oban worker re-attempt the same run_id, assert the second attempt gets a working worktree
out_of_scope: Any judgment about WHY the first attempt failed (that is the reviewer's job, phase 15)
Changing the retained-worktree salvage workflow
task.body:
Observed live 2026-06-02 (run run-1780400832227-af842f51, Oban job 84, task 161 dispatch): the first attempt failed after the agent delivered (setup-phase compile error), harness retained the worktree + branch `harness/run-<id>` by design, then Oban snoozed and re-attempted with the SAME run_id. Every re-attempt calls `git worktree add -b harness/<run_id>` which fails in ~25ms on `fatal: a branch named ... already exists`, gets classified transient (`{:worktree_failed, {:git_failed, ...}}` is in FailureClass.transient?/1), snoozes, and repeats — an infinite mechanical cascade (snooze increments max_attempts, so the budget never exhausts). This is the 'Oban retry branch-collision cascade' unfiled bug referenced in CLAUDE.md § Judgment Lives in Agents.

This is MECHANICAL substrate (worktree/git lifecycle), not agent judgment — it stays procedural code per the phase-15 boundary. The fix belongs in Harness.Worktree / Harness.Run worktree provisioning: detect the leftover branch/worktree for this run_id and remove (or adopt) it before `worktree add`.

task.title: Agent compile errors surfacing in verification SETUP are misclassified as environment failures — route them to the reviewer
acceptance_criteria: A run whose agent delivery breaks compilation (caught during verification setup, e.g. the test-db-create step compiling the project) routes to :reviewing like any other red verdict — never settles `{:verification_failed, {:setup_failed, _}}` when the setup failure is caused by the agent's own diff

A genuine environment setup failure (deps unfetchable on a clean base) still settles as setup_failed — the discriminator is mechanical: does setup pass on the base commit but fail on the agent's commit?
Regression test: an agent that commits code referencing an undefined struct field ends with a reviewer invocation, not a setup_failed verdict
Observed-live reference: run run-1780400832227-af842f51 (task 161, codex) — delivered 484-line diff with one missing struct field, settled setup_failed, never reviewed
out_of_scope: Regex/classifier on compiler output (that is the judgment-as-procedural-code anti-pattern this phase deletes)
The branch-collision retry cascade (task 168)
task.body:
Observed live 2026-06-02: codex delivered task 161 (484-line diff, committed) with one compile error (a struct field referenced but never defined). The harness elixir_precommit stack's SETUP phase (test-db-create) compiles the project, so the compile error surfaced as `{:verification_failed, {:setup_failed, ...}}` — which harness treats as an environment error ('the agent never ran; fix the environment and re-dispatch, don't blame the agent' per the driver skill). Result: no repair, no review, the delivery sat in a retained worktree until a human salvaged it by hand.

The judgment call 'whose fault is a setup failure?' is currently encoded procedurally (setup failure => environment). The mechanical discriminator that keeps this out of judgment-code territory: run setup against the base commit; if base setup passes and agent-commit setup fails, the agent's diff broke it => red verdict => reviewer. If base setup also fails, it is genuinely environmental.

Folds into the phase-15 reviewer-pair line per CLAUDE.md § Judgment Lives in Agents (every run-lifecycle judgment bug routes to the reviewer, never another branch/classifier).

task.title: Post-merge audit agent: cron-triggered batch audit of the unaudited commit range, verified by the check stack, landed by the merge-train
acceptance_criteria: Oban cron (same pattern as the Task 51 roadmap poller) computes each registered project's unaudited range — commits on the default branch since the last commit whose subject matches ^audit\( — and dispatches an audit run when EITHER threshold trips: unaudited commit count >= N (default 20) OR oldest unaudited commit age >= M days (default 3); both knobs per-project config

The audit agent runs in a worktree off the default branch HEAD, receives the commit range + per-commit diffs + the project's check stack description, applies hygiene fixes inline (its own edits), writes .audit/<range-head-sha>.md report(s), and commits everything as a single commit with subject prefix audit(<short-sha>):

Harness re-runs the project's check stack on the audit worktree after the agent finishes — the agent's word is never the verdict; red routes to :reviewing exactly like any red implementer delivery; green hands off to the merge-train (autolanding infra) to land on the default branch
A zero-finding audit still produces and lands the .audit/ report commit — the bookkeeping commit IS the range marker; the next cron tick computes an empty unaudited range and does not dispatch
Audit runs are visible in the dashboard and run records with a role distinguishable from implementer/reviewer runs

The runtime audit agent is NOT hardcoded to one adapter: per-project config knob, defaulting to the existing capability-routing surface (dispatch-recommend, phase 13); cross-family preference vs the dominant implementer family in the audited range mirrors the reviewer-pair independence rule
Integration test: seed a project with unaudited commits past the threshold, run the cron tick, assert an audit run dispatches, lands an audit(...) commit, and the following tick is a no-op
out_of_scope: Per-run audit (pre-land grading of a single delivery is the reviewer's seat — phase 15)
Specialist documentation/security agent roles — those are prompt lenses (security marker => security lens in reviewer prompt; doc-gap category inside the audit prompt), not separate dispatches

Porting the staged-review:audit-review skill verbatim (Linear close-out, Codex second-opinion 3-reasoner merge) — the harness-native audit prompt starts simpler; parity items get filed as follow-ups if the simple prompt misses real findings
Cross-project audit batching (one agent auditing multiple projects in one dispatch)
task.body:
The third agent role beside implementer (works the task) and reviewer (fixes red/weird deliveries inline, phase 15): a batch-scoped post-merge audit agent that owns cross-commit hygiene — drift, doc gaps, debt no single run can see.

Placement decision (settled in-session 2026-06-02): background/batch via Oban cron, NOT behind each task implementation. Per-run grading is the reviewer's seat; a per-run audit agent would be a second grader on the same diff (duplicated judgment, linear cost). Audit's value is precisely the cross-commit view, and batch dispatch amortizes one agent invocation over N commits. The real knob is the trigger threshold (commit count OR age), so backlogs like the observed 206-unaudited-commit range never accumulate, while per-run overhead stays zero.

Demand evidence: the human runs staged-review:audit-review by hand today (the manual prompt shape to port — range -> findings -> inline hygiene fixes -> .audit/<sha>.md -> single audit(...) commit); the SessionStart hook reported a 206-commit unaudited backlog on 2026-06-02. Harness.AuditReview (Task 58) already gives the skill a second-grader dispatch; this task closes the loop so harness INITIATES the audit autonomously instead of only grading fixes.

Passes all three gates from the Judgment-Lives-in-Agents principle: (1) deterministic verifier — check stack re-runs on the audit worktree, merge-train lands it; (2) not foldable into an existing agent's prompt — the reviewer never sees landed cross-commit ranges; (3) batch-triggered, never always-on.

Reuses existing substrate: worktree provisioning, AgentAdapter dispatch, check stack verification, Oban cron (51), merge-train landing (100), run records/dashboard. New: unaudited-range computation, threshold trigger, the audit prompt, an audit run role flag.

Sequenced after the phase-15 deletion pass (163) so the audit flow is built on the post-deletion mechanical substrate and red audit worktrees route to :reviewing rather than the deprecated repair loop.

task.title: Lander.Worker ignores the runtime landing override — dashboard auto-land fails with :no_target_branch
acceptance_criteria: Lander.Worker.perform/1 builds the land request from LandingSettings.overlay(project), not the raw registry entry
Regression test: project registered :manual/no-target + persisted :auto override lands via Worker.perform/1
Control test: no override -> {:error, :no_target_branch} still surfaces (Oban retries)
task.body: Found live 2026-06-03 while salvaging rmap task 41 (run-1780445879568-5820b2e9): Harness.Run applies Landing.Settings.overlay/1 at init (run.ex:461), so the green-settle trigger enqueues landing jobs for dashboard-flipped projects — but Harness.Lander.Worker re-resolves the project via ProjectRegistry.lookup/1 WITHOUT the overlay, so the lander sees the raw registration (landing_policy: :manual, target_branch: nil) and every landing job fails {:error, :no_target_branch} → 3 Oban retries → discarded. Any project whose auto-land is set from the dashboard (rather than registration-time config) can never land. Fix: apply LandingSettings.overlay/1 to the looked-up project in Lander.Worker.perform/1, mirroring run.ex. Regression test: registered :manual/nil project + persisted :auto override → Worker.perform lands; control case without override still surfaces :no_target_branch.
task.implemented: Lander.Worker.perform/1 applies LandingSettings.overlay/1 to the looked-up project (mirroring run.ex init); regression test (registered :manual/nil + persisted :auto override lands via Worker.perform/1) and control test (no override still surfaces :no_target_branch) in worker_test.exs

task.title: Lander: land a branch that is checked out in a retained run worktree (worktree add --detach)
acceptance_criteria: Lander.land/1 checks out the landing worktree detached (or by SHA), never by branch name
Regression test: branch checked out in another worktree + landing job -> lands successfully
Existing lander tests (ff-push, rebase, post-merge-red, conflict, push-rejected reland) stay green
task.body: Found live 2026-06-03 during the same task-41 salvage: a failed run retains its worktree (by design, for salvage), and that worktree has the run branch checked out. When an operator then enqueues a landing job for that branch (the manual-salvage workflow in docs/dogfooding-workflow.md), the lander's checkout fails: git worktree add <landing-path> <branch> -> 'fatal: <branch> is already used by worktree at <run worktree>'. Green runs never hit this (their worktree is removed at settle, before the landing job is enqueued), but the salvage path always does. Fix: the lander does not need the branch checked out, only its commit — use git worktree add --detach (or resolve the branch tip and add by SHA), so landing never collides with a retained run worktree. Push semantics unchanged (the lander pushes the rebased tip SHA to origin/<target>).

task.title: Deterministic full-pipeline E2E test: roadmap task → Oban dispatch → run → verify → review → land → writeback in one flow
acceptance_criteria: One test flow drives: fixture project with rmap roadmap → Run.Worker/Oban dispatch → worktree provision → FakeAdapter commits a real diff → check stack grades green → landing trigger enqueues on the serialized landing queue → Lander.Worker pushes to a local bare origin → fixture roadmap task marked done + ResultStore run record persisted
Red-path variant: scripted implementer delivers a red worktree, run enters :reviewing, a scripted reviewer (FakeAdapter branch) fixes it inline, the stack re-grades green, the run lands
Exercises Lander.Worker.perform/1 (not Lander.land/1 directly) so the Task 171 class of seam bug — runtime landing override applied by Run but not by the lander — cannot recur silently
Runs without real agent CLIs or network; Postgres-dependent portions tagged :integration consistent with the existing Oban tests
No Process.sleep synchronization — assert_receive / poll-until-condition only
out_of_scope: Live agent CLIs (separate follow-up task)
Dashboard LiveView assertions
Multi-project concurrent dispatch scenarios
task.body:
Every pipeline seam is tested pairwise today (run_test, oban_dispatch_test, lander_test, run_landing_trigger_test) but no test crosses all of them in one flow: roadmap task → Oban dispatch → Run gen_statem → agent commit → verification → reviewer routing → landing → roadmap/result-store writeback.

The escaped-bug evidence is cross-seam by nature: Task 171 (Run applies LandingSettings.overlay/1 at init, Lander.Worker re-resolves the project without it → every dashboard-flipped auto-land fails) and Task 172 (retained run worktree blocks the lander's branch checkout) both live in the gaps BETWEEN pairwise-tested stages — as did the week of lifecycle bugs (153–163) that settled the reviewer-pair architecture. A deterministic full-pipeline test is the guard for that class.

All scaffolding exists: FakeAdapter (:write / :write_then_hang branches commit real diffs in real worktrees), GitFixture (throwaway repos + local bare origins), ProjectFixture, the tiny elixir_project fixture, DataCase. The task is wiring them into one assertion chain, green path + red→reviewing→green path.

Sequenced after Task 171 so the E2E test lands against a fixed Lander.Worker (otherwise its own acceptance criterion fails on a known bug).
task.implemented: Hand-built inline in 3 commits: eea3fdc extracts GitFixture.init_with_origin/1 (dedup of the bare-origin fixture in lander_test + lander/worker_test); 27d4d1a adds test/harness/pipeline_e2e_test.exs green path (roadmap task -> Run.Worker.perform -> FakeAdapter :write in a real worktree -> check stack green -> seam-captured landing job -> Lander.Worker.perform -> ff-push to bare origin -> rmap writeback done/verified/shipped_in + ResultStore record); ecbf37e adds the red->reviewing->green path (:repair_noop implementer grades red, cross-family reviewer double fixes inline, re-verification grades green, the reviewed tree lands) + CHANGELOG. Runs in the default suite (no Postgres needed — all Oban interaction seam-captured, satisfying the :integration criterion vacuously), no Process.sleep, exercises Lander.Worker.perform/1 not Lander.land/1.

task.title: Live-agent E2E smoke test: one real headless agent CLI through the full pipeline, :integration/:live_agent tagged
acceptance_criteria: Tagged both :integration and :live_agent — excluded from the default suite and mix precommit; run via mix test.json --include live_agent
Fails loudly with flunk + setup instructions (CLI install command, auth step) when the agent CLI is missing or unauthenticated — never skips silently

Drives one real headless agent (default Claude, adapter selectable via env var) through the same chain as Task 173: trivial fixture task → dispatch → worktree → real agent commit → reviewer AI gate (writes .harness/review.json) → land to a local bare origin
Wall-clock bounded: trivial prompt + per-test total_timeout override so a hung CLI cannot stall the run beyond ~5 minutes
out_of_scope: Running in CI or the default suite
Cross-adapter matrix (all six agents) — one adapter proves the live seam; per-adapter scoring is owned by AgentKPI/CapabilityScore re-keyed to reviewer outcomes
Asserting anything about the agent's code quality — the reviewer's .harness/review.json verdict is the only assertion
task.body:
The deterministic pipeline E2E (Task 173) proves every harness seam with a scripted agent; this task adds the one seam it cannot prove — a real agent CLI invoked over a Port produces a commit that flows through the reviewer gate and landing. User-requested 2026-06-03 alongside Task 173.

This formalizes what daily dogfooding runs prove ad hoc into a repeatable, on-demand check: run it when upgrading an agent CLI version, changing an adapter's build_command, or validating a new host. It is hand-run by design (quota cost, host CLI + auth required), which is why it carries the handbuild marker and lives outside the default suite.

Reuses Task 173's fixture/wiring; the only new surface is the live-CLI invocation path and the missing-credential flunk guard (per the integration-test never-skip-silently rule).

task.title: Agent-gate workflow rebuild: reviewer AI is THE gate, no mechanical verification anywhere
acceptance_criteria: Run lifecycle is dispatched -> running -> committing -> reviewing -> done|failed; :verifying is deleted; reasons are :approved / {:review_rejected, report} / {:review_stuck, report}

The cross-family reviewer AI gets worktree + task + AC + implementer transcript tail + diff stat + the project's check_command hint, runs the checks itself, fixes inline, and writes .harness/review.json (verdict/report/ratings); harness reads it mechanically (Harness.Run.Review)
Reviewer prompt biases fix-and-approve as the near-absolute default; rejection is reserved for unsalvageable work and puts the task back in the queue
.harness/ is excluded from commits and diff measurement; reviewer_diff_size (0 = first-attempt pass) is carried on Result/LogRecord

Harness.Verification, Harness.CheckStack, presets, review_green, max_review_iterations, lander re-verification, the benchmark corpus, and CapabilityBenchmarkScheduler are deleted whole (no shims, no back-compat)
Project carries check_command (free-text reviewer hint) instead of check_stacks/preset
Lander uses a detached worktree, never re-verifies, and enqueues the post-merge audit job after a successful push
run_records store verdict approve/reject + review_report/review_ratings/reviewer_diff_size (migration); AgentKPI/CapabilityScore re-keyed to reviewer outcomes
Full offline suite green; mix precommit.full green; docs (CLAUDE.md, README, docs/agent-gate-workflow.md, dogfooding-workflow.md, SKILL.md, playbooks, agent rules, CHANGELOG) re-keyed
out_of_scope: Synchronous implementer-rebuttal round after a rejection (doubles wall-clock; revisit only if false-rejection data demands it)
Rejection-report writeback to the rmap task (needs an rmap CLI surface - filed in ../rmap/'s roadmap)
task.body: THE architecture decision (2026-06-03, settled - docs/agent-gate-workflow.md is the spec): everything that interprets meaning is an agent's job, never harness code. Every run-lifecycle bug from 2026-05-26 to 06-03 (tasks 153-163, 168, 169, 171, 172) traced to harness verification/lifecycle machinery; zero traced to agent judgment. The fix is deletion + moving the gate into a cross-family reviewer AI, not improving the machinery. Supersedes tasks 164/166/169/170/172 and the v0_11 reviewer-pair design (review_green / :verifying / mechanical re-verification). Plan anchor: ~/.claude/plans/agent-gate-workflow-rebuild.md.
task.implemented: Hand-built across 6 batches (2026-06-03, uncommitted on development pending operator review). Run lifecycle rewritten: committing->reviewing with Harness.Run.Review reading .harness/review.json (verdict/report/ratings); reasons :approved/{:review_rejected,r}/{:review_stuck,r}. Deleted whole: Harness.Verification(+check/result/verdict), CheckStack(+presets), :verifying, review_green, max_review_iterations, lander re-verification, benchmark corpus + scheduler. Project gained check_command. Lander: detached worktree, no reverify, enqueues audit job. run_records migration (verdict approve/reject, review_report/review_ratings/reviewer_diff_size); AgentKPI/CapabilityScore re-keyed.
