Suite 1218/1218 green, coverage 80.01%. Docs/playbooks/agent-rules/SKILL/README/CHANGELOG re-keyed. Spec: docs/agent-gate-workflow.md.

task.title: Post-merge audit agent: per-land enqueue, third-family auditor, audit(...) commits ff-pushed
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Audit (mechanics): detached worktree of origin/<target>; unaudited range = last commit whose subject matches ^audit\( (falling back to the land's base_sha) -> HEAD; rev-list count 0 -> :noop; ff-push only if HEAD advanced
Auditor selection: first dispatchable agent not in {implementer, reviewer}; explicit :auditor request override supported (test seam)

The audit agent reuses audit-review conventions: .audit/<short-sha>.md report committed in the repo, single audit(<short-sha>): commit per pass, hygiene fixes committed inline; .harness/audit.json is read best-effort and never committed

Harness.Audit.Worker: thin Oban shell on the global :audit queue (limit 1), unique per project while available/scheduled; enqueued by the lander after each successful push with base_sha = pre-land origin/<target> tip
Best-effort by contract: an audit failure is logged and dropped - it never blocks, reverts, or re-runs a merge
Outcomes: {:audited, sha} / :noop / :no_changes / {:push_rejected, out} / {:skipped, r} / {:error, r}; covered by audit_test.exs (FakeAdapter auditor double) + audit/worker_test.exs
out_of_scope: Cron-triggered count/age thresholds (the superseded task 170 design - per-land enqueue replaces it)
False-rejection flagging from rejection-report history (wired in the KPI-ratings task)
task.body: Replaces superseded task 170, whose AC described the old design (cron thresholds, check-stack verification of the audit, merge-train landing). The rebuilt audit agent is the fourth stage of the agent-gate workflow: per-land enqueue, third-family agent, direct ff-push, never blocks. This is the autonomous version of the staged-review:audit-review skill the human runs by hand.
task.implemented: Hand-built as part of the agent-gate rebuild (Batch 3 + Batch 6 test seam). Harness.Audit (mechanics: detached worktree, audit(...)-marker range computation, third-family selection, :auditor/:auditor_opts test seam, ff-push only when HEAD advanced) + Harness.Audit.Worker (Oban :audit queue, unique per project, enqueued by lander post-push). Covered by audit_test.exs (10 tests incl. FakeAdapter {:audit, sha} double) + audit/worker_test.exs (8).

task.title: Reviewer KPI ratings feed AgentKPI/CapabilityScore rollups + reviewer rejection-rate tracking
acceptance_criteria: AgentKPI aggregates the reviewer's ratings block (performance, truthfulness, code_quality, idiom_usage) per implementer agent alongside the existing success/first-attempt-pass/duration/cost rollups
CapabilityScore incorporates mean ratings per (agent, domain) so dispatch-recommend routing reflects reviewer-judged quality, not just approve rate
Per-agent rejection rate AS REVIEWER is tracked (reviewer_adapter on run_records), so a reviewer with a high rejection rate can be deprioritized in cross-family selection
The post-merge audit prompt receives the rejection-report history for tasks in its range (run_records query), enabling it to flag false rejections
Dashboard KPI view renders the ratings columns
out_of_scope: Changing the reviewer prompt or the .harness/review.json contract (already shipped in the rebuild)
Automatic reviewer blacklisting - routing stays advisory (dispatch-recommend)
task.body: The rebuild already parses + persists the reviewer's ratings (review_ratings on run_records); this task makes them load-bearing. Since rejection is near-never by design, approve/reject rate is NOT the implementer quality signal - the ratings and reviewer_diff_size are. Reviewers get rated too: false-rejection flagging closes the loop (defense #3 in the rebuild plan). Depends on the rebuild task.
task.implemented: Reviewer KPI ratings feed AgentKPI/CapabilityScore rollups + reviewer rejection-rate tracking; prioritize_reviewers/2 sinks high-rejection reviewers. Cherry-picked onto development, run_test.exs conflict (177 prioritize tests vs 182 rename) resolved keeping both.

task.title: Formalize Harness.Dashboard.Transcript.Parser as a behaviour (@callback new/feed/finalize)
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Dashboard.Transcript.Parser defines @callback new() :: state, @callback feed(state, iodata()) :: {[event()], state}, @callback finalize(state) :: {[event()], state}
All 6 parser modules (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Pi, Passthrough) declare @behaviour Harness.Dashboard.Transcript.Parser with @impl true on each callback

mix reach.check --smells no longer reports the transcript-parser behaviour_candidate finding
Existing parser tests pass unchanged
task.body: Found by mix reach.check --smells (behaviour_candidate): the 6 per-agent transcript parsers expose the same 3 public callbacks (new/0, feed/2, finalize/1) by convention only - the dispatcher pattern-matches on agent_kind but nothing enforces the contract at compile time. Formalizing it as a behaviour matches the project's AgentAdapter idiom: adding a new agent parser gets callback conformance checking for free. Pure mechanical change, no runtime behavior difference.

The 5 NDJSON parsers (Claude/Codex/Cursor/Grok/Pi) 'use' it via a __using__ macro that generates all three over a new Harness.LineParser (extracted NDJSON line-buffer+Jason.decode loop); Passthrough declares @behaviour with hand-written @impl. Doc-only, no behavior change. This task will be marked superseded and its worktree discarded after the smoke run — it exists only to exercise dispatch -> implement -> review -> verdict end to end.

task.title: Settled-:failed run teardown kills the Oban worker before {:cancel} returns -> wrongful retry storm (up to max_attempts=20)
acceptance_criteria: A settled :failed run (reject or review_stuck) results in the Oban job reaching a terminal non-retry state (cancelled/discarded) even when run teardown kills linked processes - no re-dispatch of the same task

Identify and sever whatever link path lets the run-teardown :killed reach the Oban worker task (decouple the worker's await from the run's kill blast radius, e.g. trap/convert the kill to {:cancel}, or stop subscribing via a linked pid), or guard the worker so a post-settle kill cannot override an already-determined {:cancel}
max_attempts for dispatch jobs reflects crash-only intent (a settled failure never retries; only genuine pre-settle crashes do, bounded by @max_mechanical_attempts)
Regression test: a run that settles :failed while its teardown brutally kills a monitored/linked helper process yields a cancelled Oban job and exactly one run record - no second attempt

cleanup_for_run/2 (and the orphan-rescue/retry path that invokes it) refuses to remove the worktree+branch of a run_id whose gen_statem is still alive - a live run_id is never cleaned; regression test: invoking the retry/rescue cleanup against a live run leaves its worktree+branch intact (the 2026-06-03 job-118 live-worktree-destruction case)
out_of_scope: The reviewer-not-writing-review.json root cause (separate task)
Changing the reviewer verdict artifact contract
task.body: Discovered 2026-06-03 by the first live dogfood dispatch (rmap task 42, Oban job 115). worker.ex:149 maps a settled %Result{state: :failed} to {:cancel, reason} so a rejected/review_stuck run discards the Oban job WITHOUT retry (crash-only design). But the run is started under RunSupervisor (DynamicSupervisor) and the worker only Process.monitor/1's it, yet on run teardown the run kills its linked MCP-transport/port processes with :killed (observed: 5x 'MCP transport details: %{reason: :killed}' at the exact instant the worker died), and that :killed propagated to the Oban worker task as '(EXIT from #PID<...>) killed' BEFORE result_to_oban could return {:cancel}. Oban cannot distinguish that kill from a genuine crash, so it recorded a job error and retried. With Oban.Worker max_attempts: 20 (worker.ex:6), one stuck review re-dispatched the entire ~16-min / ~5M-token claude run; run-1780488946905-b4d8528e settled :review_stuck, then attempt 3 (run-1780489665468-c6c70259) re-ran task 42 from scratch, blind. EVIDENCE: run_records row for run-1780488946905-b4d8528e shows state=failed, reason={:review_stuck,...}, agent_outcome_kind={:timed_out,:idle}, duration_ms=949457; Oban job 115 errors=[{attempt:2, error: '** (EXIT from #PID<0.754.0>) killed'}]. This is the mechanical-substrate defect class the agent-gate explicitly owns (kill propagation / Oban retry arithmetic), NOT a judgment call. Note @max_mechanical_attempts caps SETUP-failure retries via setup_failure_disposition, but an in-perform process kill bypasses that path and falls to raw Oban max_attempts. SECOND MANIFESTATION (2026-06-03, Oban job 118, run-1780493075738-47851ce5, task 183 smoke test) — WORSE than a wasteful retry: a retry/rescue invocation ran Worktree.cleanup_for_run/2 (worktree.ex:424, the ONLY git-branch deleter in the codebase: `git worktree remove --force` + `git branch -D`) against a STILL-LIVE run, destroying its worktree dir AND harness/<run-id> branch mid-flight. Codex implemented cleanly (14-line diff, mix precommit green=1229 passed, exit 0) and the run reached :reviewing with Cursor correctly auto-selected (Pi-exclusion working); the reviewer's Driver.run then hit {:worktree_missing} -> {:review_stuck, 'Reviewer failed to run'}, and terminal retain failed with {:marker_write_failed, .harness-retained, :enoent} (dir already gone). RULED OUT: codex's own 20 commands (none deleted the worktree), and the full test suite (worktree/sweeper tests are GitFixture-isolated to temp repos, never the real checkout). So the deleter is harness runtime; cleanup_for_run is the unique dir+branch deleter. worker.ex cleanup_prior_attempt only calls it on a {:start_run_failed,_} prior reason and THIS run's start_run succeeded — so the trigger is a separate attempt/orphan-rescue re-attempting job 118 while attempt-1's gen_statem was still alive (suspects: oban.ex rescue_orphaned_run_jobs / rescue_executing_run_jobs, oban.ex:147/225). ADDED INVARIANT: cleanup_for_run (and any retry/rescue) MUST refuse to act on a run_id whose gen_statem is still alive (liveness-check RunSupervisor/Registry before remove+branch-delete); and a one-shot Dispatch.task should not ride the 20-attempt retry path at all.
task.implemented: Crash-only dispatch hardening (criteria 1-4; criterion 5's cleanup_for_run liveness guard shipped in 5d1d691). Found there is NO link path from Run.Worker to the run's kill blast radius: the worker MONITORS (never links) the gen_statem, which drives agents in async_nolink tasks — a settling run's :killed teardown (OSProcess.kill + Port.close) cannot EXIT the worker. Documented monitor-not-link as the guard; lowered Oban max_attempts 20->5 (@max_dispatch_attempts = @max_mechanical_attempts) so an uncaught worker crash can't re-run a multi-hour job at the old ceiling (snoozes self-bump max_attempts, so setup-retry path unaffected). Regression test: a :failed run that brutally kills a linked helper still yields {:cancel}, no second attempt.

task.title: Reviewer can finish work but skip writing .harness/review.json and idle-timeout -> run lost to :review_stuck
acceptance_criteria: Reviewer prompt/playbook instructs the reviewer that writing .harness/review.json is the mandatory FINAL action of the review, before exiting, even when it made fixes - with the exact schema {verdict, report, ratings}

Reviewing-phase idle/total timeout accounts for the time a reviewer needs to run the project check_command (cargo test / mix precommit.full) without going idle-killed mid-check, or the check run resets the idle watchdog
When the reviewer commits changes but writes no verdict, the failure remains a loud :review_stuck (no inferring approve from a clean diff) - assert this stays true
A live or simulated reviewer run that makes fixes ends with a valid review.json and the run settles on its verdict, not :review_stuck
out_of_scope: The Oban retry-storm bug (separate task)
Inferring a verdict from commits/diff in harness code - forbidden by the agent-gate architecture
task.body: Discovered 2026-06-03 (rmap task 42, run-1780488946905-b4d8528e). The cross-family reviewer (Pi) reviewed AND committed 274 lines of fixes (review_iterations=1, reviewer_diff_size=274), but never wrote the .harness/review.json verdict artifact and then went idle until the watchdog fired (agent_outcome_kind={:timed_out,:idle}, ~15.8 min wall). Harness correctly settled :failed {:review_stuck, 'Reviewer wrote no .harness/review.json verdict artifact.'} - the gate did its job - but the run's work was discarded and (compounded by the retry-storm bug) the task re-dispatched. The verdict-artifact write is the single load-bearing mechanical output of the reviewer; the reviewer prompt/playbook must make it the non-negotiable FINAL step (write review.json before any other closing action), and the idle watchdog window for the reviewing phase may be too tight for a reviewer running a project's full check_command (rmap = cargo fmt+clippy+test). Per agent-gate philosophy the fix is in the reviewer PROMPT (make the artifact write unconditional + last) plus watchdog tuning - NOT a code classifier inferring a verdict from commits. This task also motivated excluding Pi as a reviewer for now (done separately in lib/harness/run.ex).
task.implemented: Two-part agent-gate fix (no verdict inference — forbidden). (1) Reviewer prompt (run.ex reviewer_prompt/1): the .harness/review.json write is reframed as the unconditional FINAL action — explicit warning that exiting/going idle without it discards the entire run regardless of fixes made; step 4 is now 'LAST, after every fix and check is done'. (2) Reviewing-phase idle floor: new reviewer_idle_timeout/1 floors the idle window at 10 min (@reviewer_idle_floor 600_000) so a silent cold check_command run (cargo test / mix precommit.full) can't idle-kill the reviewer before it writes the verdict; nil→floor, lower override→raised, higher override + :infinity preserved; threaded via reviewer_driver_opts/1. Tests: prompt asserts the FINAL/mandatory/idle language via review_capture_prompt; 4 idle-floor unit tests; :review_stuck-stays-loud (missing+malformed) and reviewer-makes-fixes-then-writes-verdict were already covered. 66/66 run_test green.

task.title: Settings page: per-agent reviewer-eligibility toggle (distinct from implementer enable) + select_reviewer consults it
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Agent.Settings gains reviewer_eligible?/1 + set_reviewer_eligible/2, persisted, defaulting from config :harness, :reviewer_exclude (pi ineligible by default) so the stopgap behavior is preserved on first boot
select_reviewer/1 (auto and explicit paths) refuses an agent that is not reviewer_eligible?, with a clear settle reason when no eligible cross-family reviewer exists
An agent can be enabled as implementer yet ineligible as reviewer (the two toggles are independent) - covered by a test
SettingsLive renders a per-agent matrix with implementer-enable and reviewer-eligible toggles; flipping reviewer-eligible persists and immediately affects the next dispatch's reviewer selection
The static :reviewer_exclude config read in run.ex is removed once the persisted setting is authoritative (no two sources of truth)
out_of_scope: Per-project reviewer overrides (this is global per-agent; per-project can be a follow-up)
Changing the cross-family constraint or the verdict artifact contract
The retry-storm and verdict-artifact bugs (Tasks 180/181)
task.body: User-requested 2026-06-03 during the first live dogfood session. Make reviewer selection operator-configurable from the dashboard settings page instead of code/config. Today select_reviewer/1 (lib/harness/run.ex) auto-picks the first dispatchable cross-family agent, gated by reviewer_dispatchable? = available? and installed? and reviewer_enabled?; reviewer_enabled? currently reuses the GLOBAL AgentSettings.enabled? flag, which conflates 'can implement' with 'can review'. The immediate need (exclude Pi as reviewer until OSS models are stronger) shipped as a stopgap static config (config :harness, :reviewer_exclude, default [:pi]) read in run.ex - this task replaces that stopgap with a persisted, UI-editable per-agent setting. DESIGN: add a distinct reviewer_eligible?/1 + set_reviewer_eligible/2 to Harness.Agent.Settings (so an agent like Pi can stay enabled as an implementer while being ineligible as a reviewer); seed defaults from the :reviewer_exclude config so existing behavior is preserved (pi ineligible by default); have reviewer_dispatchable?/explicit path consult reviewer_eligible? instead of (or in addition to) the static exclude; render a per-agent matrix on SettingsLive with two columns - 'enabled (implementer)' and 'eligible (reviewer)'. Persisted via the agent settings store (coordinate with Task 165's settings-store consolidation - the eligibility flag should live wherever agent settings land). Handbuild (LiveView/settings UI per the dogfooding UI rule).
task.implemented: Per-agent reviewer eligibility, distinct from implementer enable. Agent.Settings gains reviewer_eligible?/1 + reviewer_ineligible?/1 + reviewer_ineligible_agents/0 + set_reviewer_eligible/3, persisted as a reviewer_ineligible set in agent_settings.term, seeded from :reviewer_exclude config ([:pi]) until an operator override is written (persisted [] overrides the seed). run.ex reviewer_dispatchable? now consults reviewer_eligible? (static reviewer_excluded? deleted; :reviewer_exclude no longer read in run.ex). SettingsLive renders a per-agent enabled+reviewer toggle matrix with eligibility pill + toggle_reviewer_eligible handler; tokens.ex adds .agent-controls layout. Tests in settings_test/run_test/settings_live_test; browser-verified the live toggle flip on /harness/settings.

task.title: Smoke test (throwaway): add Harness.LineBuffer.empty?/1 predicate + test
acceptance_criteria: `Harness.LineBuffer.empty?/1` exists with an `@spec` and a `@doc`.
New ExUnit assertions cover both the empty and non-empty buffer cases.
`mix precommit` passes clean (format, compile --warnings-as-errors, credo --strict, doctor, test, sobelow).
task.body:
THROWAWAY agent-gate smoke-test payload — exists only to exercise the live dispatch -> implementer -> reviewer -> verdict loop end to end with a real, reviewable diff. Will be superseded once the run settles; the work is NOT expected to land (project landing_policy is :manual). Keep the change minimal and self-contained.

Add a small, spec'd convenience predicate to `lib/harness/line_buffer.ex`:

    @spec empty?(binary()) :: boolean()
    def empty?(buffer) when is_binary(buffer), do: buffer == ""

It reports whether the line buffer currently holds a pending partial line (i.e. whether `take_remainder/1` would yield no trailing fragment). Add a one-line `@doc` (no IO in examples; a doctest is fine since this is pure and API-shape only). Add focused ExUnit assertions in `test/harness/line_buffer_test.exs` covering the empty (`true`) and non-empty (`false`) cases.

task.title: Expand the descripex/MCP orchestrator surface (inventory first, then read/observe, then a deliberate write subset)
acceptance_criteria: An inventory exists (doc or task note) listing every function currently `api()`-annotated / reachable via Harness.Manifest + the MCP server + Harness.Chat.Tools, against the orchestrator-desired set, with the gap explicitly called out.

All identified read/observe operations (roadmap browse, run status/transcript, AgentKPI + CapabilityScore rollups, project/registry listing) are `api()`-annotated and reachable via BOTH Harness.Chat.Tools and the MCP server.

The chosen write-operation subset (dispatch / cancel / hold-steer-resume / project registration) is annotated, each with a one-line rationale, plus an explicit note of what was intentionally left unexposed and why.
No `api()` annotation returns a JUDGMENT value (is-this-done / is-this-good / whose-fault / should-this-merge); a reviewer can confirm every newly-exposed function is mechanical.
skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md updated to document the expanded surface (existing mandate: any public driver-surface change updates the SKILL).
In-run agent rules and the dispatch path are unchanged: implementer/reviewer agents working inside a target-project worktree still receive NO harness-control MCP tools.
task.body:
The primary user is an AI orchestrator (CLAUDE.md), driving harness via the descripex `api()`-annotated surface exposed as MCP (Harness.Manifest -> Harness.Dashboard.MCPServer) and the in-process Harness.Chat.Tools dispatcher. Today an orchestrator can self-serve only the subset currently annotated; everything else needs hand-written chat-tool glue or a human in IEx. Demand signal is direct, not speculative: the AI user asked for this during the 2026-06-03 #180 session — for an AI-native orchestrator the primary consumer IS the demand.

Do it in three steps, cheapest first:

1. INVENTORY (do first). Enumerate what is currently `api()`-annotated / MCP-callable vs. what an orchestrator would want callable. Produce the gap list BEFORE annotating anything — we do not yet know the actual gap.

2. READ/OBSERVE surface — expand generously. Roadmap browse, run status + transcript, AgentKPI + CapabilityScore rollups, project/registry listing. These are pure-mechanical, low-blast-radius, high-leverage; annotate them all.

3. WRITE subset — expose DELIBERATELY, not blanket. Dispatch, cancel, hold/steer/resume, project registration. Each is a real action an autonomous agent can trigger; pick the considered set and document the omissions.

Guardrails (agent-gate doctrine — see CLAUDE.md "Judgment Lives in Agents"):
- descripex describes MECHANICAL surfaces only. NEVER annotate an `api()` that returns a JUDGMENT (is-this-done / is-this-good / whose-fault / should-this-merge). Expose "merge this branch" (mechanical), never "should this merge?" (judgment). The gate is not "how much descripex" but "expose mechanics, let the agent supply judgment."
- Scope to ORCHESTRATOR agents only. In-run implementer/reviewer agents (working in a worktree on the target project) must NOT get the harness-control MCP surface — handing the agent implementing a task the ability to cancel/dispatch/steer runs is a footgun and a recursion risk.
- Each `api()` is a contract: any change to the public driver surface must update skills/harness-driver/SKILL.md.
- Watch context bloat: a fat MCP tool list costs tokens on every orchestrator turn. If the surface grows large, prefer a deferred/search-tool pattern (like harness's own ToolSearch) over dumping every tool into every context.

Parked in phase 6 (deferred) on purpose: this is a high-leverage ENABLER, not a blocker — the agent-gate loop works today without it (validated end-to-end on the 2026-06-03 smoke test). Revisit after the active v0_12 cut; left unpinned from any milestone so it does not inflate v0_12.
task.implemented: Agent-delivered (claude impl, cross-family reviewer approved, ratings 9/9/9/9). Added 4 mechanical write tools to Harness.Dispatch (dispatch-hold/steer/resume/register_project), each rationale'd; read/observe surface confirmed already complete (generic over Manifest.mcp_tools/1, no manifest/chat.tools/mcp_server edits needed); docs/orchestrator-surface-inventory.md inventory + 2 gaps; SKILL.md updated; in-run isolation unchanged. No judgment apis. Landed locally (cherry-pick onto development).

task.title: Same-BEAM :DOWN reaper reclaims the worktree+branch a live-run cleanup-refusal leaks when that run later crashes
acceptance_criteria: A run whose cleanup_for_run/2 was correctly refused (live gen_statem, the Task 180 liveness guard) and which then CRASHES has its worktree dir + harness/<run-id> branch reclaimed within the node's lifetime — not left until the next boot-time Harness.Worktree.Sweeper pass

The reaper distinguishes a CRASHED run (reclaim) from a SETTLED-:failed run (retain worktree+branch by design, for manual salvage per docs/dogfooding-workflow.md) — a :failed run that finishes cleanly must NOT have its worktree reaped
Mechanism is a same-BEAM signal (e.g. monitor the Run.Registry entry / Run.Supervisor child and act on the :DOWN), not a new poll loop duplicating the Sweeper
Regression test: a monitored run that crashes (abnormal exit, no settled Result) triggers worktree+branch reclamation; a run that settles :failed and exits normally leaves its worktree+branch intact
No double-free: reaper and boot Sweeper cannot both delete the same worktree (idempotent — a missing dir/branch is a no-op, not an error)
out_of_scope: The cleanup-refusal liveness guard itself (Task 180 — this task builds ON it, reclaiming what it correctly refuses to touch)
Changing the settled-:failed worktree-retention policy (retention is intended; only crashed-run leaks are in scope)
Replacing the boot-time Harness.Worktree.Sweeper (the reaper complements it for in-node lifetime; boot sweep stays the cross-boot backstop)
task.body:
Surfaced by the audit of commit 5d1d691 (.audit/5d1d691-liveness-guard-cleanup.md, finding #1, pri 6, worktree.ex:443). The Task-180 liveness guard makes cleanup_for_run/2 correctly REFUSE to remove the worktree+branch of a run whose gen_statem is still alive (fixing the job-118 live-worktree-destruction). That refusal trades a catastrophic failure (destroying a live checkout) for a recoverable one (a leaked worktree) — but the recovery today is BOOT-ONLY: if the refused run then crashes via the worker's crashed-result path (run/worker.ex:192-201, the {:DOWN,...} branch — no finish_worktree/2), its worktree dir + harness/<run-id> branch survive until the next Harness.Worktree.Sweeper pass at boot (worktree/sweeper.ex:46-58). A long-running harness node accumulates leaked worktrees between boots. There is no same-BEAM Run.Registry / Run.Supervisor :DOWN reaper to close the gap within the node's lifetime.

CRITICAL NUANCE (the reason this is design work, not a one-liner): a reaper MUST distinguish a *crashed* run (no settled Result — reclaim the worktree) from a *settled-:failed* run (reject / review_stuck — RETAIN the worktree+branch by design, so a human/agent can salvage the rejected work per docs/dogfooding-workflow.md). A naive "reap on any :DOWN" would destroy exactly the retained-for-salvage worktrees the agent-gate intends to keep. So the reaper needs the settled-vs-crashed signal (e.g. the run records its terminal disposition before exit, or the monitor correlates against the ResultStore record / a retained-marker file) before deleting anything.

This is mechanical-substrate lifecycle work the agent-gate explicitly owns (worktrees, git, process monitoring) — NOT a judgment call. Complements, does not replace, the boot Sweeper.
task.implemented: Harness.Worktree.Reaper GenServer (same-BEAM crash reaper). Run tracks at worktree-activate (run.ex dispatched->running), untracks in settle/2. On an ABNORMAL :DOWN it reaps via Worktree.cleanup_for_run iff not retained? — distinguishing crashed (reclaim) from settled-:failed (retain for salvage); idempotent so it can't double-free with the boot Sweeper. Closes the within-node leak gap the boot Sweeper only covers across restarts. Gated by :worktree,:reap_on_crash (off in test). 4 tests: crash reaps worktree+branch, retained kept, :normal kept, untracked kept.

task.title: Neuter the push remote in harness-created worktrees so in-run agents can't push/PR past landing_policy
acceptance_criteria: When harness creates a run worktree, the worktree's git config has no usable push path to origin (e.g. `remote.origin.pushurl` set to an invalid/no-op sentinel, or origin push refspec removed) — a `git push` run from inside the worktree fails locally without touching the network.
The lander is UNAFFECTED: it lands from its own detached worktree / the main checkout, not the run worktree, so neutering the run worktree's push remote does not break auto-landing on :auto projects.
Fetch still works in the run worktree (reviewer may need to fetch origin/<target> for context) — only PUSH is neutered.
A regression test asserts that a `git push origin HEAD` invoked with the run worktree's cwd/config exits non-zero and makes no network call, while the same repo's main checkout can still push.
No judgment added to harness code: this is a mechanical git-config guard applied at worktree creation, not a policy decision evaluated at runtime.
task.body:
FINDING (2026-06-04): in-run implementer/reviewer agents have unrestricted shell inside their worktree (that's how the reviewer runs `cargo test`, commits fixes, etc.). Nothing stops one from also running `git push` or `gh pr create` to origin on its own initiative. This was observed on the rmap project: rmap is `landing_policy: :manual`, the harness lander never touched origin, yet task-41 work (commit 69fc726, authored+committed by the in-run `harness@localhost` identity) reached GitHub and had to be pulled back manually. The agent pushed it, bypassing the manual-landing intent.

This violates the agent-gate doctrine that MERGE is the lander's mechanical, policy-gated job — not something an implementer/reviewer can do unilaterally. A `:manual` project should never have anything reach origin except by an explicit operator action.

FIX (mechanical substrate, NOT judgment): at worktree-creation time, neuter the push path in the run worktree's local git config so an agent's `git push` fails locally (e.g. set `remote.origin.pushurl` to a no-op sentinel like `/dev/null` or an invalid URL, or drop the push refspec). Keep fetch intact (reviewer may fetch origin/<target>). The lander is unaffected because it lands from its own detached worktree, not the run worktree.

This does NOT add a runtime branch/classifier/policy-evaluation to harness code — it's a deterministic git-config write applied uniformly at worktree setup, same class as the worktree/branch mechanics already there. `gh pr create` is harder to fully block (it uses the gh token, not the git remote); the push-remote neuter covers the `git push` vector, and a follow-up note should flag that `gh` auth in the run env is a separate, broader surface (consider scrubbing GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN from the in-run env via the existing Invocation.env scrub pairs).

Marked handbuild: touches worktree-creation substrate while the run lifecycle is still being hardened (180/185 just landed); hand-build per the dogfooding scaffolding exception.
task.implemented: Push-neuter at worktree creation: Worktree.neuter_push/1 enables extensions.worktreeConfig + sets remote.origin.pushurl=/dev/null via 'git config --worktree', scoped to the run worktree's config.worktree only. In-run agent 'git push' fails locally (no network); fetch, the operator's main checkout, and the lander's detached worktree all still push. Regression test in worktree_test.exs asserts all four invariants.

task.title: Flip Antigravity worktree_isolation to true — agy 1.0.5 honors port cwd (Task 32 finding is stale)
acceptance_criteria: Antigravity.capabilities/0 returns worktree_isolation: true; Harness.Worktree.Isolation.validate(Antigravity) returns :ok (no longer rejects dispatch)
worktree_isolation_limitation/0 is removed; the moduledoc § 'Working directory / workspace' is rewritten to state agy honors the port cwd as of 1.0.5 (cite the re-test)
antigravity_test.exs is updated (it currently asserts worktree_isolation: false and exercises worktree_isolation_limitation/0); the AgentAdapter.ConformanceCase still passes unchanged
docs/dogfooding-workflow.md no longer documents Antigravity as rejected-before-spawn

CONSCIOUS DECISION recorded in the implemented note: flipping to true makes Harness.Run trust the capability and SKIP the post-run main-checkout pollution check for Antigravity. Given agy's behavior already flipped once across a patch release, the implementer/reviewer must decide explicitly whether to (a) trust-and-skip per the current Isolation design, or (b) retain a pollution snapshot/check for Antigravity as belt-and-suspenders — and justify the choice.
out_of_scope: Fixing or working around the agy headless startup-hang flake — harness's timeout watchdog already covers it
Adding --add-dir/--sandbox flags to build_command/1 — the re-test shows the bare port cwd is sufficient; no flag earns its plumbing cost
Changing the Harness.Worktree.Isolation trust-vs-check design for OTHER adapters
task.body:
Task 32 (2026-05-22) declared `Antigravity` `worktree_isolation: false` because `agy` ignored the port cwd and resolved its workspace via git-common-dir, editing the *main checkout* instead of the run worktree. That finding is stale at agy 1.0.5.

Empirical re-test (2026-06-04, /tmp/agy-isolation-test.sh, exact harness setup: `git worktree add` linked worktree whose `.git` is a file pointing back to the common dir — the precise Task-32 trigger): 4/4 completed runs ISOLATED — baseline (no flags), `--add-dir <wt>`, `--sandbox`, and the combo. In every run agy's cwd was correctly the worktree and writes landed there with the main checkout clean. No flag is needed — the port `:cd` harness already sets (`AgentAdapter.invoke/2`) is now sufficient, so `build_command/1` does NOT need the worktree path threaded in. agy was fixed upstream somewhere across the undocumented 1.0.0→1.0.5 patch run (changelog only documents 1.0.0).

Side finding (do not fix here): one re-test run wedged agy at startup for 15+ min (empty log, no edit, no exit). That is an agy headless-reliability flake, already covered by harness's Port-close + timeout watchdog (termination is never derived from exit code). Not an isolation concern.

Make `Harness.AgentAdapter.Antigravity` declare worktree isolation and update everything that documented the limitation.
task.implemented:
Flipped `Harness.AgentAdapter.Antigravity.capabilities/0` to `worktree_isolation: true`, removed `worktree_isolation_limitation/0`, and rewrote the adapter's working-directory moduledoc around the 2026-06-04 `agy` 1.0.5 linked-worktree re-test. Updated adapter/isolation tests so Antigravity validates successfully, and removed the obsolete run test that expected pre-spawn rejection. Updated dogfooding / agent-reference / harness-driver docs so Antigravity is no longer documented as rejected-before-spawn.

CONSCIOUS DECISION: trust-and-skip per the current `Harness.Worktree.Isolation` design. Flipping Antigravity to `worktree_isolation: true` means `Harness.Run` will trust the capability and skip the post-run main-checkout pollution snapshot for Antigravity, just like the other shipped isolating adapters. I chose not to add an Antigravity-specific belt-and-suspenders pollution check because Task 187's re-test covers the exact linked-worktree failure mode, adding an adapter exception would undermine the existing capability contract, and changing the trust-vs-check design is explicitly out of scope for this task. If `agy` regresses again, the right fix is to flip the capability back or add a general correlation-based detector in a separate task, not silently special-case Antigravity here.

task.title: Scrub GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN from in-run env + assess the gh pr create vector (push-neuter follow-up)
acceptance_criteria: In-run invocation env scrubs GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN via the existing Invocation.env scrub pairs, so an in-run `gh` call has no ambient auth to reach origin/open a PR

Decision recorded: whether `gh pr create` is fully blocked by token-scrub alone, or whether a broader gh-auth isolation is needed (gh can read auth from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml independent of env vars)
Regression test asserts the scrub pairs remove both vars from the resolved in-run env
Worktree push-neuter (Task 186) covers `git push`; this task covers the `gh` vector it explicitly left open
out_of_scope: Re-litigating the git push neuter (Task 186, done)
A runtime policy classifier in harness code — this is a deterministic env scrub, same class as the existing Invocation.env mechanics
task.body:
Follow-up flagged by Task 186's own body (2026-06-04). Task 186 neutered `git push` in run worktrees via `remote.origin.pushurl=/dev/null` (worktree-scoped config), but `gh pr create` is a separate vector: it authenticates with the gh token, not the git remote, so the push-neuter does not stop an in-run agent from opening a PR to origin on its own initiative — still bypassing the lander / a `:manual` landing_policy.

FIX (mechanical substrate, NOT judgment): scrub GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN from the in-run invocation env using the existing Invocation.env set/scrub pairs (Task 25), so an in-run `gh` has no ambient token. Note gh can also read auth from `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` independent of env vars — record explicitly whether env-scrub is sufficient or whether broader gh-auth isolation (e.g. an empty GH_CONFIG_DIR in the run env) is warranted, and justify the choice.

Same agent-gate doctrine as 186: MERGE is the lander's mechanical, policy-gated job — an implementer/reviewer must not reach origin unilaterally.

task.title: Lander conflict-resolver agent: on rebase conflict, spawn a cross-family merge AI to resolve in-place instead of re-dispatching
acceptance_criteria: On a rebase conflict, the lander spawns a cross-family merge-resolver agent in the existing detached landing worktree (conflict markers left in place, MERGING state) instead of routing {:conflict,_} to re-dispatch.

The resolver is handed the conflicted file list, both sides (target = ours, the run's commit = theirs), and BOTH contributing tasks' intents (the run's task body + the body of the commit(s) that landed on target since the run branched); it edits the worktree, then the lander runs `git add` + `git rebase --continue` and proceeds to the existing ff-push (or :auto_local) path.
Resolver failure (markers still present, or the agent declines) falls back to the existing block / re-dispatch resilience path — a still-conflicted tree is NEVER landed.
Resolver does NOT re-run the project checks or re-grade the diff (no re-verification) — it reconciles conflict markers only; the reviewer already approved both sides.
Lander.Resilience.plan/2 (or its caller) gains a {:conflict,_} -> {:resolve,...} branch with re-dispatch as the fallback; covered by resilience_test.exs.
Resolver family != implementer family (same cross-family discipline as the reviewer); selection reuses reviewer-eligibility/registry.
out_of_scope: :auto_local (merge into local development without pushing to origin) — separate landing-policy decision/task.
Non-rebase merge strategies — the lander stays rebase + ff only.
Any re-verification, re-review, or check re-run of the resolved tree.
task.body:
The MERGE stage is mechanical today: the lander rebases harness/<run-id> onto the target and ff-pushes. On a rebase CONFLICT, Lander.Resilience.plan/2 routes {:conflict,_} to a fresh re-dispatch — which is wrong twice: it discards a reviewer-APPROVED diff and reruns the implementer from scratch, and it treats conflict reconciliation as something a re-run can fix when it is actually a JUDGMENT call (keep both sides, reconcile overlapping intents) that an AI does better than code or a blind redo.

This applies the agent-gate rule to the MERGE node: a clean ff-merge stays pure mechanics (no agent); a rebase conflict spawns a merge-resolver agent. Demonstrated 2026-06-04 landing task 177 — its run branch (parented before 182 landed) conflicted with 182 in test/harness/run_test.exs: 177 added prioritize_reviewers/2 tests, 182 renamed an adjacent test; the resolution was 'keep both', exactly the judgment a re-dispatch cannot make and an agent can. That hand-merge is the motivating case.

Design: when the lander's rebase exits conflicted, instead of {:redispatch,...}, leave the conflict in the already-open detached landing worktree and spawn a cross-family resolver agent there. Give it the conflicted files, both sides, and both tasks' intents (derivable: the run's task body, plus the bodies of the commits that landed on target since the run branched). The agent edits the worktree to resolve; the lander does `git add` + `git rebase --continue`, then the existing ff-push (or :auto_local once that exists). Resolver failure falls back to the current block/re-dispatch path — the resolver is an attempt, never a new gate, and never lands a still-conflicted tree.

This is NOT a re-verification step: the resolver only reconciles markers, never re-grades or re-runs checks (the reviewer already approved both sides). Gated behind landing_policy: :auto (and orthogonal to the local-only push decision, tracked separately as :auto_local).
task.implemented: Harness.Lander.Resolver: rebase conflict during auto-land spawns a cross-family merge-resolver agent in the open detached landing worktree (markers in place) instead of blind re-dispatch. Lander leaves the rebase conflicted, runs the resolver (prefers the run's approving reviewer, else first eligible cross-family per reviewer-eligibility/registry), then mechanically git-adds, asserts zero leftover markers via 'git diff --cached --check', and 'rebase --continue' (core.editor=true) before the existing ff-push. Resolver never re-runs checks/re-grades. Any failure (no resolver, declined, markers remain, continue rejects) aborts + falls back to the existing {:conflict,_}->re-dispatch path; a still-conflicted tree is never landed. Injectable via :lander_resolver env for tests. New resolver.ex + lander rewire; lander_test (resolve/markers-left/declined) + resolver_test (cross-family invariant + prompt) green.

task.title: Start the global :audit Oban queue so the post-merge audit AI actually runs
acceptance_criteria: The `:audit` queue (limit 1, the AuditWorker's queue) is started when Oban runs — not just `project_<name>`/`landing_<name>`, which are the only queues ensure_project_queue/1 currently starts.
An enqueued AuditWorker job is actually executed (not left `available` forever); proven by a test that inserts an audit job and observes it run/drain rather than a guard that only checks insertion.

Start path mirrors the existing dynamic local_only pattern (or static config) — pick one and justify in the moduledoc; do not break the deliberately-empty static `queues: []` design without saying why.
No-op safe: starting twice (boot + per-project ensure) does not crash; idempotent like ensure_project_queue/1.
out_of_scope: Turning on auto-land itself (landing_policy flip is an operator action).
Any change to what the audit agent does — this only makes the queue process the jobs the lander already enqueues.
task.body:
The post-merge audit AI is wired but dead: `Harness.Audit.Worker` is `use Oban.Worker, queue: :audit, max_attempts: 2` (a single GLOBAL serialized queue, limit 1), and `Harness.Lander.enqueue_audit/3` inserts a job on every successful land — but NOTHING ever starts the `:audit` queue. Static config is `queues: []` (config.exs), and the only dynamic starter, `Harness.Oban.ensure_project_queue/1`, starts just `project_<name>` + `landing_<name>` per project. So an inserted audit job sits `available` forever and the audit stage never fires.

This is the second of the two reasons the audit AI is currently inactive (the first being that all projects are `landing_policy: :manual`, so the lander — the only enqueue site — never runs). Flipping a project to `:auto` exposes this gap immediately: lands would push, then silently skip audit.

Fix: start the global `:audit` queue (limit 1) when Oban is up. Because it is global (not per-project), the natural home is a one-time boot start rather than ensure_project_queue/1 (which is per-project and would redundantly re-start it). Keep it idempotent and local_only-consistent with the existing project-queue startup. Mechanical substrate only — no judgment, no agent change.
task.implemented: Queue start already shipped in the agent-gate rebuild (1a02627): Harness.Oban.oban_opts/0 augments static queues:[] via enable_audit_queue/1, adding {:audit,1} at boot (limit 1, serialized, alongside the sibling :cron queue). The only gap vs acceptance was coverage — added an assertion in audit/worker_test.exs that {:audit,1} in oban_opts()[:queues], mirroring how the cron queue is verified. Insert→drain isn't runnable in test (oban_enabled:false, repo_enabled:false → no instance/repo), so the config-presence assert is the idiomatic boot proof; the worker's perform routing is already exhaustively drain-tested in the same file.

task.title: Audit-surfaced: Worktree reaper vs Run.Registry unregister ordering race
acceptance_criteria: A run gen_statem brutally killed (Process.exit(pid, :kill)) has its worktree reaped within-node, not left for the boot Sweeper
cleanup_for_run/2 can distinguish refused-for-live from done, OR a documented one-shot retry covers the monitor/registry ordering window
out_of_scope: Any change to the boot Sweeper backstop (it already catches the leak on next boot)
task.body:
Audit (claude reviewer) flagged a race in lib/harness/worktree/reaper.ex (cleanup_for_run/maybe_reap): when a run gen_statem crashes, the reaper's monitor :DOWN and the Harness.Run.Registry auto-unregister are unordered. If :DOWN is processed before the registry clears, cleanup_for_run/2's live_run? guard sees the run still registered and REFUSES the reap, so the worktree leaks until the boot Sweeper — i.e. degrades to the pre-task-185 behavior the reaper exists to fix. Trigger: a run killed with Process.exit(pid, :kill) such that the reaper drains its mailbox faster than the Registry monitor fires.

discuss-design DIVERGENCE in audit: Claude flagged it (graceful degradation, not a crash; boot Sweeper backstops); Codex found nothing on the same commit. No convergent fix, so dropped from auto-apply and filed here for the user's call. Lowest-risk mitigation: one-shot retry after a short delay when cleanup_for_run returns refused-for-live; cleaner fix touches cleanup_for_run's contract (caller can't currently distinguish refused-live from done). Confirm whether the boot-Sweeper backstop is considered sufficient before adding retry machinery.

task.title: Audit-surfaced: Task 190 — add real insert-and-drain test for the :audit Oban queue
acceptance_criteria: An :integration test inserts a Harness.Audit.Worker job and observes it run/drain on a live Oban+repo, satisfying Task 190 acceptance criterion #2 (not the config-presence proxy)
out_of_scope: Re-opening Task 190's status (queue start itself shipped and works)

task.title: Per-project reviewer override (%Harness.Project{reviewer}) + Run.init overlay + select_reviewer consults it + Settings-page runtime override
acceptance_criteria: %Harness.Project{} gains a `reviewer :: atom() | nil` field (nil = today's auto-select; an agent atom pins the cross-family reviewer for that project), defaulting nil so existing registrations and tests are byte-unchanged
Run.init/1 overlays the project's effective reviewer onto the run's :reviewer opt (mirrors the Task 155 landing_policy overlay), so select_reviewer/1 honors it without a new Run opt at the call site

select_reviewer/1 with an explicit project reviewer still enforces ensure_cross_family_reviewer/2 + reviewer-eligibility (Task 182) + dispatchability — a pinned same-family or ineligible reviewer settles :failed with a clear reason, never silently falls back to auto-select
Operator can set/clear the per-project reviewer from /harness/settings, persisted across a BEAM restart through the consolidated settings store (Task 165), NOT a new ~/.harness/*.term file
config-declared projects (config :harness, :projects) may set reviewer at registration time; the runtime override wins over the registration default, mirroring the landing-policy precedent
Existing select_reviewer, SettingsLive, and project tests pass unchanged; new tests cover the overlay precedence and the same-family/ineligible-pin rejection paths
out_of_scope: Per-project reviewer MODEL pinning — reviewer_invocation/1 threads no model today; a separate, larger change
Per-task reviewer override in rmap — deliberately not adding a reviewer field to the roadmap Task schema (couples roadmap authoring to routing the system is built to decide)
Changing the nil-default auto-selection (cross-family + rejection-rate ordering stays the default behavior)
task.body:
Wire a per-project reviewer override so an operator can pin which cross-family agent gates a given project's runs, instead of always taking the rejection-rate-ordered auto-selection. Asked for directly; the multi-project-federation case is concrete — different registered repos may warrant different reviewers.

The seam already exists on both ends: Task 155 (done) established the `%Harness.Project{}`-field + `Run.init/1` overlay + Settings-page-editable pattern for `landing_policy`; Task 182 (done) made `select_reviewer/1` consult per-agent reviewer-eligibility. This task is the same shape one layer over: a `reviewer` field on the project, overlaid in `Run.init/1`, with `select_reviewer/1`'s explicit-reviewer path (already present at run.ex:1418) reached from the project rather than only from a Run opt / app config.

Two layers, deliberately split from Task 165:
1. Struct field + Run.init overlay + select_reviewer wiring — depends on nothing in 165; config-declared projects can set `reviewer` at registration immediately.
2. The operator runtime override (Settings page, persisted) — THIS is the only 165 dependency: its persistence must ride 165's consolidated Postgres-backed settings store, never a 4th `~/.harness/*.term` file (the exact sprawl 165 exists to kill). Hence depends_on 165, NOT folded into 165 (whose out-of-scope forbids new settings).

Keep nil = auto-select as the untouched default. An explicit pin must still pass the cross-family + eligibility + dispatchable gates; a bad pin fails loudly with a settle reason, it does not silently degrade to auto-select (that would hide operator misconfiguration). Reviewer-model pinning stays out — reviewer_invocation/1 carries no model and adding one is a separate change with weak payoff (the reviewer's job is judgment, and model IDs churn).

task.title: Clean (:no_changes) post-merge audit leaves no watermark — range re-audited every land
acceptance_criteria: After a post-merge audit returns :no_changes, the next land's auditor does NOT re-audit the same already-clean commit range
A fix-bearing audit (audit() commit) and a clean audit both advance the audited watermark
out_of_scope: Writing empty audit() marker commits to the shared branch (noise on the merge-train)
task.body:
Harness.Audit.unaudited_range/2 bases the range on the last `audit(` commit reachable from HEAD (audit_base/2). A clean audit returns :no_changes (audit.ex:313, head == base_sha) and commits nothing, so NO `audit(` marker is written. Consequence: the same clean commit range is re-audited on every subsequent land until some audit actually commits a fix — bounded but wasteful auditor spend under active landing (each land re-reads a growing clean range).

Confirmed live 2026-06-04: catch-up audit of 4983985..01fc5eb (3 clean commits) returned :no_changes; origin untouched, no marker, so the next land would re-audit the same 3 + new commits.

Fix direction (mechanical, not judgment): record a last-audited-clean watermark (sha) the range logic also consults — base = the most recent of {last audit( commit, persisted clean watermark}. Persist alongside the existing ~/.harness term stores. Do NOT write empty marker commits to the shared branch. Keep :no_changes as the outcome; only the range baseline changes.

task.title: Run.Worker crash-recovery: idempotent worktree setup so an Oban retry after BEAM restart reuses the run's branch instead of colliding
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-04: an accidental BEAM restart killed two in-flight harness runs (tasks 165, 194). Oban persisted the `executing` jobs and rescued them to attempt 2, but each retry CANCELLED with:

    {:cancel, {:worktree_failed, {:git_failed, ["worktree","add","-b","harness/run-<id>", <path>, "HEAD"], 255, "fatal: a branch named 'harness/run-<id>' already exists"}}}

Root cause (mechanical, not judgment): the worktree reaper removes the crashed attempt's *worktree* but leaves its *branch*. The Oban job keeps the SAME run_id across retries, so attempt 2's `git worktree add -b harness/run-<id>` collides on the leftover branch and the run is lost -- exactly the in-flight work crash-only retry is supposed to recover.

Fix direction (idempotent setup; all mechanical -- git/worktree/Oban retry, no agent judgment):
- On worktree creation, when the branch already exists for THIS run_id (a prior crashed attempt of the same job), reuse/reset it: `git worktree add -B <branch> <path> <base>` or detect-existing-branch then `git worktree add <path> <branch>`, rather than failing on `-b`.
- Equivalently, the worker's crash-recovery prelude reaps its own orphan branch before re-creating. Reuse is safe because run_id is stable across retries (same logical run).

Acceptance: a test simulating "branch already exists for this run_id" drives the worker through a second attempt and the worktree is (re)created green instead of `{:cancel, {:worktree_failed, ...}}`. Manual repro: dispatch a run, kill the BEAM mid-run, restart -- the rescued Oban job recovers instead of cancelling.

Related litter (note, not in scope): ~23 stale rmap-project worktrees under ~/_DATA/worktrees/.harness/rmap/ from earlier runs survive across settles -- the reaper may not clear worktrees for manual (non-landing) projects. File separately if confirmed.

task.title: Runs branch from origin/<target>, not operator-checkout HEAD — fetch origin before worktree create so dispatched runs always build on the latest landed code
acceptance_criteria: When a project has a target_branch, Run fetches origin/<target> and the run worktree's base SHA equals origin/<target>'s tip -- not the operator checkout HEAD
Regression test: with origin/<target> ahead of the local checkout, a dispatched run's worktree base == origin tip (proves staleness of the operator checkout no longer affects runs)
Fetch failure (e.g. offline) logs a warning and falls back to base_ref HEAD; the run still starts (never crashes on fetch failure)
Projects with target_branch nil are unchanged (base_ref stays HEAD)
mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: An opt-in flag to branch a run from local unlanded HEAD instead of origin (rare; the dogfooding norm is to push local work before dispatching). File separately if a real need appears.
Auto-syncing the operator checkout itself -- that is the sibling lander-auto-ff task
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-04: the lander pushes to the *remote* target ref from a detached worktree and deliberately never touches the operator checkout (lander.ex:27-30 -- "the operator's local checkout is untouched"). So local `development` drifts behind origin after every autonomous land. The compounding half: `Worktree.create/2` defaults `base_ref` to "HEAD" (worktree.ex:168) and `Run` never overrides it or fetches origin first -- so when the operator checkout is stale, every DISPATCHED run also forks from stale code, and the staleness only surfaces as a rebase conflict at land time. The manual `git fetch && git rebase` the operator must run before dispatching is the only thing keeping runs current; that is the smell.

Fix (mechanical -- git/fetch/worktree lifecycle, no agent judgment): before creating a run's worktree, when the project has a `target_branch`, `git fetch origin <target>` and pass `base_ref: "origin/<target>"` to `Worktree.create`. The run branch then forks from the latest landed tip regardless of the operator checkout's state, which ALSO makes the run's base match what the lander rebases onto -> fewer/zero land conflicts.

Best-effort: if the fetch fails (offline), log and fall back to HEAD -- never crash the run on a fetch failure. Projects with `target_branch: nil` keep the current HEAD behavior.

task.title: Lander auto-fast-forwards the operator's local target ref when safe, so a land does not leave local development drifting behind origin
acceptance_criteria: After a successful land, when the operator checkout is NOT on <target>, the local <target> ref fast-forwards to the pushed tip without modifying the working tree
When on <target> with a clean tree, the local <target> fast-forwards (merge --ff-only); the operator's HEAD advances to the landed tip
Dirty tree or non-ff (local ahead) -> no checkout mutation, and a Notification is fired naming the drift
Never uses --force and never moves the checkout off the operator's current branch; ff-only is asserted by a test that sets up a non-ff local and confirms it is left untouched + notified
mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: Hot code reloading to avoid the BEAM restart (out of reach; Elixir won't hot-load structural changes)
Changing the run worktree base (sibling task)
task.body:
Sibling to the runs-branch-from-origin task. Today the lander pushes the remote ref and leaves the operator checkout alone by design (lander.ex:27-30), so local `development` drifts behind origin on every land and the operator must `git pull`/rebase by hand before any in-BEAM hand-build work. This is the friction that blocked task 167 this session and, on an accidental restart, orphaned in-flight runs against stale code.

Fix direction (mechanical git-state inspection -- needs a design pass before dispatch, hence no auto-dispatch): after a successful push, attempt a SAFE local sync of the target ref:
- Operator NOT on <target> -> `git fetch origin <target>:<target>` updates the local branch ref without touching the working tree.
- Operator ON <target> with a clean tree -> `git merge --ff-only origin/<target>`.
- Dirty tree, or local has commits not on origin (non-ff) -> SKIP and fire a Notification ("local <target> behind origin by N; sync manually").

It is fast-forward-only, so it can never overwrite operator work -- a refinement of "never touch the checkout", not a reversal. Open design questions to settle first: (1) the on-<target>+clean case is the common one (operator sits on development with the BEAM running) AND the riskiest -- confirm `merge --ff-only` against a possibly-running BEAM's CWD is safe; (2) where this hook lives (post-push in Lander.run vs a separate witness step); (3) whether it is opt-in per project. Residual after this lands: hand-build still needs a deliberate BEAM restart (Elixir won't hot-load structural changes), but the operator would restart already-synced.

task.title: Antigravity (agy) adapter leaks writes into the operator checkout instead of the run worktree — worktree isolation regression
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce: dispatch a task to the antigravity adapter and confirm whether file writes land in the run worktree (cwd) or leak into the operator checkout
Antigravity adapter honors the Port cwd so ALL writes are confined to the run worktree — a dispatched agy run never modifies the operator checkout

Harness.AgentAdapter.ConformanceCase passes for Antigravity unchanged; add a regression test asserting cwd-confinement (or a documented capability flip to worktree_isolation: false if agy genuinely cannot isolate)
CLAUDE.md's stale 2026-06-04 'agy honors cwd / isolation fixed' note is corrected to match observed reality
mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: Re-enabling agy for autonomous dispatch before isolation is proven (it stays off the assignee rotation until this lands)
Changes to other adapters
task.body:
OBSERVED 2026-06-04 (this session). A task-140 dispatch to the antigravity (agy = Gemini) adapter wrote its files — lib/harness/chat/store/file.ex, .../schema/chat_session.ex, priv/repo/migrations/*_add_chat_sessions.exs — DIRECTLY INTO THE OPERATOR CHECKOUT (/Users/efries/_DATA/code/harness) instead of its run worktree. The run's worktree (run-1780544343922-f47fcfb9) was left at the base commit with ZERO commits. The leaked, half-broken schema file (a `t()` undefined @spec) broke `recompile` in the operator's running iex. It also ran `mix ecto.migrate` against the dev DB from the operator checkout (recorded an orphan migration version).

This CONTRADICTS the CLAUDE.md claim that Antigravity's Task 32 isolation finding was 'stale as of agy 1.0.5' and that a 2026-06-04 linked-worktree re-test showed agy honoring the Port cwd. Observed behavior says agy does NOT honor cwd. Harness.Run trusts `worktree_isolation: true` and skips the main-checkout pollution snapshot for isolating adapters — so an agy leak is invisible to harness and lands in the operator's working tree.

Fix direction: trace the Antigravity adapter's build_command/1 + Port cwd handling; determine whether agy ignores the Port cwd for file writes (vs honoring it for reads only). Either make it isolate, or flip its declared capability to worktree_isolation: false (so Harness.Run re-enables the pollution snapshot / main-checkout guard for it). agy stays disabled for dispatch until this is resolved.

task.title: Run wedges in :reviewing when the reviewer process is never tracked (reviewer=nil) — add an idle/progress watchdog so a lost reviewer fails fast instead of holding a queue slot to the 90-min lifetime cap
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce: a run enters :reviewing but the reviewer process is never tracked (state data reviewer=nil, review=nil) and the gen_statem sits idle (loop_receive, no armed wakeup) until the 90-min lifetime_timeout

Add a MECHANICAL idle/progress watchdog armed on entry to :reviewing (a timer, not a judgment classifier): if the reviewer makes no progress within a bounded window, the run settles to :failed (missing verdict) and frees its queue slot — task back to queue per the agent-gate workflow
Reviewer-spawn failure is surfaced fast: if attach/spawn of the reviewer returns error or the reviewer Port never starts, do not silently sit in :reviewing
Regression test: a run whose reviewer never produces a verdict transitions to :failed within the watchdog window, not at the lifetime cap
mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: Any judgment/classifier in harness code about WHY review failed or whether the work is good — that stays the reviewer AI's job; this is purely a mechanical timeout/liveness guard (timers are substrate, per the agent-gate rules)
Reintroducing review_green / max_review_iterations / repair loops
task.body:
OBSERVED 2026-06-04 (this session). The salvaged task-140 antigravity run (run-1780544645702-1a831f01) reached state :reviewing with the implementer outcome captured (agent_kind: :exited) but the reviewer never tracked: data.reviewer = nil, data.review = nil, reviewer_adapter = Harness.AgentAdapter.Cursor. The gen_statem sat in loop_receive with message_queue_len 0 and NO armed wakeup — wedged for ~20 min. The only armed timer was lifetime_timeout (5_400_000 ms = 90 min); idle_timeout and progress_timeout were nil in :reviewing. So a run whose reviewer spawn is lost holds its project-queue concurrency slot for up to 90 minutes before the lifetime cap fails it. Had to cancel it manually (Harness.Run.cancel/1) to free the slot.

This is a MECHANICAL liveness gap, not a judgment bug: :reviewing has no idle/progress watchdog, so a never-tracked (or silently-failed-to-spawn) reviewer never trips a timeout. Fix is a timer armed on entry to :reviewing + fail-fast on reviewer-spawn error — substrate only. Do NOT add any branch/regex/classifier interpreting review meaning (that violates the agent-gate rule); the verdict still comes only from .harness/review.json.
task.implemented: Reviewing-phase watchdog: on :reviewing enter, arm a spawn state_timeout (reviewer_spawn_timeout, default 60s) + capture the reviewer Run handle via Driver :on_spawn; once spawned, switch to an idle state_timeout re-armed on each transcript chunk. Either timer settles :failed {:review_stuck} well under the 90-min lifetime cap, freeing the queue slot. terminate_reviewer/1 added to cancel/timeout/fail paths. Salvaged run.ex+run_test.exs from crashed run run-1780547458231-66f464e9 (reviewer never ran — laptop kernel panic mid-review); stale Chat.Store hunks dropped. Manually gated: diff reviewed + precommit.full green.

task.title: Bound spawned-run process memory: kill a run whose agent/check_command process tree runs away (it OOM'd the host twice)
acceptance_criteria: A per-run memory watchdog samples the resident memory of the spawned process GROUP (the Port'd agent CLI + all descendants, including the check_command mix it runs) and force-kills the whole tree + fails the run when it crosses a configurable threshold (sensible default, e.g. a few GB).
The kill reaps the entire descendant tree, not just the direct child — a leaked grandchild mix/beam.smp must not survive the run being torn down (verify no orphan process after kill).

Aggregate concurrent runs cannot drive the node into swap-thrash: the effective concurrency ceiling (sum of project_<name> Oban queue limits) is documented, and/or a node-level guard holds new dispatch under high host memory pressure.
A regression test proves a child that allocates past the threshold is killed and the run settles :failed with a clear reason — not silently, and without taking the harness node down.
No change to the reviewer-gate verdict contract — reviewer still reads .harness/review.json; this is mechanical substrate (sample/threshold/kill) only.
out_of_scope: Parsing/normalizing agent or check output (raw passthrough stays).
Any judgment moved into harness code — purely mechanical memory bounding of spawned OS processes (sample/threshold/kill), consistent with the agent-gate architecture.
Reworking the run lifecycle or reviewer flow; capping the harness node's own heap (it was calm at 30 MB — not the problem).
task.body:
On 2026-06-04 the laptop crashed twice (13:10 kernel watchdog panic — watchdogd starved; 13:48 second reboot after a 13:41 JetsamEvent/OOM with ~93 MB free).

CORRECTED root cause (process-level inspection, not just the jetsam snapshot):
- PID 48366 = the harness node (owns port 4018, cwd = main checkout). CALM at 30 MB. Not the culprit.
- PID 16184 = a `mix` beam running INSIDE a run worktree (…/worktrees/.harness/onchain/run-1780547484818-438b5f97) — i.e. the reviewer's `check_command` for that onchain run — runaway at 12–27 GB. THIS is the OOM that panicked the laptop twice.

So it is NOT the harness node's own heap and NOT raw-transcript passthrough. The reviewer AI runs the target project's `check_command` itself; harness Ports the agent CLI (lib/harness/agent_adapter/os_process.ex), the agent runs `mix …` as its own child, and that grandchild process leaked/blew up to tens of GB with nothing bounding it. Harness spawns the tree but never limits its memory — a single misbehaving project check (here an "onchain" project's mix task) takes down the whole host.

Task: bound the memory of the spawned run process tree so a runaway agent/check_command can't OOM the host.
1. Per-run memory watchdog (mechanical, alongside the existing run timeout watchdog in lib/harness/run.ex): periodically sample the resident memory of the spawned process GROUP (Port'd agent CLI + all descendants) and, past a configurable threshold (a few GB default), force-kill the entire tree and settle the run :failed with a clear reason.
2. Make the spawn killable as a group: ensure os_process.ex spawns the agent in its own process group / records the pid so the watchdog can reap the WHOLE descendant tree (a leaked grandchild mix/beam.smp must not orphan-survive the kill).
3. Bound aggregate pressure: document the effective concurrency ceiling (sum of per-project Oban queue limits) and/or hold new dispatch under high host memory pressure.

Mechanical substrate only — sample/threshold/kill of spawned OS processes. No judgment in code, no output parsing, no change to the reviewer verdict contract. Not capping the harness node's own heap (it was fine). Fits phase 16 / resilience.
task.implemented: Per-run memory watchdog: new Harness.Run.MemoryGuard (ps-based tree RSS sample + whole-tree SIGKILL reap, since Ports have no process group and macOS lacks setsid). Run arms a named {:timeout, :mem_sample} generic timeout (default 6GiB/5s, configurable per-run + app env), samples both agent and reviewer trees, and on breach kills the tree before port teardown and settles :failed {:memory_runaway, %{role, os_pid, rss_kb, threshold_kb}}. Aggregate ceiling (sum of project_<name> Oban queue limits) documented in MemoryGuard moduledoc. 7 new tests; reviewer-gate contract untouched.

task.title: Reorder terminate_reviewer/terminate_agent before cancel_task in the general cancel/lifetime/fail handlers
acceptance_criteria: In Harness.Run's general cancel, lifetime-timeout, and fail/2 handlers, terminate_reviewer(data) and terminate_agent(data) run BEFORE cancel_task(data.task) so the adapter SIGKILLs the captured os_pid before the Port owner is torn down
A regression test asserts the reviewer/agent adapter terminate/1 is invoked on these paths when a run handle was captured
mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: The reviewing-phase fail_review_stuck path (already reordered in the Task 199 audit, d23e6f2)

Closing the task that owns the Port first can reap/race the stored os_pid. Benign in practice (kill dead/own pid), but the consistent ordering is terminate-then-cancel. Same pattern affects the implementer terminate_agent path.

Regression test cancels mid-:reviewing with a real pid-writing reviewer and asserts the reviewer's spawned tree is reaped (not orphaned). Behavior-neutral consistency fix; precommit.full green.

task.title: Node-pressure dispatch gate: hold new run admission under high host memory (AC3 follow-up to task 200)
acceptance_criteria: Before a Run.Worker spawns the run gen_statem, a mechanical guard checks host/node memory pressure (e.g. :erlang.memory(:total) and/or system free RAM via the same ps substrate as MemoryGuard) and, past a configurable high-water mark, defers admission (Oban snooze/retry) instead of starting another concurrent tree.
The gate is purely mechanical (sample + threshold + snooze) — no judgment, no output parsing — and never blocks a run already in flight (it only throttles NEW admission).
Default high-water mark is configurable on the :harness :run key alongside mem_threshold_kb; a sensible default leaves headroom under host RAM.
A test proves admission is deferred when the pressure sample is over the mark and proceeds when under it, without losing the Oban job (it snoozes/retries, not discards).
No change to the reviewer-gate verdict contract or the per-run watchdog from task 200.
out_of_scope: The per-run memory watchdog itself (shipped in task 200 — this is the aggregate companion bound).
A global cross-queue concurrency cap (open-source Oban has none; the documented sum-of-queue-limits ceiling stays the steady-state bound).
Any judgment moved into harness code.
task.body:
DEFERRED follow-up to task 200's AC3. Task 200 took the "document" branch of AC3's and/or: MemoryGuard's moduledoc names the steady-state ceiling (sum of project_<name> Oban queue limits, kept × mem_threshold_kb under host RAM). The per-run watchdog stops ONE runaway tree but does not stop N concurrent well-behaved trees from summing past host RAM under high concurrency.

This task adds the optional node-pressure dispatch gate: a mechanical admission throttle at the Run.Worker boundary that holds NEW run admission (Oban snooze/retry) when host/node memory pressure is over a configurable high-water mark — the aggregate companion to the per-run cap.

Deliberately deferred / low urgency: the 2026-06-04 host crash was a single-runaway OOM, fully addressed by task 200's per-run watchdog. This aggregate gate only earns its keep once real concurrency (multiple registered projects dispatching simultaneously) approaches host RAM. File now so the AC3 surface isn't lost; pick up when concurrency actually grows. depends_on 200 (builds on the same MemoryGuard ps substrate + :run config key).

task.title: Reviewer missing-verdict recovery: re-prompt the reviewer once before discarding the run
acceptance_criteria: settle_review/2 on {:error, :missing} ONLY re-invokes the same reviewer adapter once, in the same worktree, with a terse nudge ('you exited without writing .harness/review.json — write your verdict now, nothing else') before failing the run as review_stuck
The re-prompt is bounded to exactly one retry via a counter on the gen_statem data; a second missing verdict fails as {:review_stuck, _} exactly as today (no loop)
Only the missing-file case retries: {:error, {:malformed, _}}, {:review_rejected, _}, and approve are all unchanged
Reviewer idle/total/spawn timeouts apply to the retry invocation identically to the first review pass

Design tension resolved in the PR text: a bounded single re-prompt of a mechanical artifact write is documented as MECHANICAL (re-issuing a flush), not judgment-in-harness — explicit sign-off that it does not reopen the agent-gate 'machinery interprets outcomes' door
Tests cover all three paths: missing->verdict-on-retry->approve, missing->missing->review_stuck, malformed-unchanged; offline suite + mix precommit green
out_of_scope: Retrying on malformed verdicts or on reject
More than one re-prompt (any unbounded loop)
Switching to a different reviewer adapter on the retry
Changing the primary reviewer prompt's verdict instructions or the check_command
task.body: On 2026-06-05 task 37 (hieroglyph) failed as {:review_stuck, "Reviewer wrote no .harness/review.json verdict artifact."} (run ...-f3ebb30a). The cursor implementer committed a 214-line diff; the auto-selected Claude reviewer ran the project checks (worktree _build was compiled) and exited 0 WITHOUT writing the verdict file, so harness discarded the entire run via settle_review {:error, :missing} (run.ex:1583) and re-queued task 37 from scratch. The full implementer+reviewer spend (including the Opus reviewer tokens) was thrown away for a recoverable miss. Root trigger that night was a too-heavy check_command (cold-PLT dialyzer in precommit.full rebuilds per worktree, minutes) exhausting the headless reviewer's turn budget before it reached the mandatory write step; that config is already softened to mix precommit, but the fragility is general — any reviewer that exits a hair early loses everything, no matter the project. Proposal: on {:error, :missing} ONLY, re-invoke the same reviewer once in the same worktree with a terse 'write the verdict now, nothing else' nudge, bounded to exactly one retry via a counter on the run data; a second miss fails as review_stuck as today. The retry costs one short reviewer invocation vs a full re-dispatch (implementer + reviewer) on discard, so it pays for itself the first time it saves a run. DESIGN TENSION (why assignee=human, settle before building): the agent-gate rule (CLAUDE.md) fixes run-lifecycle bugs by moving judgment into an agent prompt/artifact, never by adding a branch to harness code. A bounded single re-prompt is defensible as a mechanical retry of a mechanical artifact write — it interprets no meaning, classifies no outcome — but it IS a new branch in the :reviewing state and needs explicit sign-off that it stays mechanical and does not reopen the 'machinery interprets outcomes' door the rebuild closed. Decide that framing first; if it holds, the implementation is small and contained to Harness.Run.
task.implemented: settle_review/2 on {:error, :missing} re-enters :reviewing via :repeat_state (re-arming spawn/idle watchdogs) once, bounded by reviewer_reprompt_count; the retry invokes the same reviewer in the same worktree with a terse write-the-verdict nudge (reviewer_reprompt/1). Malformed/reject unchanged; second miss settles {:review_stuck,_}. Fix-diff baseline captured once at route_to_review so reviewer_diff_size spans the whole review across the re-prompt. Tests cover missing->verdict->approve, missing->missing->stuck, malformed-unchanged, and the cross-reprompt KPI.

Each declaration cites the source confirming the var forces API billing

task.body:
Follow-up to the auth-scrub fix (Claude/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY billed the dead API key instead of the subscription -> review_stuck across every Claude-reviewer run; Codex/OPENAI_API_KEY was silently diverting too). The other four adapters inherit auth_env_scrub: [] (default). No diverting key is currently in the node env for them, so no ACTIVE bug -- but fill the slot so a future stray key can't silently divert billing off the subscription/login.

Per CLI, verify (docs / reference impl, per RESEARCH-BEFORE-ASSERTING) which env var(s) force API-key billing over the interactive login, then declare in capabilities/0:
- cursor-agent (Cursor): likely CURSOR_API_KEY
- grok (xAI): likely XAI_API_KEY / GROK_API_KEY
- pi (pi.dev): unknown -- verify
- agy (Antigravity, Google): unknown -- likely GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY

Do NOT declare a var you haven't verified diverts billing -- an empty list is honest; a wrong scrub is silent breakage.

task.body: Today onchain's landing-policy flip silently reverted on restart: the value lived in three layers (exs registration default -> SettingsStore overlay -> app-env cache) and landing persistence was off because :landing_settings had no default root config line (cron/agent do, config.exs line 34/68; landing was only set false in the test block) so Landing.Settings.disabled? short-circuited every write.
