task.title: Thread the pinned model into the agent Invocation — requested_model is captured but never reaches --model
acceptance_criteria: `invocation/3` (run.ex:~1772) sets `model: data.requested_model` on the `%Invocation{}` so the implementer run carries the task's pinned model.
`recovery_invocation/1` (run.ex:~2086) likewise sets `model: data.requested_model` so a resumed run keeps the pin. Reviewer invocation is cross-family by design and stays unpinned.
A test asserts the built implementer Invocation has `model` equal to the run's requested_model (and nil when unpinned), so a future regression is caught.
Manual confirmation note in the commit: a `cursor` dispatch of a task with `model = "claude-opus-4-8-thinking-high"` shows `--model claude-opus-4-8-thinking-high` in the live cursor-agent argv.
task.body: BUG found 2026-06-07 while exercising the cursor multi-model lever (task 234 dispatched cursor + model=claude-opus-4-8-thinking-high). The rmap model field threads correctly through Roadmap.ingest -> Item.model -> dispatch run_start_opts -> :requested_model -> data.requested_model (run.ex:524), and surfaces in status_snapshot (1743) and the delegate prompt context. BUT the two functions that build the actual %Invocation{} — invocation/3 (implementer) and recovery_invocation/1 (resume) — never copy data.requested_model into Invocation.model. Since AgentAdapter.model_args/1 keys off invocation.model, --model is silently never passed: every cursor run uses its default composer-2.5-fast regardless of the pin. Verified against the live argv of run-1780832742494-db9aae0e: no --model present. Pure mechanics (pass-through a field), not judgment. Gated behind 239 because both edit run.ex; serialize to avoid a merge collision. Once landed, the running node must recompile (or restart) to pick it up before the pin takes effect on new dispatches.
task.implemented: Added model: data.requested_model to invocation/3 and recovery_invocation/1 in run.ex so the pinned model reaches AgentAdapter.model_args/1 and the CLI --model flag. Tests: run_test asserts the implementer invocation carries requested_model (and empty when unpinned) via a new FakeAdapter :capture_model fixture. Reviewer invocation stays cross-family/unpinned by design.

task.title: Dashboard /harness 12-15s load: parallelize + defer RoadmapSummary's per-project rmap shell-outs off the render critical path
acceptance_criteria: RoadmapSummary.for_projects/1 runs its per-project rmap shell-outs concurrently (e.g. Task.async_stream with a bounded timeout), not sequentially — N projects cost ~one shell-out of wall-clock, not N.

The roadmap rollup is computed OFF the mount render critical path: mount assigns an empty/loading summary instantly and the rollup loads asynchronously after connected mount (the existing slow roadmap_tick may drive it), so neither the disconnected HTTP render nor the connected mount blocks on the shell-outs.
Measured: /harness TTFB returns to low-hundreds-of-ms even while runs are active (was 12-15s under load on 2026-06-08); /harness/kpi parity (~56ms) is the target.
A project whose rmap read times out or errors degrades to an empty summary (current behavior preserved), never blocking or crashing the roadmap panel.
Hand-built via tidewave + browser per the UI-work rule; verify the dashboard loads fast WITH active runs present — the only condition that reproduces the regression.
out_of_scope: The StatusView.live_runs/0 + Run.status gen_statem fan-out — that is the secondary cause, split into its own task.
No change to the roadmap data shape, the rmap CLI, or the run-lifecycle modules.
task.body: First consumer: the operator watching runs on /harness. Measured 2026-06-08 from the browser: the dashboard takes 12-15s to load while runs are active vs 56ms for /harness/kpi, and it is 100 percent server-side (every SQL query logged is under 41ms — not the DB). Localized to Harness.Dashboard.Live.mount calling RoadmapSummary.for_projects, which fires N SEQUENTIAL rmap list --json OS shell-outs, one per registered project (7 projects). Idle they total ~47ms; under active-run load (an agent CLI saturating CPU/IO, the lander writing tasks.toml) each process spawn stretches and 7 stacked sequentially produce the ~11s dead-render gap seen in the logs at 09:25 (which lines up exactly with a cursor run settling). Fix: run the shell-outs concurrently AND move them off the render critical path so mount paints instantly and the rollup fills in async / on the existing slow tick. This is the dominant, high-confidence cause; the live_runs fan-out (the sibling task) is the secondary suspect and may not even need fixing once this lands.
task.implemented: PARTIAL: RoadmapSummary.for_projects/1 parallelization (Task.async_stream, bounded :roadmap_summary_timeout_ms) shipped and KEPT. But the second half — deferring the roadmap rollup off mount (assign empty :roadmap, load on post-connect tick) — was REVERTED (72edccd): an empty summaries map makes RunFeed.landed_sha skip the shipped_in witness and fall through to branch_landed_sha -> ResultStore.landed_sha_for_run, a per-row 'git fetch origin' for every history row, hanging the /harness render. The 37ms browser check missed it (no busy/unlanded-row state at the time). Root cause of the original slowness is that per-render git fetch, not the roadmap shell-outs — tracked as a follow-up.

task.title: Dashboard live_runs/0 fan-out: a busy run gen_statem must not stall the run feed (bounded Run.status read + skip)
acceptance_criteria: StatusView.live_runs/0 (and the Run.status fan-out it drives) tolerates a busy/blocked run gen_statem: a status read that cannot return promptly is bounded by a short timeout and that run is omitted from the snapshot (it reappears on the next tick) rather than blocking the whole dashboard.
A single stuck run process cannot stall mount, handle_params, or recompute_active; the run feed renders without waiting on the slowest run.
Redundant live_runs/0 calls within one render cycle are reduced (mount's snapshot + handle_params' apply_action currently each recompute it).
Unit test: a deliberately slow/blocked run process does not delay the snapshot beyond the timeout.
Verify the run feed stays responsive with active runs present.
out_of_scope: The RoadmapSummary shell-out fix (the sibling task).
No change to Run gen_statem state semantics beyond a bounded status read.
task.body: Secondary cause from the 2026-06-08 dashboard-slowness investigation. StatusView.live_runs/0 maps Run.status/1 (a synchronous gen_statem call) over every live run, and is invoked multiple times per page render (mount snapshot, handle_params apply_action, recompute_active) plus every 5s meta_tick and every run lifecycle event. When a run's gen_statem is busy (committing, driving its Port, lander rebasing) the call blocks behind that process's mailbox — fitting the 3.7-4.3s HANDLE PARAMS replies in the logs. Make the fan-out resilient: bound each status read and skip a non-responsive run, and trim redundant live_runs/0 calls per render. Lower confidence and smaller win than the sibling RoadmapSummary task — do this AFTER it and re-measure, since that fix alone may resolve the operator-visible pain. Touches the run-lifecycle module (Run.status read path), so it is deliberately split out from the pure dashboard-read-path change to keep that change low-risk.

task.title: Surface audit + lander lifecycle on /harness — broadcast their stage events on a dashboard-subscribed ops feed
acceptance_criteria: Audit runs are observable on /harness: each Harness.Audit run broadcasts its lifecycle (started / settled) on a dashboard-subscribed feed; the audit agent identity, target commit range, and outcome (clean / fixed+pushed / skipped) are visible, and the audit transcript is viewable (it is a real third-family agent run).

Land operations are observable: each Harness.Lander job broadcasts its lifecycle (rebasing / ff-pushed / blocked-by-cap / conflict->resolver / skipped) with the run_id, target branch, and resulting SHA.

Audit + land events do NOT masquerade as %Harness.Run.Status{} rows: they use a distinct feed/topic (recommend harness:ops) and a small Op event struct rendered in their own dashboard panel, so the Active/History run tables stay run-only.

Mechanical only: the feed COUNTS facts (stage, agent, sha, range, outcome) and never computes a verdict (THE MANTRA). The audit clean/fixed judgment already lives in .harness/audit.json; the feed only relays it.
PubSub-guarded like RunFeed: a consumer that skipped the dashboard subtree never crashes on a missing bus.

Tests: the audit + lander broadcast paths are unit-tested (event emitted with the right shape on each transition/terminal); the dashboard panel renders an ops row. LiveView panel hand-built and verified in-browser per the UI-work rule.
out_of_scope: The reviewer/recovery STAGE identity already shipped in commit 89ccebf — those are Harness.Run stages already on RunFeed; this task is only audit + lander, which are separate Oban workers.
Any change to what audit/land DECIDE — only their visibility.
Notification sink behavior: witness events stay as-is; this adds a dashboard feed alongside them, it does not replace sinks.
task.body: Diagnosed 2026-06-08 alongside the reviewer/recovery-identity fix (commit 89ccebf, the inline 'A' half of this investigation). The dashboard's Harness.Dashboard.RunFeed is driven SOLELY by the Harness.Run gen_statem, so only the implementer/reviewer/recovery STAGES of a run reach the dashboard. Harness.Audit.Worker (Oban :audit queue) and Harness.Lander are SEPARATE Oban workers that never broadcast to RunFeed: the post-merge audit (a full third-family agent run, transcript-producing) and every land operation (rebase / ff-push / conflict / resolver) are completely invisible on /harness. The Lander only fires Harness.Notification witness events to configured sinks, not the dashboard PubSub bus. Net effect, in the operator's words (2026-06-08): 'i only see implementer runs, but i can not see audit runs and all the other things.' Fix is mechanical and mantra-clean: give Audit + Lander lifecycle broadcasts on a dedicated harness:ops topic (a small Op event struct, PubSub-guarded like RunFeed) and render them in their own dashboard panel — counting which agent/operation did what, relaying the audit's own .harness/audit.json verdict, never recomputing meaning.
task.implemented: Added Harness.Dashboard.OpsFeed (PubSub-guarded, harness:ops topic) + OpsFeed.Op fact-only event struct; Harness.Audit broadcasts started/settled (with capped agent transcript), Harness.Lander broadcasts landing/landed/conflict/resolving/push_rejected/skipped, Harness.Lander.Resilience broadcasts blocked-at-cap. Dashboard.Live subscribes and renders a bounded newest-first 'Audit & land ops' panel with expandable audit transcripts. Distinct topic keeps Active/History run tables run-only. Unit-tested (ops_feed_test + audit/lander broadcast assertions); panel + live patching + transcript expander verified in-browser.

task.title: Dashboard render hangs on per-row git fetch: move ResultStore landed reconciliation off the /harness render path
acceptance_criteria: No network git operation runs in the synchronous LiveView render/filter path. Harness.ResultStore.landed_sha_for_run/2 currently calls refresh_remote_target/2 (result_store.ex:435 -> `git fetch origin +<target>:refs/remotes/origin/<target>`) once PER history row, reached from RunFeed.landed_sha -> branch_landed_sha -> ResultStore.landed_sha during filter_landed/landed_entry? on every /harness render. Eliminate the per-render fetch.

/harness loads in sub-second wall-clock even with up to @history_limit (200) UNLANDED history rows AND an empty roadmap summaries map (the two conditions that, combined, produced a full render hang: every row falls through the shipped_in witness to the git path). Verify with a bounded `curl -w` against http://localhost:4018/harness, not just idle.

Landed detection still works: the roadmap `shipped_in` witness (RoadmapSummary) stays the fast primary; the branch-reachability fallback must consult only LOCAL refs (origin/<target> kept fresh by the lander's own fetch/push), or be moved to a cached cold-path computation (e.g. refreshed on roadmap_tick), never a synchronous network call during render.

test/harness/dashboard/run_feed_test.exs landed / rebased-equivalent / unlanded cases still pass — that suite currently relies on refresh_remote_target populating origin/<target>; update the setup to fetch locally (or assert against local refs) so it exercises the new no-network-in-render contract.
mix precommit.full green; no dialyzer/credo regressions on the touched modules.
out_of_scope: The RoadmapSummary.for_projects parallelization (already shipped in task 241, kept).
The StatusView.live_runs/0 Run.status fan-out (separate task 242) — unless it is trivially in the same render pass.
Any change to the lander's own fetch/push or to landing semantics outside the dashboard read path.
task.body: Root cause found 2026-06-08 while debugging a full /harness hang (http=000, server never responds). Process-stacktrace capture on the hung request showed ~9 stacked requests all blocked in System.cmd -> Harness.Git.run -> ResultStore.refresh_remote_target -> `git fetch origin`, called from Harness.Dashboard.Live.landed_entry?/3 (live.ex:461) -> RunFeed.landed_sha (run_feed.ex:52) -> branch_landed_sha (run_feed.ex:113) -> ResultStore.landed_sha (result_store.ex:184) -> landed_sha_for_run (result_store.ex:416). RunFeed.landed_sha is `roadmap_landed_sha(summaries) || branch_landed_sha(projects)`: when the roadmap summaries map lacks a shipped_in for a row (every unlanded run, or — in the reverted task-241 deferral — EVERY row), it falls through to branch_landed_sha which does a network git fetch PER ROW. With up to 200 history rows this is 200 sequential network fetches inside the synchronous render = the original '12-15s under load' AND the hang. The task-241 deferral (empty :roadmap at mount) was reverted (72edccd) as a stopgap so landed rows short-circuit again, but the per-render network fetch remains the real defect for unlanded rows under load. Fix: get the network call off the render path per the harness mantra (render = mechanics only, no blocking I/O). Hand-build in a fresh session with browser/curl + the run_feed test suite.
task.implemented: Removed per-row git fetch from ResultStore.landed_sha_for_run (local refs only; lander keeps origin/<target> fresh). Render-path RunFeed.landed_sha/3 is now pure (roadmap shipped_in witness || landed_cache map lookup); branch-reachability moved to cold-path RunFeed.branch_landed_cache/3 (local git, no fetch), refreshed on connect + roadmap_tick into a :landed_cache assign. /harness renders in 52ms (curl). run_feed_test rewritten to fetch locally + assert via the cache; +witness short-circuit test. precommit.full green.

task.title: Run-lifecycle in_progress claim survives concurrent tasks.toml writers
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent in_progress claims from N simultaneous runs on the same project all persist (no lost-update) — test fires >=3 concurrent mark_in_progress writebacks and asserts every task ends in_progress.
A run that settles approved is never left at pending in tasks.toml due to a racing writer.
No new judgment in harness code; the fix is mechanical write-serialization/durability.
Existing Worker writeback semantics preserved (revert-to-pending on settled failure, stay in_progress on green-unlanded under manual policy).
out_of_scope: Mid-flight landing_policy change not reaching in-flight runs (55 captured manual at dispatch, parked despite auto enabled later) — separate concern.
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-09 during a live cron-autonomy test on onchain_aave: a 3-run wave dispatched concurrently. Each run's Worker.claim_in_progress/2 does a best-effort `rmap status <id> in_progress` writeback to the shared roadmap/tasks.toml. Under 3 simultaneous writers (plus concurrent reads), two of the three claims were lost — tasks 45 and 53 stayed `status = "pending"` even though their runs settled `:approved`. Only the lone task (55) whose claim won kept `in_progress`.

Consequence is not cosmetic: the cron poller reads the LOCAL tasks.toml via Roadmap.ready/1. An approved-but-`pending` task is re-eligible, so the next tick re-dispatches already-finished (here, already-landed) work — a full implement->review->land cycle of wasted agent tokens, or a conflicting second copy.

rmap's validate-then-write protects write VALIDITY, not against lost updates between two valid concurrent writers (documented hazard in rmap.md). The lander already solves the same class for its own roadmap writeback via the Durable path (detached worktree at target tip -> commit -> ff-push, Harness.Roadmap.Durable) so concurrent landers never clobber each other.

TODO: make the start-of-run in_progress claim resilient to concurrent writers. Candidates: (a) route the claim through the lander's Durable/serialized writeback; (b) serialize per-project roadmap mutations through one GenServer/Oban-serialized queue; (c) lock-or-retry on the file in rmap status. Pick the one fitting the mechanical-substrate rule — git/file-IO serialization, not judgment.

task.title: ResultStore MCP read tools resolve configured() store when param omitted (KPIs read empty via MCP)
acceptance_criteria: The api()-annotated ResultStore read tools (aggregate_by_agent, list_capability_scores — and any sibling whose Elixir default is `configured()` but whose api() `store` default is `nil`) resolve the configured store when the MCP/chat caller omits `store`, instead of hitting the `nil`/`false` disabled short-circuit that returns {:ok, %{}} / {:ok, []}.

Elixir-side behavior is unchanged: `false`/`nil` still explicitly short-circuits (disabled store), and an explicit store override still wins. Only the MISSING-param path changes from nil->disabled to nil->configured().

Fix is at the api() surface, not by deleting the disabled short-circuit: prefer an api() default sentinel that resolves configured() (or drop the `store` param from the tool schema and resolve internally), so `false`/`nil` overrides remain expressible.

Regression test: invoking each affected tool through the descripex/MCP dispatch path (Harness.Chat.Tools / Manifest) with no `store` arg returns the populated aggregate/list from the configured Postgres store, not the empty disabled value. A test with explicit store=false still returns the disabled value.
mix test.json green
task.body:
Observed 2026-06-10 driving harness from an orchestrator: `result_store-aggregate_by_agent` returned {} and `list_capability_scores` returned [] over MCP, while the Postgres store held 118 run records and a fully-populated per-agent rollup (verified via tidewave: `Harness.ResultStore.aggregate_by_agent(configured())` returns real KPIs). KPIs ARE persisting and changing — the MCP surface just reads them as empty.

Root cause: the Elixir fns default `store \ configured()` (lib/harness/result_store.ex), but their `api()` annotations declare the `store` param with `default: nil` (e.g. aggregate_by_agent at ~line 207-211, list_capability_scores). descripex passes the api default (nil) when the caller omits the param, which lands on the `aggregate_by_agent(nil)` / `aggregate_by_agent(false)` disabled-short-circuit clause -> {:ok, %{}}. So the two defaults diverge: Elixir callers get the configured store, MCP/chat callers get the disabled value.

Impact: any orchestrator reading KPIs / capability scores over MCP to make routing or recommendation decisions sees a false "no data" signal — exactly the input dispatch-recommend's explore/exploit routing keys off. Misleading, not just cosmetic.

Out of scope: the separate `list_run_records` MCP sharp edge (its `filters` param must be a keyword list, which JSON can't express — passing a JSON object raises a function-clause on the `is_list/1` guard). File separately if it bites; this task is only the store-default divergence on the no-arg aggregate/list reads.

task.title: Reviewer selection: AgentRegistry.available? must deprioritize, not eliminate, an installed cross-family reviewer (soft hint used as hard gate discards completed work)
acceptance_criteria: reviewer_dispatchable?/1 (run.ex:2100) no longer ANDs AgentRegistry.available?/1 as a hard eligibility gate. The real eligibility gates are installed? and reviewer_eligible? ALONE; availability moves to the ORDERING (prioritize_reviewers), not the filter — an installed, eligible, cross-family adapter is NEVER removed from the slate merely because the soft, TTL-less, restart-cleared availability hint says it's busy.

auto_reviewer_modules/1 returns a NON-EMPTY slate whenever at least one installed + reviewer_eligible? + cross-family adapter exists, regardless of every adapter's availability flag. Availability deprioritizes (sinks an unavailable reviewer in the rotation order) but never empties the slate. {:no_cross_family_reviewer, _} is reserved for the genuinely-empty case (nothing installed/eligible/cross-family), not a transient availability blip.

The same relaxation applies to the explicit-pin path: explicit_reviewer_dispatchable?/1 / resolve_single_reviewer/2 must not fail an installed, eligible, cross-family pinned reviewer with {:reviewer_unavailable, module} solely on the availability hint (it may still deprioritize / order). Same-family and not-installed pins still fail as today.

Regression test (the documented failure): an installed, reviewer-eligible, cross-family adapter that AgentRegistry.available?/1 reports false is still selected as the reviewer (settles :reviewing -> :done on approve), NOT discarded as {:review_stuck, {:reviewer_unavailable, _}} / {:no_cross_family_reviewer, _}. A second test: with NO installed cross-family adapter, the run still settles failed with the empty-slate reason (no regression of the legit-empty path).

Mantra check stated in the PR: availability-as-soft-hint is the documented contract (AgentRegistry @moduledoc: 'soft hint, not a contract... correctness lives in Oban'). This change makes reviewer selection honor that contract — it is mechanical filter/ordering, no judgment branch added.
mix test.json green; mix precommit green.
out_of_scope: Reviewer rotation on spawn/idle TIMEOUT — already shipped (Task 228); this task is strictly about the slate being emptied at SELECTION time by the availability filter, which 228's rotation cannot recover (it rotates a non-empty slate).
AgentRegistry availability semantics themselves (TTL, persistence, what marks an agent unavailable) — unchanged; this task only stops reviewer selection from treating the hint as a hard gate.
reviewer_eligible? / per-agent reviewer toggle (Task 182) — that operator gate stays a real filter; only available? moves to ordering.
The KPI attribution of the resulting review_stuck runs — Task 249.
task.body:
## Observation (KPI muster, 2026-06-10, over 118 post-agent-gate run records)
8 of 13 non-approvals are reviewer-SELECTION failures where the implementer SUCCEEDED and its work was discarded:
- 6 cursor + 1 grok runs: reason = {:review_stuck, "No cross-family reviewer adapter available: {:reviewer_unavailable, Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude}"}. agent_outcome_kind=exited, exit_status=0, real diffs (1551/1265/402/287 lines), MB of captured output — then discarded at reviewer selection.
- 1 claude run: {:review_stuck, {:same_family_reviewer, :claude, Harness.AgentAdapter.Claude}} — only candidate left was same-family.
- Clustered 2026-06-07/08 (six within 5 minutes, 01:20-01:25) — a single window where the soft availability hint had the whole cross-family slate marked unavailable. Across all 9 review_stuck records: reviewer_rotation_count=0, reviewer_reprompt_count=0, recovery_attempts=0 — no fallback fired.

This is the single biggest source of wasted agent tokens in the dataset: ~8 full implement cycles thrown away at the finish line for a reason unrelated to work quality.

## Root cause (confirmed in run.ex:2100-2105)
reviewer_dispatchable?/1 = available? AND installed? AND reviewer_eligible?. auto_reviewer_modules/1 (run.ex:2004) filters the cross-family slate by reviewer_dispatchable?, so when AgentRegistry.available?/1 (a soft latency hint — no persistence, no TTL, cleared on restart per the AgentRegistry @moduledoc) reports false for every adapter, the slate is EMPTY and the run is discarded. The comment at run.ex:2091-2097 documents fixing THIS EXACT failure mode once already — they decoupled the implementer-level enabled? flag from reviewer-dispatchability because coupling 'settled every run :review_stuck'. The identical bug survives through available? still being a hard AND.

## The fix (mechanical, honors the documented soft-hint contract)
Move available? out of the hard-gate AND in reviewer_dispatchable? and into prioritize_reviewers ordering: installed? + reviewer_eligible? + cross-family are the real gates; availability only sinks a busy reviewer lower in the rotation order. The slate is then non-empty whenever an installed eligible cross-family adapter exists, so completed implementer work is reviewed (possibly after a moment's wait / rotation) instead of discarded. This is the same shape as the enabled?-decoupling fix already in the file. No judgment added — pure filter/ordering mechanics.

Pairs with Task 228 (timeout-rotation of a non-empty slate) and Task 249 (count the residual review_stuck by cause so we can confirm this fix landed).

task.title: AgentKPI quality rollup reads legacy-empty review_ratings — repoint to review_skills so the quality signal isn't dark since the v0_13 rubric migration
acceptance_criteria: AgentKPI's per-agent quality rollup is computed from the reviewer's CURRENT scoring block — review_skills (the two-axis scored skills from Task 224/225), NOT the legacy review_ratings map that the reviewer stopped writing on 2026-06-06. record_ratings/1 (agent_kpi.ex:285) is repointed (or a new record_skills/1 added) to read review_skills, reducing the per-skill {score, note} entries to the per-agent quality mean(s) the KPI surfaces.

Back-compat: records that carry only the legacy review_ratings (pre-2026-06-06, ~52 runs) still contribute their scores — read review_skills when present, fall back to review_ratings when review_skills is empty. Neither a missing block nor a present-but-empty one crashes the rollup (=> %{} / no contribution, never an exception).

The two sibling stale reads are repointed consistently or explicitly justified: batch/agent_evaluation.ex:238 entry_ratings/1 and dispatch.ex:1223 (record.review_ratings -> ratings) — whichever feed a live quality surface. If one is intentionally legacy-only, say so in a code comment; do not silently leave a second dark read.

Verified against live data: after the change, the /harness/kpi quality column (and the AgentKPI aggregate the MCP tool returns) is NON-EMPTY for runs inserted on/after 2026-06-06 (50 approved runs that currently roll up to an empty quality mean because review_ratings is {} but review_skills is populated).

Tests cover: a record with populated review_skills yields a non-empty quality mean; a legacy record with only review_ratings still contributes (back-compat); an empty/missing both-blocks record contributes nothing without crashing. NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES assertions (flunk on unexpected), not assert-true-on-any-outcome.
mix test.json green.
out_of_scope: Changing the reviewer prompt or the review.json skills/facets contract (shipped in Task 224/225).
Migrating historical review_ratings rows into review_skills — read both, don't backfill.
The /harness/kpi facet PIVOT itself (Task 225, done) — this is only about the quality metric INSIDE each agent row reading the right field.
Any routing/dispatch-recommend change consuming the corrected quality signal — separate.
task.body:
## Observation (KPI muster, 2026-06-10)
review_ratings is populated on 52/118 run records, and ZERO of the 50 approved runs since 2026-06-06 have it. But review_skills + review_facets ARE populated on 100% of runs from 2026-06-06 on. The reviewer didn't stop scoring — Task 224/225 (v0_13 rubric foundation) REPLACED the flat 4-key review_ratings block (performance/truthfulness/code_quality/idiom) with the two-axis review_skills block (programming domains x cross-cutting qualities, each {score, note}). log_record.ex:18 literally calls review_ratings 'the legacy flat KPI block, kept for back-compat'.

## The bug
The record WRITE migrated; the KPI READ did not. agent_kpi.ex:285:
    defp record_ratings(record), do: Map.get(record, :review_ratings) || %{}
AgentKPI's quality rollup still reads review_ratings, which is {} for every run in the last 5 days. So the quality column on /harness/kpi and the AgentKPI aggregate (surfaced via the MCP KPI tool, and the input Task 177 made load-bearing) compute over empty maps for all post-rubric-migration runs — the reviewer-judged quality signal has been dark since 2026-06-06 even though every run was scored. Same stale read at batch/agent_evaluation.ex:238 (entry_ratings) and dispatch.ex:1223.

## Fix
Repoint the quality rollup to review_skills (reduce per-skill scores to the agent's quality mean), falling back to review_ratings for legacy records so the ~52 older runs still count. Pure field-migration + back-compat read — mantra-clean fact counting, no judgment. Mirrors how Task 225 already pivots the page by review_facets; this fixes the per-agent quality metric inside each row to read the field the reviewer actually writes.

task.title: KPI: surface review_stuck by cause + count selection-time stuck (nil reviewer_adapter) as orchestration health
acceptance_criteria: AgentKPI exposes a review_stuck-BY-CAUSE count, bucketed by parsing the already-persisted reason field's tag (the second element of the {:review_stuck, detail} tuple / reason atom): reviewer_unavailable, no_cross_family_reviewer, same_family_reviewer, reviewer_crashed (:killed), driver_crashed, timed_out, cancelled, other. Pure counting of an existing fact — no classifier/regex inferring fault beyond reading the tag harness itself wrote.

Selection-time stuck runs (reviewer_adapter IS NULL — no reviewer was ever assigned) are counted in this orchestration-health rollup. Task 231's per-reviewer no_verdict_rate is keyed on reviewer_adapter and therefore misses these (8 of 9 current review_stuck records have nil reviewer_adapter); this rollup is the home for them as a harness-health number, NOT attributed to any reviewer (correctly — no reviewer was at fault).

The signal is surfaced where AgentKPI already surfaces (the MCP KPI/reliability tool and/or /harness/kpi), consistent with existing presentation — a small orchestration-health line/section, no net-new design surface. Backend (AgentKPI struct + MCP) is the required deliverable; the dashboard line may ride along or be a thin follow-on if it needs LiveView hand-build.

Tests cover: by-cause bucketing from seeded reason values (incl. a nil-reviewer_adapter reviewer_unavailable run landing in the health rollup, not a per-reviewer bucket); an approve run contributes nothing to the stuck rollup. NEVER-HIDE-FAILURES assertions.
mix test.json green.
out_of_scope: Reducing the review_stuck RATE — that is the fix (Task 247); this task only instruments it so the fix is confirmable and regressions are visible.

Re-attributing stuck runs to the implementer or to a reviewer — Task 231 already settled attribution (excluded from implementer denominator; per-reviewer no_verdict_rate keyed on reviewer_adapter). This adds the by-cause health view those leave out.
Persisting more reviewer diagnostics — Task 232 (done) already captures reviewer raw output/outcome.
task.body:
## Why (KPI muster, 2026-06-10; user asked that reviewer-selection failures be tracked in KPIs)
The dominant non-approval class is review_stuck (8 of 13), and Task 247 will fix most of it — but crashes, cancellations, and any future selection regression will still produce stuck runs, and we currently can't SEE the rate by cause. Task 231 (done) handles attribution (review_stuck excluded from the implementer's success denominator; a per-reviewer no_verdict_rate keyed on reviewer_adapter). But 8 of the 9 current review_stuck records have reviewer_adapter = NULL (the run died at SELECTION, before any reviewer was assigned), so 231's per-reviewer ledger never counts them — they vanish into a nil bucket.

## What to add
A review_stuck-by-CAUSE orchestration-health count in AgentKPI, bucketed on the reason tag harness already wrote ({:review_stuck, {:reviewer_unavailable,_}} / {:no_cross_family_reviewer,_} / {:same_family_reviewer,_} / 'Reviewer crashed: :killed' / driver_crashed / timed_out / cancelled). This is the harness self-diagnostic that confirms Task 247 landed (reviewer_unavailable/no_cross_family counts should drop to ~0 after it) and catches regressions.

## Mantra check
Pure counting of an existing persisted fact — the reason field already STATES the cause; this rollup only buckets and counts it. No 'whose fault' heuristic, no classifier beyond reading the tag. Counting, not judgment.

task.title: Validate model↔resolved-adapter compatibility at dispatch — reject an incompatible pin pre-spawn, not a mid-run crash
acceptance_criteria: Each AgentAdapter declares the models/families it can run (a capability field or model_supported?/1 predicate); Antigravity's existing {:unsupported_model,_} rejection folds into the same contract.

The dispatch boundary validates the pinned model against the RESOLVED adapter (post assignee/override/recommend) BEFORE Port spawn; an incompatible pair settles loudly (e.g. {:invalid_model_for_adapter, adapter, model}), never a mid-run crash.
Regression test reproduces the T75 case: dispatching a cursor-pinned opus model on the codex adapter is rejected pre-spawn with that reason.
Unpinned tasks and compatible pairs (cursor+opus, codex+gpt-class) dispatch unchanged.
Validation is family/prefix-based or sourced from each adapter's --list-models, not a brittle baked literal allowlist; the maintenance seam is documented.
Tests cover incompatible-reject, compatible-pass, unpinned-pass, and antigravity-unsupported-model-still-handled.
out_of_scope: Reviewer-model pinning — reviewer is cross-family and unpinned by design.
Auto-rerouting a mismatched dispatch to a compatible adapter — fail loud, do not guess operator intent.
task.body:
DISCOVERED 2026-06-10 dogfooding tapakly. Task 75 (assignee=cursor, model="claude-opus-4-8-thinking-high" — a VALID cursor pairing) was dispatched with an explicit codex adapter override. codex received the cursor-only opus pin and crashed instantly ("'claude-opus-4-8-thinking-high' not supported on a ChatGPT Codex account") before producing any diff — the implementer leg was wasted and the cross-family reviewer implemented T75 from scratch, collapsing implementer/reviewer separation (FX work shipped self-graded).

The roadmap DATA was not wrong: all 7 opus-pinned tapakly tasks are assignee=cursor, and cursor is the multi-model front-end that runs opus. The mismatch was introduced at DISPATCH time — the resolved adapter (codex, via override/recommend) diverged from the model pin's compatible family, and nothing validates the {resolved_adapter, model} pair before spawn.

SURFACE: harness task 7062 (done) now threads the pinned model into Invocation -> --model. Correct, but it converted a previously-silent no-op (bad pin ignored, adapter ran its default) into a hard mid-run crash: a pin the resolved adapter cannot run now reaches the CLI.

PRIOR ART: the Antigravity adapter already rejects model overrides pre-spawn with {:error,{:unsupported_model,model}} (agy has no --model). Generalize into the contract: each adapter declares the models/families it can run (or a compat predicate); the dispatch boundary validates the pinned model against the RESOLVED adapter (after assignee/override/recommend resolution) BEFORE Port spawn, settling with a clear reason instead of crashing. Mechanical validation (family/prefix), not judgment. codex runs OpenAI/codex models, not anthropic opus; cursor runs opus/sonnet/gpt/gemini per --list-models; claude runs anthropic. Model IDs churn -> prefer family/prefix matching or the adapter's own --list-models over a baked literal allowlist.

task.title: Discovery-filing stage: implementer/reviewer/audit agents file follow-ups via rmap new, not lose them or bury them in TODO comments
acceptance_criteria: The audit-agent prompt instructs the agent that when it notices follow-up work during its commit-range review (tech debt, an orphaned code path, an uncovered edge case, a deferred decision), it files each as a real rmap task via `rmap new` against the project's roadmap_path — and names the filed task id(s) in its `.audit/<sha>.md` report.

The reviewer prompt instructs the reviewer that genuine follow-ups it surfaces while gating (and chooses NOT to fix inline) are filed via `rmap new` in its worktree (riding the merge-train commit), not just mentioned in the prose verdict where they evaporate.

rmap is available on PATH inside both worktrees (implementer/reviewer branch worktree AND the audit's detached origin/<target> worktree); if it is not already, harness ensures it is — this is mechanical plumbing, not judgment.

Mantra-clean: harness does NOT classify what is a discovery, score it, or decide whether to file — the AGENT decides and runs `rmap new` itself; harness reads nothing back and recomputes no meaning. The only harness change is making the rmap CLI reachable + the prompt text.

tasks.toml multi-writer safety is addressed: concurrent runs filing discoveries must not corrupt the file or collide on ids — rely on rmap's validate-then-write + let the merge-train rebase reconcile tasks.toml; document the residual conflict path (a rebase conflict on tasks.toml falls through to the existing Lander.Resolver), do not add a lock.

Tests: a fixture audit/review prompt-render asserts the discovery-filing instruction is present; an integration-style assertion that a `rmap new` run inside a worktree produces a parseable task (no harness-side parsing of the result).
mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: Harness deciding/ranking which discoveries are worth filing — that is the agent's judgment (mantra). Harness only supplies the CLI + prompt.
Auto-scoring filed discoveries (the agent supplies D/B/U or leaves them for a later scoring pass; harness computes no scores).
A new Oban stage or worker — this is a prompt-surface + PATH change to the EXISTING reviewer and audit stages, not a new lifecycle node.
Dedup of near-duplicate filed tasks across parallel runs (rmap.md's human dedupe gate covers it; agents filing a near-clone is acceptable churn, not a blocker).
task.body:
Surfaced 2026-06-10: dispatched runs (tapakly T90/T95) landed clean but filed ZERO follow-up
tasks — not because there were none worth filing in general, but because no harness stage
PROMPTS an agent to run `rmap new`. The implementer commits code, the reviewer gates+fixes and
writes .harness/review.json, the lander merges, the auditor writes .audit/<sha>.md — none is told
to capture discoveries into the roadmap. So any tech-debt/edge-case/orphaned-path an agent notices
lives (at best) in prose in a verdict/audit artifact and evaporates. This is the harness analogue
of the global CLAUDE.md rule "Capture Discoveries as Tasks" — which today only humans honor.

The fix is a discovery-filing instruction added to the reviewer prompt and (primarily) the
audit-agent prompt: when you notice follow-up work, FILE it via `rmap new` against the project's
roadmap_path, and name the filed id(s) in your artifact. The audit agent is the natural primary
home — it is batch-scoped, post-merge, already reflects over a commit range, and already writes
report artifacts; per-run reviewer filing is the secondary channel for follow-ups the reviewer
declines to fix inline.

Mantra discipline (non-negotiable): harness must NOT judge what counts as a discovery, score it,
or decide to file. The agent decides and runs the CLI; harness's only change is mechanical —
ensure `rmap` is on PATH in the worktrees and add the prompt text. Harness reads nothing back.

This also resolves the ROOT CAUSE behind Task 43 ("Dogfood verification reds on pre-existing TODO
comments in dispatch base"): the audit agent currently records follow-ups by inserting
`# TODO(Task NN):` source comments, which dispatched worktrees inherit and which trip `credo
--strict` TagTODO, penalizing the next agent for debt that isn't theirs. A proper rmap task is
strictly better: it is the durable, queryable, dispatchable record a source comment can never be,
and it leaves no TODO in the tree. Filing-as-rmap-task should REPLACE the TODO-comment habit in
the audit prompt.

Cross-ref: Task 43 (TODO-comment dispatch-base reds — this supersedes its workaround candidates);
bundle audit-agent (the post-merge audit role); the agent-gate workflow (docs/agent-gate-workflow.md).

task.title: Per-project warm_paths: pre-seed a project's gitignored worktree inputs (source/corpus) so agents don't relink/regenerate the corpus on every run
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Project gains a `warm_paths` field (list of repo-relative dir strings, default []); struct + @type updated; a project that omits it behaves byte-identically to today.

Persisted in ProjectRegistry: `warm_paths` column added to lib/harness/project_registry/schema/project.ex + a migration; the field round-trips through register -> lookup (DB-is-truth), default [] when absent.

Worktree.warm/2 seeds the UNION (de-duplicated) of @default_warm_paths (deps/_build/priv/plts) and the project's warm_paths — it EXTENDS, never REPLACES, the defaults: a project declaring `priv/ccxt` still warms deps/_build/PLT. The best-effort / always-:ok / seedable?(parent-present AND worktree-absent) semantics from Task 226 are unchanged.
Threaded from the project into BOTH warm call sites: run.ex (implementer+reviewer worktree, ~line 636) and audit.ex (auditor worktree, ~line 136) pass `warm_paths: project.warm_paths`.
Pure mechanics, mantra-clean: warming copies bytes and classifies nothing; no judgment/branch/regex added, and Harness.Verification is NOT reintroduced.

Tests: a project with warm_paths: ["priv/foo"] seeds priv/foo (parent-present + worktree-absent) into a fresh worktree AND still seeds deps/_build; an unset project warms byte-identically to before; the persisted warm_paths round-trips through the registry.
mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: Registering ccxt_extract with warm_paths = ["priv/ccxt", "priv/discoveries"] — that is a post-land registration/config step (config/dev.local.exs), not part of this harness change.
Regenerating the ccxt_extract discovery corpus (the operator runs `mix ccxt_extract.update` on development; warm/2 copies FROM that fresh local checkout).
Committing the gitignored corpus or editing ccxt_extract's .gitignore — the corpus stays a derived artifact; warming is how worktrees get it.
Removing/altering the global `:harness, :worktree, :warm_paths` config — per-project warm_paths EXTENDS the resolved defaults; the global config remains the cross-project fallback.
task.body:
WHAT THIS IS (reframed 2026-06-11): a worktree-warming OPTIMIZATION, not a review_stuck root-cause fix. ccxt_extract's gitignored corpus (`/priv/ccxt` vendored CCXT TS source + `/priv/discoveries/*`, .gitignore lines 21/34-35; only class_hierarchy.json is tracked) is NOT materialized by `git worktree add`, which copies tracked files only. Agents work around that TODAY by running `mix ccxt_extract.link_corpus` (links the corpus from the main checkout) — confirmed in Task 121's verdict, where the reviewer ran link_corpus itself. So worktrees are NOT corpus-less to agents; they re-acquire it every run.

The cost this removes: that per-run relink/regenerate dance is manual and fragile. Task 121's reviewer linked a SCOPED/partial corpus and still hit 2 partial-corpus test failures (missing 4 ws_* discovery files). Pre-seeding the full corpus via Worktree.warm/2 makes the worktree corpus-complete by construction — agents skip link_corpus, and partial-corpus flakiness goes away.

NOT the cause of the wave-5 review_stuck failures. 78f/63 (and 252's own first run) died `{:cancel, {:review_stuck, ...}}` because of Opus usage-limit/capacity, not a missing corpus — Task 121's implementer "hit an Opus usage limit on its first turn and produced an empty worktree," same firing-13-at-once capacity wall. Those need plain re-dispatch when capacity frees, NOT this task.

THE MECHANISM: Worktree.warm/2 (Task 226) already CoW-seeds gitignored dirs from the parent checkout, but only @default_warm_paths = ["deps", "_build", "priv/plts"], with the only override the GLOBAL `:harness, :worktree, :warm_paths` app config. A global list is the wrong granularity (ccxt_extract wants priv/ccxt + priv/discoveries; harness's own runs want none). Add a per-project `warm_paths` field on %Harness.Project{}, threaded into warm/2 as an EXTENSION of the defaults, so each project declares its own corpus/source inputs.

Operator side (out of scope here): run `mix ccxt_extract.update` on development to refresh local priv/ccxt + priv/discoveries (warm/2 copies FROM there), then register ccxt_extract with warm_paths = ["priv/ccxt", "priv/discoveries"].

Extends Task 226 (the warm/2 mechanism). First implementer run (run-1781158655671-19a1b146) delivered the full diff (commit fb1f939, branch harness/run-1781158655671-19a1b146) but the reviewer died review_stuck (Opus capacity) — salvage via re-review, not re-implement.
task.implemented: Landed by codex via merge-train; reviewer-approved (run run-1781173212312-bd2a79a1, 840f689043b4b19bd99e503bbea96a1f16fd50ed).

task.title: MCP api() param coercion breaks guarded fns: await/5 (float timeout_ms) + list_run_records/1 (map filters)
acceptance_criteria: dispatch-await with an explicit timeout_ms (e.g. 1800000) no longer raises 'no function clause matching in Harness.Dispatch.await/5' — JSON number reaches await/5 as float, missing is_integer(timeout_ms)

result_store-list_run_records (with filters object OR empty) no longer raises 'no function clause matching in Harness.ResultStore.list_run_records/1' — JSON object reaches the fn as a map, missing the is_list(filters) guard

CRITICAL: the map->keyword coercion MUST atomize keys (String.to_existing_atom, guarded) — verified live 2026-06-11 that a naive Map.to_list yields STRING-keyed pairs which silently no-op the filter (list_run_records([{"verdict","approve"}]) returned all 182 records; [{:verdict,"approve"}] correctly returned 161). A coercion that compiles but drops the filter is the hide-the-failure anti-pattern

Root cause confirmed as ONE class: descripex api() delivers JSON numbers as floats and JSON objects as maps, neither coerced to the Elixir fn's guarded type (is_integer / is_list). dispatch-task is unaffected because it has no numeric/object value param

Fix at the descripex api() value-coercion boundary (coerce per declared param kind) so every guarded MCP-exposed fn is covered, OR widen the specific guards (is_number+trunc; accept-map+Map.to_list/Enum.to_list) — default-paths (no param passed) must keep working
Regression tests: await with a float timeout_ms returns {:ok,_}; list_run_records with a map filters returns {:ok, records}
out_of_scope: dispatch-task / dispatch-compare / dispatch-bundle — no numeric/object value param to mis-coerce
Changing the default timeout value
Adding new filters to list_run_records
task.body:
Found 2026-06-11 while testing the updated harness end-to-end (run-1781171110262-3bd79d4f, task 112 tapakly,
which itself landed cleanly — implement->review->land works). TWO MCP-exposed fns fail deterministically, same root class:
(1) dispatch-await with explicit timeout_ms -> 'no function clause matching in Harness.Dispatch.await/5'; await/5 guards
is_integer(timeout_ms), the JSON number arrives as a float. (2) result_store-list_run_records (filters object or {}) ->
'no function clause matching in Harness.ResultStore.list_run_records/1'; list_run_records/1 guards is_list(filters), the
JSON object arrives as a map. dispatch-task is unaffected (no numeric/object value param; uses integer-literal defaults).
Root: descripex api() value/object params are not coerced to the Elixir fn's guarded type. The single fix site is
Harness.Chat.Tools.coerce_arg/3 (lib/harness/chat/tools.ex) — it ALREADY coerces booleans (string->bool) for both the
chat dispatcher and the MCP surface; add integer coercion (number->trunc, gated on schema type "integer" or is_integer
default) and map->keyword coercion (gated on is_list default; atomize keys via String.to_existing_atom — see the CRITICAL
AC). Both are one investigation + one reviewer pass -> one task. Live debug (tidewave): is_integer(1.8e6)=false;
await_result(_,1.0) raises FunctionClauseError, (_,1) is :ok; list_run_records(%{}) raises, ([]) is :ok.
task.implemented: Split outcome from live tidewave debug. AWAIT = genuine code bug, FIXED: Harness.Dispatch.await/5 + await_result/2 widened is_integer->is_number and trunc the timeout once at the receive boundary (lib/harness/dispatch.ex). JSON callers deliver timeout_ms as a float; the old is_integer guard FunctionClause'd the whole dispatch-await tool. 2 regression tests added (float await/5 reaches project lookup; await_result/2 truncs 20.9->20); dispatch_test 80/80 green; verified in the live node via tidewave (await_result(_,1.0)->timed_out timeout_ms:1; await(_,_,_,1.8e6 float)->reaches start). LIST_RUN_RECORDS = NOT a code bug: the map->keyword coercion WITH key-atomization already shipped in task 146 (Harness.Chat.Tools.decode_param line-231 clause + to_atom_kwlist); in-process Tools.dispatch works (182 unfiltered / 161 filtered, keys atomized) and tools_test.exs:86 passes. The live MCP result_store-list_run_records failure is real but UNREPRODUCIBLE in-process and its root cause is unconfirmed (transport/connection-level, no stale frame found via :sys.get_state); most likely the long-running node needs a restart to rebuild MCP server state. No code change made for it; if it persists after a node restart, file a separate transport-level task. Shipped c9a1b88.

task.title: decode_param: JSON-string-encoded keyword/object params from MCP clients (completes 253's list_run_records AC)
acceptance_criteria: Harness.Chat.Tools.decode_param/2 decodes a JSON-string-encoded object/array (e.g. filters arriving as the literal string '{"agent": "cursor"}') into a keyword list for list-default value params, BEFORE the binary falls through to the target fn's is_list guard

result_store-list_run_records with a real MCP-client filters argument no longer raises 'no function clause matching in Harness.ResultStore.list_run_records/1' — verified live over the wire after BEAM restart (filtered query returned the filtered record set)
A non-JSON string for a keyword param surfaces as {:error, {:dispatch_failed, _}} (the target guard rejects it) rather than being silently coerced to an empty filter set — no hide-the-failure no-op
Regression test in test/harness/chat/tools_test.exs covers: stringified JSON object -> filtered list; stringified empty object -> list; non-JSON string -> dispatch_failed
Fix is uniform across the whole MCP surface (any list-default value param: filters, env, opts), not point-patched for list_run_records
out_of_scope: The map-shaped filters path — already handled by task 146/253's clause (decode_param map->keyword)
The float-timeout await/5 fix — that is task 253, shipped c9a1b88
Adding new filters to list_run_records or changing default timeout
Declaring a JSON Schema type on descripex kind: :value params (descripex has no type option; dispatcher-level tolerance is the chosen layer)
task.body:
Found 2026-06-11 re-testing the MCP after the task-253 await fix. Task 253's AC claimed result_store-list_run_records (map filters) was fixed and shipped c9a1b88 — but that conclusion was incomplete: the in-process decode_param map->keyword clause (task 146, commit d667e66, line 231) handles filters arriving as a MAP, which is what in-process tests pass. The REAL MCP client (claude-code via anubis) does NOT send a JSON object for a typeless param — it serializes the value as a JSON STRING. Confirmed by tracing the live dispatch with :erlang.trace: anubis delivered %{"filters" => "{\"agent\": \"cursor\", \":limit\": 3}"} — filters is a binary, not a map.

Root cause: descripex's api() kind: :value emits a schema property with description only and no "type", so an MCP client with no type hint stringifies a structured argument as JSON text. decode_param/2 only converted maps (clause 231) and atom-shorthand strings (clause 235); a JSON-string object fell through to the generic binary clause unchanged, so the raw binary reached list_run_records/1 and crashed its is_list(filters) guard. No-filters worked (default [] path); ANY filtered query failed.

Lineage: task 91 added the original keyword-decode; 146 added per-key atomization (to_atom_kwlist); 253 claimed the list_run_records AC but only covered the map path. This task adds the missing clause: for a list-default value param, when the value is a binary, Jason.decode it first; a map decodes via to_atom_kwlist, a list passes through, a non-JSON/non-collection string falls through to value (the target guard then rejects it as dispatch_failed — surfaced, never silently no-op'd).

Verified end-to-end: Tools.dispatch in-process (8/8 tools_test green incl. new regression), then live over MCP after the user restarted the BEAM — result_store-list_run_records {"agent":"cursor","limit":2} returned the 2 filtered cursor records. Hand-built + hand-tested (no cross-family reviewer), so not --verified.
task.implemented: decode_param/2 gained a clause for binary value + list-default param: Jason.decode the string, then map->to_atom_kwlist / list passthrough / non-JSON falls through to value (target guard rejects as dispatch_failed, never silent no-op). Completes task 253's list_run_records AC — 253 only covered map-shaped filters (in-process); the real MCP client serializes the typeless param as a JSON string (confirmed via :erlang.trace: anubis delivered filters as a binary). 8/8 tools_test green + new regression (string-object/empty/non-json); verified live over MCP after BEAM restart (filtered cursor query returned 2 filtered records). Hand-built, not cross-family reviewed -> not verified.

task.title: Per-role reviewer model — split the reviewer model from the implementer's per-agent default
acceptance_criteria: A per-role reviewer model override exists (e.g. `{:reviewer_model, agent}` Config entries, `:string`, ui_editable?), distinct from the shared `{:agent_model, agent}` default added in the base task

Reviewer model resolution precedence: `{:reviewer_model, agent}` (if set) > `{:agent_model, agent}` > agent CLI ambient default — so an unset reviewer override falls back to the shared per-agent default exactly as today
Implementer model resolution is unchanged: task `model` pin > `{:agent_model, agent}` > ambient (the reviewer override never touches the implementer path)

A test proves cursor-implements-with-Composer + cursor-reviews-with-Opus: implementer Invocation.model and reviewer Invocation.model differ for the SAME agent when the reviewer override is set (extend the FakeAdapter :capture_model / :review_capture_model fixtures + a registered-reviewer path or a unit seam for the reviewer-agent resolution)
Settings page (/harness/settings) renders the reviewer-model overrides alongside the existing Agent models card; blank = inherit the shared default
mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: Per-PROJECT reviewer model (this is global per-agent-per-role; project-level pin is a separate task if ever needed)
Validating model ids against `--list-models` (free-text, unvalidated — ids churn, matching the base task)
Changing reviewer ADAPTER selection (cross-family auto-pick / rotation is untouched; this only sets the model the selected reviewer runs)
task.body:
Follow-up to the base task that made per-agent default model configurable (`Config.agent_model/1` → `{:agent_model, agent}`, threaded onto both implementer and reviewer Invocations, plus the Agent-models settings card).

THE GAP this closes: today the reviewer model comes from the SAME `{:agent_model, agent}` default as the implementer. So setting `cursor → claude-opus-4-8-thinking-high` forces Opus on BOTH cursor-implements and cursor-reviews runs — you cannot run the cheap tier for implementation and the strong tier for review on one agent. The asymmetry the operator actually wants (verified 2026-06-11: cursor's headless default is Composer 2.5 Fast; an Opus-grade reviewer needs an explicit pin) is "implement with Composer, REVIEW with Opus" — which a single per-agent model can't express.

THE FIX (direction, not prescription): add a per-role reviewer override that, when set, wins for the reviewer path only; unset falls back to the shared per-agent default. Mirror exactly how a task's `model` overrides the implementer's per-agent default. Reviewer model is resolved in `Harness.Run.reviewer_model/1` (added in the base task) off the selected reviewer adapter's agent; implementer model is resolved at `requested_model` init off `item.agent`.

MANTRA CHECK: this is pure mechanical config (counting/threading a string onto an Invocation), no judgment — clean.

TESTING NOTE: the base task could only prove the reviewer NEGATIVE case (FakeAdapter is unregistered → `agent_for_module` returns error → reviewer model nil), because `AgentRegistry.@agents` is a hardcoded compile-time map with no injection seam. To prove the POSITIVE asymmetry (reviewer override applied for a real reviewer agent) you will need either a registered-reviewer integration path or a small unit seam for the reviewer-agent→model resolution — decide which in the implementation and note the tradeoff.

task.title: Per-agent default model — operator-configurable Config.agent_model, threaded onto implementer + reviewer Invocations
acceptance_criteria: Config.agent_model/1 resolves a per-agent free-text {:agent_model, agent} :string default (one ui_editable entry per implementer agent); unset or blank -> nil (falls through to the agent CLI default); an agent outside the schema -> nil, never raises
Implementer model precedence: task `model` pin > {:agent_model, agent} > agent CLI ambient default (requested_model init off item.agent)
Reviewer model comes solely from {:agent_model, agent} for the selected reviewer adapter's agent (Run.reviewer_model/1); an unregistered reviewer adapter -> nil
/harness/settings renders an Agent models card editing the per-agent values live (blank clears to nil); :string entries route to this card, not the number card
Tests cover unset->nil, put-through, blank-clear, out-of-schema->nil, non-binary reject, implementer-positive + reviewer-negative threading; mix precommit.full green
out_of_scope: Per-role reviewer model override (implement-cheap / review-strong on one agent) -> Task 255
Validating model ids against --list-models (free-text, unvalidated -- ids churn)
Per-project model pin
task.body: Closes the gap between a task's explicit `model` pin and the agent CLI's ambient default: an operator-set per-agent default model, configurable from the dashboard. `Config.agent_model/1` reads a free-text `{:agent_model, agent}` `:string` entry (one per implementer agent), threaded onto BOTH the implementer Invocation (requested_model fallback off item.agent) and the reviewer Invocation (Run.reviewer_model/1 off the selected reviewer adapter's agent -- the reviewer has no task-pin axis, so this is its only model source). New "Agent models" settings card edits the values live (blank = inherit the agent default). Hand-built (config + LiveView surface); 255 builds the per-role reviewer split on top.
task.implemented: Config.agent_model/1 + {:agent_model, agent} :string schema entries (one per implementer agent, ui_editable); blank_to_nil + :string validate clause. Threaded onto implementer (requested_model || item.model || Config.agent_model(item.agent), run.ex:535) and reviewer (Run.reviewer_model/1 off AgentRegistry.agent_for_module, run.ex:2254 — unregistered adapter -> nil). New Agent models settings card (settings_live.ex) reusing set_config; :string entries rejected from the number card. Tests: 6 config_test cases (unset/put-through/blank-clear/out-of-schema/non-binary-reject/schema-shape) + 2 run_test (implementer-positive, reviewer-negative) + FakeAdapter :review_capture_model fixture. Hand-built (config+LiveView), not cross-family reviewed -> not verified.
